```html
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 Version 4.1 for AIX: Programming Concepts</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="enhxwndrestr.html"></A>Restrictions on Using Enhanced X-Windows Calls with GL Subroutines</H2>
<P><A NAME="A3C0F009489mhay"></A>Some GL and Enhanced X-Windows calls cannot be used together. Only a few routines make sense and are valid, while all others result in undefined behavior.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3C0F009510mhay"></A>As mentioned previously, the GL subroutine library is partitioned into two pieces: one, of which the X server remains ignorant, and the second, which operates through Enhanced X-Windows. Due to this partitioning, certain Enhanced X-Windows calls, when invoked with GL calls, result in unpredictable behavior. For this reason, do not use these calls together. The following sections outline restrictions on calls:</P>

<UL><LI><A NAME="A110C1ae"></A><A HREF="enhxwndrestr.html#d6m20nita">Rendering Models</A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A110C1af"></A><A HREF="enhxwndrestr.html#A27m380nita">Color Maps</A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A110C1b0"></A><A HREF="enhxwndrestr.html#F7m380nita">Fonts</A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A110C1b1"></A><A HREF="enhxwndrestr.html#B8m240nita">Internal Properties</A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A110C1b2"></A><A HREF="enhxwndrestr.html#a8m240nita">Fullscreen Mode</A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A110C1b3"></A><A HREF="enhxwndrestr.html#a9m200nita">Coordinate Transformation</A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A110C1b4"></A><A HREF="enhxwndrestr.html#QN8Sg169csol">Mixed GL and Windows Input</A></LI></UL>


<H3><A NAME="A142C11688"></A>List of GL Enhanced X-Windows Subroutines<A NAME="INDEX924" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX925" REL="I2" TITLE="subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX926" REL="I3" TITLE="Windows"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX927" REL="I1" TITLE="Windows"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX928" REL="I2" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX929" REL="I3" TITLE="subroutines"></A>
</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A142C11689"></A><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/getXdpy.html#A114C13c"><B>getXdpy</B></A>
</TD></TR>
<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>
<TD>  Returns the Enhanced X-Windows connection for the given GL session.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A142C1168a"></A><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/getXdpy.html#A114C13c"><B>getXwid</B></A>
</TD></TR>
<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>
<TD>  Returns the Enhanced X-Windows ID of the current GL window.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A142C1168b"></A><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/winX.html#A114C163"><B>winX</B></A>
</TD></TR>
<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>
<TD>  Converts the specified Enhanced X-Windows window into a GL window.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="AAE7457372ttay"></A><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/finish.html#A9URSg3c3csol"><B>finish</B></A>
</TD></TR>
<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>
<TD>  Blocks until all buffers and FIFOs are empty.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="d6m20nita"></A>Rendering Models</H3>
<P><A NAME="A3C0F009544mhay"></A>Enhanced X-Windows calls should not be used to render into a GL window, and GL calls should not be used to render into an Enhanced X-Windows window. The X server is ignorant of the state of a GL window, and the GL subroutines are not aware of Enhanced X-Windows. If rendering into the other type of window is attempted, the most likely outcome is that anything drawn appears either in the wrong colors or the wrong place, or does not appear at all. In some situations, the application exits prematurely.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3C0F009564mhay"></A>The previous restrictions do not imply that you cannot do Enhanced X-Windows and GL drawing within the same process, only that you should not use both rendering models to draw into the same <I>window</I>. As long as Enhanced X-Windows drawing is limited to Enhanced X-Windows windows, and GL drawing is limited to GL windows, there should be no conflicts.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3C0F009584mhay"></A>The following is a partial list of Enhanced X-Windows and AIX drawing routines. Do <I>not</I> use these routines to draw inside a GL window.</P>

<TABLE BORDER="2"><TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD COLSPAN="2">Enhanced X-Windows and AIX Drawing Routines Restricted from GL Windows</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>XClearArea</B></TD>

<TD><B>XDrawString16</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>XClearWindow</B></TD>

<TD><B>XDrawText</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>XDrawArc</B></TD>

<TD><B>XDrawText16</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>XDrawArcsXDrawRectangles</B></TD>

<TD><B>XFillArc</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>XDrawImageString</B></TD>

<TD><B>XFillArcs</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>XDrawImageString16</B></TD>

<TD><B>XFillPolygon</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>XDrawLine</B></TD>

<TD><B>XFillRectangle</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>XDrawLines</B></TD>

<TD><B>XFillRectangles</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>XDrawPoint</B></TD>

<TD><B>XPutImage</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>XDrawPoints</B></TD>

<TD><B>XPutPixel</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>XDrawRectangle</B></TD>

<TD><B>XmStringDraw</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>XDrawRectangles</B></TD>

<TD><B>XmStringDrawImage</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>XDrawSegments</B></TD>

<TD><B>XmStringDrawUnderline</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>XDrawString</B></TD>

<TD><BR></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P><A NAME="A3C0F009609mhay"></A>Do not use GL subroutines on an Enhanced X-Windows window unless that window has first been converted to a GL window with the <!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/winX.html#A114C163"><B>winX</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A27m380nita"></A>Color Maps</H3>
<P><A NAME="A3C0F009630mhay"></A>The AIXwindows window manager does not always install a new colormap immediately. Usually, colormaps are installed only when the input focus changes. This problem can affect color index mode windows, as well as RGB mode windows on the POWERgraphics GTO, POWER Gt4, and POWER Gt4x adapters.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3C0F009650mhay"></A>Although the X server performs overall color map management, including color map creation, allocation, and installation, do not use Enhanced X-Windows calls to change the GL color map, or GL calls to change X color maps.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3C0F009670mhay"></A>Internally, GL maintains two color maps. One is the global color-index-mode color map, and it can be modified by any GL application. The other color map is an internal color map maintained for PseudoRGB graphics adapters. For 8-bit adapters, this internal palette is loaded with a 3-3-2 dithered color map. On 24-bit adapters, this palette is loaded with an 8-8-8 straight ramp. The actual format of either of these two color maps depends on which adapter is installed in your system. Modifying either of these color maps results in unpredictable colors on the screen.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3C0F009690mhay"></A>The following is a partial list of Enhanced X-Windows color map manipulation routines. Do<I> not</I> use these routines to modify GL color maps.</P>

<TABLE BORDER="2"><TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD COLSPAN="2">Enhanced X-Windows Color Map Routines Restricted from GL</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>XAllocColor</B></TD>

<TD><B>XSetRGBColormaps</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>XAllocColorCells</B></TD>

<TD><B>XSetWindowColormaps</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>XAllocColorPlanes</B></TD>

<TD><B>XSetWMColormapWindows</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>XAllocNamedColor</B></TD>

<TD><B>XStoreColor</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>XAllocStandardColormap</B></TD>

<TD><B>XStoreColors</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>XCopyColormapAndFree</B></TD>

<TD><B>XStoreNamedColor</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>XCreateColormap</B></TD>

<TD><B>XUninstallColormap</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>XInstallColormap</B></TD>

<TD><BR></TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="F7m380nita"></A>Fonts</H3>
<P><A NAME="A3C0F009714mhay"></A>Do <I>not</I> use Enhanced X-Windows fonts calls to load a GL font<I>.</I> If you wish to use Enhanced X-Windows fonts with the GL <!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/charstr.html#A143X9cfb"><B>charstr</B></A> subroutine, use the GL <!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/loadXfont.html#vUO390nita"><B>loadXfont</B></A> subroutine to access them. The following Enhanced X-Windows routines cannot be used to load a GL font and do not affect the current GL font:</P>

<UL><LI><A NAME="A110C1bd"></A><B>XLoadFont</B></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A110C1be"></A><B>XLoadQueryFont</B></LI></UL>


<P><A NAME="A3C0F009736mhay"></A>Likewise, do not attempt to use the GL <B>loadXfont</B> subroutine to get a font for Enhanced X-Windows rendering.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3C0F009756mhay"></A>Although the internal GL font structure is almost identical to the Enhanced X-Windows font structure, each font registered with either the <!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/loadXfont.html#vUO390nita"><B>loadXfont</B></A> or <!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/defrasterfont.html#A143X9d3f"><B>defrasterfont</B></A> subroutine associates a handle with that font. GL keeps an internal hash table of all fonts registered for the process. Xfonts need to be registered with GL to be usable by GL.</P>

<H3><A NAME="B8m240nita"></A>Internal Properties</H3>
<P><A NAME="A3C0F009777mhay"></A>GL defines several Enhanced X-Windows properties that are used internally. If these properties are changed or destroyed, unpredictable behavior results. Therefore, use the following routines with caution:</P>

<UL><LI><A NAME="A110C1c2"></A><B>XChangeProperty</B></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A110C1c3"></A><B>XDeleteProperty</B></LI></UL>


<H3><A NAME="A5FADEE402csol"></A>Widgets</H3>
<P><A NAME="A3C0F009800mhay"></A>The GL widget is not properly created and initialized if it is created with the <B>XtCreateManagedWidget</B> subroutine. To properly create and initialize the GL widget, use the <B>XtCreateWidget</B> subroutine and subsequently manage the widget with the <B>XtManageChild</B> subroutine.</P>

<H3><A NAME="a8m240nita"></A>Fullscreen Mode</H3>
<P><A NAME="A3C0F009821mhay"></A>In the current implementation of the GL <!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/fullscrn.html#Qga140marj"><B>fullscrn</B></A> subroutine, the pointer is grabbed so that all input is redirected to the process that has called the <B>fullscrn</B> subroutine. Ungrabbing the pointer prematurely causes unpredictable results. Performing any other grabs or ungrabs can also cause unpredictable results within a <B>fullscrn</B>/<!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/endfullscrn.html#laa350marj"><B>endfullscrn</B></A> subroutine pair.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3C0F009840mhay"></A>The following Enhanced X-Windows functions interfere with GL fullscreen mode. Do <I>not</I> use these routines when GL is in fullscreen mode<I>.</I></P>

<TABLE BORDER="2"><TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD COLSPAN="2">Enhanced X-Windows Grab Routines Restricted from GL Fullscreen Mode</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>XChangeActive PointerGrab</B></TD>

<TD><B>XUngrabServer</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>XGrabButton</B></TD>

<TD><B>XtGrabButton</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>XGrabKey</B></TD>

<TD><B>XtGrabKey</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>XGrabKeyboard</B></TD>

<TD><B>XtGrabKeyboard</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>XGrabPointer</B></TD>

<TD><B>XtGrabPointer</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>XGrabServer</B></TD>

<TD><B>XtRemoveGrab</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>XUngrabButton</B></TD>

<TD><B>XtUngrabButton</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>XUngrabKey</B></TD>

<TD><B>XtUngrabKey</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>XUngrabKeyboard</B></TD>

<TD><B>XtUngrabPointer</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>XUngrabPointer</B></TD>

<TD><BR></TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="a9m200nita"></A>Coordinate Transformation</H3>
<P><A NAME="A3C0F009865mhay"></A>GL and Enhanced X-Windows have different coordinate mappings. The GL window origin is in the lower left and the Enhanced X-Windows window origin is in the upper left. Do not use the <B>XTranslateCoordinates</B> subroutine, an Enhanced X-Windows function, to manipulate GL coordinate data.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3C0F009885mhay"></A>Likewise, do not use GL matrix and viewport manipulation routines on Enhanced X-Windows windows.</P>

<H3><A NAME="QN8Sg169csol"></A>Mixed GL and Windows Input</H3>
<P><A NAME="A3C0F009906mhay"></A>Currently, programming that combines GL input queue handling routines (such as <B>qread</B> and <B>qtest</B>) with X input queue handling routines (such as <B>XNextEvent</B> and <B>XCheckIfEvent</B> ) on the same display connection is not recommended. X and GL input can be combined provided that such input is obtained through separate sockets.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3C0F009926mhay"></A>Although you can use the Enhanced X-Windows event mechanism to obtain Enhanced X-Windows events for a GL window, do not try to use the GL event mechanism to obtain events for some GL windows and the Enhanced X-Windows event mechanism to obtain events for other GL windows.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3C0F009946mhay"></A>The GL event queue is fed by events returning from the X server; the GL event handling library simply converts events from X format into GL format. The mapping is not one-to-one; sometimes multiple X events translate into only on GL event; sometimes multiple GL events are generated from one X event. If an unrecognized or unexpected event is encountered, it is discarded. Thus, changing the event mask for the GL connection, removing X events from the GL connection, or sending events to the GL connection results in the unpredictable or inconsistent operation of the GL input queue handling routines. It is for this reason that X and GL event routines should not be combined on the same display connection.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3C0F009966mhay"></A>In the current implementation, when a <!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/qtest.html#A143X9cd"><B>qtest</B></A> or <!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/qread.html#A143X989"><B>qread</B></A> subroutine call is made, all pending events for the process are retrieved from the X server and placed in an internal device queue. As a result, the GL and the Enhanced X-Windows event queues are no longer synchronized; that is, the arrival order of events is not preserved. Events retrieved by freely mixing calls to the GL <B>qread</B> subroutines and calls to the Enhanced X-Windows event processing routines are not guaranteed to be in chronological order.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3C0F00A328mhay"></A>In the current implementation, the GL <!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/qenter.html#A143X9152"><B>qenter</B></A> subroutine performs an <!--:libs:x11tr:--><A HREF="../x11tr/pdf/XSeEvent.pdf"><B>XSendEvent</B></A> subroutine call, and thus writes to the Enhanced X-Windows event queue.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3C0F00B152mhay"></A>The following is a partial list of Enhanced X-Windows functions that, if used in conjunction with the GL input queue, lead to asynchronous event delivery. Do <I>not</I> use these routines in conjunction with the GL input queue<I>.</I></P>

<TABLE BORDER="2"><TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD COLSPAN="2">Enhanced X-Windows Event Routines Restricted from GL Input Queue</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>XChangeKeyboardMapping</B></TD>

<TD><B>XSelectInput</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>XCheckIfEvent</B></TD>

<TD><B>XSetPlaneMask</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>XCheckMaskEvent</B></TD>

<TD><B>XWindowEvent</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>XCheckTypedEvent</B></TD>

<TD><B>XtAppMainLoop</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>XCheckTypedWindowEvent</B></TD>

<TD><B>XtAppNextEvent</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>XCheckWindowEvent</B></TD>

<TD><B>XtAppPeekEvent</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>XEventsQueued</B></TD>

<TD><B>XtAppPending</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>XIfEvent</B></TD>

<TD><B>XtAppProcessEvent</B></TD></TR>
```

## File: gl32prgd/eventsxmp.html
```html
<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">
<HTML>

<!--gl32prgd/eventsxmp.html Mon, 24 Jan 2022 16:27:48 GMT -->
<HEAD>
<META HTTP-EQUIV="Content-Type" CONTENT="text/html; charset=iso-8859-1">

   <TITLE>Events Example Program
</TITLE>
   
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="animatexmp.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="drawwithgl.html">Next</a>  |
<A HREF="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html" TARGET="_parent">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 Version 4.1 for AIX: Programming Concepts</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>



<H2><A NAME="eventsxmp.html"></A>Events Example Program </H2>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE53472mhay"></A>The first two programs demonstrated how
to draw and create animated scenes, respectively. The next program demonstrates
how to obtain input and illustrates the concept of an <I>event loop</I>.</P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE53491mhay"></A>The event loop is critical to writing
applications for a windowing system. An event loop allows a program to
respond to events occurring in the system that are beyond the control of
the application program: for example, when a user picks up a window and
moves it, has a window obscured and then unobscured by other windows, or
resizes a window. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE53511mhay"></A>At this point, return to the <A HREF="helloexmp.html#helloexmp.html">first
program</A>, change the sleep time to 50 seconds, then recompile and rerun
the program. While it is running, pick up another window (for instance,
the xclock), drop it on the <TT>HI&nbsp;THERE</TT> window, pick it up again,
and remove it. Notice that the original <TT>Hello,&nbsp;World!</TT> display
was destroyed. This occurred because the other window overwrote the pixel
data in the <TT>HI&nbsp;THERE</TT> window, and the overwritten data was
not saved (GL does not support backing store or save-under). </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE53531mhay"></A>When the contents of a window are destroyed
in this fashion, the application itself must redraw the window. GL provides
an event that indicates that a window may have to be redrawn. The application
must test for this event, and redraw the window whenever the event is received.
The discussion after the following program explains how the testing and
redrawing is done. </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A109C1517"></A>#include&nbsp;&lt;gl/gl.h&gt;
#include&nbsp;&lt;gl/device.h&gt;</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A109C1518"></A>/*&nbsp;This&nbsp;subroutine&nbsp;draws&nbsp;stuff&nbsp;*/
drawstuff&nbsp;(int&nbsp;xxx,&nbsp;int&nbsp;yyy)
{
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color&nbsp;(BLACK);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;clear&nbsp;();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color&nbsp;(GREEN);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;cmov2i&nbsp;(xxx,&nbsp;yyy);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;charstr&nbsp;(&quot;Hello,&nbsp;World!&quot;);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;swapbuffers&nbsp;();
}</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A109C1519"></A>main&nbsp;()
{
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;int&nbsp;ox,&nbsp;oy;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;int&nbsp;ix&nbsp;=&nbsp;150,&nbsp;iy&nbsp;=&nbsp;200;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;int&nbsp;update&nbsp;=&nbsp;TRUE;</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A109C151a"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;/*&nbsp;Create&nbsp;and&nbsp;configure&nbsp;window&nbsp;*/
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;prefsize&nbsp;(400,&nbsp;400);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;winopen&nbsp;(&quot;HI&nbsp;THERE&quot;);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;doublebuffer&nbsp;();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;gconfig&nbsp;();</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A109C151b"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;/*&nbsp;get&nbsp;window&nbsp;origin&nbsp;*/
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;getorigin&nbsp;(&amp;ox,&nbsp;&amp;oy);</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A109C151c"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;/*&nbsp;queue&nbsp;up&nbsp;input&nbsp;devices&nbsp;*/
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;qdevice&nbsp;(REDRAW);&nbsp;&nbsp;/*&nbsp;window&nbsp;needs&nbsp;to&nbsp;be&nbsp;redrawn&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;*/
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;qdevice&nbsp;(WINQUIT);&nbsp;/*&nbsp;user&nbsp;selected&nbsp;&quot;close&quot;&nbsp;from&nbsp;window&nbsp;menu&nbsp;*/
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;qdevice&nbsp;(MOUSEX);&nbsp;&nbsp;/*&nbsp;mouse&nbsp;x&nbsp;position,&nbsp;in&nbsp;pixels&nbsp;*/
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;qdevice&nbsp;(MOUSEY);&nbsp;&nbsp;/*&nbsp;mouse&nbsp;y&nbsp;position,&nbsp;in&nbsp;pixels&nbsp;*/
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;qdevice&nbsp;(ESCKEY);&nbsp;&nbsp;/*&nbsp;user&nbsp;pressed&nbsp;escape&nbsp;key&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;*/
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;qdevice&nbsp;(RIGHTMOUSE);/*&nbsp;user&nbsp;pressed&nbsp;right&nbsp;mouse&nbsp;button&nbsp;*/</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A109C151d"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;/*&nbsp;enter&nbsp;event&nbsp;loop&nbsp;*/
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;while&nbsp;(TRUE)&nbsp;{
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;long&nbsp;dev;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;short&nbsp;value;</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A109C151e"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;/*&nbsp;if&nbsp;there&nbsp;aren't&nbsp;any&nbsp;events,&nbsp;and&nbsp;data&nbsp;has&nbsp;changed,&nbsp;redraw&nbsp;*/
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;if&nbsp;(!qtest()&nbsp;&amp;&nbsp;update)&nbsp;{
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;drawstuff&nbsp;(ix,&nbsp;iy);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;update&nbsp;=&nbsp;FALSE;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;}</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A109C151f"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;/*&nbsp;get&nbsp;the&nbsp;next&nbsp;event&nbsp;*/
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;dev&nbsp;=&nbsp;qread&nbsp;(&amp;value);</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A109C1520"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;/*&nbsp;dispatch&nbsp;the&nbsp;next&nbsp;event&nbsp;*/
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;switch&nbsp;(dev)&nbsp;{
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;case&nbsp;MOUSEX:
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;ix&nbsp;=&nbsp;value&nbsp;-&nbsp;ox;&nbsp;/*&nbsp;update&nbsp;x&nbsp;location&nbsp;*/
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;update&nbsp;=&nbsp;TRUE;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;break;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;case&nbsp;MOUSEY:
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;iy&nbsp;=&nbsp;value&nbsp;-&nbsp;oy;&nbsp;&nbsp;/*&nbsp;update&nbsp;y&nbsp;location&nbsp;*/
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;update&nbsp;=&nbsp;TRUE;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;break;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;case&nbsp;REDRAW:&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;/*&nbsp;redraw&nbsp;it&nbsp;*/
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;getorigin&nbsp;(&amp;ox,&nbsp;&amp;oy);&nbsp;/*&nbsp;get&nbsp;window&nbsp;origin&nbsp;*/
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;update&nbsp;=&nbsp;TRUE;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;break;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;case&nbsp;ESCKEY:&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;/*&nbsp;if&nbsp;user&nbsp;presses&nbsp;escape&nbsp;key,&nbsp;quit&nbsp;*/
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;case&nbsp;RIGHTMOUSE:&nbsp;/*&nbsp;if&nbsp;user&nbsp;presses&nbsp;right&nbsp;mouse&nbsp;button,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;quit&nbsp;*/
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;case&nbsp;WINQUIT:&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;/*&nbsp;if&nbsp;&quot;close&quot;&nbsp;selected&nbsp;from&nbsp;window&nbsp;menu&nbsp;*/
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;exit();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;default:
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;break;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;}
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;}
}</PRE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE53562mhay"></A>When you run this program, you will find
that the character string <TT>Hello,&nbsp;World!</TT> follows the cursor
around. You can can pick up the window, move it, obscure it, and uncover
it, but it will always appear correctly. The following discussion examines
the operation of this complicated program in detail. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE53582mhay"></A>First, this program includes a new header
file: <B>gl/device.h</B>. This file contains definitions and type definitions
(typedefs) pertaining to GL devices. To make the program easier to read,
the drawing section has been put into its own subroutine, <TT>drawstuff</TT>,
which contains a set of GL subroutines. When you want the program to draw,
call this subroutine. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE53602mhay"></A>The program begins as before: the first
step opens a window. Next, the program obtains the window origin with the
<B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/getorigin.html#A142X91f76">getorigin</A></B>
subroutine, which will be needed later. Then, a number of devices are queued
up. These devices, the REDRAW device, the MOUSEX device, and so on, generate
events and place them on a queue. The program reads events from the bottom
of the queue and processes them according to what came in. The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/qdevice.html#A143X967">qdevice</A></B>
subroutine itself does not generate or process events, but only initializes
these devices and readies them for use. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE53621mhay"></A>Next, the program enters the event loop.
Although this looks like an infinite loop, if the user presses either the
escape key or the right mouse button, or else chooses the <B>Close</B>
option from the window menu, the program ends. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE53641mhay"></A>In the loop, the program tests to see
if there are any events on the event queue. If the queue is empty and the
picture needs to be redrawn, the program begins to draw at this time. If
the queue is not empty, then the program reads the next event and processes
it. The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/qread.html#A143X989">qread</A></B>
subroutine returns the device that generated the event and a value associated
with that event. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE53661mhay"></A>Depending on the device, the switch statement
branches to the correct code to handle the event. If, for instance, the
event is a mouse-motion event, the new <I>x</I> or <I>y</I> coordinate
(or both) is recorded. If the event is an Escape key press, then the program
is ended. After a nonterminating event is processed, the program returns
to the beginning of the event loop and processes the next event. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE53680mhay"></A>If the user moves the window, a REDRAW
event is generated. In this case, the window origin is obtained, so that
the character string can be drawn in the right place later. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE53700mhay"></A>To learn more about devices and events,
see <A HREF="cntrlques.html#cntrlques.html">&quot;Controlling Queues and Devices&quot;</A>.</P>




<hr><center>

<a href="drawwithgl.html">Next</a>  |

</center></BODY>

</HTML>
```

## File: gl32prgd/exhwindcalls.html
```html
<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">
<HTML>

<!--gl32prgd/exhwindcalls.html Mon, 24 Jan 2022 16:28:20 GMT -->
<HEAD>
<META HTTP-EQUIV="Content-Type" CONTENT="text/html; charset=iso-8859-1">

   <TITLE>Chapter 13. Using Enhanced X-Windows Calls with GL Subroutines
</TITLE>
   
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="textport.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="enhxwndrestr.html">Next</a>  |
<A HREF="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html" TARGET="_parent">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 Version 4.1 for AIX: Programming Concepts</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>



<H1><A NAME="exhwindcalls.html"></A>Chapter 13. Using Enhanced X-Windows
Calls with GL Subroutines </H1>


<P><A NAME="A3C0F009372mhay"></A>This section describes how GL drawing
subroutines can be used with AIXwindows window management
routines to control the mapping of windows, set window properties, and
create widgets. The subroutines and techniques described in this section
allow the user to mix Enhanced X-Windows and GL calls within the
same program. However, not all possible mixings of Enhanced X-Windows
and GL within the same program result in predictable behavior. To use GL
and Enhanced X-Windows together constructively, it is important to
have a basic understanding of the internal structure and implementation
of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0F009393mhay"></A>In general, there are two kinds of GL
subroutines: those used for drawing or controlling the hardware and those
used for window management, obtaining input, and managing pop-up menus.
Drawing subroutines (such as <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/v.html#A144X97a4">v3f</A></B>,
<B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/loadmatrix.html#A144X9430">loadmatrix</A></B>,
and <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/nurbssurface.html#A252X98b9">nurbssurface</A></B>)
and hardware control subroutines (such as <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/gconfig.html#hS4260nita">gconfig</A></B>
and <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/zfunction.html#A22f0MARJ">zfunction</A></B>)
access and control the graphics adapter directly. That is, there are no
complex code layers between these subroutines and the graphics adapter.
Specifically, this means that the X server remains ignorant of the current
state and contents of a GL window. Eliminating complex code layers improves
calculation time. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0F009413mhay"></A>In contrast, window management subroutines
(such as <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/winpop.html#A142X9156b">winpop</A></B>
and <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/icontitle.html#sH13240marj">icontitle</A></B>)
and input subroutines (such as <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/qread.html#A143X989">qread</A></B>
and <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/getbutton.html#A143X91">getbutton</A></B>)
are implemented as a layer on top of the Enhanced X-Windows Protocol.
As a result, all input and events are obtained from the X server, and the
X server knows about and carries out all requests to create, move, map,
and resize windows. In this way, a single centralized process manages all
windows visible on the screen. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0F009434mhay"></A>The differences between direct access
subroutines and those that work through the X server affect how GL and
Enhanced X-Windows can and cannot be used together. The following
section discusses restrictions on GL and Enhanced X-Windows use.
Later sections discuss and give examples of how GL and Enhanced X-Windows
calls can be used together. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0F009454mhay"></A>For more information on using Enhanced X-Windows
calls with GL subroutines, see: </P>


<UL><LI><A NAME="DF754C8579meki"></A><A HREF="enhxwndrestr.html#enhxwndrestr.html">Restrictions
on Using Enhanced X-Windows Calls with GL Subroutines</A> </LI>


<LI><A NAME="DF754C8631meki"></A><A HREF="enhxinterop.html#enhxinterop.html">Enhanced X-Windows
and GL Interoperability</A>  

<BLOCKQUOTE><P><A NAME="A110C1aa"></A><B>Note: </B>This section deals with an advanced
topic and may be difficult to understand unless the reader has a good conceptual
and practical grasp of GL and the Enhanced X-Windows System. </P></BLOCKQUOTE></LI></UL>




<hr><center>
[  <a href="textport.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="enhxwndrestr.html">Next</a>  |

 <A HREF="cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
</center></BODY>

</HTML>
```

```html
<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">
<HTML>

<!--gl32prgd/FORTRANnC.html Mon, 24 Jan 2022 16:28:20 GMT -->
<HEAD>
<META HTTP-EQUIV="Content-Type" CONTENT="text/html; charset=iso-8859-1">

   <TITLE>Linking FORTRAN and C Modules
</TITLE>
   
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="linkncompil.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="unsupsubs.html">Next</a>  |
<A HREF="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html" TARGET="_parent">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 Version 4.1 for AIX: Programming Concepts</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>





<H2><A NAME="FORTRANnC.html"></A>Linking FORTRAN and C Modules </H2>


<P><A NAME="A3C0F110714mhay"></A>In general FORTRAN compilers append an
underscore character ('_') to each user defined symbol. In this way name
space conflicts can be avoided between C and FORTRAN. However, the xlf
(f77) compiler does not add the trailing underscore to user defined symbols
by default. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0F110733mhay"></A>The FORTRAN GL library supports both naming
conventions by exporting symbols with and without appended underscores.
Because of a potential name space clash between the FORTRAN and C libraries,
some care must be taken when linking together modules that use both the
C and FORTRAN bindings for GL subroutines. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0F110752mhay"></A>Programs written in FORTRAN and using
GL fall into one of four categories. The following gives an example from
each category, showing how FORTRAN GL applications can be linked. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0F110772mhay"></A>To link FORTRAN-only source code, enter
the following: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="BC7B539020vbia"></A>xlf -U foof.f -lfgl -lm</PRE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0F110792mhay"></A>This binds the FORTRAN application with
the FORTRAN GL library and the Math Library. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0F110811mhay"></A>To link C and FORTRAN source where GL
is referenced <I>only</I> through the FORTRAN interface, enter the following:</P>


<PRE><A NAME="BC7B539511vbia"></A>xlc -c fooc.c
xlf -U foof.f fooc.o -lfgl -lc -lm</PRE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0F110832mhay"></A>This binds the MIXED application with
the FORTRAN GL library, the C library, and the Math Library. The C Library
is used to resolve externals from the module compiled by the <B>xlc</B>
command. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0F110851mhay"></A>To link C and FORTRAN source where GL
is referenced only through the C interface, enter the following </P>


<PRE><A NAME="BC7B53A013vbia"></A>xlf -U -c foof.f
xlc fooc.c foof.o -lgl -lxlf -lm</PRE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0F110871mhay"></A>This binds the MIXED application with
the C GL library, the XLF library, and the Math Library. The XLF Library
is used to resolve externals from the module compiled by the <B>xlf</B>
command. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0F110891mhay"></A>To link C and FORTRAN source where GL
is referenced through both the C and FORTRAN interfaces, enter the following:</P>


<PRE><A NAME="BC7B53A502vbia"></A>xlf -U -qextname -c foof.f
xlc -c fooc.c
xlc  foof.o fooc.o -lgl -lc -lfgl -lxlf -lm</PRE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0F110911mhay"></A>This creates the MIXED application. By
compiling the FORTRAN modules with the <B>-qextname</B> flag, the extended
naming rules are enforced. The extended naming rules append an underscore
to all user-defined symbols. </P>


<OL><LI><A NAME="BC7B53A998vbia"></A>The C libraries are specified first so
that all C externals are resolved for the FORTRAN GL library contains references
to functions with and without the trailing underscores. The FORTRAN libraries
will then resolve all functions with the trailing underscores.</LI>


<LI><A NAME="BC7B53B378vbia"></A>The order in which the libraries are placed
on the compile line is important. If they are not placed according to the
guidelines herein, the proper linkage will not be achieved and run-time
errors will result.</LI></OL>




<hr><center>
```

```html
<i>GL3.2 Version 4.1 for AIX: Programming Concepts</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>



<H1><A NAME="getstart.html"></A>Chapter 2. Getting Started in GL </H1>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE52574mhay"></A>GL provides a set of fully featured functions
that support graphics without depending on other graphics systems. These
functions include support for input devices, a windowing system, frame
buffer configuration and control, immediate and retained mode graphics,
and support for basic and advanced 3-D rendering. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE52594mhay"></A>GL subroutines provide basic function
and are limited in scope; subroutines do not interact in a complex fashion;
minimal use is made of stored state; and where possible, the subroutines
access hardware functionality directly. (Note that you cannot start a GL
and graPHIGS application from the same process ID.) </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE52976mhay"></A>The following series of programs introduces
you to GL functions: </P>


<UL><LI><A NAME="A109C14e9"></A><A HREF="helloexmp.html#helloexmp.html">Hello
World Example Program for GL</A> </LI>


<LI><A NAME="A109C14ea"></A><A HREF="animatexmp.html#animatexmp.html">Animation
Example Program for GL</A></LI>


<LI><A NAME="A109C14eb"></A><A HREF="eventsxmp.html#eventsxmp.html">Events Example
Program for GL</A></LI></UL>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE52000mhay"></A>To run GL programs, your system must have
an adapter installed that supports GL. The GL prerequisites are discussed
in <A HREF="glintro.html#A9o61d0nita">&quot;Hardware and Software Prerequisites&quot;</A>.
In addition, the AIXwindows server must be actively running.
If the X server is not already running, you need to start it. To do this,
enter the following at the command line prompt: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A109C14ee"></A>xinit</PRE>
```

## File: gl32prgd/glintro.html
```html
<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">
<HTML>

<!--gl32prgd/glintro.html Mon, 24 Jan 2022 16:27:48 GMT -->
<HEAD>
<META HTTP-EQUIV="Content-Type" CONTENT="text/html; charset=iso-8859-1">

   <TITLE>Introducing AIX Graphics Library
</TITLE>
   
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="gloverview.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="glsubcats.html">Next</a>  |
<A HREF="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html" TARGET="_parent">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 Version 4.1 for AIX: Programming Concepts</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>



<H2><A NAME="glintro.html"></A>Introducing AIX Graphics Library</H2>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE38579mhay"></A>The AIX GL is
a set of graphics and utility subroutines that provide high- and low-level
support for graphics. If you are using this library for the first time,
read the following sections first. </P>


<H3><A NAME="A300X9bcf"></A>GL Structure and Function </H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE38600mhay"></A>Graphics primitives are expressed in 2-D
or 3-D user-defined coordinates. These primitives go through the 
<A HREF="specialterms.html#A26P0612">graphics
pipeline</A>, which performs matrix 
<A HREF="specialterms.html#A27P021">transformations</A>
on the coordinates, clips the coordinates to normalized coordinates, and
scales the transformed, clipped coordinates to screen or window coordinates.
The output of the graphics pipeline is then sent to the raster subsystem.</P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE38620mhay"></A>The 
<A HREF="specialterms.html#A3C0F2A4190mhay">raster
subsystem</A> fills in the pixels between the endpoints of the lines and
the interiors of polygons; draws bit-mapped characters; and performs <A HREF="drawbeg-end.html#A264X911a">shading</A>,
<A HREF="depth-cueing.html">depth-cueing</A>, and <A HREF="remhidden.html#remhidden.html">hidden
surface removal</A>. A color value for each pixel is stored in the bitplanes.
The system uses the values contained in the bitplanes to display an image
on the monitor. </P>


<H3><A NAME="A8G44310marj"></A>Understanding the Hardware Used by GL</H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE38641mhay"></A>AIX GL runs
on high-resolution color workstations. GL provides a set of
graphics primitives in a combination of customized, very large scale integrated
(VLSI) circuits and conventional hardware, firmware, and software. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE38661mhay"></A>The heart of the system is the 
<A HREF="specialterms.html#A26P0612">graphics
pipeline</A>. This pipeline accepts points, vectors, polygons, characters,
and curves in user-defined coordinate systems and transforms them to screen
coordinates. It also provides hardware support for rotation, clipping,
and scaling. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE38680mhay"></A>In addition to the graphics pipeline,
the system consists of one or more general-purpose microprocessors, a raster
subsystem, a high-resolution color monitor, a keyboard, and graphics input
devices. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE38700mhay"></A>GL windowing subroutines
are implemented on top of Enhanced X-Windows. (For more information
on starting Enhanced X-Windows, see the 
<B><!--:cmds:aixcmds6:--><A HREF="aixcmds6/xinit.html#A773C66779jcat">xinit</A></B> command.) The GL drawing subroutines
are implemented by means of direct adapter access. GL applications
and other XClients can run simultaneously on the same X server. GL
works with any X-based window manager, including the AIXwindows
window manager. </P>


>

<P><A NAME="A3C0DE38720mhay"></A>On the POWER GXT1000, the multibuffer,
ancillary buffer, and overlay extensions for X must be loaded to run GL.</P>




<H3><A NAME="A9o61d0nita"></A>Hardware and Software Prerequisites for GL</H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE38750mhay"></A>There are both hardware and software prerequisites
for running the GL application programming interface (API).</P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE38763mhay"></A>Of the following hardware, GL
must have one as a prerequisite: </P>


<UL><LI><A NAME="A112C1fa"></A>A <A HREF="3dclrproc.html">3-D
Color Graphics Processor</A> adapter must be installed, with or without
the 24-bit color option, and with or without the 24-bit z-buffer option.</LI>


<LI><A NAME="A112C1fb"></A><A HREF="powerGt4.html#powerGt4.html">POWER Gt4
class machines</A>, such as the POWER Gt4, POWER Gt4x,
and POWER Gt4e adapters, must be installed.</LI>


<LI><A NAME="A112C1fd"></A>A 7235 POWERgraphics GTO must be installed.</LI>


<LI><A NAME="A112C1fe"></A>The system must be a <A HREF="powerstation730.html#powerstation730.html">POWERstation
730 with the Supergraphics Processor Subsystem</A>.</LI>



<LI><A NAME="C44705A808lpas"></A>The <A HREF="PGXT1000.html#PGXT1000.html">POWER GXT1000</A>
must be installed.</LI>


</UL>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE38784mhay"></A>GL has the following software
prerequisites: </P>


<UL><LI><A NAME="A112C1100"></A>AIX/6000 must be installed.</LI>


<LI><A NAME="A112C1101"></A>AIXwindows Environment/6000 must
be installed.</LI>


<LI><A NAME="A112C1102"></A>AIXwindows Environment/6000 3-D
Feature must be installed.</LI></UL>


<H3><A NAME="A6C852E599vbia"></A>Language Bindings </H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE38799mhay"></A>GL is available with C, FORTRAN,
and Ada language bindings. </P>


<H3><A NAME="A6C6EFF633vbia"></A>New Features, Documentation, and Programs</H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE38820mhay"></A>This release of GL includes
the following new or enhanced functions: </P>


<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A3C0DE38839mhay"></A><B>lmdef()</B> </TD>


<TD>Support for two-sided lighting is now available on the POWER Gt4 family
of graphics adapters.</TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A3C0DE38851mhay"></A><B>set_dither()</B> </TD>


<TD>Suport for enabling/disabling dither on the POWER Gt4 family of graphics
adapters is now provided.</TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A3C0DE38862mhay"></A><B>glcompat()</B> </TD>


<TD>Controls backwards compatibility modes for the overlay planes and fullscreen
function on the GXT1000.</TD></TR></TABLE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE38874mhay"></A>The GL documentation has
been updated. In particular, note that Chapter15 contains important information
about using GL with the system <B>fork()</B> and <B>exec()</B> routines
and about compiling and linking GL programs. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE38885mhay"></A>Several new example programs can be found
in<B> /usr/lpp/GL/examples</B>, including: </P>


<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A3C0DE38897mhay"></A><B>rqenter.c</B> </TD>


<TD>Example showing how to write re-entrant queueing code. The example
creates a pipe and then checks for input on both the pipe and on the GL
queue. USR1 signals caught by the process result in input being placed
on the pipe. (The shell script <B>gen_sig.sh</B> can be used to generate
signals.)</TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A3C0DE38909mhay"></A><B>xinput.c</B> </TD>


<TD>Example of X/GL integration. Shows how to simultaneously manipulate
both the GL and the X11 event queues within the same process. The example
can be extended to simultaneously read other (pipe, socket, or file-based)
event sources.</TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A3C0DE38921mhay"></A><B>Xcolormap.c</B> </TD>


<TD>Example of X/GL integration. Shows how X11 can be used to manipulate
the colormap associated with a GL window.</TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A3C0DE38932mhay"></A><B>fork_examp.c</B> </TD>


<TD>A very simple example involving GL and the system <B>fork()</B> subroutine.
Shows how the GL subsystem must be shut down before using the system <B>fork()</B>
routine.</TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A3C0DE38944mhay"></A><B>fork_examp2.c</B> </TD>


<TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;A more sophisticated <B>fork()</B> example.</TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A3C0DE38956mhay"></A><B>GLexec.c</B> </TD>


<TD>A very simple example involving GL and the system <B>exec()</B> routine.
Shows how the GL subsystem must be shut down before using any of the system
<B>exec()</B> routines.</TD></TR></TABLE>




<hr><center>
[  <a href="gloverview.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="glsubcats.html">Next</a>  |
<A HREF="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html" TARGET="_parent">| Glossary</A>

 <A HREF="cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
</center></BODY>


<!--gl32prgd/glintro.html Mon, 24 Jan 2022 16:27:48 GMT -->
</HTML>
```

```html
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="glsubcats.html"></A>Graphics Library Subroutines and Functional Categories</H2>
<P><A NAME="A3C0DE38969mhay"></A>To help you select the proper subroutines for your application, the following list comprises the functional categories for GL.</P>

<H3><A NAME="eG441f0marj"></A>Choosing the Right GL Subroutine<A NAME="INDEX2" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX3" REL="I2" TITLE="subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX4" REL="I3" TITLE="choosing"></A>
</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A264X9ad"></A>Select an entry from the left column for the list of subroutines in that category.
</TD></TR>
<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>
<TD>  </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A300X9bd7"></A>Select an entry from the right column for conceptual information on that topic.
</TD></TR>
<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>
<TD>  </TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="et4280marj"></A>Drawing Subroutines</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A264X9b9"></A><A HREF="smjaglines.html#JUI11e0marj"><B>Antialiasing</B></A>
</TD></TR>
<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>
<TD>  <A HREF="smjaglines.html#smjaglines.html">Draw smooth lines</A> or points.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A318C9b3c"></A><A HREF="setglattrib.html#Uq31180marj"><B>Attributes</B></A>
</TD></TR>
<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>
<TD>  Set or return <A HREF="setglattrib.html#setglattrib.html">attributes</A>.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A264X9bb"></A><A HREF="drawbeg-end.html#A264X925d"><B>Begin-End Style Drawing</B></A>
</TD></TR>
<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>
<TD>  Provide fast <A HREF="drawbeg-end.html">vertex-based drawing</A> primitives.</TD></TR>
```

```html
<hr size=3 noshade>


<H1><A NAME="glsubmodal.html"></A>Appendix B. GL Subroutine Modality </H1>


<P><A NAME="A3C0F1ED517mhay"></A>The following keywords from the subroutine
modality list express applicable modalities for each GL subroutine. </P>


<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TH NOWRAP="NOWRAP">Keyword</TH>


<TH>Indicates that the subroutine</TH></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="XTN180nita"></A><B>display list</B> </TD>


<TD>Can be used inside a display list (object).</TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="BUN1360nita"></A><B>current window</B> </TD>


<TD>Affects only the current window.</TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="D5N1230nita"></A><B>push</B> </TD>


<TD>Is affected by the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/pushattributes.html#Thx220marj">pushattributes</A></B>
and <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/popattributes.html#Vmx2140marj">popattributes</A></B>
subroutines.</TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="V6N190nita"></A><B>bgn</B> </TD>


<TD>Can be invoked between <B>bgn...</B>, <B>end...</B> subroutine calls.</TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="RpN11c0nita"></A><B>winopen</B> </TD>


<TD>Applies to next <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/winopen.html#A142X91549">winopen</A></B>
or <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/winconstraints.html#A142X914c1">winconstraints</A></B>
subroutine call.</TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="EBN11f0nita"></A><B>gconfig</B> </TD>


<TD>Only takes effect when the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/gconfig.html#hS4260nita">gconfig</A></B>
subroutine is called.</TD></TR></TABLE>


<TABLE><CAPTION></CAPTION>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TH NOWRAP="NOWRAP">Name</TH>


<TH>Effective Modality</TH></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A86C180f"></A><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/addtopup.html#A142X9109d">addtopup</A></B></TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>


<TD></TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A86C1810"></A><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/arc.html#tEp310nita">arc</A></B></TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>


<TD><A HREF="glsubmodal.html#XTN180nita">display list</A>, <A HREF="glsubmodal.html#BUN1360nita">current
window</A></TD></TR>
```

## File: gl32prgd/hdwrcolormap.html
```html
<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">
<HTML>

<!--gl32prgd/hdwrcolormap.html Mon, 24 Jan 2022 16:28:20 GMT -->
<HEAD>
<META HTTP-EQUIV="Content-Type" CONTENT="text/html; charset=iso-8859-1">

<TITLE>Hardware Colormap Organization
</TITLE>
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="PGXT1000.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="glsublist.html">Next</a>  |
<A HREF="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html" TARGET="_parent">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 Version 4.1 for AIX: Programming Concepts</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="hdwrcolormap.html"></A>Hardware Colormap Organization</H2>
<P><A NAME="A3C0F167184mhay"></A>Graphics hardware can be built to support several types of colormap organizations. There are two principal paradigms for colormap hardware: we refer to these as color index style and gamma ramp style. In AIXwindows X server terminology, these two styles are known as PseudoColor and DirectColor, respectively. Hardware can be built to support one or both of these styles, in a variety of combinations.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3C0F167204mhay"></A>In color-index mode (PseudoColor mode), the frame buffer stores color index values which are used to look up RGB values in a color lookup table (CLUT). The color lookup table, or colormap, may be on a per-window or a per-screen basis; that is, it may affect the contents of only a particular window, or of the entire screen.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3C0F167226mhay"></A>In RGB mode (DirectColor mode), the frame buffer stores RGB triplets. If the hardware supports gamma ramps, then each component of the triplet is passed through a separate lookup table. That is, the red value stored in the frame buffer is passed through the red lookup table; the result is a new value for the red component. Likewise, the green and blue components pass through their own separate tables. These types of color tables are often referred to as gamma-ramps, since they are often used to gamma-correct RGB color values. Note that PseudoColor mode can be emulated with DirectColor mode: if exactly the same value is written into the red, green, and blue channels of the frame buffer (and that value is the color index), and the color map is loaded into the red, green, and blue gamma ramps, then the resulting system is identical to a PseudoColor System. Note that gamma ramps may be built to operate on a per-window or a per-screen basis.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3C0F167245mhay"></A>Graphics hardware may be built with either or both types of color table organizations. In the following sections, supported graphics hardware is described, and how GL subroutines can be used to set the color tables.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A5CB0CA247vbia"></A>3-D Color Graphics Processor</H3>
<P><A NAME="A3C0F167267mhay"></A>The 24-bit High Performance 3D Color Graphics Processor contains per window color-index colormaps, and a single per-screen gamma ramp lookup table. In color index mode, the color-index table is used; in RGB mode, the color-index table is bypassed. In both modes, the gamma ramp tables are active and all RGB values, independent of their origin, pass through the gamma ramps. The <B>mapcolors</B> subroutine can be used to set the colormap; while the <B>gammaramp</B> subroutine can be used to set the gamma ramps.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3C0F167287mhay"></A>On the 3D Color Graphics Processor, the cursor colormap is physically shared with the overlay color map. Changing the overlay colormap changes the color of the cursor. Changing the cursor colormap changes the overlay colormap. The X server manages the cursor, and that cursor colormap is reloaded whenever the cursor enters or leaves a window that has defined a special cursor.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3C0F167306mhay"></A>EnterNotify and LeaveNotify events are generated by the X server whenever the cursor enters and leaves a window. Use the <B>XSelectInput</B> subroutine, with <B>EnterWindowMask</B>|<B>LeaveWindowMask</B> specified as the event mask.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A5CB0CB185vbia"></A>POWERgraphics GTO</H3>
<P><A NAME="A3C0F167328mhay"></A>The 24-bit POWERgraphics GTO does not have any color-index colormaps. It does however, contain multiple gamma-ramp style look up tables, and these operate on a per-window basis. In color index mode, the <B>mapcolors</B> subroutine can be used to set these lookup tables. When in color-index mode, the operation of the POWERgraphics GTO is indistinguishable from the operation of an adapter with actual, physical color-index style colormaps. This is due to the power of a DirectColor architecture to emulate a PseudoColor architecture, as discussed above. In color-index mode, the <B>gammaramp</B> subroutine has no effect on the POWERgraphics GTO.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3C0F167348mhay"></A>In RGB mode, the <B>gammaramp</B> subroutine can be used to set the lookup tables. The tables are set on a per-window basis; that is, setting the color table for one window does not affect the others. If the gamma ramp needs to be set for multiple windows, it must be done so for each window individually. Use the <B>winset</B> subroutine to set the current window, and then use <B>gammaramp</B> to set the color table. By default, whenever the <B>gconfig</B> subroutine is called to configure an RGB mode window, the lookup table is initialized to a linear ramp.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A5CB0CC928vbia"></A>POWER Gt4 and POWER Gt4x</H3>
<P><A NAME="A3C0F167368mhay"></A>The operation of the 24-bit POWER Gt4 and POWER Gt4x subroutines with regard to colormaps and gamma ramps is identical to that of the 24-bit POWERgraphics GTO in every respect.</P><hr><center>
```

```html
<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">
<HTML>

<!--gl32prgd/helloexmp.html Mon, 24 Jan 2022 16:27:48 GMT -->
<HEAD>
<META HTTP-EQUIV="Content-Type" CONTENT="text/html; charset=iso-8859-1">

   <TITLE>Hello World Example Program
</TITLE>
   
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="getstart.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="animatexmp.html">Next</a>  |
<A HREF="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html" TARGET="_parent">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 Version 4.1 for AIX: Programming Concepts</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>



<H2><A NAME="helloexmp.html"></A>Hello World Example Program </H2>


<P><A NAME="INDEX5"></A><A NAME="INDEX6"></A><A NAME="INDEX7"></A></P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE53033mhay"></A>The first GL program opens a window on
the screen, and prints the message <TT>Hello,&nbsp;World!</TT> inside it.
Create a <B>hello.c</B> file and enter the following text: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A109C14f1"></A>#include&nbsp;&lt;gl/gl.h&gt;</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A109C14f2"></A>main&nbsp;()</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A109C14f3"></A>{&nbsp;&nbsp;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;prefsize&nbsp;(200,&nbsp;100);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;winopen&nbsp;(&quot;HI&nbsp;THERE&quot;);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color&nbsp;(BLACK);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;clear();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color&nbsp;(GREEN);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;cmov2&nbsp;(50,&nbsp;50);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;charstr&nbsp;(&quot;Hello,&nbsp;World!&quot;);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;sleep&nbsp;(5);
}</PRE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE53056mhay"></A>To compile and link this program, enter
the following AIX command: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A109C14f5"></A>cc&nbsp;hello.c&nbsp;-o&nbsp;hello&nbsp;-lgl</PRE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE53077mhay"></A>To run the program, enter the following
at the command prompt: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A109C14f7"></A>./hello</PRE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE53099mhay"></A>Depending on the configuration of your
X server (as controlled by the <B>.Xdefaults</B> and <B>.mwmrc</B> files),
either the window is displayed immediately on the screen or a <I>rubber
band</I> is displayed. If a rubber band is displayed, you can place it
at any location; to display the window, press the left mouse button. To
learn more about customizing the X server for GL applications, see <A HREF="underwininput.html#underwininput.html">&quot;Understanding
Windows and Input Control&quot;</A>. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE53119mhay"></A>The first line of the <B>hello.c</B> program,
<TT>#include&nbsp;&lt;gl/gl.h&gt;</TT>, includes constant, type, and function
declarations needed for all GL programs. For instance, it defines the preprocessor
tokens BLACK and GREEN. This line should be included in every GL program.</P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE53139mhay"></A>The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/prefsize.html#A142X91671">prefsize</A></B>
subroutine communicates to the window manager the suggested size of the
window that is created with the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/winopen.html#A142X91549">winopen</A></B>
subroutine. The <B>prefsize</B> subroutine does not actually create the
window; it only specifies the window size preferences. In this case, the
preference is a window that is 200 pixels wide and 100 pixels high. You
can also control other window properties, such as the preferred position
or the window title. To learn more about creating and managing windows,
see <A HREF="underwininput.html#underwininput.html">&quot;Understanding Windows
and Input Control&quot;</A>. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE53159mhay"></A>The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/color.html#A146X9429">color</A></B>
subroutine sets the current color. Everything you draw is is displayed
in the current color until you change that color. The <B>color</B> subroutine
itself does not draw anything. To learn more about setting attributes,
see <A HREF="setglattrib.html#setglattrib.html">&quot;Setting Drawing Attributes&quot;</A>.
To learn more about setting colors and frame buffer modes (an advanced
topic), see <A HREF="underframebuf.html#underframebuf.html">&quot;Understanding the
Frame Buffer&quot;</A>. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE53178mhay"></A>The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/clear.html#cEH1160marj">clear</A></B>
subroutine clears the entire window to the current color. Because the program
line immediately preceding the <B>clear</B> subroutine call sets the current
color to black, the window is cleared to black. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE53198mhay"></A>The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/cmov.html#A143X9d1d">cmov2</A></B>
subroutine sets the current character position. Every character you draw
is displayed at the current character position until you change that position.
In this example, the current character position is set to 50 pixels up
and 50 pixels to the right of the lower left-hand corner of the window.</P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE53218mhay"></A>The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/charstr.html#A143X9cfb">charstr</A></B>
subroutine actually draws the text <TT>Hello,&nbsp;World!</TT>. The text
is drawn with the current color, which is now green. To learn more about
drawing text (such as choosing fonts), see <A HREF="textchars.html#textchars.html">&quot;Creating
Text Characters&quot;</A>. To learn about drawing lines and polygons, see
<A HREF="drawwithgl.html#drawwithgl.html">&quot;Drawing with the Graphics
Library&quot;</A>. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0DE53238mhay"></A>The <B><!--:cmds:aixcmds5:--><A HREF="aixcmds5/sleep.html#A2089aeb">sleep</A></B>
subroutine is an AIX system call. In this example, the <B>sleep</B>
subroutine prompts the system to do nothing for 5 seconds. After 5 seconds,
the <B>sleep</B> subroutine returns and the program exits. When a GL program
exits, any windows that it has created disappear. Without the sleep call,
the window would be created, would flash to black, with some green text,
and would then disappear immediately. You can replace the sleep call with
anything that will keep the program running: for instance, an infinite
loop. But when the program exits, the window definitely disappears. </P>




<hr><center>
[  <a href="getstart.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="animatexmp.html">Next</a>  |
<A HREF="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html" TARGET="_parent">| Glossary</A>

 <A HREF="cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
</center></BODY>
```

## File: gl32prgd/keyboardgl.html
```html
<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">
<HTML>

<!--gl32prgd/keyboardgl.html Mon, 24 Jan 2022 16:28:20 GMT -->
<HEAD>
<META HTTP-EQUIV="Content-Type" CONTENT="text/html; charset=iso-8859-1">

   <TITLE>Using the Keyboard in GL
</TITLE>
   
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="cursorgl.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="cntrlques.html">Next</a>  |
<A HREF="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html" TARGET="_parent">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 Version 4.1 for AIX: Programming Concepts</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>



<H2><A NAME="keyboardgl.html"></A>Using the Keyboard</H2>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED57927mhay"></A>The keyboard class of special devices
reports character values when keys, or a combination of keys, are pressed.
The following section discusses both international keyboard input and controlling
keyboard characteristics and behavior. </P>


<H3><A NAME="A264X92d5"></A>List of GL Keyboard Subroutines<A NAME="INDEX820"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX821"></A> <A NAME="INDEX822"></A> <A NAME="INDEX823"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX824"></A> <A NAME="INDEX825"></A> </H3>


<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A318C9bae"></A><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/clkoff.html#A213X9112de"><B>clkon,</B>
<B>clkoff</B></A> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>


<TD>Turns keyboard click on and off. </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A318C9bb0"></A><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/lampoff.html#A213X9113bc"><B>lampon,</B>
<B>lampoff</B></A> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>


<TD>Turns the keyboard display lights on and off. </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A318C9bac"></A><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/ringbell.html#A213X911463">ringbell</A></B></TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>


<TD>Rings the keyboard bell. </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A318C9bad"></A><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/setbell.html#A213X9114ae">setbell</A></B></TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>


<TD>Sets the duration of the keyboard bell sound. </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A318C9bb2"></A><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/setdblights.html#A213X911501">setdblights</A></B></TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>


<TD>Sets the lights on the dial and switch box. </TD></TR></TABLE>


<H3><A NAME="A135C1329"></A>International Keyboard Input<A NAME="INDEX826"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX827"></A> <A NAME="INDEX828"></A> <A NAME="INDEX829"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX830"></A> <A NAME="INDEX831"></A> </H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED57957mhay"></A>The KEYBD device returns code points that
correspond to the keys typed on the keyboard. The manner in which keystrokes
are matched with the returned value depends on the <I>locale</I>, a language,
territory, and code set combination used to identify a set of language
conventions. For example, in United States-English installation, the value
returned is the ASCII value that corresponds to the key pressed, taking
into account the Shift and Ctrl keys. In other language keyboard installations,
encodings from the ISO8859 family of code sets are returned. For further
information on code sets, see <!--:genprogc:--><A HREF="genprogc/codeset_over.html#A163C116e3">Code
Sets Overview</A> in  in<I> AIX General Programming Concepts: Writing and Debugging Programs</I>.. </P>


<H4><A NAME="A190C1e1"></A>Input Method </H4>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED57982mhay"></A>The method used for matching up keystrokes
to returned values is called the <I>input method</I>. The locale, which
determines the key mapping, is determined from the default setting when
the system was configured, or from the $LANG environment variable, or from
the most recent invocation of the <B><!--:libs:basetrf2:--><A HREF="../basetrf2/setlocale.html#A15096ab">setlocale</A></B>
subroutine. The input method helps correct for different key placements
on different keyboards; for instance, the letter Z on the French keyboard
appears in the same location as the letter W on the US English keyboard.
For further information on input method, see <!--:genprogc:--><A HREF="genprogc/input_method.html#A8F046">Input
Method Overview</A> in  in<I> AIX General Programming Concepts: Writing and Debugging Programs</I>. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED58005mhay"></A>The input method also automatically takes
into account cases where multiple keystrokes are needed to specify one
unique letter. The value returned may be a single-byte value (in the case
of languages with single-byte code sets), or double-byte value (for languages
supporting double-byte code sets). For further information on National
Language Support, refer to the <!--:genprogc:--><A HREF="genprogc/nls.html#A2919f7">National
Language Support Overview for Programming</A> in  in<I> AIX General Programming Concepts: Writing and Debugging Programs</I>.</P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED58028mhay"></A>In the example of the United States-English
keyboard device, events are reported only on a key downstroke. The value
returned takes into account the state of the modifier key (the Ctrl, Shift,
and Shift-lock keys). Pressing the lowercase letter a on the keyboard returns
the ASCII value 0x61, while pressing Shift-A returns the ASCII value 0x41.
Similarly, pressing the Ctrl-G key sequence returns BEL (hex value 0x07),
the Ctrl-D key sequence returns ETX (hex value 0x03) and so on, proceeding
with the standard ASCII mapping. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED58050mhay"></A>It is important to understand the difference
between the device and the values it returns when you queue the keyboard.
If your program contains the following instruction: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A16C0ca4e"></A>qdevice(KEYBD);</PRE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED58074mhay"></A>then the statement: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A16C0ca50"></A>dev&nbsp;=&nbsp;qread(&amp;val);</PRE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED58096mhay"></A>returns the following: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A16C0ca52"></A>dev&nbsp;==&nbsp;KEYBD
val&nbsp;==&nbsp;the&nbsp;ISO8859&nbsp;code&nbsp;set&nbsp;encoding&nbsp;of&nbsp;the&nbsp;character&nbsp;pressed.</PRE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED58119mhay"></A>In United States-English keyboard installations,
you can test for individual keystrokes by using instructions with the following
format: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A16C0ca55"></A>qdevice(AKEY);</PRE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED58143mhay"></A>This returns the AKEY device when the
uppercase A or lowercase a key is pressed. </P>


<BLOCKQUOTE><P><A NAME="A163C11728"></A><B>Note: </B>Currently, the keyboard mapping
for KEY devices is guaranteed to be correct only in United States-English
installations. </P></BLOCKQUOTE>


<H4><A NAME="A190C1e2"></A>Keyboard Mapping </H4>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED58167mhay"></A>The actual keyboard mapping used by the
KEYBD device is contained in an <B>imkeymap</B> file. The following locations
are searched, in the order indicated, for this file: </P>


<OL><LI><A NAME="A190C1e4"></A><B>$XDIR/imkeymap</B></LI>


<LI><A NAME="A190C1e5"></A><B>$HOME/imkeymap</B></LI>


<LI><A NAME="A190C1e6"></A><B>/usr/lib/nls/loc/$LANG</B></LI></OL>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED58193mhay"></A>If none of these files are found, the
mapping defaults to the ISO8859 (Latin-1) keyboard mapping. An input method
determines the mapping. By default, the input method used is IMSimpleMap.
For most country and language combinations, two different encodings are
supplied: the ISO8859 encoding and the IBM-850 encoding. For example, $LANG
= Fr_CH is used to indicate the IBM-850 encoding for Swiss French, while
$LANG = fr_FR indicates that the ISO8859-1 encoding should be used. </P>


<BLOCKQUOTE><P><A NAME="A190C1e8"></A><B>Note: </B>Changing the locale after initialization
has no effect. Keyboard initialization occurs at the time the X server
is brought up. Therefore, the locale (or $LANG variable) should be set
before the X server is started. </P></BLOCKQUOTE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED58217mhay"></A>For applications developed for use in
countries and languages with more complex input-composing requirements,
such as in the Asian/Pacific Rim regions, it is strongly suggested that
the AIXwindows input widget be used. Use of AIXwindows
for input requires knowledge of the X display connection and the X Window
identifier of a GL window for a GL session. This information can be obtained
with the GL <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/getXdpy.html#A114C13c">getXdpy</A></B>
or <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/getXdpy.html#A114C13c">getXwid</A></B>
subroutines. For a review of limitations, see <A HREF="exhwindcalls.html#exhwindcalls.html">&quot;Using
Enhanced X-Windows Calls with GL Subroutines&quot;</A>. Example usages
can be found in the <B>/usr/lpp/GL/examples</B> directory. </P>


<H4><A NAME="A6DA669273vbia"></A>Alt PF Key Keystroke Sequences </H4>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED58242mhay"></A>In the normal course of operations, the
window manager interprets some key sequences as having special meaning.
These key sequences typically involve pressing a PF key while holding down
the Alt key, and are used to modify a window by moving, resizing, raising,
lowering it, and so on. The window manager removes these events from the
event queue, and a GL application requesting these key events does not
receive them. The actual keystrokes that are grabbed are under control
of the <B>.mwmrc</B> file, and are known as <I>accelerators</I>. Although
the default accelerators shipped with the system are Alt-PF key sequences,
the user can change or eliminate the key sequences used as menu accelerators
by editing the <B>$HOME/.mwmrc</B> file. Note, however, that changes made
to the <B>$HOME/.mwmrc</B> file affect all applications. Currently, there
is no selective means of disabling the key grabbing for some, but not all,
applications. </P>


<H3><A NAME="A163C11729"></A>Controlling the Keyboard <A NAME="INDEX832"></A><A NAME="INDEX833"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX834"></A> <A NAME="INDEX835"></A> <A NAME="INDEX836"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX837"></A> <A NAME="INDEX838"></A> </H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED58265mhay"></A>In addition to routines that poll and
queue input devices, there are subroutines that control the characteristics
and behavior of the GL peripheral input and output devices. For example,
some of these subroutines turn the keyboard click on and off (the <B>clkon</B>
and <B>clkoff</B> subroutines, respectively) or set the keyboard bell.
You set these controls to your preference or needs. </P>


<H4><A NAME="A16C0ca58"></A>clkon and clkoff Subroutines </H4>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED58289mhay"></A>The <!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/clkoff.html#A213X9112de"><B>clkon</B>
and <B>clkoff</B></A> subroutines turn the keyboard click on and off. The
syntax for the <B>clkon</B> and <B>clkoff</B> subroutines is as follows:</P>


<PRE><A NAME="A66C016c09"></A>void&nbsp;clkon()</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A66C016c0a"></A>void&nbsp;clkoff()</PRE>


<H4><A NAME="A16C0ca5c"></A>lampon and lampoff Subroutines </H4>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED58316mhay"></A>The <!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/lampoff.html#A213X9113bc"><B>lampon</B>
and <B>lampoff</B></A> subroutines control the four lamps on the keyboard.
Each 1 (as opposed to 0) in the four lower-order bits of the <I>lamps</I>
parameter to the <B>lampon</B> subroutine causes the corresponding keyboard
lamp to be on or off, depending on the subroutine called. The syntax for
the <B>lampon</B> and <B>lampoff</B> subroutines is as follows: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A66C016c0b"></A>void&nbsp;lampon(Int8&nbsp;lamps)</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A66C016c0c"></A>void&nbsp;lampoff(Int8&nbsp;lamps)</PRE>


<H4><A NAME="A16C0ca62"></A>ringbell Subroutine </H4>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED58342mhay"></A>The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/ringbell.html#A213X911463">ringbell</A></B>
subroutine rings the keyboard bell. The syntax is as follows: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A66C016c0d"></A>void&nbsp;ringbell()</PRE>


<H4><A NAME="A16C0ca65"></A>setbell Subroutine </H4>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED58367mhay"></A>The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/setbell.html#A213X9114ae">setbell</A></B>
subroutine sets the duration of the keyboard bell. A value of 0 in the
<I>durat</I> parameter is off, 1 is a short beep, and 2 is a long beep.
The syntax is as follows: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A66C016c0e"></A>void&nbsp;setbell(Char8&nbsp;durat)</PRE>


<H4><A NAME="A16C0ca69"></A>setdblights Subroutine </H4>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED58392mhay"></A>The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/setdblights.html#A213X911501">setdblights</A></B>
subroutine controls the 32 lighted switches on a dial and switch box. For
example, to turn on switches 3 and 7, the third and seventh bits of the
mask must be set to <TT>1&nbsp;(1&lt;&lt;3)|(1&lt;&lt;7)=0x88</TT>. The
syntax is as follows: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A66C016c0f"></A>void&nbsp;setdblights(Int32&nbsp;mask)</PRE>




<hr><center>
[  <a href="cursorgl.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="cntrlques.html">Next</a>  |
<A HREF="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html" TARGET="_parent">| Glossary</A>

 <A HREF="cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
</center></BODY>


<!--gl32prgd/keyboardgl.html Mon, 24 Jan 2022 16:28:20 GMT -->
</HTML>
```
