```html
<P> </P>


<H3><A NAME="A44C012b6b"></A>Opening and Closing Windows<A NAME="INDEX778"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX779"></A> <A NAME="INDEX780"></A> <A NAME="INDEX781"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX782"></A> <A NAME="INDEX783"></A> </H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED56672mhay"></A>The GL subroutines for opening and closing
windows are the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/winopen.html#A142X91549">winopen</A></B>,
<B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/swinopen.html#A2T741b0nita">swinopen</A></B>,
and <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/winclose.html#A142X91418">winclose</A></B>
subroutines. (The <B>swinopen</B> subroutine creates subwindows from a
parent window.) Exiting a program causes any existing windows to close
automatically. </P>


<H3><A NAME="A44C012b6d"></A>Setting Window Attributes and Constraints<A NAME="INDEX784"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX785"></A> <A NAME="INDEX786"></A> <A NAME="INDEX787"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX788"></A> <A NAME="INDEX789"></A> </H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED56696mhay"></A>You can control the size, location, and
shape of windows from a GL client program. Calling the <B>winopen</B> subroutine
without specifying any of these characteristics allows you to open a window
of any size or shape anywhere on the screen. You can, however, open a specific
window, such as a small square with a border, if you specify the desired
size and shape. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED56719mhay"></A>Use the window constraint subroutines
in the following table to specify window characteristics. Call these subroutines
before opening a window with the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/winopen.html#A142X91549">winopen</A></B>
subroutine. GL applies these constraints when it opens the window. </P>


<TABLE BORDER="2"><TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD COLSPAN="2"><B>Window Constraint Subroutines</B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>To Specify</B> </TD>


<TD><B>Use</B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>Minimum size </TD>


<TD><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/minsize.html#MJ13260marj"><B>minsize</B></A> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>Maximum size </TD>


<TD><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/maxsize.html#A142X916d6">maxsize</A></B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>Aspect ratio </TD>


<TD><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/keepaspect.html#A142X91896">keepaspect</A></B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>Size, in pixels </TD>


<TD><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/prefsize.html#A142X91671">prefsize</A></B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>Size and location </TD>


<TD><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/prefposition.html#A142X9164f">prefposition</A></B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>Sizing increment </TD>


<TD><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/stepunit.html#A142X91bd2">stepunit</A></B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>Small increase in size </TD>


<TD><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/fudge.html#A142X917a6">fudge</A></B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>Size of window's icon </TD>


<TD><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/iconsize.html#LA13e0marj">iconsize</A></B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>Give a window's icon a title </TD>


<TD><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/icontitle.html#sH13240marj">icontitle</A></B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>Make a title bar for the current window </TD>


<TD><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/wintitle.html#A142X915f3">wintitle</A></B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>No window borders </TD>


<TD><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/noborder.html#A142X91d7a">noborder</A></B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>No screen space needed </TD>


<TD><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/noport.html#ZN13170marj">noport</A></B> </TD></TR></TABLE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED56747mhay"></A>To respecify constraints for a window
that is already open, first call the desired series of window constraint
subroutines from the previous table, then call the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/winconstraints.html#A142X914c1">winconstraints</A></B>
subroutine. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED56770mhay"></A>When a user interactively changes a window,
the window constraints are automatically enforced. Interactively changing
a window means using the mouse and keyboard, in cooperation with the currently
running window manager, to move, resize, or reshape a window. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED56793mhay"></A>The window constraints allow the applications
programmer to control and limit how the user resizes and reshapes a window.
The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/maxsize.html#A142X916d6">maxsize</A></B>
subroutine prevents a user from resizing a window to any size larger than
the size set by the subroutine parameters. Likewise, the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/minsize.html#MJ13260marj">minsize</A></B>
subroutine prevents the user from shrinking a window below the specified
size. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED56815mhay"></A>The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/keepaspect.html#A142X91896">keepaspect</A></B>
subroutine prevents a user from resizing a window so that the aspect ratio
is changed. The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/stepunit.html#A142X91bd2">stepunit</A></B>
subroutine allows the window to be resized only in specified discrete steps.
Normally, a window can be resized by arbitrary amounts; in other words,
the <B>stepunit</B> subroutine usually specifies one pixel. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED56839mhay"></A>The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/prefsize.html#A142X91671">prefsize</A></B>
and <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/prefposition.html#A142X9164f">prefposition</A></B>
subroutines constrain the size and position of the window. The <B>prefsize</B>
subroutine prevents a user from resizing the window. The <B>prefposition</B>
subroutine prevents a user from moving the window. To place a window on
the screen in some position, allowing the user afterwards to reposition
or resize the window, call the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/winconstraints.html#A142X914c1">winconstraints</A></B>
subroutine after the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/winopen.html#A142X91549">winopen</A></B>
subroutine (or call the <B>winconstraints</B> subroutine twice in a row.)
The <B>winconstraints</B> subroutine clears previous constraints and sets
any new ones. </P>


<H3><A NAME="BC9D0F8612vbia"></A>Controlling Window Placement </H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED56862mhay"></A>Ultimately, window placement is controlled
by the window manager. The default window manager for your system is the
AIXwindows window manager. To control the behavior of this
window manager regarding interpretation and placement, edit the <B>.Xdefaults</B>
file in the user's home directory. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED56885mhay"></A>In controlling interpretation of the <B>prefposition</B>
subroutine parameters, if you add the following line to the <B>.Xdefaults</B>
file: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A258C01c222"></A>Mwm*positionIsFrame:&nbsp;True</PRE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED56909mhay"></A>the location of the window is assumed
to include the boundary of the window. That is, the screen coordinates
are assumed to refer to the lower left-hand corner of the window border.
In contrast, if you add the following line to the <B>.Xdefaults</B> file:</P>


<PRE><A NAME="A258C01c224"></A>Mwm*positionIsFrame:&nbsp;False</PRE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED56932mhay"></A>the window manager interprets the position
as the location of the window's interior, ignoring the window border. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED56955mhay"></A>The AIXwindows window manager
normally places a window so that it is fully visible on the screen. To
open a window partly or wholly off the screen, add the following line to
the <B>.Xdefaults</B> file: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A258C01c227"></A>Mwm*positionOnScreen:&nbsp;False</PRE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED56978mhay"></A>Changing the line to read: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A258C01c229"></A>Mwm*positionOnScreen:&nbsp;True</PRE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED57002mhay"></A>makes the window manager ignore the values
specified with the <B>prefposition</B> subroutine and place the window
so that it is fully visible on the screen. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED57025mhay"></A>In controlling placement of a window,
if you add the following line to the <B>.Xdefaults</B> file: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A258C01c22c"></A>Mwm*interactivePlacement:&nbsp;True</PRE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED57048mhay"></A>a rubber-banded window appears when the
<B>winopen </B>subroutine is executed. The user can place the window where
desired on the screen. If you change the line to read: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A258C01c22e"></A>Mwm*interactivePlacement:&nbsp;False</PRE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED57072mhay"></A>the window is immediately placed on the
screen in the specified position when the <B>winopen </B>subroutine is
executed. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED57095mhay"></A>The AIXwindows window manager normally
adds an offset to the location of every new window that is opened. This
offset is used to keep new windows from piling up at one place. The offset
spreads windows evenly over the entire screen. To turn off this behavior,
specify </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A175C1d88"></A>Mwm*clientAutoPlace:&nbsp;False</PRE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED57119mhay"></A>When <TT>clientAutoPlace</TT> is turned
off, GL windows are mapped on the screen exactly at the location specified
with the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/prefposition.html#A142X9164f">prefposition</A></B>
subroutine. </P>


<H3><A NAME="A44C012b72"></A>Changing Windows Noninteractively<A NAME="INDEX790"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX791"></A> <A NAME="INDEX792"></A> <A NAME="INDEX793"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX794"></A> <A NAME="INDEX795"></A> </H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED57143mhay"></A>The applications programmer can have the
same control over windows that an applications user can. A window may be
moved, resized, raised, and lowered from the applications program with
the subroutines in the following table: </P>


<TABLE BORDER="2"><TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD COLSPAN="2"><B>Window Control Subroutines</B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>To</B> </TD>


<TD><B>Use</B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>Move and reshape the current window </TD>


<TD><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/winposition.html#A142X9158d">winposition</A></B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>Move the current window </TD>


<TD><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/winmove.html#A142X91527">winmove</A></B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>Lower the current window to bottom </TD>


<TD><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/winpush.html#A4X13320marj">winpush</A></B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>Raise the current window to top </TD>


<TD><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/winpop.html#A142X9156b">winpop</A></B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>Return the size of a window </TD>


<TD><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/getsize.html#X513200marj">getsize</A></B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>Return the origin of the window </TD>


<TD><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/getorigin.html#A142X91f76">getorigin</A></B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>Return depth of window in the window stack </TD>


<TD><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/windepth.html#A142X914e3">windepth</A></B> </TD></TR></TABLE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED57168mhay"></A>GL performs these operations on the current
window, which is set with the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/winset.html#NY1320marj">winset</A></B>
subroutine. </P>


<H3><A NAME="A8tk2130nita"></A>Managing Multiple Windows<A NAME="INDEX796"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX797"></A> <A NAME="INDEX798"></A> <A NAME="INDEX799"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX800"></A> <A NAME="INDEX801"></A> </H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED57192mhay"></A>Multiple GL windows opened by the same
process do not normally share attributes. Every window has its own current
color; its own transformation matrix stack; and its own viewport stack,
name stack, and attribute stack (which contains attributes such as the
current linestyle and linewidth). The action of subroutines such as <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/swapbuffers.html#A145X9302">swapbuffers</A></B>,
<B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/RGBmode.html#A143X93b6">RGBmode</A></B>,
<B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/depthcue.html#PNK22d0marj">depthcue</A></B>,
and <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/lmbind.html#XeZ2340marj">lmbind</A></B>
is limited to the current window. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED57215mhay"></A>The only exceptions to this rule are a
few window management subroutines (such as the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/winset.html#NY1320marj">winset</A></B>
subroutine) and the <B>def</B> subroutines: <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/deflinestyle.html#A143X9b1f">deflinestyle</A></B>,
<B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/defpattern.html#A143X9b41">defpattern</A></B>,
<B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/defrasterfont.html#A143X9d3f">defrasterfont</A></B>,
<B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/loadXfont.html#vUO390nita">loadXfont</A></B>,
<B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/lmdef.html#rgZ2250marj">lmdef</A></B>,
and <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/makeobj.html#A142X912d">makeobj</A></B>.
If a linestyle, pattern, light, font, or object is defined for one window,
it becomes available to all windows opened by the same process. These definitions
are referenced by the same index in all such windows. Information is <I>never</I>
shared between different processes. The previous comments apply only to
windows opened by one and the same process. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED57238mhay"></A>The exception made for the <B>def</B>
subroutines is provided as a convenience to the user. If a linestyle has
been defined in one window, and the user wants to use it in another, the
definition should not have to be respecified in other, possibly numerous,
windows. In addition, the <B>def</B> subroutine exception allows the system
to operate in a more efficient manner. The system does not need to keep
track of multiple copies of duplicate information. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED57261mhay"></A>Other than these shared definitions, all
other attributes that are part of GL have been made deliberately nonsharable
across windows. True multiple, independent drawing sessions can therefore
be performed in multiple windows. Separate windows do not interfere with
one another, and the applications writer does not have to engage in complicated
window attribute management. The system maintains the attribute management
automatically. </P>


<H3><A NAME="A44C012b75"></A>Other Window Subroutines </H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0ED57284mhay"></A>GL provides other subroutines to control
the windows, as shown in the following table: </P>


<TABLE BORDER="2"><TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>Miscellaneous Window Subroutines</B> </TD>


<TD><BR></TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>To</B> </TD>


<TD><B>Use</B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>Put the program in screen space </TD>


<TD><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/screenspace.html#A213X911cf1">screenspace</A></B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>Put viewport at current window position </TD>


<TD><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/reshapeviewport.html#A7LQ3b0marj">reshapeviewport</A></B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>Enable the entire screen for writing </TD>


<TD><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/fullscrn.html#Qga140marj">fullscrn</A></B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>End full-screen mode </TD>


<TD><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/endfullscrn.html#laa350marj">endfullscrn</A></B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>Return identifier of current window </TD>


<TD><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/winget.html#A142X91505">winget</A></B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>Set the current window </TD>


<TD><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/winset.html#NY1320marj">winset</A></B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>Specify length of screen blank timeout </TD>


<TD><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/blanktime.html#A144X9178">blanktime</A></B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>Control screen refresh, on/off </TD>


<TD><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/blankscreen.html#A144X9128">blankscreen</A></B> </TD></TR></TABLE>
```

```html
<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">
<HTML>

<!--gl32prgd/mapcoords2wrld.html Mon, 24 Jan 2022 16:28:18 GMT -->
<HEAD>
<META HTTP-EQUIV="Content-Type" CONTENT="text/html; charset=iso-8859-1">

   <TITLE>Mapping Screen Coordinates to World Coordinates in GL
</TITLE>
   
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="useobject.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="objectedit.html">Next</a>  |
<A HREF="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html" TARGET="_parent">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 Version 4.1 for AIX: Programming Concepts</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>



<H2><A NAME="mapcoords2wrld.html"></A>Mapping Screen Coordinates to World Coordinates</H2>


<P><A NAME="INDEX717"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX718"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX719"></A><A NAME="INDEX720"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX721"></A><A NAME="INDEX722"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX723"></A></P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC25768mhay"></A>The following subroutines map screen coordinates
to world coordinates. If you want to know what the world coordinate values
are for the screen coordinates of an object, these subroutines provide
a 2-D and a 3-D method to perform the mapping. </P>


<H3><A NAME="A13C0bd0e"></A>mapw Subroutine </H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC25789mhay"></A>The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/mapw.html#A213X9119fe">mapw</A></B>
subroutine takes a 2-D screen point and maps it onto a line in 3-D world
space. Its <I>viewobj</I> parameter contains the <A HREF="specialterms.html#A27P021">viewing</A>,
<A HREF="specialterms.html#A27P021">projection</A>, and <A HREF="specialterms-2.html">viewport
transformations</A> that map the current displayed objects to the screen.</P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC25809mhay"></A>The <B>mapw</B> subroutine reverses these
transformations and maps the 
<A HREF="specialterms.html#A27P017">screen
coordinates</A> back to 
<A HREF="specialterms.html#A27P03d">world
coordinates</A>. It returns two points in the <I>(modelx1</I>, <I>modely1</I>,
<I>modelz1)</I> and the <I>(modelx2</I>, <I>modely2</I>, <I>modelz2)</I>
parameters, which specify the endpoints of the line. The <I>screenx</I>
and <I>screeny</I> parameters specify the screen point to be mapped. The
syntax is as follows: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A58C015393"></A>void&nbsp;mapw(Int32&nbsp;viewobj,&nbsp;Screencoord&nbsp;screenx,&nbsp;Screencoord&nbsp;screeny,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Coord&nbsp;*modelx1,&nbsp;Coord&nbsp;*modely1,&nbsp;Coord&nbsp;*modelz1,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Coord&nbsp;*modelx2,&nbsp;Coord&nbsp;*modely2,&nbsp;Coord&nbsp;*modelz2)</PRE>


<H3><A NAME="A13C0bd15"></A>mapw2 Subroutine </H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC25832mhay"></A>The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/mapw2.html#A213X911a56">mapw2</A></B>
subroutine is the 2-D version of the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/mapw.html#A213X9119fe">mapw</A></B>
subroutine. In 2-D, the system maps screen coordinates to world coordinates rather than to a line. The <I>viewobj</I> parameter contains
the <A HREF="specialterms.html#A27P021">projection</A> and <A HREF="specialterms.html#A27P021">viewing</A>
transformations that map the displayed objects to world coordinates; the
<I>screenx</I> and <I>screeny</I> parameters define screen coordinates.
The <I>modelx</I> and <I>modely</I> parameters return the corresponding
world coordinates. If the transformations in the <I>viewobj</I> parameter
are not two-dimensional (orthogonal) projections, the result is undefined.
The syntax is as follows: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A58C015394"></A>void&nbsp;mapw2(Int32&nbsp;viewobj,&nbsp;Screencoord&nbsp;screenx,&nbsp;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Screencoord&nbsp;screeny,&nbsp;Coord&nbsp;*modelx,&nbsp;Coord&nbsp;*modely)</PRE>




<hr><center>
[  <a href="useobject.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="objectedit.html">Next</a>  |
```

```html
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 Version 4.1 for AIX: Programming Concepts</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="mathdetails.html"></A>Mathematical Details of the Matrix Subroutines</H2>
<P><A NAME="A3C0E9A4214mhay"></A>This section defines the formulas used by the <!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/rot.html#A144X9562"><B>rot</B></A>, <!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/rotate.html#A8g2120marj"><B>rotate</B></A>, <!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/translate.html#A144X95c8"><B>translate</B></A>, <!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/scale.html#A144X95a6"><B>scale</B></A>, <!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/lookat.html#A144X9452"><B>lookat</B></A>, <!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/polarview.html#A144X94fc"><B>polarview</B></A>, <!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/window.html#A144X95ea"><B>window</B></A>, and <!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/perspective.html#A144X94da"><B>perspective</B></A> subroutines. These formulas are placed here for information only. It is not necessary to understand their meaning to use them successfully.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3C0E9A4234mhay"></A>The <B>rot</B> and <B>rotate</B> subroutines create the following <A HREF="figures/gl32p82.jpg">matrix</A> and premultiply it into the current matrix.</P>

<P></P>

<P><A NAME="A3C0E9A4254mhay"></A>The <B>translate</B> subroutine creates the following <A HREF="figures/gl32p83.jpg">matrix</A> and premultiplies it into the current matrix.</P>

<P></P>

<P><A NAME="A3C0E9A4275mhay"></A>The <B>scale</B> subroutine creates the following <A HREF="figures/gl32p84.jpg">matrix</A> and premultiplies it into the current matrix.</P>

<P></P>

<P><A NAME="A3C0E9A4295mhay"></A>The <B>polarview</B> and <B>lookat</B> subroutines create the following <A HREF="figures/gl32p85.jpg">matrix</A> and premultiply it into the current matrix.</P>

<P></P>

<P><A NAME="A3C0E9A4316mhay"></A>The perspective transformation subroutines create the following <A HREF="figures/gl32p86.jpg">matrices</A> and load them as the projection matrix.</P>

<P></P>

<P><A NAME="A3C0E9A4336mhay"></A>The orthographic subroutines create the following <A HREF="figures/gl32p87.jpg">matrices</A> and load them as the projection matrix.</P>

<P></P><hr><center>
```

```html
<H2><A NAME="move-draw.html"></A>Drawing with Move-Draw Style Subroutines</H2>


<P><A NAME="INDEX75"></A><A NAME="INDEX76"></A><A NAME="INDEX77"></A><A NAME="INDEX78"></A><A NAME="INDEX79"></A><A NAME="INDEX80"></A><A NAME="INDEX81"></A><A NAME="INDEX82"></A></P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52C035mhay"></A>This section discusses the following aspects

<UL><LI><A NAME="A258C01c1ac"></A><A HREF="move-draw.html#IHJ4d0nita">Move-Draw
Introduction</A></LI>


<LI><A NAME="A258C01c1ad"></A><A HREF="move-draw.html#A11C0b110">Current

<LI><A NAME="A258C01c1ae"></A><A HREF="move-draw.html#A11C0b117">Points</A></LI>


<LI><A NAME="A258C01c1af"></A><A HREF="move-draw.html#A11C0b12a">Lines
and Relative Lines</A></LI>


<LI><A NAME="A258C01c1b0"></A><A HREF="move-draw.html#A11C0b153">Polygons
and Relative Polygons</A></LI></UL>


<H3><A NAME="A264X92ed"></A>List of GL Move-Draw Style Subroutines<A NAME="INDEX83"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX84"></A> <A NAME="INDEX85"></A> <A NAME="INDEX86"></A> <A NAME="INDEX87"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX88"></A> </H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52C067mhay"></A>The following GL Move-Draw Style Subroutines
are found in &amp;BkSym.TRGraphics;. </P>


<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A318C9c3c"></A><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/draw.html#EYf2e0marj">draw</A></B></TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>


<TD>Draws a line. </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A318C9c3d"></A><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/getgpos.html#CZf60marj">getgpos</A></B></TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>


<TD>Gets the current graphics position. </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A318C9c3e"></A><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/move.html#pofmarj">move</A></B></TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>


<TD>Moves the current graphics position to a specified point.</TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A318C9c3f"></A><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/pclos.html#t2g270marj">pclos</A></B></TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>


<TD>Closes a filled polygon. </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A318C9c40"></A><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/pdr.html#bqf1c0marj">pdr</A></B></TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>


<TD>Specifies the next point in a polygon. </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A318C9c41"></A><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/pmv.html#A139X91eed">pmv</A></B></TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>


<TD>Specifies the starting point for a polygon. </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A318C9c42"></A><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/pnt.html#Ptf3a0marj">pnt</A></B></TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>


<TD>Draws a point. </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A318C9c43"></A><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/rdr.html#gpf1c0marj">rdr</A></B></TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>


<TD>Draws a relative line. </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A318C9c45"></A><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/rmv.html#kzf90marj">rmv</A></B></TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>


<TD>Moves the current graphics position to a point relative to the current
point. </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A318C9c44"></A><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/rpdr.html#hrfa0marj">rpdr</A></B></TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>


<TD>Draws a relative polygon. </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A318C9c46"></A><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/rpmv.html#lXf370marj">rpmv</A></B></TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>


<TD>Moves the current graphics position to the starting point for a filled
polygon relative to the current point. </TD></TR></TABLE>


<H3><A NAME="IHJ4d0nita"></A>Move-Draw Introduction </H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52C107mhay"></A>Except for polygons, the figures drawn
by the move-draw subroutines are the same as those drawn by the begin-end
style ones. For example, points are drawn as a single pixel. However, the
subroutines draw polygons only similar to <A HREF="drawbeg-end.html#A364C9930f">point-sampled
polygons</A>; they draw lines connecting the vertices, effectively point-sampled
polygons with an outline. For many polygons, the drawing time is approximately
doubled when both the polygon and its outline are drawn. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52C132mhay"></A>The display list subroutines described
in the section entitled <A HREF="workobjects.html#workobjects.html">&quot;Working
with Objects (Display Lists)&quot;</A> (<B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/makeobj.html#A142X912d">makeobj</A></B>,
<B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/closeobj.html#A142X915b">closeobj</A></B>,
<B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/callobj.html#A142X91c8">callobj</A></B>,
and so on) are not supported in the begin-end style subroutines. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52C157mhay"></A>The move-draw style subroutines used most
often are the three-dimensional ones. Therefore, the naming convention
assigns the shortest name (for example, the<B> pnt</B> subroutine) to the
most common, 3-D form. The less-used, 2-D form is assigned the longer name,
as in the <B>pnt2</B> subroutine. The 2-D versions are assumed to lie in
the <I>z</I>=0 plane, but the 2-D primitives can be transformed out of
that plane by the various 
<A HREF="specialterms.html#A27P021">transformation</A>
subroutines. </P>


<H3><A NAME="A11C0b110"></A>Current Graphics Position<A NAME="INDEX89"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX90"></A> <A NAME="INDEX91"></A> <A NAME="INDEX92"></A> <A NAME="INDEX93"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX94"></A> <A NAME="INDEX95"></A> <A NAME="INDEX96"></A> <A NAME="INDEX97"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX98"></A> <A NAME="INDEX99"></A> </H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52C183mhay"></A>In GL, the graphical figures are sent
together: a set of points, a polyline, and a polygon are sent bracketed
by a call to the <B>bgn&lt;</B><I>type</I>&gt; and <B>end&lt;</B><I>type</I>&gt;
subroutines. The rendering of the figure does not start until the <B>end&lt;</B><I>type</I>&gt;
subroutine is received. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52C208mhay"></A>The system automatically maintains the
current graphics position, so very few applications need to access it directly,
although the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/getgpos.html#CZf60marj">getgpos</A></B>
subroutine does return the current graphics position. Its parameters include
four pointers to floating point numbers in which the homogeneous coordinates
of the current transformed point are returned. The form is <TT>getgpos(&amp;fx,&nbsp;&amp;fy,&nbsp;&amp;fz,&nbsp;&amp;fw)</TT>.</P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52C233mhay"></A>For compatibility, the current graphics
position is maintained in exactly the same way for all the move-draw style
subroutines. All other graphics subroutines do not depend on the current
graphics position, and in fact, leave it in an unpredictable state. </P>


<H3><A NAME="A11C0b117"></A>Points<A NAME="INDEX100"></A> <A NAME="INDEX101"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX102"></A> <A NAME="INDEX103"></A> <A NAME="INDEX104"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX105"></A> <A NAME="INDEX106"></A> <A NAME="INDEX107"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX108"></A> <A NAME="INDEX109"></A> <A NAME="INDEX110"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX111"></A> </H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52C258mhay"></A>The six versions of the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/pnt.html#Ptf3a0marj">pnt</A></B>
subroutine are shown in the following table. </P>


<TABLE BORDER="2"><TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD COLSPAN="3"><B>Versions of the Point Subroutine</B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>Parameter type</B> </TD>


<TD><B>2-D</B> </TD>


<TD><B>3-D</B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>short integer </TD>


<TD><B>pnt2s</B> </TD>


<TD><B>pnts</B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>long integer </TD>


<TD><B>pnt2i</B> </TD>


<TD><B>pnti</B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>floating point </TD>


<TD><B>pnt2</B> </TD>


<TD><B>pnt</B> </TD></TR></TABLE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52C286mhay"></A>The parameter lists are: pnt2<I>(x,&nbsp;y)</I>
and pnt<I>(x,&nbsp;y,&nbsp;z)</I>. In addition to drawing a point, the
<B>pnt</B> subroutine updates the current graphics position to its location.
The syntax is as follows: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A258C01c1b4"></A>void&nbsp;pnt(Coord&nbsp;x,&nbsp;Coord&nbsp;y,&nbsp;Coord&nbsp;z)&nbsp;</PRE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52C311mhay"></A>The following example program draws 100
points in a square area of the window: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A11C0b11c"></A>#include&nbsp;&lt;gl/gl.h&gt;</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A25C0f6d8"></A>main()
{</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A11C0b11f"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;int&nbsp;i,&nbsp;j;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;prefposition(100,&nbsp;500,&nbsp;100,&nbsp;500);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;winopen(&quot;pointsquare&quot;);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(BLACK);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;clear();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(BLUE);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;for&nbsp;(i&nbsp;=&nbsp;0;&nbsp;i&nbsp;&lt;&nbsp;10;&nbsp;i++)
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;for&nbsp;(j&nbsp;=&nbsp;0;&nbsp;j&nbsp;&lt;&nbsp;10;&nbsp;j++)
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;pnti(i*5,&nbsp;j*5,&nbsp;0);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;sleep(3);
}</PRE>


<H3><A NAME="A11C0b12a"></A>Lines and Relative Lines<A NAME="INDEX112"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX113"></A> <A NAME="INDEX114"></A> <A NAME="INDEX115"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX116"></A> <A NAME="INDEX117"></A> <A NAME="INDEX118"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX119"></A> <A NAME="INDEX120"></A> <A NAME="INDEX121"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX122"></A> <A NAME="INDEX123"></A> <A NAME="INDEX124"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX125"></A> <A NAME="INDEX126"></A> </H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52C340mhay"></A>Lines can be drawn using either the <B>move</B>
or <B>draw</B> subroutine. Similar subroutines draw relative lines. </P>


<H4><A NAME="A11C0b12d"></A>move and draw Subroutines </H4>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52C369mhay"></A>Lines can be drawn using either of two
subroutines, <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/move.html#pofmarj">move</A></B>
and <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/draw.html#EYf2e0marj">draw</A></B>.
The syntax for the <B>move</B> and <B>draw</B> subroutines is as follows:</P>


<PRE><A NAME="A258C01c1b6"></A>void&nbsp;move(Coord&nbsp;x,&nbsp;Coord&nbsp;y,&nbsp;Coord&nbsp;z)&nbsp;</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A258C01c1b7"></A>void&nbsp;draw(Coord&nbsp;x,&nbsp;Coord&nbsp;y,&nbsp;Coord&nbsp;z)&nbsp;</PRE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52C396mhay"></A>The <B>move</B> subroutine sets the current
graphics position to the specified point. The <B>draw</B> subroutine draws
from the current graphics position to the specified point and then updates
the current graphics position to that point. The parameters and types of
the <B>move</B> and <B>draw</B> subroutines are the same as for the point
subroutines. The following table is a complete list of the <B>move</B>
and <B>draw</B> subroutines. </P>


<TABLE BORDER="2"><TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD COLSPAN="3"><B>The move and draw Subroutines</B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>Parameter type</B> </TD>


<TD><B>2-D</B> </TD>


<TD><B>3-D</B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>short integer </TD>


<TD><B>move2s</B> </TD>


<TD><B>moves</B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>long integer </TD>


<TD><B>move2i</B> </TD>


<TD><B>movei</B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>floating point </TD>


<TD><B>move2</B> </TD>


<TD><B>move</B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>short integer </TD>


<TD><B>draw2s</B> </TD>


<TD><B>draws</B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>long integer </TD>


<TD><B>draw2i</B> </TD>


<TD><B>drawi</B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>floating point </TD>


<TD><B>draw2</B> </TD>


<TD><B>draw</B> </TD></TR></TABLE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52C423mhay"></A>The following example program draws the
outline of a blue box on the screen using the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/move.html#pofmarj">move</A></B>
and <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/draw.html#EYf2e0marj">draw</A></B>
subroutines: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A11C0b12f"></A>#include&nbsp;&lt;gl/gl.h&gt;</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A11C0b130"></A>main()
{</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A11C0b132"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;prefposition(100,&nbsp;500,&nbsp;100,&nbsp;500);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;winopen(&quot;bluebox&quot;);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(BLACK);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;clear();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(BLUE);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;move2i(200,&nbsp;200);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;draw2i(200,&nbsp;300);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;draw2i(300,&nbsp;300);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;draw2i(300,&nbsp;200);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;draw2i(200,&nbsp;200);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;sleep(3);
}</PRE>


<H4><A NAME="A11C0b141"></A>Relative Line Subroutines </H4>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52C455mhay"></A>The relative line-drawing subroutines
are similar to the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/move.html#pofmarj">move</A></B>
and <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/draw.html#EYf2e0marj">draw</A></B>
subroutines, except that their parameters are interpreted as motions relative
to the current graphics position. The relative move and draw subroutines
are the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/rmv.html#kzf90marj">rmv</A></B>
and <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/rdr.html#gpf1c0marj">rdr</A></B>
subroutines, respectively. After each call to a relative move or draw subroutine,
the current graphics position is updated to the specified position. The
syntax for the <B>rmv</B> and <B>rdr</B> subroutines is as follows: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A258C01c1b9"></A>void&nbsp;rmv(Coord&nbsp;x,&nbsp;Coord&nbsp;y,&nbsp;Coord&nbsp;z)&nbsp;</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A258C01c1ba"></A>void&nbsp;rdr(Coord&nbsp;x,&nbsp;Coord&nbsp;y,&nbsp;Coord&nbsp;z)&nbsp;</PRE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52C481mhay"></A>If the current graphics position is (<I>x</I>,
<I>y</I>, <I>z</I>), then <B>rdr</B>(<I>a</I>,&nbsp;<I>b</I>,&nbsp;<I>c</I>)
draws a line from (<I>x</I>, <I>y</I>, <I>z</I>) to (<I>x</I>+<I>a</I>,
<I>y</I>+<I>b</I>, <I>z</I>+<I>c</I>), and leaves the current graphics
position at (<I>x</I>+<I>a</I>, <I>y</I>+<I>b</I>, <I>z</I>+<I>c</I>).</P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52C506mhay"></A>The following table is a complete list
of the relative line subroutines. </P>


<TABLE BORDER="2"><TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD COLSPAN="3"><B>Relative Line Subroutines</B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>Parameter type</B> </TD>


<TD><B>2-D</B> </TD>


<TD><B>3-D</B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>short integer </TD>


<TD><B>rmv2s</B> </TD>


<TD><B>rmvs</B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>long integer </TD>


<TD><B>rmv2i</B> </TD>


<TD><B>rmvi</B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>floating point </TD>


<TD><B>rmv2</B> </TD>


<TD><B>rmv</B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>short integer </TD>


<TD><B>rdr2s</B> </TD>


<TD><B>rdrs</B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>long integer </TD>


<TD><B>rdr2i</B> </TD>


<TD><B>rdri</B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>floating point </TD>


<TD><B>rdr2</B> </TD>


<TD><B>rdr</B> </TD></TR></TABLE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52C534mhay"></A>The following program draws a blue box
identical to the blue box drawn by the previous example program. But this
time, the program uses relative drawing subroutines. </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A11C0b143"></A>#include&nbsp;&lt;gl/gl.h&gt;</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A11C0b144"></A>main()
{</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A11C0b146"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;prefposition(100,&nbsp;500,&nbsp;100,&nbsp;500);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;winopen(&quot;bluebox2&quot;);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(BLACK);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;clear();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(BLUE);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;move2i(200,&nbsp;200);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;rdr2i(0,&nbsp;100);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;rdr2i(100,&nbsp;0);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;rdr2i(0,&nbsp;-100);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;rdr2i(-100,&nbsp;0);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;sleep(3);
}</PRE>


<BLOCKQUOTE><P><A NAME="A11C0b152"></A><B>Note: </B>The first subroutine is still <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/move.html#pofmarj">move2i</A></B>;
this initializes the current graphics position. If another box were to
be drawn starting 200 units to the right of the first, it might begin with
<B>rmv2i</B>(200, 0). </P></BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A11C0b153"></A>Polygons and Relative Polygons<A NAME="INDEX127"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX128"></A> <A NAME="INDEX129"></A> <A NAME="INDEX130"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX131"></A> <A NAME="INDEX132"></A> <A NAME="INDEX133"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX134"></A> <A NAME="INDEX135"></A> <A NAME="INDEX136"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX137"></A> <A NAME="INDEX138"></A> <A NAME="INDEX139"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX140"></A> <A NAME="INDEX141"></A> </H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52C565mhay"></A>GL provides subroutines to draw filled
polygons and relative versions of filled polygons. </P>


<H4><A NAME="A11C0b155"></A>Filled Polygon Subroutines </H4>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52C593mhay"></A>The move-draw style subroutines that draw
filled polygons are the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/pmv.html#A139X91eed">pmv</A></B>
and <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/pdr.html#bqf1c0marj">pdr</A></B>
subroutines. The following table is a complete list of the filled polygon
subroutines. </P>


<TABLE BORDER="2"><TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD COLSPAN="3"><B>Filled Polygon Subroutines</B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>Parameter type</B> </TD>


<TD><B>2-D</B> </TD>


<TD><B>3-D</B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>short integer </TD>


<TD><B>pmv2s</B> </TD>


<TD><B>pmvs</B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>long integer </TD>


<TD><B>pmv2i</B> </TD>


<TD><B>pmvi</B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>floating point </TD>


<TD><B>pmv2</B> </TD>


<TD><B>pmv</B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>short integer </TD>


<TD><B>pdr2s</B> </TD>


<TD><B>pdrs</B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>long integer </TD>


<TD><B>pdr2i</B> </TD>


<TD><B>pdri</B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>floating point </TD>


<TD><B>pdr2</B> </TD>


<TD><B>pdr</B> </TD></TR></TABLE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52C621mhay"></A>The syntax for the <B>pmv</B> and <B>pdr</B>
subroutines is as follows: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A258C01c1be"></A>void&nbsp;pmv(Coord&nbsp;x,&nbsp;Coord&nbsp;y,&nbsp;Coord&nbsp;z)&nbsp;</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A258C01c1bf"></A>void&nbsp;pdr(Coord&nbsp;x,&nbsp;Coord&nbsp;y,&nbsp;Coord&nbsp;z)&nbsp;</PRE>


<H4><A NAME="A11C0b15d"></A>Relative Filled Polygon Subroutines </H4>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52C650mhay"></A>The relative versions of the filled polygon
routines are shown in the following table: </P>


<TABLE BORDER="2"><TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD COLSPAN="3"><B>Relative Filled Polygon Routines</B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>Parameter type</B> </TD>


<TD><B>2-D</B> </TD>


<TD><B>3-D</B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>short integer </TD>


<TD><B>rpmv2s</B> </TD>


<TD><B>rpmvs</B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>long integer </TD>


<TD><B>rpmv2i</B> </TD>


<TD><B>rpmvi</B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>floating point </TD>


<TD><B>rpmv2</B> </TD>


<TD><B>rpmv</B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>short integer </TD>


<TD><B>rpdr2s</B> </TD>


<TD><B>rpdrs</B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>long integer </TD>


<TD><B>rpdr2i</B> </TD>


<TD><B>rpdri</B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>floating point </TD>


<TD><B>rpdr2</B> </TD>


<TD><B>rpdr</B> </TD></TR></TABLE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52C677mhay"></A>The syntax for the <B>rpmv</B> and <B>rpdr</B>
subroutines is as follows: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A258C01c1c1"></A>void&nbsp;rpmv(Coord&nbsp;x,&nbsp;Coord&nbsp;y,&nbsp;Coord&nbsp;z)&nbsp;</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A258C01c1c2"></A>void&nbsp;rpdr(Coord&nbsp;x,&nbsp;Coord&nbsp;y,&nbsp;Coord&nbsp;z)&nbsp;</PRE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52C704mhay"></A>A polygon is specified by the following
sequence of calls: </P>


<OL><LI><A NAME="A258C01c1c4"></A>A <B>pmv</B> subroutine (or <B>rpmv</B> subroutine)
to locate the first point on the boundary</LI>


<LI><A NAME="A258C01c1c5"></A>A sequence of <B>pdr</B> (or <B>rpdr</B>)
subroutines for each additional vertex</LI>


<LI><A NAME="A258C01c1c6"></A>The <B>pclos</B> subroutine to close and
fill the polygon.</LI></OL>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52C731mhay"></A>The <B>pclos</B> subroutine has no parameters
All the other subroutines take either two or three parameters of the appropriate
type. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52C755mhay"></A>After any polygon subroutine, the current
graphics position is left at the original point of the polygon, the point
identified by the <B>pmv</B> (or <B>rpmv</B>) subroutine. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52C779mhay"></A>The following sample program draws a filled
blue polygon: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A11C0b161"></A>#include&nbsp;&lt;gl/gl.h&gt;</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A11C0b162"></A>main()
{</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A11C0b164"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;prefposition(100,&nbsp;500,&nbsp;100,&nbsp;500);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;winopen(&quot;bluebox&quot;);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(BLACK);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;clear();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(BLUE);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;pmv2i(200,&nbsp;200);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;pdr2i(200,&nbsp;300);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;pdr2i(300,&nbsp;300);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;pdr2i(300,&nbsp;200);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;pclos();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;sleep(3);
}</PRE>


<BLOCKQUOTE><P><A NAME="A11C0b170"></A><B>Note: </B>The <B>pclos</B> subroutine connects
back to the original starting point. </P></BLOCKQUOTE>




<P><A NAME="A3C0E52C808mhay"></A>Other drawing methods are explained in
<A HREF="drawbeg-end.html">Drawing with Begin-End Style Subroutines</A>and <A HREF="drawpoly.html#drawpoly.html">Drawing Rectangles, Circles,
Arcs, and Polygons</A>. </P>
```

```html
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="multiprocman.html"></A>Multiple Process Management</H2>
<P><A NAME="A3C0F110534mhay"></A>Special considerations apply to the use of the <B>fork</B>, <B>vfork</B>, and other subroutines and to rendering processes used in conjunction with asynchronous handlers.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A42664C499ttay"></A>Using the fork, execl, execv and Other Subroutines</H3>
<P><A NAME="A3C0F110556mhay"></A>When using the <B>fork</B> or <B>vfork</B> subroutine with an Enhanced X-Windows, X Toolkit, or AIXwindows application, open a separate display connection (socket) with the <B>XOpenDisplay</B> or <B>XtOpenDisplay</B> subroutines for the forked process. The child process should never use the same display connection as the parent. Display connections are embodied with sockets and sockets are inherited by the child process. Any attempt to have multiple processes writing to the same display connection results in the random interleaving of X protocol packets at the word level. The resulting data written to the socket is generally invalid in the form of undefined X protocol packets that cannot be interpreted by the X server.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3C0F110577mhay"></A>The <B>exec</B> and <B>fork</B> subroutines may be used within GL with some restrictions. The GL library manipulates a complex collection of resources. State information is stored in many places: in global (non-exported) variables in the process .data segment; in the X server; in the kernel, as part of the process table; and in the graphics hardware. Children created with the <B>fork</B> subroutine inherit (duplicate copies of) some, but not all of this state information. For example, the <B>fork</B> subroutine does not cause the X server to treat the child process as if it were a new client. In fact, the X server is ignorant of the fact that a fork has taken place. Similarly, the <B>exec</B> routine will overlay the old process image (in particular, wiping out values stored in global variables), but does not reset state contained in the X server or the kernel. (For example, the <B>exec</B> routine does not automatically close files or sockets.)</P>

<H4><A NAME="A42664D533ttay"></A>Current Restrictions</H4>
<P><A NAME="A3C0F110597mhay"></A>The following restrictions apply to the use of the <B>exec</B> and <B>fork</B> subroutines within a GL application:</P>

<UL><LI><A NAME="A5B2643114vbia"></A>If the <B>exec</B> subroutine is used alone (that is, not immediately preceded by a call to the <B>fork</B> subroutine), and the new process image or any future overlays need to use GL, then the GL <B>gexit</B> subroutine must be called before the <B>exec</B> subroutine. This is required to reset process attributes; if this is not done, GL initialization performed by the new process image will be unsuccessful.</LI>

<LI><A NAME="A5B2643386vbia"></A>If the <B>fork</B> subroutine is used alone (that is, not immediately followed by the <B>exec</B> subroutine) then the child process must not attempt to make any additional GL subroutine calls. Drawing by the child process may hang the graphics adapter or the X server, or may cause unpredictable results and place the system in an unpredictable state.


<P><A NAME="A5B2643665vbia"></A>In particular, the child process should not call the <B>gexit</B> subroutine. Because of a known implementation problem, the <B>gexit</B> subroutine adversely affects the parent process and the GL subroutine call in the child process.</P></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A5B2643954vbia"></A>If the <B>fork</B> subroutine is used alone (that is, without a trailing <B>exec</B> subroutine) and both the child and the parent processes use GL, then the <B>gexit</B> subroutine must be called before the <B>fork</B> subroutine.</LI>

<LI><A NAME="A5B2644188vbia"></A>If the <B>fork</B> subroutine is followed by an <B>exec</B> subroutine, the procedures for gracefully resetting the system depend on whether the <B>exec</B> subroutine occurs in the parent or in the child.


<P><A NAME="A5B2644400vbia"></A>If the <B>exec</B> subroutine is performed in the parent, then a <B>gexit</B> subroutine must precede the <B>exec</B> subroutine.</P>




<P><A NAME="A5B2644656vbia"></A>If the <B>exec</B> subroutine is performed by the child, then calling the <B>gexit</B> routine can be avoided, but at a risk. Failing to call the <B>gexit</B> subroutine leaves connections and shared memory segments open; this will prevent a process from performing more than nine consecutive forks in a row.</P></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A5B2645099vbia"></A>For programs that end normally (for example, by using the <B>exit</B> subroutine), the <B>gexit</B> subroutine should be called first. In some circumstances, failure to do so can leave a process in the zombie state. Zombies are most likely to occur if the exiting process has child processes that are using GL subroutine calls.</LI></UL>


<H3><A NAME="A42664D979ttay"></A>Using Signals and Other Asynchronous Event Systems</H3>
<P><A NAME="A3C0F110628mhay"></A>GL is not designed to support rendering in a re-entrant fashion from within the same process. In particular, GL rendering from asynchronous handlers, such as signal handlers, is not recommended.</P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0F110649mhay"></A>All GL rendering routines are interruptable; they do not mask any signals. GL rendering routines are particularly vulnerable when communicating with the graphics adapter. Adapter commands may be many words in length but must arrive in atomic units; adapter commands with embedded miscellaneous text or symbols may hang the adapter. If a GL routine is interrupted while writing to the adapter, and the interrupting routine also writes to the adapter, the resulting adapter command is embedded in the previously started data stream, thus corrupting it.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3C0F110669mhay"></A>If the application performs rendering from within a signal handler, then the application must protect itself. This can be accomplished by masking all relevant signals before beginning rendering and unmasking them after completion. The application must mask all occurrences of rendering, whether within the signal handler or within the main program. Failure to do so risks corruption of the data stream and a hang of the graphic adapter.</P>

<hr><center>
```

```html
<H2><A NAME="objectedit.html"></A>Object Editing</H2>


<P><A NAME="INDEX724"></A><A NAME="INDEX725"></A><A NAME="INDEX726"></A><A NAME="INDEX727"></A><A NAME="INDEX728"></A><A NAME="INDEX729"></A><A NAME="INDEX730"></A></P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC25854mhay"></A>This section discusses the following topics</P>


<UL><LI><A NAME="A258C01c0dc"></A><A HREF="objectedit.html#A13C0bd28">Identifying
Display List Items with Tags</A></LI>


<LI><A NAME="A258C01c0dd"></A><A HREF="objectedit.html#A13C0bd3e">Inserting,
Deleting, and Replacing Within Objects</A></LI>


<LI><A NAME="A258C01c0de"></A><A HREF="objectedit.html#A65C0167ec">Object
Editing Examples</A></LI>


<LI><A NAME="A258C01c0df"></A><A HREF="objectedit.html#A13C0bd75">Object
Memory Management</A></LI></UL>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC25879mhay"></A>You can change an object by editing it.
Editing requires you to identify and locate the drawing routines that you
want to change. You use two types of routines when you edit an object:</P>


<UL><LI><A NAME="A13C0bd1d"></A>Editing subroutines, which add, remove, or
replace drawing routines.</LI>


<LI><A NAME="A13C0bd1e"></A>Tag subroutines, which identify locations of
drawing routines within an object.</LI></UL>


<H3><A NAME="A13C0bd20"></A>editobj Subroutine </H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC25902mhay"></A>To open an object for editing, use the
<B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/editobj.html#A142X9360">editobj</A></B>
subroutine. A pointer acts as a cursor that appends new routines. The pointer
is initially set to the end of the object. The system appends graphics
routines to the object until either a <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/closeobj.html#A142X915b">closeobj</A></B>
subroutine or a pointer positioning routine (the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/objdelete.html#A142X9afd">objdelete</A></B>,
<B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/objinsert.html#A142X9adb">objinsert</A></B>,
or <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/objreplace.html#A142X9b50">objreplace</A></B>
subroutines) executes. The syntax is as follows: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A58C015395"></A>void&nbsp;editobj(Int32&nbsp;object)</PRE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC25923mhay"></A>The system interprets the editing routines
following the <B>editobj</B> subroutine call. Use the <B>closeobj</B> subroutine
to terminate your editing session. If you specify an undefined object,
an error message appears. </P>


<H3><A NAME="A13C0bd25"></A>getopenobj Subroutine </H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC25944mhay"></A>To determine if an object is open for
editing, use the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/getopenobj.html#A142X9382">getopenobj</A></B>
subroutine. If an object is open, it returns the object's numeric identifier.
If no object is open, it returns -1. The syntax is as follows: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A58C015396"></A>Int32&nbsp;getopenobj()</PRE>


<H3><A NAME="A13C0bd28"></A>Identifying Display List Items with Tags </H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC25966mhay"></A>Tags locate display list items you want
to edit. Editing routines require tag names as parameters. The STARTTAG
value is a predefined tag that goes before the very first item to mark
the beginning of the list. The STARTTAG value does not have any effect
on drawing or modifying the object; use it only to return to (find) the
beginning of the list. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC25986mhay"></A>The ENDTAG value is a predefined tag that
is positioned after the last item to mark the end of the list. Like STARTTAG,
ENDTAG does not have any effect on drawing or modifying the object; use
it to find the end of the graphical object. When you call the <B>makeobj</B>
subroutine to create a list, STARTTAG and ENDTAG automatically appear.
You cannot delete these tags. When an object is opened for editing, a pointer
appears at ENDTAG, after the last routine in the object. To perform edits
on other items, refer to them by their tags. </P>


<H3><A NAME="A13C0bd2a"></A>maketag Subroutine </H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC26007mhay"></A>Use tags to mark display list items you
may want to change. You explicitly tag routines with the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/maketag.html#A142X942c">maketag</A></B>
subroutine. You specify a signed 32-bit numeric identifier and the system
places a marker between two list items. You can use the same tag name in
different objects. The syntax is as follows: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A58C015397"></A>void&nbsp;maketag(Int32&nbsp;tag)</PRE>


<H3><A NAME="A13C0bd2e"></A>newtag Subroutine </H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC26029mhay"></A>The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/newtag.html#A142X93a4">newtag</A></B>
subroutine also adds tags to an object, but uses an existing tag to determine
its relative position within the object. The <B>newtag</B> subroutine creates
a new tag that is offset beyond the other tag by the number of lines given
in its parameter offset. The syntax is as follows: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A58C015398"></A>void&nbsp;newtag(Int32&nbsp;newt,&nbsp;Int32&nbsp;oldtag,&nbsp;Int32&nbsp;offset)</PRE>


<H3><A NAME="A13C0bd33"></A>istag Subroutine </H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC26052mhay"></A>The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/istag.html#JXw220marj">istag</A></B>
subroutine tells whether a given tag is in use within the current open
object. The subroutine returns TRUE if the tag is in use, and FALSE if
it is not. The result is undefined if there is no currently open object.
The syntax is as follows: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A58C015399"></A>Int32&nbsp;istag(Int32&nbsp;tag)</PRE>


<H3><A NAME="A13C0bd37"></A>gentag Subroutine </H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC26074mhay"></A>The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/gentag.html#A48x2120marj">gentag</A></B>
subroutine generates a unique integer to use as a tag within the current
open object. The syntax is as follows: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A58C01539a"></A>Int32&nbsp;gentag()</PRE>


<H3><A NAME="A13C0bd3a"></A>deltag Subroutine </H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC26096mhay"></A>The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/deltag.html#A1N61210marj">deltag</A></B>
subroutine deletes tags from the object currently open for editing. Remember,
you cannot delete the special STARTTAG and ENDTAG tags. The syntax is as
follows: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A58C01539b"></A>void&nbsp;deltag(Int32&nbsp;tag)</PRE>


<H3><A NAME="A13C0bd3e"></A>Inserting, Deleting, and Replacing within Objects</H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC26118mhay"></A>The following subroutines allow you to
edit an object by moving the subroutines inside the object using tags as
markers for inserting or deleting. </P>


<H3><A NAME="A13C0bd3f"></A>objinsert Subroutine </H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC26139mhay"></A>Use the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/objinsert.html#A142X9adb">objinsert</A></B>
subroutine to add routines to an object at the location specified in the
<I>tag </I>parameter. The <B>objinsert</B> subroutine positions an editing
pointer on the tag specified in the <I>tag </I>parameter. The system inserts
graphics routines immediately after the tag. To terminate the insertion,
use the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/closeobj.html#A142X915b">closeobj</A></B>
subroutine or the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/objdelete.html#A142X9afd">objdelete</A></B>
or <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/objreplace.html#A142X9b50">objreplace</A></B>
editing subroutines. The syntax is as follows: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A58C01539c"></A>void&nbsp;objinsert(Int32&nbsp;tag)</PRE>


<H3><A NAME="A13C0bd43"></A>objdelete Subroutine </H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC26161mhay"></A>The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/objdelete.html#A142X9afd">objdelete</A></B>
subroutine removes routines from the current open object. It removes everything
between the <I>tag1</I> and <I>tag2</I> parameters, including routines
and other tag names. For example, <TT>objdelete(STARTTAG,&nbsp;ENDTAG)</TT>
would delete every routine. The system ignores the <B>objdelete</B> subroutine
if no object is open for editing. This routine leaves the pointer at the
<I>tag1</I> parameter location after it executes. The syntax is as follows:</P>


<PRE><A NAME="A58C01539d"></A>void&nbsp;objdelete(Int32&nbsp;tag1,&nbsp;Int32&nbsp;tag2)</PRE>


<H3><A NAME="A13C0bd47"></A>objreplace Subroutine </H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC26183mhay"></A>The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/objreplace.html#A142X9b50">objreplace</A></B>
subroutine combines the functions of the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/objdelete.html#A142X9afd">objdelete</A></B>
and <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/objinsert.html#A142X9adb">objinsert</A></B>
subroutines. It provides a quick way to replace one routine with another
that occupies the same amount of display list space. Its <I>tag</I> parameter
is a single tag. Graphics routines that follow the <B>objreplace</B> subroutine
overwrite existing routines until an occurrence of the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/closeobj.html#A142X915b">closeobj</A></B>
or an editing subroutine (<B>objinsert</B> or <B>objdelete</B>) terminates
the replacement. </P>


<BLOCKQUOTE><P><A NAME="A13C0bd49"></A><B>Note: </B>The <B>objreplace</B> subroutine
requires that the new routine to be exactly the same length in bytes as
the previous one. If it is not, there is a danger that the display list
will be scrambled. Use the <B>objdelete</B> and <B>objinsert</B> subroutines
for more general replacement. </P></BLOCKQUOTE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC26204mhay"></A>The syntax is as follows: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A58C01539e"></A>void&nbsp;objreplace(Int32&nbsp;tag)</PRE>


<H3><A NAME="A65C0167ec"></A>Object Editing Examples </H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC26225mhay"></A>The following is an example of object
editing. The object <TT>star</TT> is defined. </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A65C0167ee"></A>makeobj(star);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(GREEN);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;maketag(BOX);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;recti(1,&nbsp;1,&nbsp;9,&nbsp;9);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;maketag(INNER);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(BLUE);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;poly2i(8,&nbsp;Inner);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;maketag(OUTER);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(RED);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;poly2i(8,&nbsp;Outer);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;maketag(CENTER);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(YELLOW);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;pnt2i(5,&nbsp;5);
closeobj();</PRE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC26247mhay"></A>This object is then edited with the following
routine to produce a modified object: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A65C0167f0"></A>editobj(star);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;circi(1,&nbsp;5,&nbsp;5);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;objinsert(BOX);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;recti(0,&nbsp;0,&nbsp;10,&nbsp;10);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;objreplace(INNER);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(GREEN);
closeobj();</PRE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC26268mhay"></A>The object resulting from the editing
session is equivalent to an object created by the following code. </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A65C0167f2"></A>makeobj(star);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(GREEN);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;maketag(BOX);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;recti(0,&nbsp;0,&nbsp;10,&nbsp;10);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;recti(1,&nbsp;1,&nbsp;9,&nbsp;9);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;maketag(INNER);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(GREEN);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;poly2i(8,&nbsp;Inner);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;maketag(OUTER);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(RED);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;poly2i(8,&nbsp;Outer);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;maketag(CENTER);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(YELLOW);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;pnt2i(5,&nbsp;5);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;circi(1,&nbsp;5,&nbsp;5);
closeobj();</PRE>


<H3><A NAME="A13C0bd75"></A>Object Memory Management </H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC26289mhay"></A>Editing can require large amounts of memory.
The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/compactify.html#A142X9c5a">compactify</A></B>
and <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/chunksize.html#A142X9c38">chunksize</A></B>
subroutines perform memory management tasks. </P>


<H3><A NAME="A13C0bd78"></A>compactify Subroutine </H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC26310mhay"></A>As memory is modified by the various editing
routines, an open object can become fragmented and stored inefficiently.
When the amount of wasted space becomes large, the system automatically
calls the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/compactify.html#A142X9c5a">compactify</A></B>
subroutine during the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/closeobj.html#A142X915b">closeobj</A></B>
operation. The routine allows you to perform the compaction explicitly.
Unless new routines are inserted in the middle of an object, compaction
is not necessary. </P>


<BLOCKQUOTE><P><A NAME="A13C0bd7a"></A><B>Note: </B>The <B>compactify</B> subroutine
uses a significant amount of computing time. Do not call it unless the
amount of available storage space is critical; use it sparingly when performance
is a consideration. </P></BLOCKQUOTE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC26331mhay"></A>The syntax is as follows: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A58C01539f"></A>void&nbsp;compactify(Int32&nbsp;object)</PRE>


<H3><A NAME="A38C012071"></A>chunksize Subroutine </H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC26353mhay"></A>The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/chunksize.html#A142X9c38">chunksize</A></B>
subroutine specifies the minimum chunk of memory necessary to accommodate
the largest GL command call. Normally, this is a call to the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/poly.html#avf2c0marj">poly</A></B>
or <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/polf.html#Zsf1c0marj">polf</A></B>
subroutine with a very large number of vertices. If there is a memory shortage,
use the <B>chunksize</B> subroutine to allocate memory differently to an
object. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC26373mhay"></A>The <B>chunksize</B> subroutine specifies
the minimum amount of memory that the system allocates to an object. The
default chunk is 1020 bytes. When a chunk is specified, its size varies
according to the needs of the application. As the object grows, more memory
is allocated in units of the size specified in the <I>chunk</I> parameter.
The <B>chunksize</B> subroutine is called once after the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/ginit.html#LDg21c0marj">ginit</A></B>
or <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/winopen.html#A142X91549">winopen</A></B>
subroutine, and once before the first <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/makeobj.html#A142X912d">makeobj</A></B>
subroutine. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC26392mhay"></A>The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/chunksize.html#A142X9c38">chunksize</A></B>
subroutine helps use memory economically. For example, when graphical objects
require very little memory, the system can be used more efficiently by
specifying smaller chunks of memory. There are drawbacks to the use of
the <B>chunksize</B> subroutine. There is both memory and execution time
overhead associated with each chunk. Many small chunks can be inefficient
in both ways. The syntax is as follows: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A68C017192"></A>void&nbsp;chunksize(Int32&nbsp;chunk)</PRE>
```
