```html
<H2><A NAME="pushviewport.html"></A>pushviewport Subroutine </H2>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E9FE694mhay"></A>The system maintains a stack of viewports
and screenmasks, and the top element in the stack is the current viewport
and screenmask. The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/pushviewport.html#A213X911bee">pushviewport</A></B>
subroutine duplicates the current viewport and screenmask and pushes this
duplicate element on the stack. The syntax is as follows: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A258C01c1a0"></A>void&nbsp;pushviewport()</PRE>




<hr><center>
```

```html
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="querysys.html"></A>Querying the System

</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX875" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX876" REL="I2" TITLE="querying the system"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX877" REL="I1" TITLE="query"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX878" REL="I2" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX879" REL="I3" TITLE="system"></A>
<P><A NAME="A3C0ED59540mhay"></A>Certain GL subroutines obtain information about various processes in or aspects of the system. These include current cursor characteristics, maximum character height in the current raster font, and the current display, color map, or drawing mode.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3C0ED59561mhay"></A>Other subroutines furnish lists, such as the <!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/blkqread.html#A143X91fc"><B>blkqread</B></A> subroutine, which reads a block of event queue entries, and the <!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/getdev.html#A143X923"><B>getdev</B></A> subroutine, which polls the specified valuators.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A4x2190marj"></A>List of GL Query Subroutines<A NAME="INDEX880" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX881" REL="I2" TITLE="subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX882" REL="I3" TITLE="query"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX883" REL="I1" TITLE="query"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX884" REL="I2" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX885" REL="I3" TITLE="subroutines"></A>
</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A39C01237a"></A><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/blkqread.html#A143X91fc"><B>blkqread</B></A> 
</TD></TR>
<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>
<TD>  Reads multiple entries from the event queue.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A39C01237b"></A><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/genobj.html#A142X91ea"><B>genobj</B></A> 
</TD></TR>
<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>
<TD>  Returns a unique integer for use as an object identifier.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A39C01237c"></A><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/gentag.html#A48x2120marj"><B>gentag</B></A> 
</TD></TR>
<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>
<TD>  Returns a unique integer for use as a tag number.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A39C01237d"></A><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/getbackface.html#A143X976d"><B>getbackface</B></A> 
</TD></TR>
<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>
<TD>  Indicates whether backfacing polygon removal is on or off.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A39C01237e"></A><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/getbuffer.html#A145X9f6"><B>getbuffer</B></A> 
</TD></TR>
<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>
<TD>  Indicates which buffers are enabled for drawing.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A39C01237f"></A><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/getbutton.html#A143X91"><B>getbutton</B></A> 
</TD></TR>
<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>
<TD>  Returns the current state of a button.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A39C012380"></A><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/getcmmode.html#A146X948e"><B>getcmmode</B></A> 
</TD></TR>
<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>
<TD>  Returns the organization of the current color map.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A39C012381"></A><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/getcolor.html#A146X924b"><B>getcolor</B></A> 
</TD></TR>
<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>
<TD>  Returns the current color in color map mode.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A39C012382"></A><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/getcpos.html#A144X9364"><B>getcpos</B></A> 
</TD></TR>
<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>
<TD>  Returns the current character position.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A39C012383"></A><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/getcursor.html#sP1160nita"><B>getcursor</B></A> 
</TD></TR>
<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>
<TD>  Returns the cursor characteristics.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A39C012384"></A><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/getdcm.html#A5OK230marj"><B>getdcm</B></A> 
</TD></TR>
<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>
<TD>  Indicates whether depth-cue mode is on or off.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A39C012385"></A><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/getdescender.html#A144X9386"><B>getdescender</B></A> 
</TD></TR>
<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>
<TD>  Returns the baseline extent of the longest character descender.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A39C012386"></A><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/getdev.html#A143X923"><B>getdev</B></A> 
</TD></TR>
<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>
<TD>  Reads a list of valuators.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A39C012387"></A><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/getdisplaymode.html#A145X9206"><B>getdisplaymode</B></A> 
</TD></TR>
<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>
<TD>  Returns the current display mode.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A39C012388"></A><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/getdrawmode.html#A143X9482"><B>getdrawmode</B></A> 
</TD></TR>
<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>
<TD>  Returns the current drawing mode.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A39C012389"></A><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/getfont.html#A144X93a8"><B>getfont</B></A> 
</TD></TR>
<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>
<TD>  Returns the current raster font number.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A78C144b"></A><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/getgdesc.html#t9311e0marj"><B>getgdesc</B></A> 
</TD></TR>
<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>
<TD>  Returns information about currently installed graphics hardware.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A39C01238a"></A><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/getgpos.html#CZf60marj"><B>getgpos</B></A> 
</TD></TR>
<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>
<TD>  Gets the current graphics position.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A39C01238b"></A><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/getheight.html#A144X93ca"><B>getheight</B></A> 
</TD></TR>
```

```html
<HTML>
```

```html
<HEAD>
<META HTTP-EQUIV="Content-Type" CONTENT="text/html; charset=iso-8859-1">

   <TITLE>Reading and Writing Pixels in GL
</TITLE>
   
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="drawpoly.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="textchars.html">Next</a>  |

 <A HREF="cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 Version 4.1 for AIX: Programming Concepts</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>



<H2><A NAME="rwpixels.html"></A>Reading and Writing Pixels</H2>


<P><A NAME="INDEX227"></A><A NAME="INDEX228"></A><A NAME="INDEX229"></A><A NAME="INDEX230"></A><A NAME="INDEX231"></A><A NAME="INDEX232"></A><A NAME="INDEX233"></A><A NAME="INDEX234"></A><A NAME="INDEX235"></A></P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52D739mhay"></A>Information in this section includes the
following: </P>


<UL><LI><A NAME="A52C0142c7"></A>Pixel <A HREF="rwpixels.html#A18C0dc63">Formats</A></LI>


<LI><A NAME="A52C0142c8"></A>Efficient Pixel <A HREF="rwpixels.html#A18C0dc69">Reading
and Writing</A></LI>


<LI><A NAME="C4ED94E420lpas"></A><A HREF="rwpixels.html#A6DACA5410vbia">Reading
and Writing to Overlay Planes</A></LI>


<LI><A NAME="A52C0142c9"></A>Other Pixel <A HREF="rwpixels.html#A48C013776">Access</A>
Subroutines</LI></UL>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52D767mhay"></A>A pixel is a rectangular picture element.
The display screen is composed of an array of pixels. In a black-and-white
system, pixels are turned on and off to form images. In a color system,
each pixel has three components: red, green, and blue. The intensity of
each component can be controlled. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52D791mhay"></A>Pixels, like 
<A HREF="specialterms.html#A26P073b">raster
fonts</A>, are not as easy to transform as geometric figures. Coding for
pixel representation on the screen often requires information about the
window dimensions, the screen resolution, and so forth. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52D815mhay"></A>Another problem with reading and writing
pixels is that the contents of each pixel can mean different things depending
on the display mode. The same physical <A HREF="specialterms.html#A3C0F2A3129mhay">bitplanes</A>
are used to store either color index information or RGB information. Accordingly,
the mode of the window determines whether the contents are interpreted
as RGB triples or as indexes into the color map. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52D838mhay"></A>The GL pixel-handling subroutines operate
on arbitrarily sized rectangles, and they operate in all modes. </P>


<H3><A NAME="A264X9329"></A>List of GL Pixel Block Transfer Subroutines<A NAME="INDEX236"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX237"></A> <A NAME="INDEX238"></A> <A NAME="INDEX239"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX240"></A> <A NAME="INDEX241"></A> </H3>


<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A58C0153cd"></A><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/logicop.html#iM521a0marj">logicop</A></B></TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>


<TD>Specifies a logical operation for pixel writes.</TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A78C144a"></A><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/pixmode.html#bav30marj">pixmode</A></B></TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>


<TD>Controls the operation of the <B>lrectread</B> and <B>lrectwrite</B>
subroutines.</TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A38C012067"></A><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/readpixels.html#A142X91059">readpixels</A></B></TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>


<TD>Returns a row of specific pixels in color map mode. </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A38C012068"></A><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/readRGB.html#A142X9107b">readRGB</A></B></TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>


<TD>Returns a row of specific pixels in RGB mode.</TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A38C012069"></A><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/readsource.html#A142X9cc0">readsource</A></B></TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>


<TD>Specifies the source for pixels to be read.</TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A38C01206a"></A><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/rectcopy.html#A142X9d04">rectcopy</A></B></TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>


<TD>Copies a rectangle of pixels screen to screen with optional zoom. </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A38C01206b"></A><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/rectread.html#A142X9c7c">rectread,
lrectread</A></B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>


<TD>Reads a rectangular array of pixels into host memory.</TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A38C01206c"></A><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/rectwrite.html#A142X9c9e">rectwrite,
lrectwrite</A></B> </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>


<TD>Draws a rectangular array of pixels into the frame buffer. </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A38C01206d"></A><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/rectzoom.html#A142X9d26">rectzoom</A></B></TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>


<TD>Specifies the zoom factor for rectangle copies and writes. </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A38C01206e"></A><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/writepixels.html#A142X9e62">writepixels</A></B></TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>


<TD>Paints a row of pixels on screen in color map mode.</TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A38C01206f"></A><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/writeRGB.html#A142X9ff2">writeRGB</A></B></TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>


<TD>Paints a row of pixels on screen in RGB mode. </TD></TR></TABLE>


<P> </P>


<H3><A NAME="A18C0dc63"></A>Pixel Formats </H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52D876mhay"></A>The following three pixel formats constitute
the standard GL pixel formats: </P>


<UL><LI><A NAME="A18C0dc66"></A>Pixel data to be interpreted as red-green-blue-alpha
packs 8 bits for each into a 32-bit word. Bits 0-7 represent red, bits
8-15 represent green, bits 16-23 represent blue, and bits 24-31 represent
alpha. For example, 0x01020304 corresponds to a pixel whose red, green,
blue, and alpha values are 4, 3, 2, and 1, respectively. This is exactly
the same format used by the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/cpack.html#A143X9284">cpack</A></B>
subroutine. See &quot;<A HREF="workcolor.html#workcolor.html">Working in Color
Map and RGB Modes</A>&quot; for more information. 

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A38C012066"></A><B>Note: </B>Alpha functions require specialized
alpha hardware. The High-Performance 3-D Color Graphics Processor does
not have alpha bitplanes. </BLOCKQUOTE></LI>


<LI><A NAME="A18C0dc67"></A>Pixels interpreted as indexes into a single,
4096-entry color map interpret the low-order 12 bits as the color index.
The high-order 20 bits should be zero.</LI>


<LI><A NAME="A18C0dc68"></A>Pixels that read or write the <A HREF="specialterms.html#A154P1160a">z
buffer </A>directly. The <I>z</I> buffer contains 24 bits of data, stored
as the low-order 24 bits of a 32-bit word. The top 8 bits should be zero.</LI></UL>


<H3><A NAME="A18C0dc69"></A>Efficient Pixel Reading and Writing </H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52D907mhay"></A>This section describes subroutines that
read and write pixels with the highest possible performance. </P>


<BLOCKQUOTE><P><A NAME="A19C0e0d2"></A><B>Note: </B>These subroutines do not check
to make sure that the data is valid. If you read pixel data from a window
in <A HREF="specialterms.html#A25P03e3">color map mode </A>and
then write the data into an RGB window or into the <I>z</I> buffer, the
data is interpreted according to the new mode. The results are unpredictable.</P></BLOCKQUOTE>


<H4><A NAME="A258C01c1fe"></A>pixmode Subroutine </H4>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52D936mhay"></A>The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/pixmode.html#bav30marj">pixmode</A></B>
subroutine controls the format in which pixmaps are transferred to and
from the adapter. You can use the <B>pixmode</B> subroutine to specify
the format of a pixmap as handled by your application. The <B>pixmode</B>
subroutine performs the following functions: </P>


<UL><LI><A NAME="A33D882446ttay"></A>Describes the format of a pixmap so that
the hardware can operate with it.</LI>


<LI><A NAME="A33D882624ttay"></A>Provides a device-independent interface
to pixel block transfers (BLITs).</LI>


<LI><A NAME="A33D882805ttay"></A>Allows the casual user to perform BLITs
without having to understand the frame buffer organization in detail.</LI>


<LI><A NAME="A33D882974ttay"></A>Provides convenience by understanding
a large variety of pixmap formats.</LI>


<LI><A NAME="A33D883149ttay"></A>Provides the most efficient interface
to the hardware by minimizing unneccesary data copying. 

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A33D883334ttay"></A><B>Note: </B>The <B>pixmap</B> subroutine
is not intended to be an &quot;image processing function&quot; or to be
used for pixmap format conversion. </BLOCKQUOTE></LI></UL>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52D966mhay"></A>After you specify the pixmap format, the
<B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/rectread.html#A142X9c7c">lrectread</A></B>
and <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/rectwrite.html#A142X9c9e">lrectwrite</A></B>
subroutines automatically perform the transfer from this format to the
internal format of the <A HREF="specialterms.html#A270A984a">frame
buffer</A>.  The syntax is as follows: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A258C01c200"></A>void&nbsp;pixmode&nbsp;(Int32&nbsp;mode,&nbsp;Int32&nbsp;value)</PRE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52D991mhay"></A>FASTMODE is useful when it is important
to store and retrieve images quickly, and when the internal format of the
image is not important. A compatible mode is supplied by setting FASTMODE
to FALSE. Using FASTMODE on certain adapters, for example the Supergraphics
Processor Subsystem, can result in significantly improved pixel transfer
capabilities. </P>


<H4><A NAME="A18C0dc6b"></A>rectread and lrectread Subroutines </H4>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52E017mhay"></A>The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/rectread.html#A142X9c7c">rectread</A></B>
subroutine reads a rectangular array of pixels from the window where the
<I>xll</I>,&nbsp;<I>yll</I> parameters are the coordinates for the lower-left
corner of the rectangle and the <I>xur</I>,&nbsp;<I>yur</I> parameters
are the coordinates for the upper-right corner. All coordinates are relative
to the lower-left corner of the window in screen coordinates. The syntax
is as follows: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A258C01c203"></A>Int32&nbsp;rectread(Screencoord&nbsp;xll,&nbsp;Screencoord&nbsp;yll,
Screencoord&nbsp;xur,&nbsp;Screencoord&nbsp;xur,&nbsp;Int16&nbsp;*parray) </PRE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52E043mhay"></A>The <I>parray</I> parameter is an array
of 16-bit values. Only the low-order 16 bits of each pixel are read, so
the <B>rectread </B>subroutine is useful primarily for windows drawn in
color map mode. The data is loaded into the <I>parray</I> parameter left
to right, and then bottom to top. In other words, if the pixel data on
the screen looked like this: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A18C0dc6d"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;1&nbsp;&nbsp;2&nbsp;&nbsp;3&nbsp;&nbsp;4</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A18C0dc6e"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;5&nbsp;&nbsp;6&nbsp;&nbsp;7&nbsp;&nbsp;8</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A18C0dc6f"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;9&nbsp;10&nbsp;11&nbsp;12</PRE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52E070mhay"></A>The <I>parray</I> parameter would contain
<TT>parray[0]&nbsp;=&nbsp;9,&nbsp;parray[1]&nbsp;=&nbsp;10</TT>, or <TT>{9,&nbsp;10,&nbsp;11,&nbsp;12,&nbsp;5,&nbsp;6,&nbsp;7,&nbsp;8,&nbsp;1,&nbsp;2,&nbsp;3,&nbsp;4}</TT>,
and so forth. The <B>rectread</B> subroutine returns the number of pixels
successfully read. Normally, this is defined as: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A18C0dc71"></A>(x2&nbsp;-&nbsp;x1&nbsp;+&nbsp;1)(y2&nbsp;-&nbsp;y1&nbsp;+&nbsp;1)</PRE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52E097mhay"></A>If any part of the specified rectangle
is off the screen, or if the coordinates are mixed up, the behavior of
the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/rectread.html#A142X9c7c">rectread</A></B>
subroutine is undefined. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52E121mhay"></A>Errors occur only outside the screen,
not in the window. It is possible to read pixels outside a window, as long
as they are on the physical screen. This can be useful for certain applications
that magnify data in other windows or that process images produced by other
programs. The main difficulty is that the data can come from areas of the
screen that are in different modes (<A HREF="specialterms.html#A25P03e3">color
map mode</A> or <A HREF="specialterms.html#A26P0743">RGB mode</A>).
Because the <B>rectread</B> subroutine is not restricted to the current
window, any or all of the coordinates can be negative. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52E145mhay"></A>The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/rectread.html#A142X9c7c">lrectread</A></B>
subroutine is very similar to the <B>rectread</B> subroutine. It differs
in that its operation is controlled by the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/pixmode.html#bav30marj">pixmode</A></B>
subroutine and that the <I>parray</I> parameter contains 32-bit quantities.
Although the <B>lrectread</B> subroutine is useful for any kind of data,
it wastes space if the data is known to be from a window in color map mode.
The syntax is as follows: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A258C01c205"></A>Int32&nbsp;lrectread(Screencoord&nbsp;xll,&nbsp;Screencoord&nbsp;yll,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Screencoord&nbsp;xur,&nbsp;Screencoord&nbsp;xur,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Int32&nbsp;*parray)</PRE>


<H4><A NAME="A18C0dc75"></A>readsource Subroutine </H4>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52E172mhay"></A>The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/readsource.html#A142X9cc0">readsource</A></B>
subroutine determines the source of pixels read by the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/rectread.html#A142X9c7c">rectread</A></B>,
<B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/rectread.html#A142X9c7c">lrectread</A></B>,
<B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/rectcopy.html#A142X9d04">rectcopy</A></B>,
<B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/readpixels.html#A142X91059">readpixels</A></B>,
and <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/readRGB.html#A142X9107b">readRGB</A></B>
subroutines. The <I>source</I> parameter has four possible values defined
in the <B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B> file. They are SRC_AUTO, SRC_FRONT,
SRC_BACK, and SRC_ZBUFFER. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52E196mhay"></A>The default value is SRC_AUTO, which selects
the front buffer in <A HREF="specialterms.html#A27P01c">single
buffer mode </A>and the back buffer in 
<A HREF="specialterms.html#A26P0474">double
buffer mode</A>. The SRC_FRONT value always reads from the 
<A HREF="specialterms.html#A26P051c">front
buffer</A> (this is always valid), and the SRC_BACK value always reads
from the <A HREF="specialterms.html#A26P051c">back buffer </A>(valid
only in double buffer mode). Finally, SRC_ZBUFFER reads 24-bit data from
the <A HREF="specialterms.html#A154P1160a">z buffer</A>. The SRC_ZBUFFER
value is valid in both single and double buffer modes. The syntax is as
follows: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A258C01c207"></A>void&nbsp;readsource(Int32&nbsp;source)</PRE>


<H4><A NAME="A18C0dc77"></A>rectwrite and lrectwrite Subroutines </H4>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52E224mhay"></A>The subroutines that draw rectangular
arrays of pixels, <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/rectwrite.html#A142X9c9e">rectwrite</A></B>
and <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/rectwrite.html#A142X9c9e">lrectwrite</A></B>,
are similar to those that read pixels. The data in the <I>parray</I> parameter
is 16-bit quantities for the <B>rectwrite</B> subroutine, and 32-bit quantities
for the <B>lrectwrite</B> subroutine. The destination buffer is determined
by the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/frontbuffer.html#A145X9a0">frontbuffer</A></B>,
<B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/backbuffer.html#A145X94a">backbuffer</A></B>,
and <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/zdraw.html#A143X97f5">zdraw</A></B>
subroutines (see <A HREF="animatescene.html#A300X9c17">&quot;Double and Single
Buffering&quot;</A> and <A HREF="Z-Buffering.html">&quot;Z-Buffering&quot;</A>).
The syntax for the <B>rectwrite</B> and <B>lrectwrite</B> subroutines is
as follows: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A258C01c208"></A>Int32&nbsp;rectwrite(Screencoord&nbsp;xll,&nbsp;Screencoord&nbsp;yll,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Screencoord&nbsp;xur,&nbsp;Screencoord&nbsp;xur,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Int16&nbsp;*parray)</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A258C01c209"></A>Int32&nbsp;lrectwrite(Screencoord&nbsp;xll,&nbsp;Screencoord&nbsp;yll,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Screencoord&nbsp;xur,&nbsp;Screencoord&nbsp;xur,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Int32&nbsp;*parray)</PRE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52E250mhay"></A>Data is stored in the same order as in
the <B>rectread</B> subroutine. In other words, if you call the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/rectread.html#A142X9c7c">rectread</A></B>
subroutine and then the <B>rectwrite</B> (or <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/rectread.html#A142X9c7c">lrectread</A></B>
followed by <B>lrectwrite</B>) subroutine with the same parameters, exactly
the same data is written as is read. The <B>rectwrite</B> and <B>lrectwrite</B>
subroutines obey the zoom factors set by the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/rectzoom.html#A142X9d26">rectzoom</A></B>
subroutine. </P>


<H4><A NAME="A18C0dc79"></A>rectcopy Subroutine </H4>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52E277mhay"></A>The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/rectcopy.html#A142X9d04">rectcopy</A></B>
subroutine copies the pixels from a rectangular region of the screen to
a new region. As was the case with the <!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/rectread.html#A142X9c7c"><B>rectread</B>
and <B>lrectread</B></A> subroutines, the source rectangle must be on the
physical screen, but not necessarily constrained to the current window.
The bitplane source for the pixels is determined by the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/readsource.html#A142X9cc0">readsource</A></B>
subroutine, and the destination is determined by the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/frontbuffer.html#A145X9a0">frontbuffer</A></B>,
<B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/backbuffer.html#A145X94a">backbuffer</A></B>,
and <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/zdraw.html#A143X97f5">zdraw</A></B>
subroutines (see <A HREF="animatescene.html#A300X9c17">&quot;Double and Single
Buffering&quot;</A> and <A HREF="Z-Buffering.html">&quot;Z-Buffering&quot;</A>).
Self-intersecting rectangles work correctly in all cases. The syntax is
as follows: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A258C01c20b"></A>void&nbsp;rectcopy(Screencoord&nbsp;xll,&nbsp;Screencoord&nbsp;yll,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Screencoord&nbsp;xur,&nbsp;Screencoord&nbsp;xur,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Screencoord&nbsp;newx,&nbsp;Screencoord&nbsp;newy)</PRE>


<H4><A NAME="A19C0e0d3"></A>rectzoom Subroutine </H4>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52E306mhay"></A>With the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/rectcopy.html#A142X9d04">rectcopy</A></B>
subroutine, the source rectangle can be zoomed by independent amounts in
both the <I>x</I> and <I>y</I> directions. The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/rectzoom.html#A142X9d26">rectzoom</A></B>
subroutine accomplishes this, where its <I>xfactor</I> and <I>yfactor</I>
parameters are floating-point values defaulting to 1.0. The syntax is as
follows: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A258C01c20c"></A>void&nbsp;rectzoom(Float32&nbsp;xfactor,&nbsp;Float32&nbsp;yfactor)</PRE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52E331mhay"></A>The current system supports only integer
values for the <I>xfactor</I> and <I>yfactor</I> parameters. If <TT>rectzoom(2.0,&nbsp;3.0)</TT>
is called and the following rectangle is copied: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A18C0dc7c"></A>1&nbsp;&nbsp;2</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A18C0dc7d"></A>3&nbsp;&nbsp;4</PRE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52E356mhay"></A>the&nbsp;following&nbsp;copy&nbsp;is&nbsp;made:</P>


<PRE><A NAME="A18C0dc7f"></A>1&nbsp;&nbsp;1&nbsp;&nbsp;2&nbsp;&nbsp;2</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A18C0dc80"></A>1&nbsp;&nbsp;1&nbsp;&nbsp;2&nbsp;&nbsp;2</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A18C0dc81"></A>1&nbsp;&nbsp;1&nbsp;&nbsp;2&nbsp;&nbsp;2</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A18C0dc82"></A>3&nbsp;&nbsp;3&nbsp;&nbsp;4&nbsp;&nbsp;4</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A18C0dc83"></A>3&nbsp;&nbsp;3&nbsp;&nbsp;4&nbsp;&nbsp;4</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A18C0dc84"></A>3&nbsp;&nbsp;3&nbsp;&nbsp;4&nbsp;&nbsp;4</PRE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52E386mhay"></A>The following program, <TT>zoom</TT>,
magnifies the rectangular area above and to the right of the cursor to
fill the window: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A258C01c20e"></A>#include&nbsp;&lt;gl/gl.h&gt;
#include&nbsp;&lt;device.h&gt;</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A258C01c20f"></A>main()
{
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Int32&nbsp;xsize,&nbsp;ysize,&nbsp;readxsize,&nbsp;readysize,&nbsp;x,&nbsp;y;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Int32&nbsp;xorg,&nbsp;yorg;</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A258C01c210"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;winopen(&quot;zoom&quot;);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;getsize(&amp;xsize,&nbsp;&amp;ysize);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;getorigin(&amp;xorg,&nbsp;&amp;yorg);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;readxsize&nbsp;=&nbsp;xsize/3;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;readysize&nbsp;=&nbsp;ysize/3;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;rectzoom(3.0,&nbsp;3.0);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;while&nbsp;(1)&nbsp;{
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;x&nbsp;=&nbsp;getvaluator(MOUSEX);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;y&nbsp;=&nbsp;getvaluator(MOUSEY);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;rectcopy(x-xorg,y-yorg,x-xorg+readxsize,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;y-yorg+readysize,0,0);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;}
}</PRE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52E412mhay"></A>After determining the size and shape of
the window, the program simply loops, copying a properly sized rectangle
above and to the right of the cursor into the window magnified by a factor
of 3 in each direction. The expressions <TT>x-xorg</TT> and <TT>y-yorg</TT>
convert the cursor's <A HREF="specialterms.html#A27P017">screen
coordinates</A> into window coordinates. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52E436mhay"></A>If you use the previous program as it
is, note that regions of the screen drawn in 
<A HREF="specialterms.html#A26P0743">RGB
mode</A> appear incorrect, and color-mapped portions look fine. Also, notice
that with <A HREF="animatescene.html#A300X9c17">double-buffered</A> programs,
the zoom window appears to blink. This happens because the program is continually
switching buffers, while zoom is always reading the same buffer. If you
magnify the program's own window some fairly interesting effects can appear;
that is, a sort of recursion takes place. These effects are enhanced if
the zoom factor is set to (1.0,1.0). </P>


<H3><A NAME="A6DACA5410vbia"></A>Reading and Writing to Overlay Planes</H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52E461mhay"></A>To read from the overlay planes, set the
pixel source with readsource (SRC_OVER). The <B>rectread</B> subroutine
returns one pixel per short word; the <B>lrectread</B> subroutine returns
one pixel per long word. When reading, all other bits in the short or long
word are set to zero. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52E485mhay"></A>To write to the overlay planes, set drawmode
(OVERDRAW), and then use the <B>rectwrite</B> or <B>lrectwrite</B> subroutine.
Pixels must be specified one pixel per short word for the <B>rectwrite</B>
subroutine and one pixel per long word for the <B>lrectwrite</B> subroutine.
The pixel must lie in the lowest order bits of the short or long word.
All other bits in the short or long word are ignored during a write. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52E509mhay"></A>To copy from one location in the overlay
planes to another, specify readsource (SRC_OVER) and drawmode (OVERDRAW),
and then use the <B>rectcopy</B> subroutine. The <B>rectcopy</B> subroutine
does not support pixel block copies from the main frame buffer to the overlays,
or vice versa. To copy to or from the main frame buffer to or from the
overlays, adjust the <B>readsource</B> subroutine, use either the <B>rectread</B>
or <B>lrectread</B> subroutine, adjust the <B>drawmode</B> subroutine,
and then use either the <B>lrectwrite</B> or <B>rectwrite</B> subroutine.</P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52E532mhay"></A>The setting for pixmode (PM_SIZE) is ignored
when performing transfers to or from the overlay planes. </P>


<H3><A NAME="A48C013776"></A>Other Pixel Access Subroutines </H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52E557mhay"></A>The following GL subroutines provide other
types of access to pixel blocks: </P>


<H4><A NAME="nQA52c0marj"></A>readpixels Subroutine </H4>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52E583mhay"></A>The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/readpixels.html#A142X91059">readpixels</A></B>
subroutine returns values of specific pixels from the frame buffer in <A HREF="specialterms.html#A25P03e3">color
map mode.</A> It reads them into the array starting from the current character
position along a single scan line (constant <I>y</I>) in the direction
of increasing <I>x</I>. The syntax is as follows: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A258C01c212"></A>Int32&nbsp;readpixels(Int16&nbsp;number,&nbsp;Colorindex&nbsp;colors[])</PRE>


<H4><A NAME="JAA560marj"></A>readRGB Subroutine </H4>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52E611mhay"></A>The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/readRGB.html#A142X9107b">readRGB</A></B>
subroutine attempts to read specific pixel values from the frame buffer
in RGB mode. The returned value of this function is the number of pixels
actually read. A returned function value of 0 (zero) indicates that the
starting point is not a valid character position. </P>


<BLOCKQUOTE><P><A NAME="A48C013779"></A><B>Note: </B>The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/rectread.html#A142X9c7c">rectread</A></B>
subroutine provides significantly better performance for pixel block transfers.
Even when only one row of pixels needs to be read, use the <B>rectread</B>
subroutine. Do not use the <B>readpixels</B> or <B>readRGB </B>subroutines
in new development. </P></BLOCKQUOTE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52E635mhay"></A>The syntax is as follows: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A258C01c213"></A>Int32&nbsp;readRGB(Int16&nbsp;number,&nbsp;RGBvalue&nbsp;red[],&nbsp;RGBvalue&nbsp;green[],&nbsp;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;RGBvalue&nbsp;blue[])</PRE>


<H4><A NAME="ySB5360marj"></A>writepixels Subroutine </H4>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52E662mhay"></A>The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/writepixels.html#A142X9e62">writepixels</A></B>
subroutine paints a row of pixels on the screen in color map mode.The system
reads elements from the <I>colors</I> array and draws a pixel of the appropriate
color for each. The syntax is as follows: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A258C01c214"></A>void&nbsp;writepixels(Int16&nbsp;number,&nbsp;Colorindex&nbsp;colors[])</PRE>


<H4><A NAME="QTB5240marj"></A>writeRGB Subroutine </H4>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52E689mhay"></A>The <B>writeRGB</B> subroutine paints
a row of pixels on the screen in RGB mode. The system reads elements from
the <I>red</I>, <I>green</I>, and <I>blue</I> arrays and draws a pixel
of the appropriate color for each. </P>


<BLOCKQUOTE><P><A NAME="A48C01377c"></A><B>Note: </B>The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/rectwrite.html#A142X9c9e">rectwrite</A></B>
subroutine provides significantly better performance for pixel block transfers.
Even when only one row of pixels needs to be read, use the <B>rectwrite</B>
subroutine. Do not use the <B>writepixels </B>subroutine in new development.</P></BLOCKQUOTE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52E714mhay"></A>The syntax is as follows: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A258C01c215"></A>void&nbsp;writeRGB(Int16&nbsp;number,&nbsp;RGBvalue&nbsp;red[],&nbsp;RGBvalue&nbsp;green[],&nbsp;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;RGBvalue&nbsp;blue[])</PRE>




<P><A NAME="A3C0E52E738mhay"></A>Other topics affected by reading and writing
pixels are &quot;Creating <A HREF="textchars.html#textchars.html">Text Characters&quot;</A>
and &quot;Working in <A HREF="workcolor.html#workcolor.html">Color Map and RGB
Modes&quot;</A>. </P>




<hr><center>
```

## File: gl32prgd/scrmask.html
```html
<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">
<HTML>

<!--gl32prgd/scrmask.html Mon, 24 Jan 2022 16:28:07 GMT -->
<HEAD>
<META HTTP-EQUIV="Content-Type" CONTENT="text/html; charset=iso-8859-1">

   <TITLE>scrmask Subroutine
</TITLE>
   
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="getviewport.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="getscrmask.html">Next</a>  |
<A HREF="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html" TARGET="_parent">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 Version 4.1 for AIX: Programming Concepts</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>



<H2><A NAME="scrmask.html"></A>scrmask Subroutine </H2>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E9FE592mhay"></A>The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/scrmask.html#fwN250marj">scrmask</A></B>
subroutine specifies a two-dimensional rectangular clipping mask. The 
<A HREF="specialterms.html#A27P018">screenmask</A>
is specified in window coordinates. Every drawing primitive is clipped
to this area: that is, no drawing primitive can draw outside the screenmask.
The clipping performed by the screenmask is separate from and independent
of the 3-D clipping performed by the system. The syntax is as follows:</P>


<PRE><A NAME="A258C01c197"></A>void&nbsp;scrmask(Screencoord&nbsp;*left,&nbsp;Screencoord&nbsp;*right,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Screencoord&nbsp;*bottom,&nbsp;Screencoord&nbsp;*top)</PRE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E9FE613mhay"></A>Normally, the screenmask is precisely
the same size as the window. The screenmask cannot be made larger than
the window. When the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/viewport.html#qrY270marj">viewport</A></B>
subroutine is called, it resets the screenmask to be the same size as the
<A HREF="specialterms.html#A27P039">viewport</A>. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E9FE633mhay"></A>Although the <B>scrmask</B> subroutine
clips all primitives, it is not useful except for performing character
clipping. The 3-D clipping performed by the system is sufficient for all
other clipping. However, in reference to character strings, the 3-D clipping
mechanism only clips the origin of the character string. That is, if the
origin of the character string is inside the viewport, the entire string
would be drawn if the screenmask was not in effect. If the origin is outside
the viewport, none of the character string would be drawn, even if, logically,
some of the string ought to be visible. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E9FE653mhay"></A>This type of clipping is called 
<A HREF="specialterms.html#A26P0613">gross
clipping</A>. The screenmask is provided for 
<A HREF="specialterms.html#A26P0519">fine
clipping</A>, clipping down to a subcharacter level. To use it, set the
screenmask to be smaller than the viewport. Strings that begin inside the
viewport are drawn, but only starting at the character (or fraction of
the character) that lies inside the screenmask. Please refer to &quot;<A HREF="textchars.html#textchars.html">Creating
Text Characters</A>&quot; for more information. </P>




<hr><center>
[  <a href="getviewport.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="getscrmask.html">Next</a>  |
```

## File: gl32prgd/Selecting.html
```html
<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">
<HTML>

<!--gl32prgd/Selecting.html Mon, 24 Jan 2022 16:28:19 GMT -->
<HEAD>
<META HTTP-EQUIV="Content-Type" CONTENT="text/html; charset=iso-8859-1">

   <TITLE>Selecting
</TITLE>
   
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="Picking.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="underwininput.html">Next</a>  |
<A HREF="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html" TARGET="_parent">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 Version 4.1 for AIX: Programming Concepts</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>



<H2><A NAME="Selecting.html"></A>Selecting </H2>


<P><A NAME="INDEX762"></A><A NAME="INDEX763"></A><A NAME="INDEX764"></A><A NAME="INDEX765"></A></P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC61635mhay"></A>Selecting is much like picking, but is
more general. The same concept of hits is used, and the same name stack
manipulation routines apply. The returned data buffer is filled in the
same way. The only difference is in the way the selecting region is defined.</P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC61655mhay"></A>The selecting region corresponds to a
rhomboid in world coordinates. Any drawing primitive that intersects with
this rhomboid causes a hit and is recorded in the same manner as in picking.
There is no special call to set the selecting volume; instead, the matrix
manipulation routines are used. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC61675mhay"></A>Like picking, no actual drawing occurs
while the system is in select mode. Instead, all drawing primitives are
transformed through the geometry pipeline and compared to the canonical
3-D unit cube clipping volume. If the drawing primitive is inside this
volume, it causes a hit. If it is wholly outside, there is no hit recorded.
Transforming through the pipeline means that every drawing primitive is
run through the combination of the modeling, viewing, and projection transformations.
If, after these transformations, any portion of the primitive ends up inside
the volume -<I>w</I> &amp;le; <I>x</I>, <I>y</I>, <I>z</I> &amp;le; +<I>w</I>,
a hit has occurred. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC61695mhay"></A>To perform selecting, you must set up
your viewing/projection matrices correctly. You can set up the matrices
either immediately before or after a call to the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/gselect.html#A213X9118b2">gselect</A></B>
subroutine. The <B>gselect</B> subroutine, unlike the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/pick.html#h632f0nita">pick</A></B>
subroutine, does not alter the matrix stack. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC61715mhay"></A>In most applications, only the viewing
matrix is changed, not the projection matrix. The viewing matrix controls
what portion of the world space ends up inside the NDC unit cube (-<I>w</I>
&amp;le; <I>x</I>, <I>y</I>, <I>z</I> &amp;le; +<I>w</I>). Also, the individual
modeling routines are not changed because they only serve to embed individual
subportions of the drawing into the world coordinate frame. The usual process
is to draw the same primitives in the same places they previously occupied
while selecting is going on. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC61734mhay"></A>To end selecting mode, call the <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/endselect.html#A213X91190c">endselect</A></B>
subroutine. The returned data is in exactly the same format as for the
<B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/endpick.html#A213X91185b">endpick</A></B>
subroutine. </P>


<H3><A NAME="A15C0c69a"></A>gselect Subroutine </H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC61755mhay"></A>The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/gselect.html#A213X9118b2">gselect</A></B>
subroutine turns on the selection mode. The <B>gselect</B> and <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/pick.html#h632f0nita">pick</A></B>
subroutines are identical, except that the <B>gselect </B>subroutine is
more general. It allows you to define an arbitrary rhomboid in world coordinates
as the selecting region. The syntax is as follows: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A66C016c01"></A>void&nbsp;gselect(Int16&nbsp;buffer[],&nbsp;Int32&nbsp;numnames)</PRE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC61776mhay"></A>The <I>numnames</I> parameter specifies
the maximum number of values that the buffer can store. Each drawing routine
that intersects the selecting region causes a hit. The contents of the
name stack, preceded by the length of the name stack, are written into
the buffer only if this is the first hit since the last time that the name
stack was touched. The name stack is controlled in the same way as in picking.</P>


<H3><A NAME="A15C0c6a0"></A>endselect Subroutine </H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC61797mhay"></A>The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/endselect.html#A213X91190c">endselect</A></B>
subroutine takes the system out of selecting mode mode and returns the
number of times the name stack was dumped into the buffer. If this number
is positive, the buffer was large enough to contain all of the name stacks
written to it. If the number is negative, the buffer was too small to store
all the name lists. The magnitude of the returned number is the number
of name stacks that were recorded. The syntax is as follows: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A66C016c02"></A>Int32&nbsp;endselect(Int16&nbsp;buffer[])</PRE>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC61818mhay"></A>The <I>buffer</I> parameter contains copies
of the name stack that were recorded as hits occurred. As explained previously,
not every hit causes the name stack to be recorded; only the first hit
after the name stack has been touched is recorded. When stored in the buffer,
each name stack is preceded by the length of the name stack. If the name
stack is empty when a hit occurs, the length is recorded as 0 (zero), and
the stack is not recorded. </P>


<H3><A NAME="A258C01c0fc"></A>Selecting Example Program </H3>


<P><A NAME="A3C0EC61839mhay"></A>The following program demonstrates a simple
application of selecting. This program draws a planet and then draws a
box representing the ship each time the left mouse button is pressed. The
program prints <TT>CRASH</TT> and exits when the ship collides with the
planet: </P>


<PRE><A NAME="A65C01682a"></A>/***
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;crash.c&nbsp;-&nbsp;example&nbsp;of&nbsp;selecting
***/</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A65C01682b"></A>#include&nbsp;&lt;gl/gl.h&gt;
#include&nbsp;&lt;gl/device.h&gt;
#define&nbsp;BUFSIZE&nbsp;50
#define&nbsp;PLANET&nbsp;109
#define&nbsp;SHIPWIDTH&nbsp;20
#define&nbsp;SHIPHEIGHT&nbsp;10</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A65C01682c"></A>void
drawplanet()
{
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;circfi(200,&nbsp;200,&nbsp;20);
}</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A65C01682d"></A>int
main()
{
short&nbsp;dev,&nbsp;val;
short&nbsp;buffer[BUFSIZE];
int&nbsp;count,&nbsp;i;
float&nbsp;shipx,&nbsp;shipy,&nbsp;shipz;
int&nbsp;xorigin,&nbsp;yorigin;</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A65C01682e"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;minsize(300,&nbsp;300);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;(void)&nbsp;winopen(&quot;crash&quot;);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;getorigin(&amp;xorigin,&nbsp;&amp;yorigin);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;qdevice(LEFTMOUSE);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;qdevice(ESCKEY);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(BLACK);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;clear();</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A65C01682f"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;for&nbsp;(i&nbsp;=&nbsp;0;&nbsp;&nbsp;i&nbsp;&lt;&nbsp;BUFSIZE;&nbsp;&nbsp;i++)&nbsp;&nbsp;buffer[i]&nbsp;=&nbsp;0;</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A65C016830"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(RED);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;drawplanet();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;while&nbsp;(TRUE)&nbsp;&nbsp;{
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;dev&nbsp;=&nbsp;qread(&amp;val);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;switch&nbsp;(dev)&nbsp;&nbsp;{
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;case&nbsp;LEFTMOUSE:
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;if&nbsp;(val)&nbsp;&nbsp;{
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;shipz&nbsp;=&nbsp;0;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;shipx&nbsp;=&nbsp;getvaluator(MOUSEX)&nbsp;-&nbsp;xorigin;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;shipy&nbsp;=&nbsp;getvaluator(MOUSEY)&nbsp;-&nbsp;yorigin;</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A65C016831"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(BLUE);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;rect(shipx,&nbsp;shipy,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;shipx&nbsp;+&nbsp;SHIPWIDTH,&nbsp;shipy&nbsp;+&nbsp;SHIPHEIGHT);</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A65C016832"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;/*&nbsp;specify&nbsp;the&nbsp;selecting&nbsp;region&nbsp;to&nbsp;be&nbsp;a&nbsp;box
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;surrounding&nbsp;the&nbsp;rocket&nbsp;ship&nbsp;*/
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;pushmatrix();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;ortho2(shipx,&nbsp;shipx&nbsp;+&nbsp;SHIPWIDTH,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;shipy,&nbsp;shipy&nbsp;+&nbsp;SHIPHEIGHT);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;initnames();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;gselect(buffer,&nbsp;BUFSIZE);&nbsp;/*enter&nbsp;selecting&nbsp;mode*/
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;loadname(PLANET);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;drawplanet();&nbsp;/*&nbsp;no&nbsp;actual&nbsp;drawing&nbsp;takes&nbsp;place&nbsp;*/
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;count&nbsp;=&nbsp;endselect(buffer);&nbsp;/*&nbsp;exit&nbsp;select&nbsp;mode&nbsp;*/
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;popmatrix();</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A65C016833"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;/*&nbsp;check&nbsp;to&nbsp;see&nbsp;if&nbsp;PLANET&nbsp;was&nbsp;selected&nbsp;*/
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;if&nbsp;((count&nbsp;&gt;&nbsp;0)&nbsp;&amp;&amp;&nbsp;(buffer[0]&nbsp;==&nbsp;1)&nbsp;&amp;&amp;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;(buffer[1]&nbsp;==&nbsp;PLANET)&nbsp;&nbsp;)&nbsp;&nbsp;{
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;printf(&quot;CRASH!\n&quot;);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;}
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;}
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;break;</PRE>


<PRE><A NAME="A65C016834"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;case&nbsp;ESCKEY:
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;return&nbsp;0;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;break;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;}
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;}
}</PRE>




<hr><center>

<a href="underwininput.html">Next</a>  |
```

## File: gl32prgd/setglattrib.html
```html
<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">
<HTML>

<!--gl32prgd/setglattrib.html Mon, 24 Jan 2022 16:27:51 GMT -->
<HEAD>
<META HTTP-EQUIV="Content-Type" CONTENT="text/html; charset=iso-8859-1">

   <TITLE>Setting Drawing Attributes in GL
</TITLE>
   
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="move-draw.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="setglpipeops.html">Next</a>  |
<A HREF="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html" TARGET="_parent">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 Version 4.1 for AIX: Programming Concepts</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>


<H2><A NAME="setglattrib.html"></A>Setting Drawing Attributes </H2>


<P><A NAME="INDEX142"></A><A NAME="INDEX143"></A><A NAME="INDEX144"></A><A NAME="INDEX145"></A><A NAME="INDEX146"></A><A NAME="INDEX147"></A><A NAME="INDEX148"></A></P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52C824mhay"></A>GL contains subroutines designed to define
the attributes for drawing <A HREF="specialterms.html#A26P0702">primitives</A>.
These subroutines set the 
<A HREF="specialterms.html#A3C0F2A3323mhay">current color</A>
in either <A HREF="specialterms.html#A25P03e3">color map mode</A> or 
<A HREF="specialterms.html#A26P0743">RGB
mode</A>; the current linestyle, width, and color for line drawings; and
the current fill pattern for solid objects. The <B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/shademodel.html#A143X9ab9">shademodel</A></B>
subroutine sets the shading model for drawing shaded polygons. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52C848mhay"></A>You may want to read about the effects
of certain attributes in &quot;Creating <A HREF="crlighteff.html#crlighteff.html">Lighting
Effects&quot;</A> and in &quot;Working in <A HREF="workcolor.html#workcolor.html">Color
Map and RGB Modes&quot;</A>. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52C873mhay"></A>To read about the effects of certain attribute
subroutines, see Creating <A HREF="crlighteff.html#crlighteff.html">Lighting Effects</A>
in GL and Working in <A HREF="workcolor.html#workcolor.html">Color Map and RGB
Modes</A> in GL. </P>


<H3><A NAME="Uq31180marj"></A>List of GL Drawing Attribute Subroutines<A NAME="INDEX149"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX150"></A> <A NAME="INDEX151"></A> <A NAME="INDEX152"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX153"></A> <A NAME="INDEX154"></A> </H3>


<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A300X9bf1"></A><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/c.html#A143X9262">c</A></B></TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>


<TD>Sets the current color in RGB mode.</TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A300X9bf0"></A><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/color.html#A146X9429">color</A></B></TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>


<TD>Sets the current color in color map mode. </TD></TR>


<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP" COLSPAN="2"><A NAME="A300X9bef"></A><B><!--:libs:gl32tref:--><A HREF="../gl32tref/cpack.html#A143X9284">cpack</A></B></TD></TR>
```

```html
<hr size=3 noshade>


<H2><A NAME="setglpipeops.html"></A>Setting Pipeline Options </H2>


<P><A NAME="INDEX155"></A><A NAME="INDEX156"></A><A NAME="INDEX157"></A><A NAME="INDEX158"></A></P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52C911mhay"></A>Setting pipeline options is accomplished
by a group of subroutines that allows a programmer to turn off and on optional
tasks provided by the graphics pipeline. Turning off these tasks when they
are not needed speeds the rendering process. </P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52C936mhay"></A>You may want to read about the various
pipeline options in &quot;Creating <A HREF="crlighteff.html#crlighteff.html">Lighting
Effects</A>&quot;, &quot;Removing <A HREF="remhidden.html#remhidden.html">Hidden
Surfaces</A>&quot;, &quot;<A HREF="setglattrib.html#setglattrib.html">Setting Drawing
Attributes</A>&quot;, &quot;Working with <A HREF="workcoords.html#workcoords.html">Coordinate
Systems</A>&quot;, and &quot;Performing <A HREF="depth-cueing.html">Depth-Cueing</A>&quot;.</P>


<P><A NAME="A3C0E52C960mhay"></A>Various pipeline options are explained
in Creating <A HREF="crlighteff.html#crlighteff.html">Lighting Effects</A> in
GL, Performing <A HREF="depth-cueing.html">Depth-Cueing</A> in GL,
Removing <A HREF="remhidden.html#remhidden.html">Hidden Surfaces</A> in GL,
<A HREF="setglattrib.html#setglattrib.html">Setting Drawing Attributes</A> in GL,
and Working with <A HREF="workcoords.html#workcoords.html">Coordinate Systems</A>
in GL. </P>


<H3><A NAME="A264X931d"></A>List of GL Pipeline Option-Setting Subroutines<A NAME="INDEX159"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX160"></A> <A NAME="INDEX161"></A> <A NAME="INDEX162"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX163"></A> <A NAME="INDEX164"></A> </H3>
```

```html
<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">
<HTML>

<!--gl32prgd/SGIfiletrans.html Mon, 24 Jan 2022 16:28:21 GMT -->
<HEAD>
<META HTTP-EQUIV="Content-Type" CONTENT="text/html; charset=iso-8859-1">

<TITLE>SGI GL File Transfer Compiling and Linking
</TITLE>
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="portSGIapps.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="SGIperformance.html">Next</a>  |
<A HREF="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html" TARGET="_parent">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 Version 4.1 for AIX: Programming Concepts</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="SGIfiletrans.html"></A>SGI GL File Transfer Compiling and Linking</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX980" REL="I1" TITLE="GL environment"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX981" REL="I2" TITLE="SGI GL file transfer compiling, &amp; linking"></A>
<P><A NAME="A3C0F27A585mhay"></A>The Silicon Graphics workstations offered since1990 include: Personal IRIS, GT Graphics, POWERSeries 4D/200, and POWERSeries 4D/300. Data in each pair of bytes is restored in different order on these platforms than the order data is restored on your system. There are two ways to overcome this problem while transferring files:</P>

<OL><LI><A NAME="C1C7A5B901chuc"></A>Receive original archive files from the source platform, and swap bytes on the destination platform: 

<PRE><A NAME="C1C7A5B975chuc"></A>dd if=/dev/rmt0 conv=swab | tar -xf -</PRE></LI>

<LI><A NAME="C1C7A5C052chuc"></A>Use the nonswap tape device when writing tapes on SGI systems. This will write a QIC 150 format tape on an IRIS machine, which then can be read by your system.

<PRE><A NAME="C1C7A5C123chuc"></A>tar -cf/dev/rmt0/tps0d7ns</PRE></LI></OL>

<P><A NAME="A3C0F27A601mhay"></A>To code a C program in your GL environment, the related GL include files should be specified in the program.</P>
<PRE><A NAME="C1C7A5C268chuc"></A>#include &lt;gl/gl.h></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="C1C7A5C339chuc"></A>#include &lt;gl.device.h></PRE>

<P><A NAME="A3C0F27A623mhay"></A>Application programs from a source platform usually invoke unsupported and obsolete subroutines. The <B>glport.h</B> file is provided for those who do not wish to clean up these old interfaces. Include the following statements in the application to declare these old subroutines void:</P>
<PRE><A NAME="C1C7A5C491chuc"></A>#define _GL_PORT_C_ 1</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="C1C7A5C561chuc"></A>#include &lt;gl/glport.h></PRE>

<P><A NAME="A3C0F27A646mhay"></A><B>On SGI platforms, </B>GL is shipped in two libraries: <B>libgl.a</B> and <B>libgl_s.a</B>. Linking to the first library results in a static link to GKL subroutines: the code for the GL routines is placed directly in the application binary, swelling its size considerably. The second library is a shared library. Linking to it does not pull GL library code into the application binary; rather, the shared library is dynamically loaded when the application is run. This results in a smaller application binary and in decreased memory usage when multiple GL applications are running simultaneously.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3C0F27A666mhay"></A>On your platform, there is only one library, <B>libgl.a</B>. This library is a shared library by default. One must not link a GL application nonshared on your equipment. On newer SGI GL releases, GL applications must link to both <B>libgl.a</B> and <B>libX11.a</B>, even though X11 is not being used directly. This is not required on your platform; such linkage is performed automatically.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3C0F27A686mhay"></A>The following GL subroutines are no longer supported. The functions that they formerly accomplished are not applicable to the current system. They are considered obsolete and should not be used in new code development. As an aid to portability, stubs for these subroutines can be found in the <B>/usr/lpp/gl/examples/gifts/glports.h</B> file.</P>

<H3><A NAME="C1C7A5C788chuc"></A>Undefined Functions</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="C1C7A5C857chuc"></A><B>dbtext</B></TD>
<TD>  <B>endpupmode</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="C1C7A5C926chuc"></A><B>pupmode</B></TD>
<TD>  <B>setfastcom </B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="C1C7A5C993chuc"></A><B>setslowcom</B></TD>
<TD>  </TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="C1C7A5D064chuc"></A>Redefined Functions</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="C1C7A5D138chuc"></A><B>#define getdepth lgetdepth  </B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="C1C7A5D210chuc"></A><B>#define RGBrange IRGBrange</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="C1C7A5D281chuc"></A><B>#define setdepth lsetdepth </B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="C1C7A5D358chuc"></A>Functions Returning Only One Value</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="C1C7A5D426chuc"></A><B>endfeedback</B></TD>
<TD>  0   </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="C1C7A5D496chuc"></A><B>gethitcode</B></TD>
<TD>  0   </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="C1C7A5D565chuc"></A><B>ismex</B></TD>
<TD>  TRUE     </TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="C1C7A5D641chuc"></A>Functions Having Null Definitions</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="C1C7A5D711chuc"></A><B>clearhitcode</B></TD>
<TD>  devport  </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="C1C7A5D783chuc"></A><B>feedback</B></TD>
<TD>  foreground   </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="C1C7A5D853chuc"></A><B>getlsbackup</B></TD>
<TD>  getpor   </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="C1C7A5D922chuc"></A><B>getport</B></TD>
<TD>  getresetls  </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="C1C7A5D990chuc"></A><B>gettp</B></TD>
<TD>  gewrite   </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="C1C7A5E062chuc"></A><B>gRGBcursor</B></TD>
<TD>  imakebackground  </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="C1C7A5E132chuc"></A><B>lsbackup</B></TD>
<TD>  pagecolor  </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="C1C7A5E206chuc"></A><B>pagewritemask</B></TD>
<TD>  passthrough   </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="C1C7A5E275chuc"></A><B>resetls</B></TD>
<TD>  RGBcursor   </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="C1C7A5E345chuc"></A><B>setshade</B></TD>
<TD>  shaderange   </TD></TR>
```

```html
<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">
<HTML>

<!--gl32prgd/SGIperformance.html Mon, 24 Jan 2022 16:28:21 GMT -->
<HEAD>
<META HTTP-EQUIV="Content-Type" CONTENT="text/html; charset=iso-8859-1">

<TITLE>SGI GL Performance and System Environment Considerations
</TITLE>
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="SGIfiletrans.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="specialterms.html">Next</a>  |
<A HREF="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html" TARGET="_parent">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 Version 4.1 for AIX: Programming Concepts</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="SGIperformance.html"></A>SGI GL Performance and System Environment Considerations</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX982" REL="I1" TITLE="GL environment"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX983" REL="I2" TITLE="SGI GL performance and system environ. consid."></A>
<P><A NAME="A3C0F27A749mhay"></A><B>Your display subsystem architecture is designed to support a wide range of application programming interfaces (API), such as graPHIGS, X11, and </B>GL. Your GL subsystem is implemented in two pieces: GL windowing, input, and event queue functions are implemented as a module on top of <B>Xlib</B>; and GL drawing commands are sent directly to the graphics hardware. The internals of the 3D drawing subsystem are implemented in a high-performance, object-directed fashion, allowing GL applications to run transparently on different 3D graphics hardware without requiring recompilation or relinking. Additional information about your graphics subsystem architecture can be found in the Xhibition '91 Conference Proceedings (published by Integrated Computer Solutions, Inc. 201 Broadway, Cambridge MA 02139, xhibit@ics.com).</P>

<P><A NAME="A3C0F27A769mhay"></A>Performance characteristics of your GL implementation differs from the characteristics of the SGI GL implementation. Three system environments affect performance: the "raw" speed of the hardware, the software interface to the hardware, and the structure of application programs. Because some of your GL functions are supported by AIXwindows, these functions operate significantly slower in your GL, such as:</P>

<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="C1C8DA4441chuc"></A><B>mapcolor</B></TD>
<TD>  <B>getmcolor</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="C1C8DA4628chuc"></A><B>viewport</B></TD>
<TD>  <B>scrnmask</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="C1C8DA4842chuc"></A><B>curson</B></TD>
<TD>  <B>cursoff</B></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P><A NAME="A3C0F27A792mhay"></A>To avoid using the above functions excessively, use the following substitutions to improve the performance of your GL implementation:</P>

<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="C1C8DA5135chuc"></A><B>mapcolors</B></TD>
<TD>  <B>getmcolors</B></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P><A NAME="A3C0F27A813mhay"></A>Certain functions behave differently because of the operating system. The return of gversion is AIX GL Version 3.2 on your platform while it is GL4DPI-3.2 or GL4DPI2-3.2 on the SGI platform.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3C0F27A833mhay"></A>The drawmode (PUPDRAW) call redirects the <B>mapcolor</B> and <B>getcolor</B> subroutines to affect the pop-up menus. In AIX Version 3.1, GL pop-up menus were implemented as separate X11 windows, on top of <B>Xlib</B>. This design caused the pop-ups to generate excessive REDRAW events to GL applications. To solve this problem, GL pop-up menus were redesigned in AIX Version 3.2 to operate in the overlay planes, using GL rendering calls.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3C0F27A853mhay"></A>In Color Map Mode, the value stored in the standard bit planes is interpreted as an index into a color map. With GL (AIXwindows environment), the order of the lowest 8 values was modified to be more compatible with X11: black was placed in slot 0 and white in slot 1. To be portable, these colors should be accessed with the #define'd token names found in <SAMP>&lt;gl/gl.h></SAMP> and never directly through their numeric value. The following table shows the color map's color values:</P>

<TABLE BORDER="2"><TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>R</B></TD>

<TD><B>G</B></TD>

<TD><B>B</B></TD>

<TD><B>Color</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>0
</TD>

<TD>0
</TD>

<TD>0
</TD>

<TD>Black
</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>255
</TD>

<TD>0
</TD>

<TD>0
</TD>

<TD>Red
</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>0
</TD>

<TD>255
</TD>

<TD>0
</TD>

<TD>Green
</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>255
</TD>

<TD>255
</TD>

<TD>0
</TD>

<TD>Yellow
</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>0
</TD>

<TD>0
</TD>

<TD>255
</TD>

<TD>Blue
</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>255
</TD>

<TD>0
</TD>

<TD>255
</TD>

<TD>Magenta
</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>0
</TD>

<TD>255
</TD>

<TD>255
</TD>

<TD>Cyan
</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>255
</TD>

<TD>255
</TD>

<TD>255
</TD>

<TD>White
</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P><A NAME="A3C0F27A875mhay"></A>With the SGI GL, the lowest 8 values in the default color map are loaded in a different order. </P>

<P><A NAME="A3C0F27A895mhay"></A>The font management facilities provided by SGI as part of the operating system are not part of your GL. The SGI FontManager library provides a font management system that allows scaling and rotating of annotation text fonts. The default font for the Personal IRIS has not been licensed by your supplier. Programs must choose fonts from those provided by AIX and AIXwindows. To set default GL fonts for any programs inheriting the environment from a shell, execute the following: </P>
<PRE><A NAME="C1C8DA6991chuc"></A>GLFONT0=Rom10; export GLFONT0; glprog</PRE>

<P><A NAME="A3C0F27A917mhay"></A>All AIXwindows fonts are available for use in GL programs. Use the <B>XListFonts</B> call for an array of available font names, and then use <B>loadXfont</B> to load the specified font and return the font ID. Example programs demonstrating this usage can be found in <B>/usr/lpp/GL/examples</B>. With AIXwindows fonts available to your GL, most functions that are provided by SGI FontManager are satisfied.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3C0F27A937mhay"></A>In AIX Version 3.2, <B>Xlib</B> calls can be mixed with GL calls in the same application. The guidelines for doing this, and the routines that enable this, can be found in <A HREF="exhwindcalls.html#exhwindcalls.html">Using Enhanced X-Windows Calls with GL Subroutines</A><A HREF="exhwindcalls.html" REL="PAGENUM"></A>. Example programs demonstrating integration can be found in <B>/usr/lpp/GL/examples</B>.</P><hr><center>
[  <a href="SGIfiletrans.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="specialterms.html">Next</a>  |

</center></BODY>
```
