## File: gl32tref/addtopup.html
```html
<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">
<HTML>
<HEAD>
<META HTTP-EQUIV="Content-Type" CONTENT="text/html; charset=iso-8859-1">

<TITLE>addtopup Subroutine
</TITLE>
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="../gl32tref/frame1_toc.html#top_link">Previous</a>  |
<a href="arc.html">Next</a>  |
<A href="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A142X9109d"></A>addtopup Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX2" REL="I1" TITLE="addtopup subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX3" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX4" REL="I2" TITLE="popp menus"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX5" REL="I3" TITLE="adding items to existing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX6" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX7" REL="I2" TITLE="popp menu"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX8" REL="I3" TITLE="addtopup"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A142X9109f"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0362548ceb"></A>Adds items to an existing pop-up menu.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1110"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0362697ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0362800ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A142X910a3"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X91215a"></A><B>void addtopup</B>
<B>(Int32 </B><A HREF="addtopup.html#A213X91215f"><I>popup</I></A><B>,</B>
<B>Char8 *</B> <A HREF="addtopup.html#A213X912160"><I>string</I></A><B>,</B>
<B>Int32</B> <A HREF="addtopup.html#A213X912168"><I>argument</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010b4e"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0363069ceb"></A><B>SUBROUTINE ADDTOP(</B><A HREF="addtopup.html#A213X91215f"><I>popup</I></A><B>,</B> <A HREF="addtopup.html#A213X912160"><I>string</I></A><B>, </B><A HREF="addtopup.html#A142X910a8"><I>length</I></A><B>, </B><A HREF="addtopup.html#A213X912168"><I>argument</I></A><B>)</B></P>

<P><B>INTEGER*4</B> <I>popup</I></P>

<P><B>CHARACTER*(*)</B> <I>string</I><B>(*)</B></P>

<P><B>INTEGER*4</B> <I>length</I></P>

<P><B>INTEGER*4</B> <I>argument</I></P>

<H3><A NAME="A142X910a5"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0363226ceb"></A>The <B>addtopup </B>subroutine adds items to the bottom of an existing pop-up menu. You can build a menu by using a call to the <A HREF="newpup.html#A142X91125"><B>newpup</B></A> subroutine to create a menu, followed by a call to the <B>addtopup </B>subroutine for each menu item that you want to add to the menu. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0363333ceb"></A>To activate and display the menu, submit the menu to the <A HREF="dopup.html#A142X910e1"><B>dopup</B></A> subroutine. </P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9dda"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a display list.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A142X910a7"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X91215f"></A><I>popup</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the identifier of the menu to which to add. The menu identifier is the returned function value of the menu creation call to either the <A HREF="newpup.html#A142X91125"><B>newpup</B></A> or <A HREF="defpup.html#A142X910bf"><B>defpup</B></A> subroutines.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912160"></A><I>string</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the pointer to the text to add as a menu item. There are seven menu item type flags for optional pairing with each menu item: 


<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912161"></A><B>%t </B></TD>
<TD>  Marks item text as the menu title string. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912162"></A><B>%F </B></TD>
<TD>  Invokes a routine for every selection from this menu except those marked with a <B>%n</B> flag. You must specify the invoked routine in the <A HREF="addtopup.html#A213X912168"><I>argument</I></A> parameter. The value of the menu item is used as a parameter of the executed routine. Thus, if you select the third menu item, the system passes 3 as a parameter to the function specified by the <B>%F</B> flag. Produces unpredictable results in FORTRAN.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912163"></A><B>%f </B></TD>
<TD>  Invokes a routine when this particular menu item is selected. You must specify the invoked routine in the <A HREF="addtopup.html#A213X912168"><I>argument</I></A> parameter. The value of the menu item is passed as a parameter of the routine. Thus, if you select the third menu item, the system passes 3 as a parameter to the routine specified by the <B>%f</B> flag. If you have also used the<B> %F</B> flag within this menu, then the result of the <B>%f </B>flag is passed as a parameter of the <B>%F</B> flag. Produces unpredictable results in FORTRAN.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912164"></A><B>%l </B></TD>
<TD>  Adds a line under the current entry. This is useful in providing visual clues for grouping like entries together. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912165"></A><B>%m </B></TD>
<TD>  Pops up a menu whenever this menu item is selected. You must provide the menu identifier of the new menu in the <I>argument</I> parameter.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912166"></A><B>%n </B></TD>
<TD>  Like the <B>%f</B> flag, this flag invokes a routine when the user selects this menu item. However, the <B>%n</B> flag differs from the <B>%f</B> flag in that it ignores the routine (if any) specified by the <B>%F</B> flag. The value of the menu item is passed as a parameter of the executed routine. Thus, if you select the third menu item, the system passes 3 as a parameter to the function specified by the <B>%f</B> flag. Produces unpredictable results in FORTRAN.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912167"></A><B>%x</B><I>n </I></TD>
<TD>  Assigns a numeric value to this menu item. This value overrides the default position-based value assigned to this menu item (third item=3). You must enter the numeric value as the part of the text string specified by the <I>n</I> flag. Do not use the <A HREF="addtopup.html#A213X912168"><I>argument</I></A> parameter to specify the numeric value.</TD></TR></TABLE>



<BLOCKQUOTE><B>Notes: </B>
<OL><LI><A NAME="A139X91ed7"></A>With the <B>|</B> (vertical bar) delimiter, you can specify multiple menu items in a text string. However, because there is only one <A HREF="addtopup.html#A213X912168"><I>argument</I></A> parameter, the text string can contain no more than one item type that references the <I>argument</I> parameter. </LI>

<LI><A NAME="A108C1bc3"></A>In FORTRAN programming language, there is no pointer to a function. This restriction causes the <B>%f</B>, <B>%n</B>, and <B>%F</B> flags to produce unpredictable results.</LI></OL></BLOCKQUOTE>

</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A142X910a8"></A><I>length</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the length of the text string (for FORTRAN syntax).</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912168"></A><I>argument</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the command or submenu to assign to the menu item. There can be only one <I>argument</I> parameter for each call to the <B>addtopup</B> subroutine. </TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A64C0165b8"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0364406ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1113"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1114"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1115"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A258C01c6a0"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0364737ceb"></A>Defining a pop-up menu with the <A HREF="defpup.html#A142X910bf"><B>defpup</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0364853ceb"></A>Displaying a pop-up menu with the <A HREF="dopup.html#A142X910e1"><B>dopup</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0364984ceb"></A>Deallocating a pop-up menu and its data structures with the <A HREF="freepup.html#A142X91103"><B>freepup</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0365093ceb"></A>Allocating and initializing a structure for a new pop-up menu with the <A HREF="newpup.html#A142X91125"><B>newpup</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0365231ceb"></A>Enabling or disabling a given pop-up entry with the <A HREF="setpup.html#A5um1280marj"><B>setpup</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0365346ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A> and Creating and Managing <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/popupmenus.html#popupmenus.html">Pop-Up Menus</A>.</P><hr><center>
```

```html
<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">

<H2><A NAME="A114C19c9"></A>alias_back.c Example C Language Program</H2>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E961526ttay"></A>#include &lt;gl/gl.h>
#include &lt;gl/device.h>
#include &lt;stdlib.h>
#include &lt;math.h></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E962019ttay"></A>/* 
* This program illustrates the drawing of anti-aliased lines of
* multiple foreground colors on a monochrome background.
* 
* Note that this style of drawing is limited to precisely one
* background color. The number of foreground colors is also
* limited;
* the maximum number of foreground colors is
* one-sixteenth of the total number of colormap entries.
*
* The basic idea behind the algorithm is to divide the available
* bitplanes into two groups: those containing the foreground line
* colors, and those containing the antialiasing coverage
* information.  A color-ramp is loaded in the color map ranges
* corresponding to the coverage information.  The foreground line
* drawing colors can be arbitrary.
*
* Note that proper gamma correction is absolutely vital to
* getting antialiased lines that look truly smooth to the user.
* The gamma exponent depends on the monitor (specifically, on the
* type of phosphors) and therefore needs to be tuned to the model
* of the monitor.  */</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E962174ttay"></A>draw_fan()
{
  int i; /* draw fan */</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E962369ttay"></A>  for (i=0; i&lt;= 90; i+=10) {
    pushmatrix();
    rot (-(float) i, 'z');
    move (0.0, 0.0, 0.0);
    draw (0.0, 200.0, 0.0);
    popmatrix();
  }</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E962513ttay"></A>}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E962689ttay"></A>#define AABLACK  0
#define AAGREEN  16
#define AARED    32
#define AAPURPLE 48
#define AAWHITE  64</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E962854ttay"></A>/* experimentally determined gamma factor */
double gammy = 2.4;</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E963373ttay"></A>/* a utility macro used to build the color ramp */
#define ADD_TO_RAMP(COL)                                                \ 
{                                                                       \ 
   for (j=0; j&lt;16; j++) {                                               \ 
      col_idx = COL + j;                                                \ 
      rramp[col_idx] = (j*foreground_r + (16-j)*background_r) / 16;     \ 
      gramp[col_idx] = (j*foreground_g + (16-j)*background_g) / 16;     \ 
      bramp[col_idx] = (j*foreground_b + (16-j)*background_b) / 16;     \ 
      rramp[col_idx] = (int)                                            \ 
        (255.0 * pow (((double) rramp[col_idx])/255.0 , 1.0 / gammy));  \ 
      gramp[col_idx] = (int)                              \ 
        (255.0 * pow (((double) gramp[col_idx])/255.0 , 1.0 / gammy));  \ 
      bramp[col_idx] = (int)                                            \ 
        (255.0 * pow (((double) bramp[col_idx])/255.0 , 1.0 / gammy));  \ 
   }                                                                    \ 
}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E963651ttay"></A>/* This routine creates an "random" color ramp and loads it */
void load_background_cmap (short background_r,
short background_g,
short background_b)
{
  int i, j, col_idx;
  int foreground_r, foreground_g, foreground_b;
  short rramp[256], gramp[256], bramp[256];
    /* update gamma correction factor */
  if (getbutton (WKEY)) gammy +=0.02;
  if (getbutton (SKEY)) gammy -=0.02;</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E963801ttay"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;/* create color ramp */</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E964143ttay"></A>  /* AABLACK */
  foreground_r = 0;
  foreground_g = 0;
  foreground_b = 0;
  ADD_TO_RAMP (AABLACK); /* AAGREEN */
  foreground_r = 0;
  foreground_g = 255;
  foreground_b = 0;
  ADD_TO_RAMP (AAGREEN); /* AARED */
  foreground_r = 255;
  foreground_g = 127;
  foreground_b = 0;
  ADD_TO_RAMP (AARED); /* AAPURPLE */
  foreground_r = 150;
  foreground_g = 25;
  foreground_b = 120;
  ADD_TO_RAMP (AAPURPLE); /* AAWHITE */
  foreground_r = 225;
  foreground_g = 235;
  foreground_b = 255;
  ADD_TO_RAMP (AAWHITE);
  mapcolors (0, 127, rramp, gramp, bramp);
}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E964302ttay"></A>#define RRRANDO ( (float) (400*rand()/32767))</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E964479ttay"></A>/* This routine draws a background of random polygons.
 * One of five colors are selected randomly.  */</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E964634ttay"></A>void draw_foreground()
{
  int i, j;</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E964860ttay"></A>  color (AABLACK);
  clear();
  linesmooth(TRUE);
  translate (-100.0, -100.0, 0.0);
  for (j=0; j&lt;9; j++) {
    color (16*(5*rand()/32767));
    pushmatrix();
    translate ( RRRANDO, RRRANDO, 0.0);
    draw_fan();
    popmatrix();
  }</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E965003ttay"></A>}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E965162ttay"></A>main ()
{
  int i, j, k, iinc=1, jinc=3, kinc=7;</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E965509ttay"></A>  prefsize (400.0, 400.0);
  winopen ("antialiased lines");
  cmode();
  singlebuffer();
  gconfig();
  save_cmap();
  /* create the color ramp--the background color will be black */
  load_background_cmap (0, 0, 0);
  /* draw multicolored line drawing */
  draw_foreground();
  /* loop until the right mouse button is depressed */
  while (!getbutton(RIGHTMOUSE) &amp;&amp; !getbutton(ESCKEY)) {
    /* cycle through a random set of background colors */
    i+=iinc;
    j+=jinc;
    k+=kinc;
    if ((i+iinc>5*255) || (i+iinc&lt;0)) {
      iinc = -iinc;
      i+=iinc;
    }</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E965678ttay"></A>    if ((j+jinc>5*255) || (j+jinc&lt;0)) {
      jinc = -jinc;
      j+=jinc;
    }</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E965848ttay"></A>    if ((k+kinc>5*255) || (k+kinc&lt;0)) {
      kinc = -kinc;
      k+=kinc;
    }</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E966028ttay"></A>    if ( i%5 == 0) {
      load_background_cmap ( (i/5)%255, (j/5)%255,(k/5)%255);
    }
  }
  restore_cmap();</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E966170ttay"></A>}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E966347ttay"></A>/*This saves the colormap*/
#define lo_end 0
#define hi_end 255
short *CarrayR, *CarrayG, *CarrayB;</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E966545ttay"></A>save_cmap()
{
  CarrayR = calloc (lo_end+hi_end,sizeof(short));
  CarrayG = calloc (lo_end+hi_end,sizeof(short));
  CarrayB = calloc (lo_end+hi_end,sizeof(short));</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E966719ttay"></A>  getmcolors ((Int16 const)lo_end,(Int16 const)hi_end,
     CarrayR, CarrayG, CarrayB);
}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E966907ttay"></A>/*This restores the colormap*/
restore_cmap()
{
  mapcolors ((Int16 const)lo_end,(Int16 const)hi_end,
     CarrayR, CarrayG, CarrayB);
}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E967090ttay"></A>/*
  Changes:
    -  Added the restoring of the colormap
    -  Added escape key and right mouse exiting cleanly
*/</PRE>
```

```html
<PRE><A NAME="A64E980702ttay"></A>/* 
* This program illustrates the drawing of antialiased lines, of
* multiple foreground colors, on an arbitrary multi-colored

*
* Note that this style of drawing is limited as to the number
* of foreground and background colors. The total number of
* colors is one-sixteenth of the total number of color map
* entries.
* 
* The basic idea behind the algorithm is to divide the
* available bitplanes into three groups: those containing
* the background image, those containing the foreground line
* colors and those containing the antialiasing coverage
* information. Color ramps are loaded in the color map ranges
* corresponding to the coverage information. The color ramps
* must blend between all possible foreground and all possible
* background colors.
*
* Note that proper gamma correction is absolutely vital to 
* getting antialiased lines that look truly smooth to the user.
* The gamma exponent depends on the monitor (specifically, on
* the type of phosphors) and therefore needs to be tuned to the
* model of the monitor.
* 
* Antialiased lines are supported on the 8 and 24 bit 3D adapters.
* Colormode antialiased lines is not supported on the
* High Speed Graphics Adapter.
*/ </PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E980860ttay"></A>draw_fan()
{
  /* draw fan */
  
  int i;</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E981054ttay"></A>  for (i=0; i&lt;= 90; i+=10) {

<PRE><A NAME="A64E982055ttay"></A>/* a utility macro used to build the color ramp */

     gramp[col_idx] = (j*fore_g + (16-j)*back_g) / 16;    \ 
     bramp[col_idx] = (j*fore_b + (16-j)*back_b) / 16;    \ 
     corr = 255.0 * pow (((double) rramp[col_idx])/255.0, \ 
       1.0/gammy);                                        \ 
     rramp[col_idx] = (int) corr;                         \ 
     corr = 255.0 * pow (((double) gramp[col_idx])/255.0, \

     bramp[col_idx] = (int) corr;                         \ 
  }                                                       \ 
}</PRE>
```

```html
<PRE><A NAME="A64E970084ttay"></A>/*

 * background.

 * Note that this style of drawing is limited to precisely one

 * The basic idea behind the algorithm is to divide the available

 * image, and those containing the anti-aliasing coverage
 * information.  A color-ramp is loaded in the color map ranges
 * corresponding to the coverage information.  The background
 * image colors can be arbitrary.
 *
 * Note that proper gamma correction is absolutely vital to
 * getting antialiased lines that look truly smooth to the user.
 * The gamma exponent depends on the monitor (specifically, on the 
 * type of phosphors) and therefore needs to be tuned to the model
 * of the monitor.
 */</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E970240ttay"></A>draw_fan()
{
  int i;   /* draw fan */</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E970435ttay"></A>  for (i=0; i&lt;= 90; i+=10) {
    pushmatrix();
    rot (-(float) i, 'z');
    move (0.0, 0.0, 0.0);
    draw (0.0, 300.0, 0.0);
    popmatrix();
  }</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E970577ttay"></A>}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E970753ttay"></A>#define AABLACK  0
#define AAGREEN  16
#define AARED    32
#define AAPURPLE 48
#define AAWHITE  64</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E970917ttay"></A>/* experimentally determined gamma factor */
double gammy = 2.4;</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E973271ttay"></A>/* a utility macro used to build the color ramp */
#define ADD_TO_RAMP(COL)                                                 \ 
{                                                                        \ 
   for (j=0; j&lt;16; j++) {                                                \ 
      col_idx = COL + j;                                                 \ 
      rramp[col_idx] = (j*foreground_r + (16-j)*background_r) / 16;      \ 
      gramp[col_idx] = (j*foreground_g + (16-j)*background_g) / 16;      \ 
      bramp[col_idx] = (j*foreground_b + (16-j)*background_b) / 16;      \ 
      rramp[col_idx] = (int)                                             \ 
         (255.0 * pow (((double) rramp[col_idx])/255.0 , 1.0 / gammy));  \ 
      gramp[col_idx] = (int)                                             \ 
         (255.0 * pow (((double) gramp[col_idx])/255.0 , 1.0 / gammy));  \ 
      bramp[col_idx] = (int)                                             \ 
         (255.0 * pow (((double) bramp[col_idx])/255.0 , 1.0 / gammy));  \ 
   }                                                                     \ 
}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E973505ttay"></A>/* this routine creates an "random" color ramp and loads it */
void load_foreground_cmap (short foreground_r,
short foreground_g,
short foreground_b)
{
  int i, j, col_idx;
  int background_r, background_g, background_b;
  short rramp[256], gramp[256], bramp[256];</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E973687ttay"></A>    /* update gamma correction factor */
  if (getbutton (WKEY)) gammy +=0.02;
  if (getbutton (SKEY)) gammy -=0.02;</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E974077ttay"></A>    /* create color ramp */
  /* AABLACK */
  background_r = 0;
  background_g = 0;
  background_b = 0;
  ADD_TO_RAMP (AABLACK);   /* AAGREEN */
  background_r = 0;
  background_g = 255;
  background_b = 0;
  ADD_TO_RAMP (AAGREEN);   /* AARED */
  background_r = 255;
  background_g = 127;
  background_b = 0;
  ADD_TO_RAMP (AARED);   /* AAPURPLE */
  background_r = 150;
  background_g = 25;
  background_b = 120;
  ADD_TO_RAMP (AAPURPLE);   /* AAWHITE */
  background_r = 225;
  background_g = 235;
  background_b = 255;
  ADD_TO_RAMP (AAWHITE);
  mapcolors (0, 127, rramp, gramp, bramp);
}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E974236ttay"></A>#define RRRANDO ( (float) (400*rand()/32767));</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E974449ttay"></A>/* This routine draws a background of random polygons. 
 * One of five colors are selected randomly.  */
void draw_background() {
  float vv[2];
  int i, j;
  srand (234515);
  color (AABLACK);
  clear();</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E974693ttay"></A>    /* the writemask guarentees that drawing is occuring only
     * into the "background" bitplanes */
  writemask (0xf0);
  for (j=0; j&lt;12; j++) {
    color (16*(5*rand()/32767));
    bgnpolygon();
    for (i=0; i&lt;6; i++) {
      vv[0] = RRRANDO;
      vv[1] = RRRANDO;
      v2f (vv);
    }</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E974843ttay"></A>    endpolygon();
  }</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E974985ttay"></A>}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E975144ttay"></A>main ()
{
  int i, j, k, iinc=1, jinc=3, kinc=7;</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E975322ttay"></A>  prefsize (400.0, 400.0);
  winopen ("antialiased lines");
  cmode();
  doublebuffer();
  gconfig();</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E975540ttay"></A>  save_cmap();
  /* create the color ramp --- the foreground color will be white */
  load_foreground_cmap (255, 255, 255);
    /* draw the random background */
  draw_background();
  swapbuffers ();
  draw_background();</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E975850ttay"></A>    /* the writemask write-protects the background while the lines 
     * are being drawn */
  writemask (0x0f);
    /* loop until the right mouse button is depressed */
  while (!getbutton(RIGHTMOUSE) &amp;&amp; !getbutton(ESCKEY)) {
    color (0);
    clear ();
    pushmatrix();
      /* draw normal, jaggy lines */
    linesmooth(FALSE);
    color (15);
    pushmatrix();
    translate (10.0, 10.0, 0.0);
    rotate( 500-getvaluator (MOUSEY), 'z');
    draw_fan();
    popmatrix();</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E976137ttay"></A>      /* draw smooth, anti-aliased lines */
    linesmooth(TRUE);
    pushmatrix();
    translate (390.0, 30.0, 0.0);
    rotate( getvaluator (MOUSEY) + 400, 'z');
    draw_fan();
    popmatrix();
    popmatrix();
    swapbuffers();
      /* cycle through a random set of foreground colors */
    i+=iinc;
    j+=jinc;
    k+=kinc;
    if ((i+iinc>5*255) || (i+iinc&lt;0)) {
      iinc = -iinc;
      i+=iinc;
    }</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E976307ttay"></A>    if ((j+jinc>5*255) || (j+jinc&lt;0)) {
      jinc = -jinc;
      j+=jinc;
    }</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E976478ttay"></A>    if ((k+kinc>5*255) || (k+kinc&lt;0)) {
      kinc = -kinc;
      k+=kinc;
    }</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E976659ttay"></A>    if ( i%5 == 0) {
      load_foreground_cmap ( (i/5)%255, (j/5)%255,  (k/5)%255);
    }
  }
  restore_cmap();</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E976801ttay"></A>}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E976977ttay"></A>/*This saves the colormap*/
#define lo_end 0
#define hi_end 255
short *CarrayR, *CarrayG, *CarrayB;</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E977175ttay"></A>save_cmap()
{
  CarrayR = calloc (lo_end+hi_end,sizeof(short));
  CarrayG = calloc (lo_end+hi_end,sizeof(short));
  CarrayB = calloc (lo_end+hi_end,sizeof(short));</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E977349ttay"></A>  getmcolors ((Int16 const)lo_end,(Int16 const)hi_end,
     CarrayR, CarrayG, CarrayB);
}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E977578ttay"></A>/*This restores the colormap*/
restore_cmap()
{
  mapcolors ((Int16 const)lo_end,(Int16 const)hi_end,
     CarrayR, CarrayG, CarrayB);
}
/*
  Changes:
    -  Added the restoring of the colormap
    -  Added escape key and right mouse for clean exit
*/</PRE>
```

```html
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="tEp310nita"></A>arc Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX9" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX10" REL="I2" TITLE="high-level drawing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX11" REL="I3" TITLE="arc"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX12" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX13" REL="I2" TITLE="arc"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX14" REL="I3" TITLE="circular"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX15" REL="I1" TITLE="arc subroutine (GL)"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A213X911581"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0385361ceb"></A>Draws a circular arc.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C124f"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0385509ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0385616ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="Az140nita"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A3L1180nita"></A><B>void arc</B>
<B>(Coord </B><A HREF="arc.html#mop40nita"><I>x</I></A><B>, Coord </B><A HREF="arc.html#jpp140nita"><I>y</I></A><B>, Coord </B><A HREF="arc.html#hqp280nita"><I>radius</I></A><B>, </B>
<B>Angle </B><A HREF="arc.html#Rrp360nita"><I>startang</I></A><B>, Angle </B><A HREF="arc.html#trpa0nita"><I>endang</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="IL1nita"></A><B>void arci</B>
<B>(Icoord </B><A HREF="arc.html#mop40nita"><I>x</I></A><B>, Icoord </B><A HREF="arc.html#jpp140nita"><I>y</I></A><B>, Icoord </B><A HREF="arc.html#hqp280nita"><I>radius</I></A><B>, </B>
<B>Angle </B><A HREF="arc.html#Rrp360nita"><I>startang</I></A><B>, Angle </B><A HREF="arc.html#trpa0nita"><I>endang</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="WL160nita"></A><B>void arcs</B>
<B>(Scoord </B><A HREF="arc.html#mop40nita"><I>x</I></A><B>, Scoord </B><A HREF="arc.html#jpp140nita"><I>y</I></A><B>, Scoord </B><A HREF="arc.html#hqp280nita"><I>radius</I></A><B>, </B>
<B>Angle </B><A HREF="arc.html#Rrp360nita"><I>startang</I></A><B>, Angle </B><A HREF="arc.html#trpa0nita"><I>endang</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911561"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X911564"></A><B>SUBROUTINE ARC(</B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>, </B><I>radius</I><B>, </B><I>startang</I><B>, </B><I>endang</I><B>)</B>
<B>REAL </B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>, </B><I>radius</I>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>startang</I><B>, </B><I>endang</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A28C010734"></A><B>SUBROUTINE ARCI(</B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>, </B><I>radius</I><B>, </B><I>startang</I><B>, </B><I>endang</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>, </B><I>radius</I><B>,</B><I> startang</I><B>, </B><I>endang</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A28C010737"></A><B>SUBROUTINE ARCS(</B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>, </B><I>radius</I><B>, </B><I>startang</I><B>, </B><I>endang</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*2 </B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>, </B><I>radius</I><B>,</B><I> startang</I><B>, </B><I>endang</I></PRE>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A78C1252"></A><B>Note: </B>For FORTRAN users, this subroutine accepts long integer parameters (INTEGER*4) when invoked from a FORTRAN program, although it accepts short integers when invoked from a C program. The C and FORTRAN syntax shown here reflect this difference. Also, the FORTRAN INTEGER*2 version, the <B>ARCS</B> subroutine, should not be called with integer constant parameters. For example, 2 is an integer constant; JJ is an integer variable. The XL FORTRAN compiler, invoked by the <B>xlf</B> command, stores all integer constants as long integers (INTEGER*4), not as short integers (INTEGER*2). Invoking the short version of this subroutine with an integer constant will result in unexpected behavior.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A213X911589"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0386274ceb"></A>The <B>arc</B> subroutine draws a circular arc in the x-y plane (z = 0), using the current line attributes: 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A31996bc">color</A>, 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A172P1436">linestyle</A>, 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A172P1437">linewidth</A> and 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A3C0F2A4599mhay">writemask</A>. To draw an arc in a plane other than the x-y plane, define the arc in the x-y plane and then rotate or translate the arc.  </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0386382ceb"></A>All of the routines listed in the syntax are functionally the same. They differ only in the type declarations for the coordinates. After the <B>arc</B> subroutine executes, the graphics position is left undefined.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0386490ceb"></A>The syntax for each of the subroutine forms is the same except for the first argument.  They differ only in that <A HREF="arc.html#A3L1180nita"><B>arc</B></A> expects real coordinates, <A HREF="arc.html#IL1nita"><B>arci</B></A> expects integer coordinates, and <A HREF="arc.html#WL160nita"><B>arcs</B></A> expects short integer coordinates. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X91158e"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="mop40nita"></A><I>x</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>x </I>coordinate of the center of the arc, which is the center of the circle that would contain the arc.    </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="jpp140nita"></A><I>y</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>y </I>coordinate of the center of the arc, which is the center of the circle that would contain the arc.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="hqp280nita"></A><I>radius</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the length of the radius of the arc, which is the radius of the circle that would contain the arc. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="Rrp360nita"></A><I>startang</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the measure of the start angle of the arc, which is measured in tenths of a degree from the positive x-axis.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="trpa0nita"></A><I>endang</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the measure of the end angle of the arc, which is measured in tenths of a degree from the positive x-axis.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911590"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0386981ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="tpbig_c.html#A16C0c9bd"><B>tpbig.c</B></A> uses the <B>arc</B> subroutine and the <B>arci </B>subroutine to draw two circular arcs in the default linestyle. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015ccc"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0387146ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C1253"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C1254"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C1255"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A258C01c546"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0387466ceb"></A>Drawing a filled circular arc with the <A HREF="arcf.html#AJp60nita"><B>arcf</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0387575ceb"></A>Drawing a circle with the <A HREF="circ.html#ZJpnita"><B>circ</B></A> subroutine. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0387688ceb"></A>Drawing a filled circle with the <A HREF="circf.html#sJp120nita"><B>circf</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0387794ceb"></A>Drawing a curve with the <A HREF="crv.html#ZMS220marj"><B>crv</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0387905ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A>, <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/setglattrib.html#setglattrib.html">Setting Drawing Attributes</A>, and <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawpoly.html#drawpoly.html">Drawing Rectangles, Circles, Arcs, and Polygons</A>.</P><hr><center>
```

```html
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="AJp60nita"></A>arcf Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX16" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX17" REL="I2" TITLE="high-level drawing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX18" REL="I3" TITLE="arcf"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX19" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX20" REL="I2" TITLE="arc"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX21" REL="I3" TITLE="filled circular"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX22" REL="I1" TITLE="arcf subroutine (GL)"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A213X9115cd"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B03A9206ceb"></A>Draws a filled, pie-slice-shaped, circular arc.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C1256"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B03A9361ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B03A9481ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X9115d0"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X9115d1"></A><B>void arcf</B>
<B>(Coord </B><A HREF="arcf.html#A213X9115df"><I>x</I></A><B>, Coord</B> <A HREF="arcf.html#A213X9115e0"><I>y</I></A><B>, Coord</B> <A HREF="arcf.html#A213X9115e1"><I>radius</I></A><B>,</B>
<B>Angle</B> <A HREF="arcf.html#A213X9115e2"><I>startang</I></A><B>, Angle</B> <A HREF="arcf.html#A213X9115e4"><I>endang</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X9115d2"></A><B>void arcfi</B>
<B>(Icoord </B><A HREF="arcf.html#A213X9115df"><I>x</I></A><B>, Icoord</B> <A HREF="arcf.html#A213X9115e0"><I>y</I></A><B>, Icoord</B> <A HREF="arcf.html#A213X9115e1"><I>radius</I></A><B>,</B>
<B>Angle</B> <A HREF="arcf.html#A213X9115e2"><I>startang</I></A><B>, Angle</B> <A HREF="arcf.html#A213X9115e4"><I>endang</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X9115d3"></A><B>void arcfs</B>
<B>(Scoord </B><A HREF="arcf.html#A213X9115df"><I>x</I></A><B>, Scoord</B> <A HREF="arcf.html#A213X9115e0"><I>y</I></A><B>, Scoord</B> <A HREF="arcf.html#A213X9115e1"><I>radius</I></A><B>,</B>
<B>Angle</B> <A HREF="arcf.html#A213X9115e2"><I>startang</I></A><B>, Angle</B> <A HREF="arcf.html#A213X9115e4"><I>endang</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X9115ab"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X9115ae"></A><B>SUBROUTINE ARCF(</B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>, </B><I>radius</I><B>, </B><I>startang</I><B>, </B><I>endang</I><B>)</B>
<B>REAL </B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>, </B><I>radius</I>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>startang</I><B>, </B><I>endang</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A28C01073c"></A><B>SUBROUTINE ARCFI(</B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>, </B><I>radius</I><B>, </B><I>startang</I><B>, </B><I>endang</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>, </B><I>radius</I><B>,</B><I> startang</I><B>, </B><I>endang</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A28C01073f"></A><B>SUBROUTINE ARCFS(</B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>, </B><I>radius</I><B>, </B><I>startang</I><B>, </B><I>endang</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*2 </B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>, </B><I>radius</I><B>,</B><I> startang</I><B>, </B><I>endang</I></PRE>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A78C1259"></A><B>Note: </B>For FORTRAN users, this subroutine accepts long integer parameters (INTEGER*4) when invoked from a FORTRAN program, although it accepts short integers when invoked from a C program. The C and FORTRAN syntax shown here reflect this difference. Also, the FORTRAN INTEGER*2 version, the <B>ARCFS</B> subroutine, should not be called with integer constant parameters. For example, 2 is an integer constant; JJ is an integer variable. The XL FORTRAN compiler, invoked by the <B>xlf</B> command, stores all integer constants as long integers (INTEGER*4), not as short integers (INTEGER*2). Invoking the short version of this subroutine with an integer constant will result in unexpected behavior.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A213X9115d8"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B03AA143ceb"></A>The <B>arcf</B> subroutine draws a circular filled arc in the <I>x</I>-<I>y </I>plane (<I>z </I>= <I>0</I>) and fills the arc with the current 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A13791abd">pattern</A>. The filled area is bounded by the arc and by the start and end radii. The subroutine uses the current area attributes: 
 <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A27P020">texture</A>, 
 <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A31996bc">color</A>, and 
 <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A3C0F2A4599mhay">writemask</A>. To draw a filled arc in a plane other than the <I>x</I>-<I>y </I>plane, define the filled arc in the <I>x</I>-<I>y </I>plane and then rotate or translate the arc.  </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B03AA251ceb"></A>The syntax for each of the subroutine forms is the same except for the first argument.  They differ only in that the <A HREF="arcf.html#A213X9115d1"><B>arcf</B></A> subroutine expects real coordinates for the first argument, the <A HREF="arcf.html#A213X9115d2"><B>arcfi</B></A> subroutine expects integer coordinates, and the <A HREF="arcf.html#A213X9115d3"><B>arcfs</B></A> subroutine expects short integer coordinates.  After the <B>arcf</B> subroutine executes, the graphics position is undefined.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X9115de"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X9115df"></A><I>x</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>x </I>coordinate of the center of the filled arc, which is the center of the circle that would contain the arc.    </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X9115e0"></A><I>y</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>y </I>coordinate of the center of the filled arc, which is the center of the circle that would contain the arc.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X9115e1"></A><I>radius</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the length of the radius of the filled arc, which is the radius of the circle that would contain the arc. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X9115e2"></A><I>startang</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the measure of the start angle of the filled arc, which is measured from the positive x-axis.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X9115e4"></A><I>endang</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the measure of the end angle of the filled arc, which is measured from the positive x-axis.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X9115e7"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B03AA817ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="tpbig_c.html#A16C0c9bd"><B>tpbig.c</B></A> uses the <B>arcfi</B> subroutine to draw a scoop of ice cream. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015cce"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B03AB008ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C125a"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C125b"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C125c"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A258C01c54a"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B03AB334ceb"></A>Drawing a circular arc with the <A HREF="arc.html#tEp310nita"><B>arc</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B03AB457ceb"></A>Drawing a circle with the <A HREF="circ.html#ZJpnita"><B>circ</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B03AB563ceb"></A>Drawing a filled circle with the <A HREF="circf.html#sJp120nita"><B>circf</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B03AB669ceb"></A>Drawing a curve with the <A HREF="crv.html#ZMS220marj"><B>crv</B></A> subroutine.</P>
```

```html
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A71D6F2375csol"></A>attachcursor Subroutine </H2>
<H3><A NAME="A71D6F2542csol"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B03D0056ceb"></A>Couples cursor position to valuator device.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A71D6F2939csol"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B03D0219ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B03D0328ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A71D6F3459csol"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A71D6F3696csol"></A><B>void attachcursor (</B><I>Device vx</I>, <I>Device vy</I><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A71D6F3882csol"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A71D6F4063csol"></A><B>SUBROUTINE ATTACH (</B><I>vx</I><B>,</B> <I>vy</I><B>)</B> <B>INTEGER*4</B><I> vx</I><B>,</B> <I>vy</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A71D6F4266csol"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B03D0744ceb"></A>The <B>attachcursor</B> subroutine couples the pointer location to the indicated valuators. As the values generated by the valuators change, the cursor position is updated to reflect the new readings. The values are interpreted as screen coordinates (as measured in pixels) from the lower-left hand corner of the screen. Currently, the only devices supported by the <B>attachcursor</B> subroutine are the MOUSEX, MOUSEY, GHOSTX and GHOSTY devices. This subroutine cannot be used to add to a display list.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A71D6F5009csol"></A><B>Note: </B>For FORTRAN users, this subroutine accepts long integer parameters (INTEGER*4) when started from a FORTRAN program, although it accepts short integers when started from a C program. The C and FORTRAN syntax shown here reflect this difference.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A71D6F5219csol"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A71D6F5441csol"></A>vx </TD>
<TD>  Token representing the valuator device that controls the horizontal location of the cursor. By default, the x position of the cursor is attached to the MOUSEX device.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A71D6F5655csol"></A>vy</TD>
<TD>  Token representing the valuator device that controls the vertical location of the cursor. By default, the y position of the cursor is attached to the MOUSEY device.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A71D6F5830csol"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B03D1149ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A71D6F6334csol"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A71D6F6538csol"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A71D6F6748csol"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A71D6F6945csol"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B03D1489ceb"></A>Tying valuators to a button with the <A HREF="tie.html#A143X9196"><B>tie</B></A> subroutine. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B03D1637ceb"></A>Filtering valuator motion with the <A HREF="noise.html#A143X9174"><B>noise</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B03D1749ceb"></A>Setting the minimum, maximum, and current value of a valuator with the <A HREF="setvaluator.html#A143X921e"><B>setvaluator</B></A> subroutine.</P>
```

```html
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>

<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A145X94a"></A>backbuffer Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX23" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX24" REL="I2" TITLE="animation"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX25" REL="I3" TITLE="backbuffer"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX26" REL="I1" TITLE="backbuffer subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX27" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX28" REL="I2" TITLE="drawing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX29" REL="I3" TITLE="into back buffer"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX30" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX31" REL="I2" TITLE="back buffer"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX32" REL="I3" TITLE="drawing into"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX33" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX34" REL="I2" TITLE="frame buffer configuration"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX35" REL="I3" TITLE="backbuffer"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX36" REL="I1" TITLE="Graphics Library"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A145X94e"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B03F2224ceb"></A>Enables or disables drawing into the back buffer.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A77C11"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B03F2372ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B03F2485ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A145X951"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A145X952"></A><B>void backbuffer(Int32 </B><A HREF="backbuffer.html#A145X940"><I>bool</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A145X928"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A145X92b"></A><B>SUBROUTINE BACKBU(</B><I>bool</I><B>)</B>
<B>LOGICAL </B><I>bool</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A145X955"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B03F2856ceb"></A>The <B>backbuffer</B> subroutine enables or disables drawing into the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P051c">back frame buffer</A>. By default, drawing into the back frame buffer is enabled. In common usage, drawing is done to the back buffer, after which a call to the <A HREF="swapbuffers.html#A145X9302"><B>swapbuffers</B></A> subroutine is made to exchange buffers. The <B>backbuffer</B> subroutine can be used to override this default.  </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B03F2963ceb"></A>This routine is useful only in 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0474">double buffer mode</A>, and is ignored in 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A27P01c">single buffer mode</A>.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A145X945"></A>Parameter</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A145X940"></A><I>bool</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies a value for the state of the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P051c">back frame buffer</A>. The settings for the <I>bool</I> parameter are:</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A145X920"></A></TD>
<TD>  True = drawing into the back buffer is enabled.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A327C9400d"></A></TD>
<TD>  False = drawing into the back buffer is disabled.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P><A NAME="E1B03F3310ceb"></A>The <A HREF="gconfig.html#hS4260nita"><B>gconfig</B></A> subroutine sets the back buffer to True.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015c9b"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B03F3479ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 withAIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A6C0a405"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C14"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C15"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="wR12a0nick"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B03F3913ceb"></A>Setting the display mode to double buffer mode with the <A HREF="doublebuffer.html#A145X91a7"><B>doublebuffer</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B03F4040ceb"></A>Enabling drawing into the front buffer with the <A HREF="frontbuffer.html#A145X9a0"><B>frontbuffer</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B03F4185ceb"></A>Finding out which buffers are enabled for writing with the <A HREF="getbuffer.html#A145X9f6"><B>getbuffer</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B03F4313ceb"></A>Exchanging the front and back buffers with the <A HREF="swapbuffers.html#A145X9302"><B>swapbuffers</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B03F4466ceb"></A>Understanding the <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/glintro.html#A8G44310marj">Hardware Used by GL</A> in<I> GL3.2 Version 4 for AIX: Programming Concepts</I>.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B03F4612ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/configframebuf.html#configframebuf.html">Configuring the Frame Buffer</A>, <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/animatescene.html#animatescene.html">Creating Animated Scenes</A>.</P><hr><center>
```

```html
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>

<a href="boxcirc_c.html">Next</a>  |
<A HREF="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A16C0c7a2"></A>backface.c Example C Language Program
</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX2164" REL="I1" TITLE="backface.c example program (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2165" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2166" REL="I2" TITLE="example programs"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2167" REL="I3" TITLE="drawing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2168" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2169" REL="I2" TITLE="cube"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2170" REL="I3" TITLE="drawing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2171" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2172" REL="I2" TITLE="drawing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2173" REL="I3" TITLE="cube"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2174" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2175" REL="I2" TITLE="example programs"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2176" REL="I3" TITLE="hidden surface removal"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2177" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2178" REL="I2" TITLE="cube"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2179" REL="I3" TITLE="drawing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2180" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2181" REL="I2" TITLE="hidden surface removal"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2182" REL="I3" TITLE="example program"></A>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E991570ttay"></A>/*
backface.c:</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E991783ttay"></A>Draw a cube that can run with backface() turned on or
off.  Turn backface() on with the F key.
Turn backface() off with the B key.  Cube is moved
when LEFTMOUSE is pressed and mouse itself is moved.
*/</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E991939ttay"></A>#include &lt;gl/gl.h>
#include &lt;gl/device.h></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E992097ttay"></A>#define CUBE_SIZE 200
#define CUBE_OBJ 1</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E992243ttay"></A>main ()
{</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E992407ttay"></A>  Device  dev;
  int      moveit;
  short    val, x = 30,y = 30;</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E992556ttay"></A>  initialize();</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E992704ttay"></A>  while (TRUE) {</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E992853ttay"></A>    while (qtest()) {</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E993004ttay"></A>      dev = qread(&amp;val);</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E993327ttay"></A>      if (dev == ESCKEY) {
        backface(FALSE);
        gexit();
        exit();
      }
      else if (dev == REDRAW) {
        reshapeviewport();
        drawcube(x,y);
      }
      else if (dev == LEFTMOUSE)
        moveit = val;
        /* left mouse is down */
      else if (dev == BKEY) {
        backface(TRUE);
        /* turn back facing off */
        drawcube(x,y);
      }
      else if (dev == FKEY) {
        backface(FALSE);
        /* turn back facing on */
        drawcube(x,y);
      }</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E993472ttay"></A>    }</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E993651ttay"></A>    if (moveit) {
      x = getvaluator(MOUSEX);
      y = getvaluator(MOUSEY);
      drawcube(x,y);
    }</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E993794ttay"></A>  }</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E993937ttay"></A>}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E994085ttay"></A>initialize()
{</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E994232ttay"></A>  int gid;</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E994412ttay"></A>  prefposition(XMAXSCREEN/4, XMAXSCREEN*3/4, 
      YMAXSCREEN/4, YMAXSCREEN*3/4);
  gid = winopen("backface");</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E994572ttay"></A>  doublebuffer();
  gconfig();
  shademodel(FLAT);</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E994761ttay"></A>  ortho((float)-XMAXSCREEN, (float)XMAXSCREEN,
      (float)-YMAXSCREEN, (float)YMAXSCREEN,
      (float)-YMAXSCREEN, (float)YMAXSCREEN);</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E994944ttay"></A>  qdevice(ESCKEY);
  qdevice(REDRAW);
  qdevice(LEFTMOUSE);
  qdevice(BKEY);
  qdevice(FKEY);
  qenter(REDRAW,gid);</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E995107ttay"></A>  backface(TRUE);
  /* turn on back facing polygon removal */</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E995250ttay"></A>}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E995402ttay"></A>/* define a cube */
cube()
{ </PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E995608ttay"></A>  /* front face */
  pushmatrix();
  translate(0.0,0.0,CUBE_SIZE);
  color(RED);
  rectfi(-CUBE_SIZE,-CUBE_SIZE,CUBE_SIZE,CUBE_SIZE);
  popmatrix();  /* right face */
  pushmatrix();</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E995810ttay"></A>  translate(CUBE_SIZE, 0.0, 0.0);
  rotate(900, 'y');
  color(GREEN);
  rectfi(-CUBE_SIZE,-CUBE_SIZE,CUBE_SIZE,CUBE_SIZE);
  popmatrix();  /* back face */
  pushmatrix();</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E996011ttay"></A>  translate(0.0, 0.0, -CUBE_SIZE);
  rotate(1800, 'y');
  color(BLUE);
  rectfi(-CUBE_SIZE,-CUBE_SIZE,CUBE_SIZE,CUBE_SIZE);
  popmatrix();  /* left face */
  pushmatrix();</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E996213ttay"></A>  translate(-CUBE_SIZE, 0.0, 0.0);
  rotate(-900, 'y');
  color(CYAN);
  rectfi(-CUBE_SIZE,-CUBE_SIZE,CUBE_SIZE,CUBE_SIZE);
  popmatrix();  /* top face */
  pushmatrix();</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E996415ttay"></A>  translate(0.0, CUBE_SIZE, 0.0);
  rotate(-900, 'x');
  color(MAGENTA);
  rectfi(-CUBE_SIZE,-CUBE_SIZE,CUBE_SIZE,CUBE_SIZE);
  popmatrix();  /* bottom face */
  pushmatrix();</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E996606ttay"></A>  translate(0.0, -CUBE_SIZE, 0.0);
  rotate(900, 'x');
  color(YELLOW);
  rectfi(-CUBE_SIZE,-CUBE_SIZE,CUBE_SIZE,CUBE_SIZE);
  popmatrix();</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E996749ttay"></A>}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E996900ttay"></A>drawcube(x,y)
short x,y;
{</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E997087ttay"></A>  pushmatrix();
  rotate(2*x, 'x');
  rotate(2*y, 'y');
  color(BLACK);
  clear();
  cube();
  popmatrix();
  swapbuffers();</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E997255ttay"></A>}
/*Changes
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;-The constant CUBE_SIZE had a .0 append to the end of it
*/</PRE>
```

```html
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A143X974b"></A>backface Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX37" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX38" REL="I2" TITLE="hidden surface"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX39" REL="I3" TITLE="backface"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX40" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX41" REL="I2" TITLE="backfacing polygons"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX42" REL="I3" TITLE="display"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX43" REL="I1" TITLE="backface subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A143X974d"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0417702ceb"></A>Enables and disables backfacing polygon removals.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C1215"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0417849ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0417953ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9751"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A143X9752"></A><B>void backface(Int32 </B><A HREF="backface.html#A143X9756"><I>bool</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X96c7"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A143X96c8"></A><B>SUBROUTINE BACKFA(</B><I>bool</I><B>)</B>
<B>LOGICAL </B><I>bool</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9753"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0418317ceb"></A>The <B>backface </B>subroutine allows or suppresses the display of backfacing filled polygons. With the <A HREF="frontface.html#A74C12"><B>frontface</B></A> subroutine, it is useful for drawing polygons that have different colors on each side. The <B>frontface</B> subroutine can also be useful for performing a primitive kind of 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P061d">hidden surface</A> removal.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0418426ceb"></A>A backfacing polygon is defined as a polygon whose vertices are in clockwise order in screen coordinates. When backfacing polygon removal is on, the system displays only polygons whose vertices are in counterclockwise order.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0418534ceb"></A>For programs representing solid objects as collections of polygons, this subroutine can be used to help remove hidden surfaces. The <B>backface </B>subroutine works best for simple convex objects that do not obscure other objects.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0418642ceb"></A>For complicated objects, this routine alone may not remove all hidden surfaces. To remove hidden surfaces for more complicated objects or groups of objects, use the <A HREF="zbuffer.html#A143X97b1"><B>zbuffer</B></A> subroutine. The <B>zbuffer</B> subroutine checks the relative distances of the figure from the viewer (z values) and draws only the nearest figures.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0418754ceb"></A>If both frontfacing and backfacing polygon removal is enabled, no filled polygons are displayed. (An exception is made if the graphics pipeline cannot determine if a polygon is front- or backfacing because it is degenerate or otherwise exceptional.)</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><B>Notes: </B>
<OL><LI><A NAME="A237X9474f"></A>Matrices that negate coordinates, such as <SAMP>scale(-1.0,&nbsp;1.0,&nbsp;1.0)</SAMP>, reverse the directional order of a polygon's points and can cause the <B>backface </B>subroutine to do the opposite of what is intended.</LI>

<LI><A NAME="A95C1230e"></A>If a polygon is extremely small or has degenerate vertices, the graphics pipeline cannot determine if the polygon is backfacing. In such cases, the polygon is rendered by default.</LI></OL></BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A143X9755"></A>Parameter</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X9756"></A><I>bool </I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies a value for the state of backfacing polygon removal. The settings for the <I>bool</I> parameter are:</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"></TD>
<TD>  </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"></TD>
<TD>  False = backfacing polygon removal disabled.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A258C01c51a"></A></TD>
<TD>  True = backfacing polygon removal enabled.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X975b"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0419285ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="backface_c.html#A16C0c7a2"><B>backface.c</B></A> uses the <B>backface</B> subroutine to draw a cube two ways to demonstrate the difference between allowing or suppressing the display of backfacing polygons.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A64C0165e4"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0419445ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows Desktop/3D Feature.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0419554ceb"></A>On the POWERgraphics GTO adapter, either frontfacing polygon removal or backfacing polygon removal can be specified, but not both simultaneously. Enabling backfacing culling disables frontfacing culling.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C1218"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C1219"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C121a"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A258C01c51b"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0419880ceb"></A>Initiating z-buffer mode with the <A HREF="zbuffer.html#A143X97b1"><B>zbuffer</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0419990ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A> and Removing <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/remhidden.html#remhidden.html">Hidden Surfaces</A>.</P><hr><center>

 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html">| Glossary</A>
```

```html
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A142X922e"></A>bbox2 Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX44" REL="I1" TITLE="bbox2 subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX45" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX46" REL="I2" TITLE="object (display list)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX47" REL="I3" TITLE="controlling subroutine execution"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX48" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX49" REL="I2" TITLE="object (display list)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX50" REL="I3" TITLE="specifying bounding box"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX51" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX52" REL="I2" TITLE="object (display list)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX53" REL="I3" TITLE="culling and pruning"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX54" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX55" REL="I2" TITLE="object (display list)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX56" REL="I3" TITLE="bbox2"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX57" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX58" REL="I2" TITLE="display list"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A142X9230"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0439709ceb"></A>Specifies the bounding box and minimum pixel radius.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C11"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0439856ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0439960ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A142X9234"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A142X9235"></A><B>void bbox2</B>
<B>(Screencoord </B><A HREF="bbox2.html#A142X9239"><I>xmin</I></A><B>, Screencoord </B><A HREF="bbox2.html#A142X923a"><I>ymin</I></A><B>,</B>
<B>Coord</B> <A HREF="bbox2.html#cQu2d0marj"><I>x1</I></A><B>, Coord</B> <A HREF="bbox2.html#yQu2170marj"><I>y1</I></A><B>,</B>
<B>Coord </B><A HREF="bbox2.html#DAu2290marj"><I>x2</I></A><B>,</B> <B>Coord</B> <A HREF="bbox2.html#A142X923b"><I>y2</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X911f50"></A><B>void bbox2i</B>
<B>(Screencoord </B><A HREF="bbox2.html#A142X9239"><I>xmin</I></A><B>, Screencoord </B><A HREF="bbox2.html#A142X923a"><I>ymin</I></A><B>,</B>
<B>Icoord</B> <A HREF="bbox2.html#cQu2d0marj"><I>x1</I></A><B>, Icoord</B> <A HREF="bbox2.html#yQu2170marj"><I>y1</I></A><B>,</B>
<B>Icoord </B><A HREF="bbox2.html#DAu2290marj"><I>x2</I></A><B>,</B> <B>Icoord</B> <A HREF="bbox2.html#A142X923b"><I>y2</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X911f51"></A><B>void bbox2s</B>
<B>(Screencoord </B><A HREF="bbox2.html#A142X9239"><I>xmin</I></A><B>, Screencoord </B><A HREF="bbox2.html#A142X923a"><I>ymin</I></A><B>,</B>
<B>Scoord</B> <A HREF="bbox2.html#cQu2d0marj"><I>x1</I></A><B>, Scoord</B> <A HREF="bbox2.html#yQu2170marj"><I>y1</I></A><B>,</B>
<B>Scoord </B><A HREF="bbox2.html#DAu2290marj"><I>x2</I></A><B>,</B> <B>Scoord</B> <A HREF="bbox2.html#A142X923b"><I>y2</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010a75"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010a76"></A><B>SUBROUTINE BBOX2(</B><I>xmin</I><B>,</B><I> ymin</I><B>,</B> <I>x1</I><B>,</B><I> y1</I><B>,</B><I> x2</I><B>,</B><I> y2</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>xmin</I><B>,</B><I> ymin</I>
<B>REAL </B><I>x1</I><B>,</B><I> y1</I><B>,</B><I> x2</I><B>,</B><I> y2</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010a77"></A><B>SUBROUTINE BBOX2I(</B><I>xmin</I><B>,</B><I> ymin</I><B>,</B> <I>x1</I><B>,</B><I> y1</I><B>,</B><I> x2</I><B>,</B><I> y2</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>xmin</I><B>,</B><I> ymin</I><B>,</B><I> x1</I><B>,</B><I> y1</I><B>,</B><I> x2</I><B>,</B><I> y2</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010a78"></A><B>SUBROUTINE BBOX2S(</B><I>xmin</I><B>,</B><I> ymin</I><B>,</B> <I>x1</I><B>,</B><I> y1</I><B>,</B><I> x2</I><B>,</B><I> y2</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*2 </B><I>xmin</I><B>,</B><I> ymin</I><B>, </B><I>x1</I><B>,</B><I> y1</I><B>,</B><I> x2</I><B>,</B><I> y2</I></PRE>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A139X91ed8"></A><B>Note: </B>For FORTRAN users, this subroutine accepts long integer parameters (INTEGER*4) when invoked from a FORTRAN program, although it accepts short integers when invoked from a C program. The C and FORTRAN syntax shown here reflect this difference. Also, the FORTRAN INTEGER*2 version, the <B>BBOX2S</B> subroutine, should not be called with integer constant parameters. For example, 2 is an integer constant; JJ is an integer variable. The XL FORTRAN compiler, invoked by the 
<B>xlf</B> command, stores all integer constants as long integers (INTEGER*4), not as short integers (INTEGER*2). Invoking the short version of this subroutine with an integer constant will result in unexpected behavior.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A142X9236"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B043A612ceb"></A>The <B>bbox2</B> subroutine controls the execution of routines in a GL object by performing the graphical functions known as 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A25P03e8">culling</A> and 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0706">pruning</A>.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B043A721ceb"></A>The <B>bbox2</B> subroutine calculates the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A255B966">bounding box</A>, transforms it to
 <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A27P017">screen coordinates</A>, and compares it to the 
 <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A27P039">viewport</A>. If the bounding box is completely outside the viewport, the routines between the call to the <B>bbox2</B> subroutine and the end of the object are ignored. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B043A830ceb"></A>If the bounding box is within the viewport, the system compares it with the minimum feature size. If the box is too small in both the <I>x</I> and <I>y</I> dimensions, the rest of the routines in the object are ignored. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B043A937ceb"></A>Overuse of the <B>bbox2</B> subroutine can impair performance, so it is best reserved for complicated object definitions.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9d84"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine can be used only to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>. </BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A142X9238"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A142X9239"></A><I>xmin </I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the width, in pixels, of the smallest displayable feature.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A142X923a"></A><I>ymin</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the height, in pixels, of the smallest displayable feature.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="cQu2d0marj"></A><I>x1 </I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>x </I>coordinate of a corner of the bounding box.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="yQu2170marj"></A><I>y1 </I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>y </I>coordinate of a corner of the bounding box.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="DAu2290marj"></A><I>x2 </I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>x </I>coordinate of a corner of the bounding box. This corner must be diagonally opposite the corner (<I>x1,</I> <I>y1</I>).</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A142X923b"></A><I>y2 </I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>y </I>coordinate of a corner of the bounding box. This corner must be diagonally opposite the corner (<I>x1,</I> <I>y1</I>).</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015cf8"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B043B540ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C14"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C15"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>
```

```html
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A144X960c"></A>bgnclosedline or endclosedline Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX59" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX60" REL="I2" TITLE="begin-end style"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX61" REL="I3" TITLE="bgnclosedline"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX62" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX63" REL="I2" TITLE="vertex"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX64" REL="I3" TITLE="closed line"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX65" REL="I1" TITLE="bgnclosedline subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX66" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX67" REL="I2" TITLE="begin-end style"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX68" REL="I3" TITLE="endclosedline"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX69" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX70" REL="I2" TITLE="vertex"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX71" REL="I3" TITLE="closed line"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX72" REL="I1" TITLE="endclosedline subroutine (GL)"></A>


<H3><A NAME="A60C0157bb"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B045B967ceb"></A>Begins or ends interpretation of vertex routines as closed line vertices.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A77C151"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B045C115ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B045C219ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A60C0157bf"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A60C0157c0"></A><B>void bgnclosedline(&nbsp;)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X912850"></A><B>void endclosedline(&nbsp;)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A60C0157c1"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A60C0157c2"></A><B>SUBROUTINE BGNCLO</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A20C0e2e2"></A><B>SUBROUTINE ENDCLO</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A60C0157c3"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B045C673ceb"></A>The <B>bgnclosedline </B>subroutine marks the start of a group of vertex <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawbeg-end.html#A264X925d">(begin-end style)</A> subroutines to be interpreted as points on a closed line. It is the same as the <A HREF="bgnline.html#A144X962e"><B>bgnline</B></A> subroutine, except that it connects the last vertex to the first.  For example,</P>
<PRE><A NAME="A60C0157c5"></A>bgnclosedline();
v3f(vert1);
v3f(vert2);
v3f(vert3);
endclosedline();</PRE>

<P><A NAME="E1B045C834ceb"></A>draws the outline of a triangle.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B045C953ceb"></A>The group of <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawbeg-end.html#A264X925d">begin-end style</A> subroutines terminates with the <B>endclosedline</B> subroutine. After the <B>endclosedline </B>subroutine, the system draws a line from the final vertex back to the initial vertex, and the current graphics position is left undefined. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B045D064ceb"></A>All line segments use the current linestyle and linewidth. The <B>bgnclosedline</B> subroutine resets the linestyle counter; that is, the first pixel drawn uses the first bit of the linestyle, and so on. The linestyle counter is <I>not </I>reset on subsequent vertices; instead, the pattern continues around corners, until the <B>endclosedline</B> subroutine is reached. To reset the pattern, call the <B>endclosedline</B> subroutine and then the <B>bgnclosedline</B> subroutine again.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B045D173ceb"></A>If the color changes between a pair of vertices, the color of the line segment is constant if the current shading model is FLAT and interpolated if the current shading model is GOURAUD. In 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A25P03e3">color map mode</A>, the colors vary through the color map; to get reasonable results, the color map should contain a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0610">gamma ramp</A>. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B045D322ceb"></A>Between calls to the <B>bgnclosedline</B> and <B>endclosedline</B> subroutines, you can issue calls to the following GL subroutines only: </P>

<UL><LI><A NAME="A87C01957e"></A><A HREF="c.html#A143X9262"><B>c</B></A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A87C01957f"></A><A HREF="color.html#A146X9429"><B>color</B></A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A87C019580"></A><A HREF="cpack.html#A143X9284"><B>cpack</B> </A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A87C019582"></A><A HREF="lmbind.html#XeZ2340marj"><B>lmbind </B></A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A87C019581"></A><A HREF="lmcolor.html#ofZ220marj"><B>lmcolor</B></A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A87C019583"></A><A HREF="lmdef.html#rgZ2250marj"><B>lmdef</B></A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A87C019584"></A><A HREF="n3f.html#A139X91ef3"><B>n3f</B></A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A87C019585"></A><A HREF="normal.html#A142X9b7"><B>normal</B></A> </LI>

<LI><A NAME="A87C019586"></A><A HREF="RGBcolor.html#A143X9394"><B>RGBcolor</B></A> </LI>

<LI><A NAME="A87C019587"></A><A HREF="v.html#A144X97a4"><B>v</B></A> </LI></UL>


<P><A NAME="E1B045D889ceb"></A>Use the <A HREF="lmdef.html#rgZ2250marj"><B>lmdef</B></A> and <A HREF="lmbind.html#XeZ2340marj"><B>lmbind</B></A> subroutines to respecify only materials and their properties. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015d62"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B045E054ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B045E161ceb"></A>The POWERgraphics GTO and the 3D Color Graphics Processor support a maximum of 255 vertices between the <B>bgnclosedline</B> and <B>endclosedline</B> subroutines.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3CBCC3B585bolt"></A>The POWERgraphics Gt4 and GXT1000 support an arbitrary number of vertices between the <B>bgnclosedline</B> and <B>endclosedline</B> subroutines.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A77C154"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C155"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C156"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A258C01c3d4"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B045E490ceb"></A>Drawing vertex-based lines with the <A HREF="bgnline.html#A144X962e"><B>bgnline</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B045E601ceb"></A>Selecting a linestyle pattern with the <A HREF="setlinestyle.html#XFM1310marj"><B>setlinestyle</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B045E707ceb"></A>Transferring a vertex to the graphics pipe with the <A HREF="v.html#A144X97a4"><B>v</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B045E815ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A>, <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawbeg-end.html">Drawing with Begin-End Style</A> Subroutines, <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/glintro.html#A8G44310marj">Understanding the Hardware Used by GL</A>, and <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/workcolor.html#workcolor.html">Working in Color Map and RGB Modes</A>.</P><hr><center>
```
