<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A144X962e"></A>bgnline or endline Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX73" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX74" REL="I2" TITLE="begin-end style"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX75" REL="I3" TITLE="bgnline"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX76" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX77" REL="I2" TITLE="line"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX78" REL="I3" TITLE="vertex-based"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX79" REL="I1" TITLE="bgnline subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX80" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX81" REL="I2" TITLE="begin-end style"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX82" REL="I3" TITLE="endline"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX83" REL="I1" TITLE="endline subroutine (GL)"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A144X9630"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B047C989ceb"></A>Begins or ends interpretation of vertex routines as line vertices.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A77C1353"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B047D137ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B047D241ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A144X9634"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A144X9635"></A><B>void bgnline(&nbsp;)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A107C116c"></A><B>void endline(&nbsp;)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A20C0e2da"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A20C0e2db"></A><B>SUBROUTINE BGNLIN</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A107C116d"></A><B>SUBROUTINE ENDLIN</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A144X9636"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B047D694ceb"></A>The <B>bgnline</B> subroutine begins the interpretation of vertex <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawbeg-end.html#A264X925d">(begin-end style)</A> subroutines as line vertices. It is like the <A HREF="bgnclosedline.html#A144X960c"><B>bgnclosedline</B></A> subroutine, except that the last vertex does not connect to the first vertex.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B047D803ceb"></A>Vertices specified after the <B>bgnline</B> subroutine and before the <B>endline</B> subroutine are interpreted as endpoints of a series of line segments. Use the <A HREF="v.html#A144X97a4"><B>v</B></A> subroutine to specify a vertex. The first vertex connects to the second; the second connects to the third; and so on until the next-to-last vertex connects to the last one. All segments use the current linestyle and linewidth.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B047D910ceb"></A>After the <B>endline</B> subroutine executes, the current graphics position is undefined.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B047E023ceb"></A>All line segments use the current linestyle and linewidth. The <B>bgnline</B> subroutine resets the linestyle counter; that is, the first pixel drawn uses the first bit of the linestyle, and so on. The linestyle counter is <I>not</I> reset on subsequent vertices; instead, the pattern continues around corners, until the <B>endline</B> subroutine is reached. To reset the pattern, call the <B>endline</B> subroutine and then the <B>bgnline</B> subroutine again.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B047E132ceb"></A>If the color changes between a pair of vertices, the color of the line segment is constant if the current shading model is FLAT and interpolated if the current shading model is GOURAUD. In 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A25P03e3">color map mode</A>, the colors vary through the color map; to get reasonable results, the color map should contain a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0610">gamma ramp</A>>. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B047E281ceb"></A>Between calls to the <B>bgnline</B> and <B>endline</B> subroutines, you can issue calls to the following Graphics Library subroutines only: </P>

<UL><LI><A NAME="A228C1239"></A><A HREF="c.html#A143X9262"><B>c</B></A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A228C123a"></A><A HREF="color.html#A146X9429"><B>color</B></A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A228C123b"></A><A HREF="cpack.html#A143X9284"><B>cpack</B></A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A228C123c"></A><A HREF="lmbind.html#XeZ2340marj"><B>lmbind</B></A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A228C123d"></A><A HREF="lmcolor.html#ofZ220marj"><B>lmcolor</B></A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A228C123e"></A><A HREF="lmdef.html#rgZ2250marj"><B>lmdef</B></A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A228C123f"></A><A HREF="n3f.html#A139X91ef3"><B>n3f</B></A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A228C1240"></A><A HREF="normal.html#A142X9b7"><B>normal</B></A> </LI>

<LI><A NAME="A228C1241"></A><A HREF="RGBcolor.html#A143X9394"><B>RGBcolor</B></A> </LI>

<LI><A NAME="A228C1242"></A><A HREF="v.html#A144X97a4"><B>v</B></A></LI></UL>


<P><A NAME="E1B047E849ceb"></A>Use the <B>lmdef</B> and <B>lmbind</B> subroutines to respecify only materials and their properties. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015d64"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B047F067ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B047F174ceb"></A>The POWER Gt4, POWER Gt4x, and POWER GXT1000 adapters support an arbitrary number of vertices between the <B>bgnline</B> and <B>endline</B> subroutines.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B047F291ceb"></A>The POWERgraphics GTO and the 3-D Color Graphics Processor support a maximum of 255 vertices between the <B>bgnline</B> and <B>endline</B> subroutines.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3CBCC68870bolt"></A>The POWER Gt4x will restart the linestyle stipple pattern periodically if a large number of vertices is issued between a <B>bgnline()</B> and <B>endline</B> pair. Such a reset will not occur within the first 255 vertices but will occur sometime between the first 400 and 2000 vertices and will then restart at multiples of this amount. The actual point at which the restart occurs depends on whether normals, colors, and/or materials have been specified in addition to the vertex data.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A77C1356"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C1357"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C1358"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A258C01c3d8"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B047F611ceb"></A>Drawing closed line vertices with the <A HREF="bgnclosedline.html#A144X960c"><B>bgnclosedline</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B047F717ceb"></A>Setting the current color in RGB mode with the <A HREF="c.html#A143X9262"><B>c</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B047F825ceb"></A>Selecting the shading model with the <A HREF="shademodel.html#A143X9ab9"><B>shademodel</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B047F933ceb"></A>Transferring a vertex to the graphics pipe with the <A HREF="v.html#A144X97a4"><B>v</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0480041ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A>, Drawing with <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawbeg-end.html">Begin-End Style</A> Subroutines, Understanding the <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/glintro.html#A8G44310marj">Hardware Used by GL</A>, and Working in <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/workcolor.html#workcolor.html">Color Map and RGB Modes</A>.</P><hr><center>

 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
</center></BODY>

 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A144X9650"></A>bgnpoint or endpoint Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX84" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX85" REL="I2" TITLE="begin-end style"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX86" REL="I3" TITLE="bgnpoint"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX87" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX88" REL="I2" TITLE="points"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX89" REL="I3" TITLE="vertex-based"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX90" REL="I1" TITLE="bgnpoint subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX91" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX92" REL="I2" TITLE="begin-end style"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX93" REL="I3" TITLE="endpoint"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX94" REL="I1" TITLE="endpoint subroutine (GL)"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A144X9652"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B049F983ceb"></A>Begins or ends interpretation of vertex subroutines as points.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A77C135e"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B04A0131ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B04A0234ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A144X9656"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X912804"></A><B>void bgnpoint(&nbsp;)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A107C126d"></A><B>void endpoint( )</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A20C0e2dc"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A77C1361"></A><B>SUBROUTINE BGNPOI</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A107C126e"></A><B>SUBROUTINE ENDPOI</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A144X9658"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B04A0684ceb"></A>The <B>bgnpoint </B>subroutine marks the beginning of a list of vertex <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawbeg-end.html#A264X925d">(begin-end style)</A> subroutines to interpret as points. Use the <B>endpoint</B> subroutine to mark the end of the list. For each vertex, the system draws a one-pixel point into the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A270A984a">frame buffer</A>. After the <B>endpoint</B> subroutine completes, the current graphics position is undefined. Use the <A HREF="v.html#A144X97a4"><B>v</B></A> subroutine to specify a vertex.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B04A0792ceb"></A>Between the <B>bgnpoint</B> and <B>endpoint</B> subroutines, you can issue only the following Graphics Library subroutines:</P>

<UL><LI><A NAME="A228C124d"></A><A HREF="c.html#A143X9262"><B>c</B></A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A228C124e"></A><A HREF="color.html#A146X9429"><B>color</B></A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A228C124f"></A><A HREF="cpack.html#A143X9284"><B>cpack</B> </A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A228C1250"></A><A HREF="lmbind.html#XeZ2340marj"><B>lmbind </B></A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A228C1251"></A><A HREF="lmcolor.html#ofZ220marj"><B>lmcolor</B></A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A228C1252"></A><A HREF="lmdef.html#rgZ2250marj"><B>lmdef</B></A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A228C1253"></A><A HREF="n3f.html#A139X91ef3"><B>n3f</B></A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A228C1254"></A><A HREF="normal.html#A142X9b7"><B>normal</B></A> </LI>

<LI><A NAME="A228C1255"></A><A HREF="RGBcolor.html#A143X9394"><B>RGBcolor</B></A> </LI>

<LI><A NAME="A228C1256"></A><A HREF="v.html#A144X97a4"><B>v</B></A> </LI></UL>


<P><A NAME="E1B04A1361ceb"></A>Use the <A HREF="lmbind.html#XeZ2340marj"><B>lmbind</B></A> and <A HREF="lmdef.html#rgZ2250marj"><B>lmdef</B></A> subroutines to respecify only materials and their properties.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015d66"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B04A1579ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B04A1687ceb"></A>The POWER Gt4 and POWER Gt4xThe POWER Gt4, POWER Gt4x, and POWER GXT1000 adapters support an arbitrary number of vertices between the <B>bgnpoint</B> and <B>endpoint</B> subroutines.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B04A1794ceb"></A>The POWERgraphics GTO and the 3D Color Graphics Processor support a maximum of 255 vertices between the <B>bgnpoint</B> and <B>endpoint</B> subroutines.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A77C1362"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C1363"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C1364"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A258C01c3e0"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B04A2112ceb"></A>Setting the current color in RGB mode with the <A HREF="c.html#A143X9262"><B>c</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B04A2219ceb"></A>Transferring a vertex to the graphics pipe with the <A HREF="v.html#A144X97a4"><B>v</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>

<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A144X9672"></A>bgnpolygon or endpolygon Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX95" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX96" REL="I2" TITLE="begin-end style"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX97" REL="I3" TITLE="bgnpolygon"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX98" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX99" REL="I2" TITLE="polygons"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX100" REL="I3" TITLE="vertex-based"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX101" REL="I1" TITLE="bgnpolygon subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX102" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX103" REL="I2" TITLE="begin-end style"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX104" REL="I3" TITLE="endpolygon"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX105" REL="I1" TITLE="endpolygon subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A144X9674"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B04BF950ceb"></A>Begins or ends interpretation of vertex subroutines as polygon vertices.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A77C1359"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B04C0098ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B04C0201ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A144X9678"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X91281b"></A><B>void bgnpolygon(&nbsp;)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A107C1294"></A><B>void endpolygon(&nbsp;)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A20C0e2dd"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A20C0e2de"></A><B>SUBROUTINE BGNPOL</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A107C1295"></A><B>SUBROUTINE ENDPOL</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A144X967a"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B04C0654ceb"></A>The <B>bgnpolygon</B> subroutine begins the interpretation of vertex <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawbeg-end.html#A264X925d">(begin-end style)</A> subroutines as polygon vertices. Vertices specified after the <B>bgnpolygon</B> subroutine and before the <B>endpolygon</B> subroutine form a single polygon. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B04C0770ceb"></A>Self-intersecting polygons (other than four-point bowties) may render incorrectly. To force the system to render concave polygons correctly, call the <A HREF="concave.html#HXf320marj"><B>concave</B></A> subroutine with the parameter set to True.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B04C0918ceb"></A>Between the <B>bgnpolygon</B> and <B>endpolygon</B> subroutines, you can issue only the following Graphics Library subroutines:</P>

<UL><LI><A NAME="A228C1243"></A><A HREF="c.html#A143X9262"><B>c</B></A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A228C1244"></A><A HREF="color.html#A146X9429"><B>color</B></A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A228C1245"></A><A HREF="cpack.html#A143X9284"><B>cpack</B> </A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A228C1246"></A><A HREF="lmbind.html#XeZ2340marj"><B>lmbind </B></A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A228C1247"></A><A HREF="lmcolor.html#ofZ220marj"><B>lmcolor</B></A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A228C1248"></A><A HREF="lmdef.html#rgZ2250marj"><B>lmdef</B></A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A228C1249"></A><A HREF="n3f.html#A139X91ef3"><B>n3f</B></A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A228C124a"></A><A HREF="normal.html#A142X9b7"><B>normal</B></A> </LI>

<LI><A NAME="A228C124b"></A><A HREF="RGBcolor.html#A143X9394"><B>RGBcolor</B></A> </LI>

<LI><A NAME="A228C124c"></A><A HREF="v.html#A144X97a4"><B>v</B></A> </LI></UL>


<P><A NAME="E1B04C1486ceb"></A>After the <B>endpolygon</B> subroutine completes, the current graphics position is undefined. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B04C1594ceb"></A>Use the <A HREF="lmbind.html#XeZ2340marj"><B>lmbind</B></A> and <A HREF="lmdef.html#rgZ2250marj"><B>lmdef</B></A> subroutines to respecify only materials and their properties.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B04C1704ceb"></A>Use the <B>v</B> subroutine to specify a vertex.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B04C1811ceb"></A>Use the <A HREF="backface.html#A143X974b"><B>backface</B></A> subroutine to eliminate backfacing polygons. Polygons with vertices specified in clockwise order are not drawn.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A237X94785"></A><B>Attention: </B>Calling <B>concave(TRUE)</B> guarantees that all polygons are drawn correctly, but may cause degradation of performance. Do not set <B>concave(TRUE)</B> if you plan to draw only convex polygons.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A144X9682"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B04C2027ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="cylinder2_c.html#A16C0c87c"><B>cylinder2.c</B></A> uses the <B>bgnpolygon</B> subroutine to define the beginning of a description of a polygon.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015d68"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B04C2187ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B04C2299ceb"></A>The POWER Gt4 and POWER Gt4x adapters support only a limited number of vertices between the <B>bgnpolygon</B> and <B>endpolygon</B> subroutines. The actual limit can vary from less than 200 vertices to more than 400 vertices, depending on whether or not colors, normals, or material properties are specified between the begin and end pair. If only vertices are specified between a begin and end pair, then at least 255 vertices are supported. Specifying normals, colors, or material properties decreases the overall maximum number of vertices.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B04C2407ceb"></A>The POWERgraphics GTO and the 3D Color Graphics Processor support a maximum of 255 vertices between the <B>bgnpolygon</B> and <B>endpolygon</B> subroutines.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3CBCCCE103bolt"></A>The POWERgraphics GXT1000 supports an arbitrary number of vertices between the <B>bgnpolygon</B> and <B>endpolygon</B> subroutines, if the concave flag has been set to FALSE. If concave polygon checking is enabled, then a maximum of 255 vertices is supported. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A12C0b7e0"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C135c"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C135d"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A258C01c3dc"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B04C2728ceb"></A>Allowing the system to draw concave polygons with the <A HREF="concave.html#HXf320marj"><B>concave</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B04C2876ceb"></A>Transferring a vertex to the graphics pipe with the <A HREF="v.html#A144X97a4"><B>v</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B04C2989ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A>, Drawing with <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawbeg-end.html">Begin-End Style</A> Subroutines, Understanding the <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/glintro.html#A8G44310marj">Hardware Used by GL</A>, and Working in <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/workcolor.html#workcolor.html">Color Map and RGB Modes</A>.</P><hr><center>

</center></BODY>

</TITLE>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="bgnpolygon.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="bgntmesh.html">Next</a>  |
<A href="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A251X9d7"></A>bgnsurface or endsurface Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX106" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX107" REL="I2" TITLE="NURBS curves and surfaces"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX108" REL="I3" TITLE="endsurface"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX109" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX110" REL="I2" TITLE="NURBS curves and surfaces"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX111" REL="I3" TITLE="bgnsurface"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX112" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX113" REL="I2" TITLE="surface (NURBS)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX114" REL="I3" TITLE="delimiting definition"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX115" REL="I1" TITLE="endsurface subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX116" REL="I1" TITLE="bgnsurface subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A251X9d9"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B04DF900ceb"></A>Delimit a NURBS surface definition.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C132f"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B04E0048ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B04E0152ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A251X9dc"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A251X9dd"></A><B>void bgnsurface(&nbsp;)</B>
<B>void endsurface(&nbsp;)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A251X9b6"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A251X9b9"></A><B>SUBROUTINE BGNSUR</B>
<B>SUBROUTINE ENDSUR</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A251X9e0"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B04E0519ceb"></A>The <B>bgnsurface </B>and <B>endsurface </B>subroutines mark the beginning and end, respectively, of a Non-Uniform Rational B-Spline (NURBS) surface definition. Between calls to these two subroutines, only those subroutines that define the surface and provide the trimming information can be invoked. They are: </P>

<UL><LI><A NAME="A252X9838"></A><A HREF="bgntrim.html#A251X98d"><B>bgntrim</B></A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A252X9839"></A><A HREF="bgntrim.html#A251X98d"><B>endtrim</B></A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A252X983a"></A><A HREF="nurbscurve.html#A255X93ca"><B>nurbscurve</B></A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A252X983b"></A><A HREF="nurbssurface.html#A252X98b9"><B>nurbssurface</B></A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A252X983c"></A><A HREF="pwlcurve.html#A257X9fc"><B>pwlcurve</B></A></LI></UL>


<P><A NAME="E1B04E0864ceb"></A>The NURBS surface definition must consist of exactly one call to the <A HREF="nurbssurface.html#A252X98b9"><B>nurbssurface</B></A> subroutine (to define the shape of the surface), followed by a list of zero or more 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A154P11542">trimming loop</A> definitions (to define the boundaries of the surface). Each trimming loop definition consists of one call to the <A HREF="bgntrim.html#A251X98d"><B>bgntrim</B></A> subroutine, one or more calls to the <A HREF="pwlcurve.html#A257X9fc"><B>pwlcurve</B></A> or <A HREF="nurbscurve.html#A255X93ca"><B>nurbscurve</B></A> subroutines, and one call to the <A HREF="bgntrim.html#A251X98d"><B>endtrim</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B04E0973ceb"></A>The system renders a NURBS surface as a polygonal mesh, and calculates normal vectors at the corners of the polygons within the mesh. Therefore, your program should specify a lighting model if it uses NURBS surfaces; otherwise much surface information is lost. When using a lighting model, define or modify materials and their properties with the <A HREF="lmdef.html#rgZ2250marj"><B>lmdef</B></A> and <A HREF="lmbind.html#XeZ2340marj"><B>lmbind</B></A> subroutines.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B04E1083ceb"></A>The following code fragment draws a NURBS surface trimmed by two closed loops. The first closed loop is a single 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#rEf3b0nita">piecewise linear curve</A> (defined by the <A HREF="pwlcurve.html#A257X9fc"><B>pwlcurve</B></A> subroutine), and the second loop consists of two NURBS curves joined end to end: </P>
<PRE><A NAME="A251X9e5"></A>bgnsurface(...); 
    nurbssurface(...);
    bgntrim();
        pwlcurve(...); 
    endtrim();
    bgntrim();
        nurbscurve(...);
        nurbscurve(...); 
    endtrim(); 
endsurface();</PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015d9c"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B04E1300ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C1332"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C1333"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C1334"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A251X9ed"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B04E1620ceb"></A>Marking the beginning and end of a NURBS surface trimming loop with the <A HREF="bgntrim.html#A251X98d"><B>bgntrim</B> and <B>endtrim</B></A> subroutines. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B04E1727ceb"></A>Returning the current value of a trimmed NURBS surface display property with the <A HREF="getnurbsproperty.html#A252X986e"><B>getnurbsproperty</B></A> subroutine. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B04E1834ceb"></A>Controlling the shape of a NURBS trimming curve with the <A HREF="nurbscurve.html#A255X93ca"><B>nurbscurve</B></A> subroutine. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B04E1941ceb"></A>Controlling the shape of a NURBS surface with the <A HREF="nurbssurface.html#A252X98b9"><B>nurbssurface</B></A> subroutine. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B04E2050ceb"></A>Describing a piecewise linear trimming curve for NURBS surfaces with the <A HREF="pwlcurve.html#A257X9fc"><B>pwlcurve</B></A> subroutine. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B04E2157ceb"></A>Setting a property for the display of trimmed NURBS with the <A HREF="setnurbsproperty.html#A257X911b"><B>setnurbsproperty</B></A> subroutine. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B04E2265ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A>, Creating <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/crlighteff.html#crlighteff.html">Lighting Effects</A>, and Drawing <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawnurbs.html#drawnurbs.html">NURBS Curves and Surfaces</A>.</P><hr><center>
[  <a href="bgnpolygon.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="bgntmesh.html">Next</a>  |

 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
</center></BODY>

</HTML>

<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A144X9694"></A>bgntmesh or endtmesh Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX117" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX118" REL="I2" TITLE="begin-end style"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX119" REL="I3" TITLE="bgntmesh"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX120" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX121" REL="I2" TITLE="vertex"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX122" REL="I3" TITLE="triangle mesh"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX123" REL="I1" TITLE="bgntmesh subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX124" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX125" REL="I2" TITLE="begin-end style"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX126" REL="I3" TITLE="endtmesh"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX127" REL="I1" TITLE="endtmesh subroutine (GL)"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A144X9696"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B04FF617ceb"></A>Begins or ends interpretation of vertex subroutines as triangle mesh vertices.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A77C1365"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B04FF765ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B04FF870ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A144X969a"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X912837"></A><B>void bgntmesh(&nbsp;)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A107C1292"></A><B>void endtmesh(&nbsp;)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A20C0e2df"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A20C0e2e0"></A><B>SUBROUTINE BGNTME</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A107C1293"></A><B>SUBROUTINE ENDTME</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A144X969c"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0500321ceb"></A>The <B>bgntmesh</B> subroutine begins the system interpretation of vertex <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawbeg-end.html#A264X925d">(begin-end style)</A> subroutines as triangle mesh vertices, which are used to define a mesh of triangles.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0500431ceb"></A>The <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0612">graphics pipeline</A> maintains two vertex registers. The first and second vertices are loaded into the registers. When the third vertex routine is executed, the system draws a triangle through the vertices and replaces the older of the register vertices with the third vertex.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0500542ceb"></A>For each new vertex subroutine, the system draws a triangle through the new vertex and the stored vertices, then replaces the older stored vertex with the new vertex. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0500650ceb"></A>To replace the more recent of the stored vertices, call the <A HREF="swaptmesh.html#A144X9782"><B>swaptmesh</B></A> subroutine. For example, the code sequence: </P>
<PRE><A NAME="A16C0cd13"></A>bgntmesh();
&nbsp;v3f(zero);
&nbsp;v3f(one);
&nbsp;v3f(two);
&nbsp;v3f(three);
endtmesh();</PRE>

<P><A NAME="E1B0500816ceb"></A>draws two triangles, <SAMP>(zero,one,two)</SAMP> and <SAMP>(one,two,three)</SAMP>, while the code sequence: </P>
<PRE><A NAME="A16C0cd15"></A>bgntmesh();
&nbsp;v3f(zero);
&nbsp;v3f(one);
&nbsp;swaptmesh();
&nbsp;v3f(two);
&nbsp;v3f(three);
endtmesh();</PRE>

<P><A NAME="E1B0500981ceb"></A>draws two triangles, <SAMP>(zero,one,two)</SAMP> and <SAMP>(zero,two,three)</SAMP>. There is no limit to the number of times that the <B>swaptmesh</B> subroutine can be called. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0501089ceb"></A>Between the <B>bgntmesh</B> and <B>endtmesh</B> subroutines, you can issue only the following Graphics Library subroutines:</P>

<UL><LI><A NAME="A228C1257"></A><A HREF="c.html#A143X9262"><B>c</B></A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A228C1258"></A><A HREF="color.html#A146X9429"><B>color</B></A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A228C1259"></A><A HREF="cpack.html#A143X9284"><B>cpack</B> </A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A228C125a"></A><A HREF="lmbind.html#XeZ2340marj"><B>lmbind </B></A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A228C125b"></A><A HREF="lmcolor.html#ofZ220marj"><B>lmcolor</B></A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A228C125c"></A><A HREF="lmdef.html#rgZ2250marj"><B>lmdef</B></A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A228C125d"></A><A HREF="n3f.html#A139X91ef3"><B>n3f</B></A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A228C125e"></A><A HREF="normal.html#A142X9b7"><B>normal</B></A> </LI>

<LI><A NAME="A228C125f"></A><A HREF="RGBcolor.html#A143X9394"><B>RGBcolor</B></A> </LI>

<LI><A NAME="A228C1260"></A><A HREF="v.html#A144X97a4"><B>v</B></A> </LI></UL>


<P><A NAME="E1B0501658ceb"></A>Use the <A HREF="lmbind.html#XeZ2340marj"><B>lmbind</B></A> and <A HREF="lmdef.html#rgZ2250marj"><B>lmdef</B></A> subroutines to respecify only materials and their properties.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0501766ceb"></A>If you want to use the <A HREF="backface.html#A143X974b"><B>backface</B></A> subroutine, specify the vertices of the first triangle in counterclockwise order. All triangles in the mesh have the same rotation as the first triangle in a mesh so that backfacing works correctly.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015d6a"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0501926ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0502038ceb"></A>The POWER Gt4 and POWER Gt4x adapters support only a limited number of vertices between the <B>bgntmesh</B> and <B>endtmesh</B> subroutines. The actual limit can vary from less than 200 vertices to more than 400 vertices, depending on whether or not colors, normals, or material properties are specified between the begin and end pair. If only vertices are specified between a begin and end pair, then at least 255 vertices are supported. Specifying normals, colors, material properties, or the <B>swaptmesh</B> subroutine decreases the overall maximum. If all attributes are specified, only 198 vertices are supported.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0502147ceb"></A>The POWERgraphics GTO and the 3D Color Graphics Processor support a maximum of 255 vertices between the <B>bgntmesh</B> and <B>endtmesh</B> subroutines.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3CBCD36402bolt"></A>The POWERgraphics GXT1000 supports an arbitrary number of vertices between the <B>bgntmesh</B> and <B>endtmesh</B> subroutines. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A77C1368"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C1369"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C136a"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A258C01c3e4"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0502467ceb"></A>Setting the current color in RGB mode with the <A HREF="c.html#A143X9262"><B>c</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0502573ceb"></A>Toggling the triangle mesh register pointer with the <A HREF="swaptmesh.html#A144X9782"><B>swaptmesh</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0502681ceb"></A>Transferring a vertex to the graphics pipe with the <A HREF="v.html#A144X97a4"><B>v</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0502788ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A>, Drawing with <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawbeg-end.html">Begin-End Style</A> Subroutines, and Understanding the <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/glintro.html#A8G44310marj">Hardware Used by GL</A> in<I> GL3.2 Version 4 for AIX: Programming Concepts</I>.</P><hr><center>

</TITLE>
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="bgntmesh.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="blankscreen.html">Next</a>  |

 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A251X98d"></A>bgntrim or endtrim Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX128" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX129" REL="I2" TITLE="NURBS curves and surfaces"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX130" REL="I3" TITLE="bgntrim"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX131" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX132" REL="I2" TITLE="surface (NURBS)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX133" REL="I3" TITLE="trimming loop"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX134" REL="I1" TITLE="endtrim subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX135" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX136" REL="I2" TITLE="NURBS curves and surfaces"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX137" REL="I3" TITLE="endtrim"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX138" REL="I1" TITLE="bgntrim subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A251X98f"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B051F651ceb"></A>Delimit a NURBS surface trimming loop.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C1335"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B051F798ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B051F902ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A251X992"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A251X993"></A><B>void bgntrim(&nbsp;)</B>
<B>void endtrim(&nbsp;)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A251X96c"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A251X96f"></A><B>SUBROUTINE BGNTRI</B>
<B>SUBROUTINE ENDTRI</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A251X996"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0520266ceb"></A>The <B>bgntrim </B>and <B>endtrim </B>subroutines mark the beginning and end of a definition for a trimming loop. A trimming loop is a set of oriented curves (forming a closed curve) that defines boundaries of a Non-Rational B-Spline (NURBS) surface. Include these trimming loop definitions in the definition of a NURBS surface.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0520376ceb"></A>The definition for a NURBS surface may contain many trimming loops. For example, in a definition for NURBS surface that resembles a rectangle with a hole punched out, there are two trimming loops. One loop defines the outer edge of the rectangle. The other trimming loop defines the hole punched out of the rectangle. The definitions of each of these trimming loops is bracketed by a <B>bgntrim/endtrim </B>pair.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0520487ceb"></A>The definition of a single closed trimming loop may consist of multiple curve segments, each described as a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#rEf3b0nita">piecewise linear curve</A> (as defined by the <A HREF="pwlcurve.html#A257X9fc"><B>pwlcurve</B></A> subroutine), or as a single NURBS curve (as defined by the <A HREF="nurbscurve.html#A255X93ca"><B>nurbscurve</B></A> subroutine), or as a combination of both in any order. The only GL subroutines that can appear in a trimming loop definition (between the <B>bgntrim</B> and <B>endtrim</B> subroutines) are the <B>pwlcurve</B> and <B>nurbscurve</B> subroutines.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0520593ceb"></A>The following code fragment defines a single trimming loop that consists of one piecewise linear curve and two NURBS curves: </P>
<PRE><A NAME="A251X99b"></A>bgntrim();&nbsp;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;pwlcurve(...);&nbsp;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;nurbscurve(...);&nbsp;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;nurbscurve(...);&nbsp;
endtrim();</PRE>

<P><A NAME="E1B0520760ceb"></A>The area of the NURBS surface that the system displays is the region in the domain to the left of the trimming curve as the curve parameter increases. Thus, the resultant visible region of the NURBS surface is inside for a counterclockwise trimming loop and outside for a clockwise trimming loop. For the rectangle mentioned previously, the trimming loop for the outer edge of the rectangle should run counterclockwise, and the trimming loop for the hole punched out should run clockwise.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0520868ceb"></A>If you use more than one curve to define a single trimming loop, the curve segments must form a closed loop. In other words, the endpoint of each curve must be the starting point of the next curve, and the endpoint of the final curve must be the starting point of the first curve. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0520976ceb"></A>If the endpoints of the curve are sufficiently close together but not exactly coincident, the system coerces the endpoints to match. If the endpoints are not sufficiently close, the system generates an error message and ignores the entire trimming loop.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0521086ceb"></A>If a trimming loop definition contains multiple curves, the direction of the curves must be consistent. In other words, the inside must be to the left of the curves. Nested trimming loops are legal as long as the curve orientations alternate correctly. If no trimming information is given for a NURBS surface, the entire surface is drawn.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015d9a"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0521246ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C1338"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C1339"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C133a"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A251X9a3"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0521565ceb"></A>Marking the beginning and end of a NURBS surface definition with the <A HREF="bgnsurface.html#A251X9d7"><B>bgnsurface</B> and <B>endsurface</B></A> subroutines. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0521671ceb"></A>Returning the current value of a trimmed NURBS surfaces display property with the <A HREF="getnurbsproperty.html#A252X986e"><B>getnurbsproperty</B></A> subroutine. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0521780ceb"></A>Controlling the shape of a NURBS trimming curve with the <A HREF="nurbscurve.html#A255X93ca"><B>nurbscurve</B></A> subroutine. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0521887ceb"></A>Controlling the shape of a NURBS surface with the <A HREF="nurbssurface.html#A252X98b9"><B>nurbssurface</B></A> subroutine. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0521994ceb"></A>Describing a piecewise linear trimming curve for NURBS surfaces with the <A HREF="pwlcurve.html#A257X9fc"><B>pwlcurve</B></A> subroutine. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0522101ceb"></A>Setting a property for the display of trimmed NURBS with the <A HREF="setnurbsproperty.html#A257X911b"><B>setnurbsproperty</B></A> subroutine. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0522209ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A> and Drawing <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawnurbs.html#drawnurbs.html">NURBS Curves and Surfaces</A>.</P><hr><center>

<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A144X9128"></A>blankscreen Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX139" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX140" REL="I2" TITLE="window"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX141" REL="I3" TITLE="blankscreen"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX142" REL="I1" TITLE="blankscreen subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX143" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX144" REL="I2" TITLE="windows"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX145" REL="I3" TITLE="controlling screen refresh"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A144X912a"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0545571ceb"></A>Turns screen refresh on and off.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C12ab"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0545720ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0545823ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A144X912e"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A144X911a"></A><B>void blankscreen(Int32</B> <A HREF="blankscreen.html#A144X9114"><I>bool</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A144X9118"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A17C0d9af"></A><B>SUBROUTINE BLANKS(</B><I>bool</I><B>)</B>
<B>LOGICAL</B><I> bool</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A144X9130"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0546189ceb"></A>The <B>blankscreen </B>subroutine turns screen refresh on and off. Normally, the screen is refreshed 60 times a second. If the screen is not regularly refreshed, it goes blank. The screen refresh is turned on or off immediately upon invocation of this subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0546300ceb"></A>The action of this subroutine is not affected by the <A HREF="blanktime.html#A144X9178"><B>blanktime</B></A> subroutine. The <B>blankscreen</B> subroutine affects the entire screen, not just an individual window.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><B>Notes: </B>
<OL><LI><A NAME="A79C12ae"></A>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</LI>

<LI><A NAME="A79C12af"></A>This call is intended for use by a window manager. If a window manager is already running, it is possible that this call will be overridden by the window manager.</LI></OL></BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A144X9132"></A>Parameter</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A144X9114"></A><I>bool</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies a value for the screen display. The settings for the <I>bool</I> parameter are:</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X9124f8"></A></TD>
<TD>  True = Display stops and screen turns black <I>immediately</I>. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X9124f9"></A></TD>
<TD>  False = Display is restored.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015ca9"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0546834ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C12b0"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C12b1"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C12b2"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A144X9148"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0547163ceb"></A>Setting the screen-blanking time out with the <A HREF="blanktime.html#A144X9178"><B>blanktime</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A144X9178"></A>blanktime Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX146" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX147" REL="I2" TITLE="window"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX148" REL="I3" TITLE="blanktime"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX149" REL="I1" TITLE="blanktime subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX150" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX151" REL="I2" TITLE="windows"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX152" REL="I3" TITLE="setting screen blanking timeout"></A>

<H3><A NAME="C41D7B2833nqui"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0566362ceb"></A>Sets the screen-blanking timeout.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C12b4"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0566541ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0566645ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="C41D7B3114nqui"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A144X916a"></A><B>void blanktime(Int32</B> <A HREF="blanktime.html#A144X9164"><I>nframe</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A144X9169"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A17C0d9b0"></A><B>SUBROUTINE BLANKT(</B><I>nframe</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4</B> <I>nframe</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="C41D7B3343nqui"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0567011ceb"></A>The <B>blanktime</B> subroutine changes the amount of time the system waits before it blanks the screen to protect the color display. The default delay before the screen turns black is 15 minutes after the last input. This subroutine can also disable the screen-blanking feature. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0567122ceb"></A>To calculate the value of the <A HREF="blanktime.html#A144X9164"><I>nframe</I></A> parameter, multiply the desired blanking delay period (in seconds) by 60. For example, when <I>nframe </I>is 18000, the blanking delay period is 5 minutes. If there are 60 frames per second, <I>nframe </I>is 60 times the number of seconds that the system waits before blanking the screen. To disable screen blanking, use 0 (zero) as the value for <I>nframe. </I></P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><B>Notes: </B>
<OL><LI><A NAME="A258C01c328"></A>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</LI>

<LI><A NAME="A258C01c329"></A>This call is intended for use by a window manager. If a window manager is already running, it is possible that this call will be overridden by the window manager.</LI></OL></BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="C41D7B3713nqui"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A144X9164"></A><I>nframe</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the number of frames after which to blank the screen. This subroutine assumes 60 frames per second.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015cab"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0567547ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C12b7"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C12b8"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C12b9"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A144X9198"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0567866ceb"></A>Turning screen refresh off or on with the <A HREF="blankscreen.html#A144X9128"><B>blankscreen</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0567976ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/managewinds.html#managewinds.html">Creating and Managing Windows</A>, <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/glintro.html#A8G44310marj">Understanding the Hardware Used by GL</A>, <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/underwininput.html#underwininput.html">Windows and Input Control</A>.</P><hr><center>

<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">
<HTML>
<HEAD>
<META HTTP-EQUIV="Content-Type" CONTENT="text/html; charset=iso-8859-1">

<TITLE>blendfunction Subroutine
</TITLE>
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="blanktime.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="blink.html">Next</a>  |
<A href="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A143X9240"></A>blendfunction Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX153" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX154" REL="I2" TITLE="frame buffer update control"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX155" REL="I3" TITLE="blendfunction"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX156" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX157" REL="I2" TITLE="alpha blending ratio"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX158" REL="I3" TITLE="specifying"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX159" REL="I1" TITLE="blendfunction subroutine (GL)"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A143X9242"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0587936ceb"></A>Specifies the function to be used for alpha blending.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C11df"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0588085ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0588189ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9246"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A143X9247"></A><B>void blendfunction(Int32 </B><A HREF="blendfunction.html#A143X924b"><I>sfactor</I></A><B>, Int32 </B><A HREF="blendfunction.html#A143X924c"><I>dfactor</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A28C01077d"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A28C01077e"></A><B>SUBROUTINE BLENDF(</B><I>sfactor</I><B>, </B><I>dfactor</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>sfactor</I><B>, </B><I>dfactor</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9248"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0588559ceb"></A>In <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0743">RGB mode</A>, the system draws 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P06fd">pixels</A> using a function that blends the current (destination) RGBA values of the pixel with the RGBA values to be superimposed on that pixel (the source values). </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0588667ceb"></A>Most often, blending is simple: the source RGBA values replace the destination RGBA values of the pixel. However, if a colored transparent
 <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0702">primitive</A> is drawn on top of another primitive, then the RGBA values of the new primitive must be blended with the RGBA values of the underlying primitive. (The transparency or opacity of a primitive can be stored as an alpha value.) </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0588774ceb"></A>To determine the blended RGBA values of a pixel when drawing in RGB mode, the system uses the following functions:</P>
<PRE><A NAME="A139X91ed4"></A>Rblended = (Rsource * sfactor) + (Rdestination * dfactor) 
Gblended = (Gsource * sfactor) + (Gdestination * dfactor)
Bblended = (Bsource * sfactor) + (Bdestination * dfactor) 
Ablended = (Asource * sfactor) + (Adestination * dfactor)</PRE>

<P><A NAME="E1B0588940ceb"></A>where R is a red value, G is a green value, B is a blue value, and A is an alpha value.  Blending is available with or without z-buffer mode. Blending works properly only in 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0743">RGB mode</A>.  In 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A25P03e3">color map mode</A>, the results are unpredictable. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0589050ceb"></A>Blending is effectively deactivated by setting the <A HREF="blendfunction.html#A143X924b"><I>sfactor</I></A> parameter to BF_ONE  and  <A HREF="blendfunction.html#A143X924c"><I>dfactor</I></A> to BF_ZERO (the default values). RGB mode fill rates are significantly higher when blending is effectively deactivated.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0589159ceb"></A>By default, the destination RGBA values are read from the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P051c">front buffer</A> in 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A27P01c">single buffer mode</A> and from the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P051c">back buffer</A> in 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0474">double buffer mode</A>. If the front buffer is not enabled in single buffer mode, the RGBA values are taken from the z-buffer. If the back buffer is not enabled in double buffer mode, the RGBA values are taken from the front buffer (if possible) or from the z-buffer. These default values can be changed with the <A HREF="readsource.html#A142X9cc0"><B>readsource</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0589267ceb"></A>Blending factors use RGBA values converted to percentages of maximum value (255 in current hardware). To improve performance, conversion calculations are approximate. However, 0 converts exactly to 0.0, and maximum value converts exactly to 1.0.</P>

<TABLE BORDER="2"><TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD COLSPAN="2"><B>Symbolic Constants</B></TD>

<TD><BR></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>C</B></TD>

<TD><B>FORTRAN</B></TD>

<TD><B>Description</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>BF_ZERO</TD>

<TD>BFZERO</TD>

<TD>0</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>BF_ONE</TD>

<TD>BFONE</TD>

<TD>1</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>BF_DC</TD>

<TD>BFDC</TD>

<TD>(destination RGBA)/(maximum value)</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>BF_SC</TD>

<TD>BFSC</TD>

<TD>(source RGBA)/(maximum value)</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>BF_MDC</TD>

<TD>BFMDC</TD>

<TD>1 - (destination RGBA)/(maximum value)</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>BF_MSC</TD>

<TD>BFMSC</TD>

<TD>1 - (source RGBA)/(maximum value)</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>BF_SA</TD>

<TD>BFSA</TD>

<TD>(source alpha)/(maximum value)</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>BF_MSA</TD>

<TD>BFMSA</TD>

<TD>1 - (source alpha)/(maximum value)</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>BF_DA</TD>

<TD>BFDA</TD>

<TD>(destination alpha)/(maximum value)</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>BF_MDA</TD>

<TD>BFMDA</TD>

<TD>1 - (destination alpha)/(maximum value)</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X924a"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X924b"></A><I>sfactor </I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies a symbolic constant that identifies the blending factor by which to scale contributions from source (incoming) pixel RGBA (red, green, blue, alpha) values.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X924c"></A><I>dfactor </I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies a symbolic constant that identifies the blending factor by which to scale contributions from destination (current) pixel RGBA values.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X925a"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0589756ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3CBCE1E731bolt"></A>The POWERgraphics GXT1000 supports source alpha blending. However, the GXT1000 does not support destination alpha blending. Destination blending is available using OpenGL.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0589936ceb"></A>When rendering semi-transparent polygons, it is recommended that z-buffering should be enabled, with the the z compare function set to ZF_LESS. Because the POWERgraphics GTO graphics adapter always renders "fat" triangles (that is, non-point sampled triangles whose upper and left edges are one pixel wider than those of a point-sampled triangle), the edges of bordering triangles are drawn twice, and thus double-blended, unless z-buffering is used to eliminate the double-rendering of edges. The POWERgraphics GTO graphics adapter forms all polygons into triangles; thus, the internal form of the polygon's edges become visible unless z-buffering is used to eliminate the edges.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B058A046ceb"></A>The POWERgraphics GTO graphics adapter supports transparency by implementing a limited subset of the <B>blendfunction</B> subroutine functionality. The BF_SA and BF_MSA alpha-blending modes are supported when used in combination.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B058A164ceb"></A>Semi-transparent lines and polygons are supported (this class includes circles, arcs, spline curves and NURBS surfaces); semi transparent blits (including raster text) are not supported. The alpha-blending factor must be a constant for the entire primitive; the interpolation of alpha values from vertex to vertex is not supported. Alpha values can be set with the <B>cpack</B>, <B>c4[isf]</B>, or<B> lmdef</B> subroutines.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C11e2"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C11e3"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C11e4"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9260"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B058A485ceb"></A>Specifying RGBA color with a single, packed 32-bit integer using the <A HREF="cpack.html#A143X9284"><B>cpack</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B058A597ceb"></A>Specifying the source for pixels to be read with the <A HREF="readsource.html#A142X9cc0"><B>readsource</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B058A704ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/writemasks.html#writemasks.html">Writemasks and Logical Operations</A>, and Working in <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/workcolor.html#workcolor.html">Color Map and RGB Modes</A>.</P><hr><center>

<a href="blink.html">Next</a>  |

</center></BODY>

<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">
<HTML>
<HEAD>
<META HTTP-EQUIV="Content-Type" CONTENT="text/html; charset=iso-8859-1">

<TITLE>blink Subroutine
</TITLE>
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="blendfunction.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="blkqread.html">Next</a>  |
<A href="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A146X937c"></A>blink Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX160" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX161" REL="I2" TITLE="animation"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX162" REL="I3" TITLE="blink"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX163" REL="I1" TITLE="blink subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX164" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX165" REL="I2" TITLE="color map"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX166" REL="I3" TITLE="changing"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A146X937e"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B05A8637ceb"></A>Changes a color map entry at a selectable rate.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A77C17"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B05A8784ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B05A8888ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A146X9381"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B05A9046ceb"></A><B>void blink(Int16 </B><A HREF="blink.html#A146X9368"><I>rate</I></A><B>, Colorindex </B><A HREF="blink.html#mgJ1350marj"><I>color</I></A><B>, Int16 </B><A HREF="blink.html#EiJ130marj"><I>red</I></A><B>, Int16 </B><A HREF="blink.html#KlJ1f0marj"><I>green</I></A><B>, Int16 </B><A HREF="blink.html#llJ1270marj"><I>blue</I></A><B>)</B></P>

<H3><A NAME="A146X9359"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A146X935c"></A><B>SUBROUTINE BLINK(</B><I>rate</I><B>,</B> <I>color</I><B>,</B> <I>red</I><B>,</B><I> green</I><B>,</B><I> blue</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>rate</I><B>,</B> <I>color</I><B>,</B> <I>red</I><B>,</B><I> green</I><B>,</B><I> blue</I></PRE>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A77C1a"></A><B>Note: </B>For FORTRAN users, this subroutine accepts long integer parameters (INTEGER*4) when started from a FORTRAN program, although it accepts short integers when started from a C program. The C and FORTRAN syntax shown here reflect this difference.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A146X9385"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B05A9368ceb"></A>The <B>blink</B> subroutine alternates the color located at index <A HREF="blink.html#mgJ1350marj"><I>color</I></A> in the current color map with the color defined by the parameters <A HREF="blink.html#EiJ130marj"><I>red</I></A>, <A HREF="blink.html#KlJ1f0marj"><I>green</I></A>, and <A HREF="blink.html#llJ1270marj"><I>blue</I></A>. The rate at which the two colors are alternated is set by the <A HREF="blink.html#A146X9368"><I>rate</I></A> parameter.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B05A9477ceb"></A>Up to 20 colors can blink simultaneously, each at a different rate. The blink rate is changed by calling the <B>blink</B> subroutine with the same <I>color</I> parameter and a different <I>rate</I> parameter.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B05A9586ceb"></A>For example, if the <I>rate</I> parameter is 3, the color changes (blinks) every third vertical retrace. Its value alternates between the original value and the new value supplied by the parameters <A HREF="blink.html#EiJ130marj"><I>red</I></A>, <A HREF="blink.html#KlJ1f0marj"><I>green</I></A>, and <A HREF="blink.html#llJ1270marj"><I>blue</I></A>.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B05A9693ceb"></A>The length of time between retraces varies according to the monitor used. When using a 60Hz monitor, a rate of 60 would cause the color to change once every second.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B05A9801ceb"></A>To terminate blinking and restore the original color for a single color map entry, set the <A HREF="blink.html#mgJ1350marj"><I>color</I></A> parameter to the color map entry for which to stop blinking and call the <B>blink</B> subroutine with the <A HREF="blink.html#A146X9368"><I>rate</I></A> parameter set to 0.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B05A9910ceb"></A>To terminate all blinking colors simultaneously, call the <B>blink</B> subroutine with the <I>rate</I> parameter set to -1. When <I>rate</I> is -1, the other parameters are ignored. </P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9c75"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A146X938a"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A146X9368"></A><I>rate</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the number of vertical retraces per blink. On a standard 60 Hz monitor, there are 60 vertical retraces per second.  </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="mgJ1350marj"></A><I>color</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the index into the current color map. The color defined at that index is the color that is blinked (alternated).  </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="EiJ130marj"></A><I>red</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the red value of the alternate color that blinks against the color selected from the color map by the <I>color</I> parameter.  </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="KlJ1f0marj"></A><I>green</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the green value of the alternate color that blinks against the color selected from the color map by the <I>color</I> parameter.  </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="llJ1270marj"></A><I>blue</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the blue value of the alternate color that blinks against the color selected from the color map by the <I>color</I> parameter.  </TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015ca5"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B05AA516ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B05AA623ceb"></A>The POWER GXT1000 adapter does not support the <B>blink</B> subroutine.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A146X9376"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C1b"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C1c"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="WU1f0nick"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B05AA940ceb"></A>Setting the current color in color map mode with the <A HREF="color.html#A146X9429"><B>color</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A143X91fc"></A>blkqread Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX167" REL="I1" TITLE="blqread subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX168" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX169" REL="I2" TITLE="query"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX170" REL="I3" TITLE="blqread"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX171" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX172" REL="I2" TITLE="queue"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX173" REL="I3" TITLE="reading event queue entries"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX174" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX175" REL="I2" TITLE="queue and device"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX176" REL="I3" TITLE="blqread"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX177" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX178" REL="I2" TITLE="device"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A143X91fe"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B05C8433ceb"></A>Reads multiple entries from the event queue.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1138"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B05C8582ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B05C8685ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9202"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A143X9203"></A><B>Int32 blkqread(Int16 *</B><A HREF="blkqread.html#A143X9207"><I>data</I></A><B>, Int16</B> <A HREF="blkqread.html#A143X9208"><I>number</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A27C010474"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A27C010475"></A><B>INTEGER*4 FUNCTION BLKQRE(</B><I>data</I><B>, </B><I>number</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*2 </B><I>data</I><B>(</B><I>number</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>number</I></PRE>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A213X912c57"></A><B>Note: </B>For FORTRAN users, this function accepts long integer parameters (INTEGER*4) when invoked from a FORTRAN program, although it accepts short integers when invoked from a C program. The C and FORTRAN syntax shown here reflect this difference.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A143X9204"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B05C9109ceb"></A>The <B>blkqread</B> subroutine reads multiple entries from the <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/cntrlques.html#A29C0109de">event queue</A> and stores them in the buffer designated by the <A HREF="blkqread.html#A143X9207"><I>data</I></A> parameter.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B05C9218ceb"></A>The returned value of the function is the number of queue entries actually read into the <I>data</I> buffer. This function fills the <I>data </I>buffer alternatively with device numbers and device values. Thus, the number of entries read is never more than the value or the <A HREF="blkqread.html#A143X9208"><I>number</I></A> parameter divided by two. </P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9f98"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A143X9206"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X9207"></A><I>data </I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies a pointer to the buffer that is to receive the queue information.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X9208"></A><I>number</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the length of the buffer.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X920a"></A>Return Value</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B05C9600ceb"></A>The number of 16-bit words of data actually read into the buffer pointed to by the <I>data</I> parameter. This number is twice the number of complete queue entries read because each queue entry consists of two 16-bit words.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A61C015a0a"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B05C9762ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9218"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C113b"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C113c"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C113d"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/device.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C113e"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fdevice.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X921c"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B05CA194ceb"></A>Enabling an input device for event queuing with the <A HREF="qdevice.html#A143X967"><B>qdevice</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B05CA311ceb"></A>Reading the first entry in the event queue with the <A HREF="qread.html#A143X989"><B>qread</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B05CA418ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A>, <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/cntrlques.html#cntrlques.html">Controlling Queues and Devices</A>.</P><hr><center>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">

<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A16C0c7bb"></A>boxcirc.c Example C Language Program
</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX2183" REL="I1" TITLE="boxcirc.c example program (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2184" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2185" REL="I2" TITLE="example programs"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2186" REL="I3" TITLE="drawing"></A>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E9A6524ttay"></A>/*
boxcirc.c:</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E9A6694ttay"></A>A simple example which draw a 2d box and circle, press ESCape key
to exit.
*/</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E9A6850ttay"></A>#include &lt;gl/gl.h>
#include &lt;gl/device.h></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E9A6997ttay"></A>main()
{    </PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E9A7146ttay"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;int&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;dev,val;    </PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E9A7295ttay"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;initialize();    </PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E9A7525ttay"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;while (TRUE) {        
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;if (qtest()) {            
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;dev = qread(&amp;val);            
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;if (dev == ESCKEY) {
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;gexit();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;exit();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;}
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;else if (dev == REDRAW) {
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;reshapeviewport();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;drawboxcirc();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;}
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;}
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;}
}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E9A7672ttay"></A>initialize()
{</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E9A7817ttay"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;int gid;</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E9A7987ttay"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;prefposition(XMAXSCREEN/4, XMAXSCREEN*3/4, YMAXSCREEN/4, 
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;    YMAXSCREEN*3/4);</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E9A8159ttay"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;gid = winopen("boxcirc");
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;qdevice(ESCKEY);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;qdevice(REDRAW);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;qenter(REDRAW,gid);</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E9A8302ttay"></A>}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E9A8450ttay"></A>drawboxcirc()
{</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E9A8650ttay"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;pushmatrix();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;translate(200.0, 200.0, 0.0);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(BLACK);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;clear();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(BLUE);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;recti(0, 0, 100, 100);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(RED);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;circi(50, 50, 50);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;popmatrix();</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E9A8792ttay"></A>}</PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A200C1119"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D777C424ceb"></A>The <A HREF="circ.html#ZJpnita"><B>circ</B></A> subroutine<A HREF="ZJpnita" REL="PAGENUM"></A>, <A HREF="clear.html#cEH1160marj"><B>clear</B></A> subroutine<A HREF="cEH1160marj" REL="PAGENUM"></A>, <A HREF="color.html#A146X9429"><B>color</B></A> or <B>colorf</B> subroutine<A HREF="A146X9429" REL="PAGENUM"></A>.</P>

<H2><A NAME="A143X9262"></A>c Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX179" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX180" REL="I2" TITLE="attribute"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX181" REL="I3" TITLE="c"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX182" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX183" REL="I2" TITLE="colors"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX184" REL="I3" TITLE="current"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX185" REL="I1" TITLE="c subroutine (GL)"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A143X9264"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B05EC242ceb"></A>Sets the current color in RGB mode.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A77C158"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B05EC389ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B05EC494ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9268"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<TABLE BORDER="2"><TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>  </B></TD>

<TD><B>3-D</B></TD>

<TD><B>4-D</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>Int16</B></TD>

<TD><B>void c3s(Int16 </B><I>vector</I>[3])</TD>

<TD><B>void c4s(Int16 </B><I>vector</I>[4])</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>Int32</B></TD>

<TD><B>void c3i(Int32 </B><I>vector</I>[3])</TD>

<TD><B>void c4i(Int32 </B><I>vector</I>[4])</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>float</B></TD>

<TD><B>void c3f(float </B><I>vector</I>[3])</TD>

<TD><B>void c4f(float </B><I>vector</I>[4])</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A19C0e0dc"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<TABLE BORDER="2"><TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>  </B></TD>

<TD><B>3-D</B></TD>

<TD><B>4-D</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>INTEGER*2</B></TD>

<TD><B>SUBROUTINE C3S(</B><I>vector</I>) INTEGER*2 <I>vector</I>(3)</TD>

<TD><B>SUBROUTINE C4S(</B><I>vector</I>) INTEGER*2 <I>vector</I>(4)</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>INTEGER*4</B></TD>

<TD><B>SUBROUTINE C3I(</B><I>vector</I>) INTEGER*4 <I>vector</I>(3)</TD>

<TD><B>SUBROUTINE C4I(</B><I>vector</I>) INTEGER*4 <I>vector</I>(4)</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>FLOAT</B></TD>

<TD><B>SUBROUTINE C3F(</B><I>vector</I>) REAL <I>vector</I>(3)</TD>

<TD><B>SUBROUTINE C4F(</B><I>vector</I>) REAL <I>vector</I>(4)</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X926a"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B05EC855ceb"></A>The <B>c</B> subroutine changes the current 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0742">RGBA</A>
 (red, green, blue, alpha) color. Array components 0, 1, 2, and 3 are red, green, blue, and alpha, respectively. In the three-component cases, alpha defaults to 1.0 (float) or 255 (integer).</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B05EC970ceb"></A>Floating-point components range from 0.0 through 1.0. Integer components range from 0 through 255.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A139X91ed5"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine is available only in 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0743">RGB mode</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A143X926c"></A>Parameter</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X926d"></A><I>vector</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies, for the <B>c4</B> subroutines, a four-element array containing RGBA (red, green, blue, and alpha) values. For <B>c3</B> subroutines, a three-element array containing 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A255B9de">RGB values</A>.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X926e"></A></TD>
<TD>  Array components 0, 1, 2, and 3 are red, green, blue, and alpha respectively.  Floating point 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0742">RGBA values</A> range from 0.0 through 1.0.  Integer RGBA values range from 0 through 255.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9272"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B05ED345ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="cylinder1_c.html#Ggi2e0marj"><B>cylinder1.c</B></A> calls the <B>c3f</B> subroutine, with a three element array initialized with all zeros as the <I>vector</I> parameter, to clear the screen to black.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A11C0b4b7"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C15b"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C15c"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X927c"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B05ED664ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B05ED771ceb"></A>If your system does not have alpha bitplanes, set the alpha values to zero.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9282"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B05ED933ceb"></A>Setting the current color in color map mode with the <A HREF="color.html#A146X9429"><B>color</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B05EE041ceb"></A>Specifying RGBA color with a single packed 32-bit integer using the <A HREF="cpack.html#A143X9284"><B>cpack</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B05EE148ceb"></A>Returning the current color in RGB mode with the <A HREF="gRGBcolor.html#ESL13a0marj"><B>gRGBcolor</B></A> subroutine.  </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B05EE257ceb"></A>Setting the current color in RGB mode with the <A HREF="RGBcolor.html#A143X9394"><B>RGBcolor</B></A> subroutine.</P>
