<H2><A NAME="A142X91c8"></A>callobj Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX186" REL="I1" TITLE="callobj subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX187" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX188" REL="I2" TITLE="object (display list)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX189" REL="I3" TITLE="callobj"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX190" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX191" REL="I2" TITLE="object (display list)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX192" REL="I3" TITLE="drawing an instance of"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A142X91ca"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B060A916ceb"></A>Draws an instance of an object (display list).</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C17"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B060B065ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B060B171ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A142X91ce"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A142X91cf"></A><B>void callobj(Int32 </B><A HREF="callobj.html#A142X91d3"><I>object</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010a62"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010a63"></A><B>SUBROUTINE CALLOB(</B><I>object</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>object</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A142X91d0"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B060B532ceb"></A>The <B>callobj</B> subroutine draws an instance of a previously defined 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A> (object). If the subroutine specifies an undefined object, the system ignores the routine. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B060B641ceb"></A>Global state 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A78P0561">attributes</A> are not saved before a call to the <B>callobj</B> subroutine. Thus, if you change a variable within an object, such as color, the change can affect the caller as well. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B060B749ceb"></A>Use the <A HREF="pushattributes.html#Thx220marj"><B>pushattributes</B></A> and <A HREF="popattributes.html#Vmx2140marj"><B>popattributes</B></A> subroutines to preserve global state attributes across calls. Also, the object may execute transformations that change the matrix stack. Use the <A HREF="pushmatrix.html#A144X9540"><B>pushmatrix</B></A> and <A HREF="popmatrix.html#A144X951e"><B>popmatrix</B></A> subroutines to restore the state of the matrix stack. </P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A29C010a64"></A><B>Note: </B>This editing subroutine can be added to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A142X91d2"></A>Parameter</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A142X91d3"></A><I>object</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the identifier of the object to be drawn.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A30C010ff8"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B060C067ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="depthcue_c.html#A16C0c8ff"><B>depthcue.c</B></A> uses the <B>callobj</B> subroutine, after specifying a rotation transformation, to rotate a graphical object (a cube). </P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015cf0"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B060C227ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1a"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1b"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1c"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A142X91e8"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B060C545ceb"></A>Creating an object with the <A HREF="makeobj.html#A142X912d"><B>makeobj</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B060C652ceb"></A>Popping the attribute stack with the <A HREF="popattributes.html#Vmx2140marj"><B>popattributes</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B060C760ceb"></A>Popping the transformation matrix stack with the <A HREF="popmatrix.html#A144X951e"><B>popmatrix</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B060C867ceb"></A>Saving the global state attributes with the <A HREF="pushattributes.html#Thx220marj"><B>pushattributes</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B060C974ceb"></A>Pushing down the transformation matrix stack with the <A HREF="pushmatrix.html#A144X9540"><B>pushmatrix</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/setglattrib.html#setglattrib.html">Setting Drawing Attributes</A>, 
and Working with <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/workcoords.html#workcoords.html">Coordinate Systems</A>.</P><hr><center>

<TITLE>charstr Subroutine
</TITLE>
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="callobj.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="chunksize.html">Next</a>  |

 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A143X9cfb"></A>charstr Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX193" REL="I1" TITLE="charstr subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX194" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX195" REL="I2" TITLE="text"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX196" REL="I3" TITLE="charstr"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX197" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX198" REL="I2" TITLE="text"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX199" REL="I3" TITLE="drawing raster character string"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A143X9cfd"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B062B095ceb"></A>Draws a string of raster characters on the screen.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C120d"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B062B243ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B062B348ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9d01"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A143X9d02"></A><B>void charstr(Char8 *</B><A HREF="charstr.html#A143X9d06"><I>string</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010be5"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010be6"></A><B>SUBROUTINE CHARST(</B><A HREF="charstr.html#A143X9d06"><I>string</I></A>, <A HREF="charstr.html#A143X9d07"><I>length</I></A><B>)</B>
<B>CHARACTER*(*) </B><I>string</I>
<B>INTEGER*4</B> <I>length</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9d03"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B062B713ceb"></A>The <B>charstr </B>subroutine draws a string of text, using the current 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P073b">raster font</A>. After each character is drawn, the character width is added to the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A25P03e9">current character position</A>. The text string is drawn in the current raster font and color, using the current 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A3C0F2A4599mhay">writemask</A>. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B062B821ceb"></A>Characters that are not defined in the current raster font are treated as having zero size and are therefore ignored. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B062B928ceb"></A>The <B>charstr</B> subroutine supports both single- and double-byte raster character renderings.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B062C047ceb"></A>If the current font is a double-byte font, this subroutine expects the first two bytes to represent the first character, the second two bytes to represent the next character, and so on. Double-byte fonts are useful in languages with extremely large character sets such as Japanese and Chinese.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B062C163ceb"></A>If the current font is a single-byte font, each byte represents one character. The ASCII code set is an example of a single-byte font.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B062C271ceb"></A>It is the user's responsibility to determine if the currently bound font is a single- or double-byte font and to pass the appropriate string. To determine the font type, use the <A HREF="getfonttype.html#Y89340nita"><B>getfonttype</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<H4><A NAME="A4758C1819bett"></A>Character Clipping</H4>
<P><A NAME="E1B062C431ceb"></A>The beginning of the string is positioned at the current character position. The string is drawn from left to right, parallel to the surface of the screen. The string is fine clipped to the rectangular area defined with the <B>scrnmask</B> subroutine. The current color and writemask are used. Characters not defined in the current raster font are assumed to have zero width and are not drawn.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B062C540ceb"></A>Strings drawn by the <B>charstr</B> subroutine are subject to clipping and z-buffering. The algorithmic details of this process are as follows:</P>

<OL><LI><A NAME="A4758C3327bett"></A>Trivial accept/trivial reject test. If the start point of the test string (after transformation by all matrices) is <I>not</I> within the NDC unit cube (-w&lt;x,y,z&lt;+w&lt; x,y,z &lt; +1.0) then the <I>entire</I> string is trivially rejected (not drawn).</LI>

<LI><A NAME="A4758C4011bett"></A>If the preceding test passes, then z-buffering proceeds on a pixel-by-pixel basis. At the start point, the string is mapped to window-relative pixel coordinates. The z-value of the reference point is used as the z-value of the entire string. Then, for every pixel of every letter in the string:


<OL TYPE="a"><LI><A NAME="A4758C4436bett"></A>If that pixel is outside of the screenmask, the pixel is not drawn.</LI>

<LI><A NAME="A4758C4940bett"></A>If the pixel is inside the screenmask, then use z-compare. If the z-test passes, then update the frame buffer, <I>and</I> update the z-buffer (for that pixel only).</LI></OL></LI></OL>

<H4><A NAME="A4758C5307bett"></A>Glyph Lookup for SBCS and DBCS Strings</H4>
<P><A NAME="E1B062C947ceb"></A>Each character of the string should be thought of as a <I>glyph index</I>. That is, each byte (for an SBCS font) or each pair of bytes (for a DBCS font) serves as an index into a table of raster glyphs. The table of glyphs is the table that was loaded with the <B>defrasterfont</B> subroutine or the <B>loadXfont</B> subroutine. The mapping of glyph indices to glyphs is a constant, and is locale-independent. There is no processing or translation that is applied to the glyph index before the raster is looked up. The <I>raw</I> value is used unmodified. A single null byte is sufficient to indicate end-of-string for ordinary (single-byte) fonts; a null short integer (two consecutive null bytes) is required to terminate a DBCS string.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B062D058ceb"></A>Because the <B>charstr</B> routine does not perform any translation and conversion, it is left up to the application to make sure that appropriate fonts are loaded, and that multibyte text strings are converted into sequences of glyph indices. Some tools for performing such conversions are provided by the base operating system.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A4758C7309bett"></A><B>Note: </B>The default font (font index 0) is locale-dependent; during initialization, a different default font is loaded, depending on the locale. The default font is always chosen from the iso8859 family of fonts.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A143X9d05"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X9d06"></A><I>string </I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies a pointer to the variable containing the string.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X9d07"></A><I>length</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the length (number of characters) of the string.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A30C011050"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B062D432ceb"></A>The example C language programs <A HREF="curved_c.html#A16C0c830"><B>curved.c</B></A> and <A HREF="font3_c.html#A149C18a9"><B>font3.c</B></A> use the <B>charstr</B> subroutine to draw a character string in the current raster font. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015d82"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B062D592ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1210"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1211"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1212"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9d1b"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B062D914ceb"></A>Determining the font format with the <A HREF="getfonttype.html#Y89340nita"><B>getfonttype</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B062E022ceb"></A>Determining the font name with the <A HREF="getfontencoding.html#Az7960nita"><B>getfontencoding</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B062E130ceb"></A>Moving the current character position with the <A HREF="cmov.html#A143X9d1d"><B>cmov</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B062E237ceb"></A>Defining bitmaps for a raster font with the <A HREF="defrasterfont.html#A143X9d3f"><B>defrasterfont</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B062E346ceb"></A>Selecting a raster font with the <A HREF="font.html#A143X9d61"><B>font</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B062E454ceb"></A>Returning the width of the specified text string with the <A HREF="strwidth.html#A144X93ec"><B>strwidth</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B062E561ceb"></A><!--:genprogc:--><A HREF="../genprogc/nls.html#A2919f7">National Language Support Overview for Programming</A> in<I> AIX General Programming Concepts: Writing and Debugging Programs</I>.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B062E668ceb"></A>Creating <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/textchars.html#textchars.html">Text Characters</A>.</P><hr><center>

<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A142X9c38"></A>chunksize Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX200" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX201" REL="I2" TITLE="object (display list)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX202" REL="I3" TITLE="chunksize"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX203" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX204" REL="I2" TITLE="display list"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX205" REL="I3" TITLE="specifying the amount of memory for"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX206" REL="I1" TITLE="chunksize subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A142X9c3a"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B064A903ceb"></A>Specifies the amount of memory to be allocated for a display list.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1d"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B064B053ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B064B157ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A142X9c3e"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A142X9c3f"></A><B>void chunksize(Int32 </B><A HREF="chunksize.html#A142X9c43"><I>chunk</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010aa1"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010aa2"></A><B>SUBROUTINE CHUNKS(</B><I>chunk</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>chunk</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A142X9c40"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B064B519ceb"></A>The <B>chunksize</B> subroutine gives the system a hint about the appropriate amount of memory to be allocated when compiling a display list. The system may, on occasion, override the hint.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B064B628ceb"></A>As you add primitives to a display list, the <A HREF="chunksize.html#A142X9c43"><I>chunk</I></A> parameter is the unit size (in bytes) by which the memory allocated to the display list grows. The default chunk size is 1024 bytes. A chunk size that is much smaller than the final size of the display list leads to inefficiencies due to fragmentation. A chunk size that is larger than the final display list contains unused, and therefore wasted, memory. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B064B737ceb"></A>Most subroutines add from 4 to 28 bytes to the display list; subroutines that accept arrays as parameters (for example, the <A HREF="poly.html#avf2c0marj"><B>poly</B></A> subroutine and <A HREF="polf.html#Zsf1c0marj"><B>polf</B></A> subroutine) typically add to the display list in proportion to the length of the array. Some experimentation may be necessary to determine the optimal chunk size for an application.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A10C0abff"></A><B>Note: </B>This editing subroutine itself cannot be added to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>. </BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A142X9c42"></A>Parameter</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A142X9c43"></A><I>chunk </I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the minimum memory size to allocate for an object.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015d0c"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B064C061ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C110"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C111"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C112"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A142X9c58"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B064C380ceb"></A>Unfragmenting and compacting the memory storage of an object with the <A HREF="compactify.html#A142X9c5a"><B>compactify</B></A> subroutine. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B064C487ceb"></A>Initializing the system with the <A HREF="ginit.html#LDg21c0marj"><B>ginit</B></A> subroutine. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B064C593ceb"></A>Creating an object with the <A HREF="makeobj.html#A142X912d"><B>makeobj</B></A> subroutine. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B064C702ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A> and Creating <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/workobjects.html#workobjects.html">Objects (Display Lists)</A>.</P><hr><center>

<H2><A NAME="ZJpnita"></A>circ Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX207" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX208" REL="I2" TITLE="high-level drawing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX209" REL="I3" TITLE="circ"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX210" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX211" REL="I2" TITLE="circles"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX212" REL="I3" TITLE="drawing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX213" REL="I1" TITLE="circ subroutine (GL)"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A213X91162a"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B066B810ceb"></A>Outlines a circle.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C125d"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B066B958ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B066C063ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X91162d"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X91162e"></A><B>void circ(Coord </B><A HREF="circ.html#A213X91163a"><I>x</I></A><B>, Coord </B><A HREF="circ.html#A213X91163b"><I>y</I></A><B>, Coord</B> <A HREF="circ.html#A213X91163c"><I>radius</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X91162f"></A><B>void circi(Icoord </B><A HREF="circ.html#A213X91163a"><I>x</I></A><B>, Icoord</B> <A HREF="circ.html#A213X91163b"><I>y</I></A><B>, Icoord</B> <A HREF="circ.html#A213X91163c"><I>radius</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X911630"></A><B>void circs(Scoord </B><A HREF="circ.html#A213X91163a"><I>x</I></A><B>, Scoord</B> <A HREF="circ.html#A213X91163b"><I>y</I></A><B>, Scoord</B> <A HREF="circ.html#A213X91163c"><I>radius</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911608"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X91160b"></A><B>SUBROUTINE CIRC(</B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>, </B><I>radius</I><B>)</B>
<B>REAL </B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>, </B><I>radius</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A28C010742"></A><B>SUBROUTINE CIRCI(</B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>, </B><I>radius</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>, </B><I>radius</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A28C010743"></A><B>SUBROUTINE CIRCS(</B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>, </B><I>radius</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*2 </B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>, </B><I>radius</I></PRE>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A78C1260"></A><B>Note: </B>For FORTRAN users, the INTEGER*2 version, the <B>CIRCS</B> subroutine, should not be called with integer constant parameters. For example, 2 is an integer constant; JJ is an integer variable. The XL FORTRAN compiler, invoked by the <B>xlf</B> command, stores all integer constants as long integers (INTEGER*4), not as short integers (INTEGER*2). Invoking the short version of this subroutine with an integer constant will result in unexpected behavior.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A213X911635"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B066C711ceb"></A>The <B>circ </B>subroutine draws an unfilled circle in the <I>x</I>-<I>y </I>plane (<I>z =</I> 0). The system draws the circle using the current line attributes: 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A31996bc">color</A>, 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A172P1436">linestyle</A>, 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A172P1437">linewidth</A>,
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0741">repeat factor</A>, and 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A3C0F2A4599mhay">writemask</A>. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B066C819ceb"></A>To create a circle that does not lie in the <I>x</I>-<I>y </I>plane, draw the circle in the <I>x</I>-<I>y</I> plane, then rotate or translate the circle. Circles rotated outside the 2-D <I>x</I>-<I>y </I>plane appear as ellipses. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B066C927ceb"></A>All of the routines listed in the syntax are functionally the same. They differ only in the type declarations for the coordinates. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911639"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X91163a"></A><I>x</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>x</I> coordinate of the center of the circle specified in modeling coordinates.   </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X91163b"></A><I>y</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>y</I> coordinate of the center of the circle specified in modeling coordinates.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X91163c"></A><I>radius</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the length of the radius of the circle.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X91163f"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B066D299ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="boxcirc_c.html#A16C0c7bb"><B>boxcirc.c</B></A> uses the <B>circi</B> subroutine to draw a red circle.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015cd0"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B066D459ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C1261"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C1262"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C1263"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X91164f"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B066D776ceb"></A>Drawing a circular arc with the <A HREF="arc.html#tEp310nita"><B>arc</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B066D882ceb"></A>Drawing a filled circular arc with the <A HREF="arcf.html#AJp60nita"><B>arcf</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B066D989ceb"></A>Drawing a filled circle with the <A HREF="circf.html#sJp120nita"><B>circf</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B066E098ceb"></A>Drawing a curve with the <A HREF="crv.html#ZMS220marj"><B>crv</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<H2><A NAME="sJp120nita"></A>circf Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX214" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX215" REL="I2" TITLE="high-level drawing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX216" REL="I3" TITLE="circf"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX217" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX218" REL="I2" TITLE="circles"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX219" REL="I3" TITLE="filled"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX220" REL="I1" TITLE="circf subroutine (GL)"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A213X911682"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B068A673ceb"></A>Draws a filled circle.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C1264"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B068A821ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B068A925ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911685"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X911686"></A><B>void circf(Coord </B><A HREF="circf.html#A213X911692"><I>x</I></A><B>, Coord</B> <A HREF="circf.html#A213X911693"><I>y</I></A><B>, Coord</B> <A HREF="circf.html#A213X911694"><I>radius</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X911687"></A><B>void circfi(Icoord </B><A HREF="circf.html#A213X911692"><I>x</I></A><B>, Icoord</B> <A HREF="circf.html#A213X911693"><I>y</I></A><B>, Icoord</B> <A HREF="circf.html#A213X911694"><I>radius</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X911688"></A><B>void circfs(Scoord </B><A HREF="circf.html#A213X911692"><I>x</I></A><B>, Scoord</B> <A HREF="circf.html#A213X911693"><I>y</I></A><B>, Scoord</B> <A HREF="circf.html#A213X911694"><I>radius</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911660"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X911663"></A><B>SUBROUTINE CIRCF(</B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>, </B><I>radius</I><B>)</B>
<B>REAL </B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>, </B><I>radius</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A28C010745"></A><B>SUBROUTINE CIRCFI(</B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>, </B><I>radius</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>, </B><I>radius</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A28C010746"></A><B>SUBROUTINE CIRCFS(</B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>, </B><I>radius</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*2 </B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>, </B><I>radius</I></PRE>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A78C1267"></A><B>Note: </B>For FORTRAN users, the INTEGER*2 version, the <B>CIRCFS</B> subroutine, should not be called with integer constant parameters. For example, 2 is an integer constant; JJ is an integer variable. The XL FORTRAN compiler, invoked by the <B>xlf</B> command, stores all integer constants as long integers (INTEGER*4), not as short integers (INTEGER*2). Invoking the short version of this subroutine with an integer constant will result in unexpected behavior.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A213X91168d"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B068B608ceb"></A>The <B>circf </B>subroutine draws a filled circle in the <I>x</I>-<I>y </I>plane (<I>z =</I> zero). The system draws the circle using the current area attributes: 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A31996bc">color</A>, 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0741">repeat factor</A>, and 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A3C0F2A4599mhay">writemask</A>. To create a filled circle that does not lie in the <I>x</I>-<I>y </I>plane, draw the circle in the <I>x</I>-<I>y</I> plane, then rotate or translate the circle. Filled circles rotated outside the 2-D <I>x</I>-<I>y </I>plane appear as filled ellipses. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B068B715ceb"></A>All of the routines listed in the syntax are functionally the same. They differ only in the type declarations for the coordinates. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911691"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X911692"></A><I>x</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>x</I> coordinate of the center of the circle specified in 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A27P03d">modeling coordinates</A>.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X911693"></A><I>y</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>y</I> coordinate of the center of the circle specified in modeling coordinates.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X911694"></A><I>radius</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the length of the radius of the circle.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911697"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B068C092ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="tpbig_c.html#A16C0c9bd"><B>tpbig.c</B></A> uses the <B>circf</B> subroutine to draw a scoop of cherry ice cream. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015cd2"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B068C256ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C1268"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C1269"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C126a"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X9116a7"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B068C576ceb"></A>Drawing a circular arc with the <A HREF="arc.html#tEp310nita"><B>arc</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B068C683ceb"></A>Drawing a filled circular arc with the <A HREF="arcf.html#AJp60nita"><B>arcf</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B068C789ceb"></A>Drawing a circle with the <A HREF="circ.html#ZJpnita"><B>circ</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B068C895ceb"></A>Drawing a curve with the <A HREF="crv.html#ZMS220marj"><B>crv</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B068D002ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A>, <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/setglattrib.html#setglattrib.html">Setting Drawing Attributes</A>, and <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawpoly.html#drawpoly.html">Drawing Rectangles, Circles, Arcs, and Polygons</A>.</P><hr><center>

</TITLE>
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>

<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="Ua32d0nita"></A>circuit.c Example C Language Program
</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX2187" REL="I1" TITLE="circuit.c example program (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2188" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2189" REL="I2" TITLE="example programs"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2190" REL="I3" TITLE="writemasks"></A>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E9B2276ttay"></A>Here is a very simple complete program that draws 
power and ground circuitry.  The interface consists of
the keys P draw power rectangles, G draw ground
rectangles, C clear the window, and Q quit.  To draw a
rectangle, press down the left mouse button at one
corner, hold it down and slide to the other corner,
and release it.</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E9B2480ttay"></A>When you use the program, be sure to exit by typing Q.
This resets the four lowest entries in the color map
(which are used by all the windows) back to the default
values. 
*/</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E9B2636ttay"></A>#include &lt;gl/gl.h>
#include &lt;gl/device.h></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E9B2836ttay"></A>#define BACKGROUND      0       /* = 00 */
#define POWER           1       /* = 01 */
#define GROUND          2       /* = 10 */
#define SHORT           3       /* = 11 */</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E9B3585ttay"></A>long    xorg, yorg, xsize, ysize;
main()
{
  short val, drawtype;
  short x1, y1, x2, y2;
  drawtype = GROUND;
  prefposition (0,800,0,800);
  winopen("circuit");
  winconstraints();
  getorigin(&amp;xorg, &amp;yorg);
  getsize (&amp;xsize,&amp;ysize);
  ortho2 (-0.5,(Coord)xsize,-0.5,(Coord)ysize);
  /*Allow any size to work*/
  gconfig();
  mapcolor(0, 255, 255, 255);
  mapcolor(1, 0, 0, 255);
  mapcolor(2, 0, 0, 0);
  mapcolor(3, 255, 0, 0);
  qdevice(PKEY);                /* draw power rectangles */
  qdevice(GKEY);                /* draw ground rectangles */
  qdevice(CKEY);                /* clear screen */
  qdevice(QKEY);                /* quit */
  qdevice(REDRAW);        
  qdevice(LEFTMOUSE); /* mark rectangle corners */
  tie(LEFTMOUSE, MOUSEX, MOUSEY);
  color(0);
  clear();
  while (1)
    switch (qread(&amp;val)) {
    case PKEY:
      drawtype = POWER;
      break;
    case GKEY:
      drawtype = GROUND;
      break;
    case REDRAW:
      reshapeviewport();
      getorigin(&amp;xorg, &amp;yorg);
      getsize (&amp;xsize,&amp;ysize);
      ortho2 (-0.5,(Coord)xsize,-0.5,(Coord)ysize);
      clearscreen();
      gconfig();
    case CKEY:
      clearscreen();
      break;
    case QKEY:                /* restore default colors */
      mapcolor(0, 0, 0, 0);
      mapcolor(1, 255, 0, 0);
      mapcolor(2, 0, 255, 0);
      mapcolor(3, 255, 255, 0);
      return;
    case LEFTMOUSE:
      qread(&amp;x1);
      qread(&amp;y1);
      qread(&amp;val);
      qread(&amp;x2);
      qread(&amp;y2);
      if (drawtype == POWER)
        powerrect(x1-xorg, y1-yorg,
            x2-xorg, y2-yorg);
      else
        groundrect(x1-xorg, y1-yorg,
            x2-xorg, y2-yorg);
      break;
    }</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E9B3806ttay"></A>}
clearscreen()
{
  writemask(3);                /* clear window before drawing. */
  color(BACKGROUND);
  clear();
}
powerrect(x1, y1, x2, y2)
short x1, y1, x2, y2;
{
  writemask(1);
  color(1);
  rectfs(x1, y1, x2, y2);
}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E9B3985ttay"></A>groundrect(x1, y1, x2, y2)
short x1, y1, x2, y2;
{
  writemask(2);
  color(2);
  rectfs(x1, y1, x2, y2);
}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E9B4278ttay"></A>/*
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Changes:
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;-The program now starts from the default size window
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;prefposition (0,800,0,800);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;getsize (&amp;xsize,&amp;ysize);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;qdevice(REDRAW);        
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;-The program now handles resize/redraw
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;case REDRAW:
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;reshapeviewport();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;getorigin(&amp;xorg, &amp;yorg);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;getsize (&amp;xsize,&amp;ysize);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;ortho2 (-0.5,(Coord)xsize,-0.5,(Coord)ysize);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;clearscreen();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;gconfig();
*/</PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A200C111f"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7789542ceb"></A>The <A HREF="writemask.html#A143X9592"><B>writemask</B></A> subroutine<A HREF="A143X9592" REL="PAGENUM"></A>.</P>

<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="cEH1160marj"></A>clear Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX221" REL="I1" TITLE="clear subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX222" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX223" REL="I2" TITLE="initializing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX224" REL="I3" TITLE="clear"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX225" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX226" REL="I2" TITLE="initializing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX227" REL="I3" TITLE="clearing the screenmask"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX228" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX229" REL="I2" TITLE="screenmask"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX230" REL="I3" TITLE="clearing"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912438"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B06AA342ceb"></A>Clears to the screenmask.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C11ab"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B06AA489ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B06AA592ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X91243b"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X91243c"></A><B>void clear(&nbsp;)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010bd4"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010bd5"></A><B>SUBROUTINE CLEAR</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X91243f"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B06AA942ceb"></A>The <B>clear </B>subroutine sets the screen area inside the current 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A27P018">screenmask</A> to the current color, using the current 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A3C0F2A4599mhay">writemask</A> and 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A13791abd">pattern</A>. Only the portion of the current screenmask that is inside the current window is actually cleared.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B06AB051ceb"></A>By default, the screenmask is exactly the same size as the window. Use the <A HREF="scrmask.html#fwN250marj"><B>scrmsk</B></A> subroutine to change the size of the screenmask.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A79C11ae"></A><B>Note: </B>The <A HREF="viewport.html#qrY270marj"><B>viewport</B></A> subroutine resets the screenmask to be precisely the same size as the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A27P039">viewport</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A213X912441"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B06AB263ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="boxcirc_c.html#A16C0c7bb"><B>boxcirc.c</B></A> uses the <B>clear</B> subroutine to clear the viewport before drawing a box and a circle.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A64C016607"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B06AB423ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C11af"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C11b0"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C11b1"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X91244c"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B06AB751ceb"></A>Clearing the color bitplanes and the z-buffer simultaneously with the <A HREF="czclear.html#A143X92c8"><B>czclear</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B06AB868ceb"></A>Drawing a filled screen-aligned rectangle with the <A HREF="sboxf.html#Jte1190marj"><B>sboxf</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B06AB983ceb"></A>Clearing the z-buffer with the <A HREF="zclear.html#A143X97d3"><B>zclear</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B06AC092ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/glintro.html#A8G44310marj">Understanding the Hardware</A> Used by GL in<I> GL3.2 Version 4 for AIX: Programming Concepts</I>.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B06AC199ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/clrrstintgl.html#clrrstintgl.html">Clearing, Resetting, and Initializing GL</A>, <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/setglattrib.html#setglattrib.html">Setting Drawing Attributes</A>, and Using <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/useviewprts.html#useviewprts.html">Viewports and Screenmasks</A>.</P><hr><center>

</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A213X9112de"></A>clkoff or clkon Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX231" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX232" REL="I2" TITLE="keyboard control"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX233" REL="I3" TITLE="clkon"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX234" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX235" REL="I2" TITLE="keyboard control"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX236" REL="I3" TITLE="clkoff"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX237" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX238" REL="I2" TITLE="keyboard click"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX239" REL="I3" TITLE="turning off or on"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX240" REL="I1" TITLE="clkoff subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX241" REL="I1" TITLE="clkon subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A213X9112e0"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B06C8313ceb"></A>Turns on or off the keyboard click.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C12a5"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B06C8460ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B06C8563ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X9112e3"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X9112e4"></A><B>void clkoff(&nbsp;)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A339C9645e"></A><B>void clkon(&nbsp;)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X9112bf"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X9112c2"></A><B>SUBROUTINE CLKOFF</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A28C01078e"></A><B>SUBROUTINE CLKON</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X9112e7"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B06C9009ceb"></A>The <B>clkoff</B> subroutine turns off the keyboard click, and the <B>clkon</B> subroutine turns it on.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9e70"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A62C015d58"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B06C9226ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C12a8"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C12a9"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C12aa"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X9112f4"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B06C9544ceb"></A>Turning off the keyboard display lights with the <A HREF="lampoff.html#A213X9113bc"><B>lampon</B> or <B>lampoff</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B06C9651ceb"></A>Ringing the keyboard bell with the <A HREF="ringbell.html#A213X911463"><B>ringbell</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B06C9758ceb"></A>Setting the duration of the keyboard bell sound with the <A HREF="setbell.html#A213X9114ae"><B>setbell</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B06C9864ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A> and <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/keyboardgl.html#keyboardgl.html">Using the Keyboard</A>.</P><hr><center>

<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A142X915b"></A>closeobj Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX242" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX243" REL="I2" TITLE="object (display list)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX244" REL="I3" TITLE="closeobj"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX245" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX246" REL="I2" TITLE="object (display list)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX247" REL="I3" TITLE="closing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX248" REL="I1" TITLE="closeobj subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A142X915d"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B06E6584ceb"></A>Closes an object.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C113"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B06E6733ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B06E6836ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A142X9161"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A142X9162"></A><B>void closeobj(&nbsp;)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010a5e"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010a5f"></A><B>SUBROUTINE CLOSEO</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A142X9163"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B06E7190ceb"></A>The <B>closeobj</B> subroutine closes an open object definition. Use the <A HREF="makeobj.html#A142X912d"><B>makeobj</B></A> subroutine to open a definition for a new object. All display list routines between the <B>makeobj</B> subroutine and the <B>closeobj</B> subroutine become part of the object definition. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B06E7297ceb"></A>Use the <A HREF="editobj.html#A142X9360"><B>editobj</B></A> subroutine to open an existing object for editing and the <B>closeobj</B> subroutine to end the editing session. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B06E7403ceb"></A>If no object is open, the <B>closeobj</B> subroutine is ignored.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9d77"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine, <I>itself</I>, cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A30C010ff6"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B06E7614ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="depthcue_c.html#A16C0c8ff"><B>depthcue.c</B></A> uses the <B>closeobj</B> subroutine to specify the end of a graphical object definition. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015cee"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B06E7774ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C116"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C117"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C118"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A142X917b"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B06E8094ceb"></A>Opening an object for editing with the <A HREF="editobj.html#A142X9360"><B>editobj</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B06E8201ceb"></A>Creating an object with the <A HREF="makeobj.html#A142X912d"><B>makeobj</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B06E8309ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A> and Creating <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/workobjects.html#workobjects.html">Objects (Display Lists)</A>.</P><hr><center>

<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A146X93d6"></A>cmode Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX249" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX250" REL="I2" TITLE="color map and RGB mode"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX251" REL="I3" TITLE="cmode"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX252" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX253" REL="I2" TITLE="color map mode"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX254" REL="I3" TITLE="setting current color in"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX255" REL="I1" TITLE="cmode subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A146X93d8"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B070D080ceb"></A>Sets color map mode as the current mode.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C12b"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B070D228ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B070D333ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A146X93db"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A146X93dc"></A><B>void cmode(&nbsp;)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A146X93b4"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A146X93b7"></A><B>SUBROUTINE CMODE</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A146X93df"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B070D683ceb"></A>The <B>cmode</B> subroutine sets 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A25P03e3">color map mode</A> as the current mode. This mode is the default.  </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B070D851ceb"></A>If your workstation has more than 12 standard bitplanes, you can write color indexes between 0 and 4095 into the standard bitplanes. The 
drawing mode
 must be set to <A HREF="drawmode.html#A143X946b">NORMALDRAW</A> to write into the standard bitplanes (NORMALDRAW is the default drawing mode). The system must be in color map mode in order to draw into the overlay or underlay bitplanes.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B070D968ceb"></A>You must call the <A HREF="gconfig.html#hS4260nita"><B>gconfig</B></A> subroutine after the <B>cmode</B> subroutine in order to have the <B>cmode</B> subroutine take effect. The system does not enter color map mode until the <B>gconfig</B> subroutine is called.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9cae"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A64C016558"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B070E473ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature. </P>

<P><A NAME="A3CBD17E975bolt"></A>The POWERgraphics GXT1000 will ignore the <B>cmode</B> subroutine when applied to windows created with the <B>winX</B> subroutine. The <B>cmode</B> subroutine can still be used with windows created with the <B>winopen</B> subroutine. See the <A HREF="winX.html#A114C163"><B>winX</B></A> subroutine for more detail.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C12e"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C12f"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C130"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A146X93f5"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B070E794ceb"></A>Choosing a set of bitplanes for drawing with the <A HREF="drawmode.html#A143X9460"><B>drawmode</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B070E901ceb"></A>Configuring the system with the <A HREF="gconfig.html#hS4260nita"><B>gconfig</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B070F009ceb"></A>Setting a display mode that bypasses the color map with the <A HREF="RGBmode.html#A143X93b6"><B>RGBmode</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B070F117ceb"></A>Working in <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/workcolor.html#workcolor.html">Color Map and RGB Modes</A>.</P><hr><center>

<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A143X9d1d"></A>cmov Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX256" REL="I1" TITLE="cmov subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX257" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX258" REL="I2" TITLE="text"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX259" REL="I3" TITLE="cmov"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX260" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX261" REL="I2" TITLE="text"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX262" REL="I3" TITLE="updating text character position"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A143X9d1f"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B072C742ceb"></A>Updates the current text character position.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1213"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B072C891ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B072C995ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9d23"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A143X9d24"></A><B>void cmov(Coord </B><A HREF="cmov.html#A143X9d28"><I>x</I></A><B>, Coord</B> <A HREF="cmov.html#A143X9d29"><I>y</I></A><B>, Coord</B> <A HREF="cmov.html#A143X9d2a"><I>z</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X9125f6"></A><B>void cmovi(Icoord </B><A HREF="cmov.html#A143X9d28"><I>x</I></A><B>, Icoord</B> <A HREF="cmov.html#A143X9d29"><I>y</I></A><B>, Icoord</B> <A HREF="cmov.html#A143X9d2a"><I>z</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<PRE><A NAME="A213X9125f7"></A><B>void cmovs(Scoord </B><A HREF="cmov.html#A143X9d28"><I>x</I></A><B>, Scoord</B> <A HREF="cmov.html#A143X9d29"><I>y</I></A><B>, Scoord</B> <A HREF="cmov.html#A143X9d2a"><I>z</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X9125f8"></A><B>void cmov2(Coord </B><A HREF="cmov.html#A143X9d28"><I>x</I></A><B>, Coord</B> <A HREF="cmov.html#A143X9d29"><I>y</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<PRE><A NAME="A213X9125f9"></A><B>void cmov2i(Icoord </B><A HREF="cmov.html#A143X9d28"><I>x</I></A><B>, Icoord</B> <A HREF="cmov.html#A143X9d29"><I>y</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X9125fa"></A><B>void cmov2s(Scoord </B><A HREF="cmov.html#A143X9d28"><I>x</I></A><B>, Scoord</B> <A HREF="cmov.html#A143X9d29"><I>y</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010be9"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010bea"></A><B>SUBROUTINE CMOV(</B><I>x</I><B>,</B> <I>y</I><B>,</B> <I>z</I><B>)</B>
<B>REAL </B><I>x</I><B>,</B> <I>y</I><B>,</B> <I>z</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010beb"></A><B>SUBROUTINE CMOVI(</B><I>x</I><B>,</B> <I>y</I><B>,</B> <I>z</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>x</I><B>,</B> <I>y</I><B>,</B> <I>z</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010bec"></A><B>SUBROUTINE CMOVS(</B><I>x</I><B>,</B> <I>y</I><B>,</B> <I>z</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*2 </B><I>x</I><B>,</B> <I>y</I><B>,</B> <I>z</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010bed"></A><B>SUBROUTINE CMOV2(</B><I>x</I><B>,</B> <I>y</I><B>)</B>
<B>REAL </B><I>x</I><B>,</B> <I>y</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010bee"></A><B>SUBROUTINE CMOV2I(</B><I>x</I><B>,</B> <I>y</I><B>,</B> <I>z</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>x</I><B>,</B> <I>y</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010bef"></A><B>SUBROUTINE CMOV2S(</B><I>x</I><B>,</B> <I>y</I><B>,</B> <I>z</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*2 </B><I>x</I><B>,</B> <I>y</I></PRE>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A79C1216"></A><B>Note: </B>For FORTRAN users, the INTEGER*2 versions of this subroutine, <B>CMOVS</B> and <B>CMOV2S</B>, should not be called with integer constant parameters. For example, 2 is an integer constant; JJ is an integer variable. The XL FORTRAN compiler, invoked by the <B>xlf</B> command, stores all integer constants as long integers (INTEGER*4), not as short integers (INTEGER*2). Invoking one of the short versions of this subroutine with an integer constant will result in unexpected behavior.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<P><A NAME="E1B072D921ceb"></A>All of the functions are essentially the same except for the type declarations of the parameters. In addition, the <B>cmov2*</B> routines assume a 2-D point instead of a 3-D point.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9d25"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B072E081ceb"></A>The <B>cmov </B>subroutine moves the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A25P03e9">current character position</A> to a specified point (just as the <A HREF="move.html#pofmarj"><B>move</B></A> subroutine sets the current graphics position). The <B>cmov</B> subroutine transforms the specified 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A27P03d">modeling coordinates</A> into 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A27P017">screen coordinates</A>, which become the new character position. If the transformed point is outside the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A27P039">viewport</A>, the character position is undefined. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B072E188ceb"></A>The <B>cmov</B> subroutine does not affect the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A25P03eb">current graphics position</A>.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9d27"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X9d28"></A><I>x</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>x </I>location of the point (in modeling coordinates) to which to move the current character position.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X9d29"></A><I>y</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>y </I>location of the point (in modeling coordinates) to which to move the current character position. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X9d2a"></A><I>z</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>z </I>location of the point (in modeling coordinates) to which to move the current character position. (This parameter is not used by the 2-D subroutines.)</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A30C011052"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B072E571ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="curved_c.html#A16C0c830"><B>curved.c</B></A> uses the <B>cmov2</B> subroutine to move the character position to a specific location before drawing text. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015d84"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B072E731ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1217"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1218"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1219"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9d3d"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B072F049ceb"></A>Drawing a string of raster characters on the screen with the <A HREF="charstr.html#A143X9cfb"><B>charstr</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B072F160ceb"></A>Moving the current graphics position with the <A HREF="move.html#pofmarj"><B>move</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A146X9429"></A>color or colorf Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX263" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX264" REL="I2" TITLE="attribute"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX265" REL="I3" TITLE="color"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX266" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX267" REL="I2" TITLE="colors"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX268" REL="I3" TITLE="current"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX269" REL="I1" TITLE="color subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A146X942b"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B074C899ceb"></A>Sets the current color in color map mode.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A77C15d"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B074D050ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B074D156ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A146X942e"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A146X942f"></A><B>void  color(Colorindex </B><A HREF="color.html#A146X9438"><I>color</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X910d88"></A><B>void  colorf(Float32 </B><A HREF="color.html#A146X9438"><I>color</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A146X9407"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A146X940a"></A><B>SUBROUTINE COLOR(</B><I>color</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>color</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X910d89"></A><B>SUBROUTINE COLORF(</B><I>color</I><B>)</B>
<B>REAL </B><I>color</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A146X9432"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B074D628ceb"></A>The <B>color</B> subroutine selects a color from the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A31996bc">color map</A>, and sets that color as the default in the current drawing mode. For example, if the drawing mode is <A HREF="drawmode.html#A143X946b">NORMALDRAW</A> (the default), the color index is written to the standard bitplanes during all drawing routines.  </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B074D736ceb"></A>In NORMALDRAW mode, the <A HREF="color.html#A146X9438"><I>color</I></A> parameter allows you to access up to 12 bitplanes in <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/workcolor.html#a3P1390marj">onemap mode</A> and up to 8 bitplanes in <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/workcolor.html#a3P1390marj">multimap mode</A>. However, since the 8-bit High-Performance 3-D Color Graphics Processor has only one 8-bit main frame buffer, the 12-bit onemap mode is not available on this machine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B074D844ceb"></A>In <A HREF="drawmode.html#A143X946b">OVERDRAW and UNDERDRAW</A> modes, 0, 2, or 4 bitplanes are accessible.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B074D951ceb"></A>In alternate drawing modes such as OVERDRAW the <B>color</B> subroutine serves the same function as in NORMALDRAW, except that different bitplanes are used, and a separate, smaller map is indexed.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B074E062ceb"></A>The <B>colorf </B>subroutine is identical to the <B>color </B>subroutine, except that it expects a floating point color index. Before the color is written into display memory, it is rounded to the nearest integer value. When drawing with the GOURAUD shading model, machines that iterate color indexes with fractional precision yield more precise shading results using the <B>colorf </B>subroutine than with the <B>color</B> subroutine. The results of these subroutines are indistinguishable when drawing with FLAT shading. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B074E170ceb"></A>The <B>color</B> and <B>colorf </B>subroutines serve no purpose in 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0743">RGB mode</A> because the RGB components of the color are written directly to the bitplanes.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A146X9437"></A>Parameter</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A146X9438"></A><I>color</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies a color index (0 to 4095 in onemap mode, 0 to 255 in multimap mode).</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A146X943b"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B074E428ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="boxcirc_c.html#A16C0c7bb"><B>boxcirc.c</B></A> uses the <B>color</B> subroutine to set the color for subsequent drawing routines. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015c6d"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B074E589ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A146X9424"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C160"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C161"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A146X944b"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B074E904ceb"></A>Choosing a set of bitplanes for drawing with the <A HREF="drawmode.html#A143X9460"><B>drawmode</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B074F011ceb"></A>Returning the current color with the <A HREF="getcolor.html#A146X924b"><B>getcolor</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B074F119ceb"></A>Getting a copy of the RGB values for a color map entry with the <A HREF="getmcolor.html#nXI1100marj"><B>getmcolor</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B074F227ceb"></A>Changing a color map entry with the <A HREF="mapcolor.html#A146X9535"><B>mapcolor</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B074F333ceb"></A>Setting  the current color in RGB mode with the <A HREF="RGBcolor.html#A143X9394"><B>RGBcolor</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B074F440ceb"></A>Setting a display mode that bypasses the color map with the <A HREF="RGBmode.html#A143X93b6"><B>RGBmode</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B074F546ceb"></A>Gaining write access to a subset of available bitplanes with the <A HREF="RGBwritemask.html#A143X93fa"><B>RGBwritemask</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B074F653ceb"></A>Gaining write access to the available bitplanes with the <A HREF="writemask.html#A143X9592"><B>writemask</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B074F761ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A>, <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/setglattrib.html#setglattrib.html">Setting Drawing Attributes</A>, Understanding the <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/glintro.html#A8G44310marj">Hardware Used by GL</A>, and Working in <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/workcolor.html#workcolor.html">Color Map and RGB Modes</A>.</P><hr><center>

 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="colored_c.html"></A>colored.c Example C Language Program</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX2191" REL="I1" TITLE="colored.c example program (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2192" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2193" REL="I2" TITLE="example programs"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2194" REL="I3" TITLE="color map editor"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2195" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2196" REL="I2" TITLE="color map editor"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2197" REL="I3" TITLE="example program"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2198" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2199" REL="I2" TITLE="editor"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2200" REL="I3" TITLE="color map"></A>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E9BE586ttay"></A>/*Example colored.c</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E9BE752ttay"></A>Edit the colormap and display the results in the graphics window.</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E9BE908ttay"></A>This program works on any 3d adapter.
*/</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E9BF064ttay"></A>#include &lt;gl/gl.h>
#include &lt;gl/device.h></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E9BF280ttay"></A>#define START 64
#define CURRENTCOLOR 63
#define BARWIDTH 67
#define REDBAR   934
#define GREENBAR 800
#define BLUEBAR  666
#define STARTBAR 250
#define ENDBAR   1082
#define indextovalue(index) (4*index + 3)</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E9BF473ttay"></A>short redindex = 0, greenindex = 0, blueindex = 0;
short whichbar();
long xorg,yorg,xsize,ysize;
long redbar,greenbar,bluebar;
long startbar,endbar;</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E9BF902ttay"></A>main()
{
  short index, val;
  Device xpos, ypos;
  initialize();
  while (TRUE) {
    switch (qread(&amp;val)) {
    case ESCKEY:
      greset();
      gexit();
      exit(0);
    case REDRAW:
      reshapeviewport();
      getwindowsize();
      buildmap();
      displaymap();
      break;
    case LEFTMOUSE:
      if (val){
        qread(&amp;xpos);
        qread(&amp;ypos);
        qread(&amp;val);
        qread(&amp;val);
        qread(&amp;val);
        if (insideport(xpos,ypos)) {
          index = -1;
          switch (whichbar(xpos,ypos,&amp;index)) {
          case 0:
            redindex = index;
            break;
          case 1:
            greenindex = index;
            break;
          case 2:
            blueindex = index;
            break;
          default:
            break;
          }</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E9C0091ttay"></A>          if (index != -1) {
            buildmap();
            displaymap();
          }
        }
      }
      break;
    }
  }</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E9C0234ttay"></A>}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E9C0385ttay"></A>initialize()
{
  int gid;</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E9C2253ttay"></A>  prefposition(10, XMAXSCREEN-10, 10, YMAXSCREEN-20);
  keepaspect(5,4);
  gid = winopen("colored");
  ortho2(-0.5, (float)XMAXSCREEN-0.5, -0.5, (float)YMAXSCREEN-0.5);
  color(0);
  clear();
  mapcolor(CURRENTCOLOR, 0, 0, 0);
  qdevice(LEFTMOUSE);
  tie(LEFTMOUSE, MOUSEX, MOUSEY);
  qdevice(ESCKEY);
  qdevice(REDRAW);
  qenter(REDRAW,gid);
}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E9C2514ttay"></A>getwindowsize()
{
  getorigin(&amp;xorg,&amp;yorg);
  getsize(&amp;xsize,&amp;ysize);
  redbar = ((REDBAR * ysize) / YMAXSCREEN) + yorg;
  greenbar = ((GREENBAR * ysize) / YMAXSCREEN) + yorg;
  bluebar = ((BLUEBAR * ysize) / YMAXSCREEN) + yorg;
  startbar = ((STARTBAR * xsize) / XMAXSCREEN) + xorg;
  endbar = ((ENDBAR * xsize) / XMAXSCREEN) + xorg;
}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64E9C2884ttay"></A>buildmap()
{
  register i, j;
  for (i = 0; i &lt; 3; i++) {
    for (j = 0; j &lt; 64; j++) {
      switch (i) {
      case 0:                /* red */
        mapcolor(START+i*64+j, indextovalue(j),
            indextovalue(greenindex),
            indextovalue(blueindex));
        break;
      case 1:                /* green */
        mapcolor(START+i*64+j, indextovalue(redindex),
            indextovalue(j),
            indextovalue(blueindex));
        break;
      case 2:                /* blue */
        mapcolor(START+i*64+j, indextovalue(redindex),
            indextovalue(greenindex),
            indextovalue(j));
        break;
      }</PRE>

      indextovalue(greenindex),

}</PRE>

<PRE><A NAME="A64E9C4599ttay"></A>/* return 1 if the position of the cursor is within the window */
insideport(x,y)
int x, y;
{
  if(x&lt;xorg)
    return 0;
  if(x>(xorg+xsize))
    return 0;
  if(y&lt;yorg)
    return 0;
  if(y>(yorg+ysize))
    return 0;
  return 1;
}
/*
returns 0 if in the redbar, 1 if in the greenbar and 2 if in the 
blue bar
*/
short whichbar(xpos,ypos,index)
long xpos,ypos;
short *index;
{
  short i;
  i = -1;
  if (redbar - BARWIDTH &lt;= ypos &amp;&amp; ypos &lt;= redbar)  /* red color bar */
    i = 0;
  else if (greenbar-BARWIDTH &lt;= ypos &amp;&amp; 
      ypos &lt;= greenbar)                   /* green color bar */
    i = 1;
  else if (bluebar - BARWIDTH &lt;= ypos &amp;&amp; 
      ypos &lt;= bluebar) /* blue color bar */
    i = 2;
  if (i != -1) {
    if (startbar &lt;= xpos &amp;&amp; xpos &lt; endbar) {
      *index = (xpos - startbar)/13;
      return(i);
    }</PRE>

  return(-1);</PRE>

<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A142X9c5a"></A>compactify Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX270" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX271" REL="I2" TITLE="object (display list)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX272" REL="I3" TITLE="compactify"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX273" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX274" REL="I2" TITLE="object (display list)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX275" REL="I3" TITLE="compacting memory storage of"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX276" REL="I1" TITLE="compactify subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A142X9c5c"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B076C400ceb"></A>Unfragments and compacts the memory storage of an object.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C119"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B076C547ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B076C651ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A142X9c60"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A142X9c61"></A><B>void compactify(Int32 </B><A HREF="compactify.html#A142X9c65"><I>object</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010aa5"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010aa6"></A><B>SUBROUTINE COMPAC(</B><I>object</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>object</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A142X9c62"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B076D014ceb"></A>The <B>compactify</B> subroutine unfragments and compacts the memory storage of an object.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B076D124ceb"></A>Using the 
object editing subroutines
 to modify an open object definition can fragment the memory storage for the definition. The <B>compactify</B> subroutine eliminates wasted space, but calling it is rarely necessary because the <A HREF="closeobj.html#A142X915b"><B>closeobj</B></A> subroutine automatically compacts an object definition that is too fragmented. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B076D231ceb"></A>Because the <B>compactify </B>subroutine requires a significant amount of time to execute, calls to it should be avoided unless storage space is critical.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9da4"></A><B>Note: </B>This editing subroutine itself cannot be added to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A142X9c64"></A>Parameter</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A142X9c65"></A><I>object</I><B></B></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the identifier for the object to be compacted.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015d0e"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B076D550ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C11c"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C11d"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C11e"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A142X9c7a"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B076D868ceb"></A>Specifying the minimum object size in memory with the <A HREF="chunksize.html#A142X9c38"><B>chunksize</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B076D974ceb"></A>Closing an object with the <A HREF="closeobj.html#A142X915b"><B>closeobj</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B076E082ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A> and Creating <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/workobjects.html#workobjects.html">Objects (Display Lists)</A>.</P><hr><center>

<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="HXf320marj"></A>concave Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX277" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX278" REL="I2" TITLE="pipeline optionetting"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX279" REL="I3" TITLE="concave"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX280" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX281" REL="I2" TITLE="high-level drawing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX282" REL="I3" TITLE="concave"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX283" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX284" REL="I2" TITLE="polygons"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX285" REL="I3" TITLE="concave"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX286" REL="I1" TITLE="concave subroutine (GL)"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A213X912d20"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B078D129ceb"></A>Forces the system to draw accurate concave polygons.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C126f"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B078D277ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B078D381ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912d23"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X912d24"></A><B>void concave(Int32 </B><A HREF="concave.html#A213X912d2b"><I>bool</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A28C010763"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A28C010764"></A><B>SUBROUTINE CONCAV(</B><I>bool</I><B>)</B>
<B>LOGICAL </B><I>bool</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912d27"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B078D743ceb"></A>The <B>concave </B>subroutine forces the system to draw accurate 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A60P0188">concave polygons</A>. When the <A HREF="concave.html#A213X912d2b"><I>bool</I></A> parameter is True (1), the system draws accurate concave polygons. When the value of the <I>bool</I> parameter is False (0) (the default), the results of drawing a concave polygon are unpredictable.  </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B078D852ceb"></A>The system draws polygons significantly faster if checking for concavity is turned off. Therefore, unless you specifically want to draw concave polygons, you should generally operate with the <I>bool</I> parameter set to False.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912d2a"></A>Parameter</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912d2b"></A><I>bool</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies a value for the state of concavity. The settings for the <I>bool</I> parameter are: 


<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912d2c"></A>True</TD>
<TD>  System draws accurate concave and convex polygons. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912d2d"></A>False</TD>
<TD>  System draws only accurate convex polygons. This is the default. </TD></TR></TABLE></TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015ce0"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B078E231ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3CBD2DA177bolt"></A>On the POWERgraphics GXT1000, the value of the <B>concave</B> flag is ignored when drawing into the overlay planes. </P>

<P><A NAME="A3CBD2DA281bolt"></A>If the <B>concave</B> flag has been set to TRUE, then the GXT1000 limits the number of vertices that can appear between a <B>bgnline</B> and <B>endline</B> pair to 255 vertices. Otherwise, an unlimited number of vertices can be specified.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C1272"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C1273"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C1274"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912d3b"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B078E558ceb"></A>Drawing a vertex-based polygon with the <A HREF="bgnpolygon.html#A144X9672"><B>bgnpolygon</B></A> subroutine. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B078E665ceb"></A>Specifying the next point in a polygon with the <A HREF="pdr.html#bqf1c0marj"><B>pdr</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B078E772ceb"></A>Specifying the starting point for a polygon with the <A HREF="pmv.html#A139X91eed"><B>pmv</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B078E879ceb"></A>Drawing a filled polygon with the <A HREF="polf.html#Zsf1c0marj"><B>polf</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B078E986ceb"></A>Drawing a polygon with the <A HREF="poly.html#avf2c0marj"><B>poly</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B078F097ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A>, <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/setglpipeops.html#setglpipeops.html">Setting Pipeline Options</A>, <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawpoly.html#drawpoly.html">Drawing Rectangles, Circles, Arcs, and Polygons</A>.</P><hr><center>

<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A143X9284"></A>cpack Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX287" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX288" REL="I2" TITLE="attribute"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX289" REL="I3" TITLE="cpack"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX290" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX291" REL="I2" TITLE="colors"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX292" REL="I3" TITLE="current"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX293" REL="I1" TITLE="cpack subroutine (GL)"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A143X9286"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B07AF969ceb"></A>Specifies RGBA color with a single packed 32-bit integer.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A77C162"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B07B0151ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B07B0255ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X928a"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A143X928b"></A><B>void cpack(unsigned Int32 </B><A HREF="cpack.html#A143X928f"><I>pack</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A19C0e0dd"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A19C0e0de"></A><B>SUBROUTINE CPACK(</B><I>pack</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>pack</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X928c"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B07B0619ceb"></A>The <B>cpack </B>subroutine changes the current RGBA (red, green, blue, alpha) values. It is valid only in 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0743">RGB mode</A>. Red is the least significant byte in the packed integer, then green, blue, and alpha. Components must range from 0 through 255.  For example, </P>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X9121f4"></A>cpack(0xFF004080); </PRE>

<P><A NAME="E1B07B0777ceb"></A>sets red to <SAMP>0x80</SAMP>, green to <SAMP>0x40</SAMP>, blue to <SAMP>0x0</SAMP>, and alpha to <SAMP>0xFF</SAMP>. On systems without alpha bitplanes, set the alpha bit values to zero.  </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B07B0883ceb"></A>Note that the <B>cpack</B> subroutine can be used while a 
lighting model
 is active. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X928e"></A>Parameter</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X928f"></A><I>pack</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies a packed integer containing the RGBA (red, green, blue, alpha) values to assign as the current color. </TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9294"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B07B1145ceb"></A>To clear the screen to black, then set the color to white, the example C language program <A HREF="localatten_c.html#A10C0abc5"><B>localatten.c</B></A> calls the <B>cpack</B> subroutine with a value of <SAMP>0</SAMP> (black) before a <B>clear</B> subroutine, then calls the <B>cpack</B> subroutine with a value of <SAMP>0xFFFFFF</SAMP> (white).</P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015c6f"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B07B1305ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A11C0b4bb"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C165"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C166"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X92a4"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B07B1623ceb"></A>Setting the current color in RGB mode with the <A HREF="c.html#A143X9262"><B>c</B></A> subroutine.</P>
