<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A143X92c8"></A>czclear Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX361" REL="I1" TITLE="czclear subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX362" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX363" REL="I2" TITLE="initializing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX364" REL="I3" TITLE="czclear"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX365" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX366" REL="I2" TITLE="initializing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX367" REL="I3" TITLE="clearing color bitplanes and z buffer"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A143X92ca"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B08EC330ceb"></A>Clears the color bitplanes and the z-buffer simultaneously.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C11b3"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B08EC477ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B08EC581ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X92ce"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A143X92cf"></A><B>void czclear(Int32 </B><A HREF="czclear.html#A143X92d3"><I>cval</I></A><B>, Int32 </B><A HREF="czclear.html#F2F11e0marj"><I>zval</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010b9c"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010b9d"></A><B>SUBROUTINE CZCLEA(</B><I>cval</I><B>,</B> <I>zval</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>cval</I><B>,</B><I> zval</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X92d0"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B08EC951ceb"></A>The <B>czclear</B> subroutine simultaneously clears the color bitplanes to the value of the <A HREF="czclear.html#A143X92d3"><I>cval</I></A> parameter and the 
z-buffer
 to the value of the <A HREF="czclear.html#F2F11e0marj"><I>zval</I></A> parameter. The <B>czclear </B>subroutine clears all active color bits (8 or 12 in 
 <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A25P03e3">color map mode</A>, 24 in 
 <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0743">RGB mode</A>), and all 24 z-buffer bits. Pattern 0 (zero) is always used, regardless of the current pattern specification. The system ignores the current 
 <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A3C0F2A4599mhay">writemask</A>.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B08ED060ceb"></A>Only the screen area inside the current 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A27P018">screenmask</A> is cleared. The screenmask cannot be made larger than the window. By default, the screenmask is exactly the same size as the window. Use the <A HREF="scrmask.html#fwN250marj"><B>scrmsk</B></A> subroutine to change the size of the screenmask.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A79C11b6"></A><B>Note: </B>The <A HREF="viewport.html#qrY270marj"><B>viewport</B></A> subroutine resets the screenmask to be precisely the same size as the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A27P039">viewport</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<P><A NAME="E1B08ED227ceb"></A>In RGB mode, the <A HREF="czclear.html#A143X92d3"><I>cval</I></A> parameter requires a packed integer of the same format used by the <A HREF="cpack.html#A143X9284"><B>cpack</B></A> subroutine, 0x<I>aaggbbrr</I>, where <I>rr</I> is the red value, <I>gg</I> is the green value, <I>bb</I> is the blue value, and <I>aa</I> is the alpha value. In color map mode, the <I>cval </I>parameter requires an index into the current color map, so that only the bottom 8 or 12 bits are significant.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B08ED336ceb"></A>Whenever you need to clear both the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A154P1160a">z-buffer</A> and the color bitplanes to constant values at the same time, use the <B>czclear</B> subroutine. The <B>czclear</B> subroutine executes as fast as, or faster than, the <A HREF="clear.html#cEH1160marj"><B>clear</B></A> and <A HREF="zclear.html#A143X97d3"><B>zclear</B></A> subroutines called sequentially.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B08ED443ceb"></A>The <B>czclear</B> subroutine can be called whether z-buffer mode is on or off. The current color does not change.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A258C01c816"></A><B>Note: </B>The operation of this subroutine for the Supergraphics Processor Subsystem is modified. (See <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/powerstation730.html#NITAXIO">"Hardware Considerations"</A> in<I> GL3.2 Version 4 for AIX: Programming Concepts</I>.)</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A143X92d2"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X92d3"></A><I>cval</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the color to which to clear the color bitplanes.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="F2F11e0marj"></A><I>zval</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the depth to which to clear the 
z-buffer. The <I>zval</I> parameter has the following values:


<TABLE BORDER="2"><TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD COLSPAN="2"><B>Values for the zval parameter</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>Min</B></TD>

<TD><B>Max</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>-0x800000</TD>

<TD>0x7FFFFF</TD></TR></TABLE></TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A64C0165f2"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B08ED865ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C11b7"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C11b8"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C11b9"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X92e8"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B08EE232ceb"></A>Clearing to the screenmask with the <A HREF="clear.html#cEH1160marj"><B>clear</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B08EE345ceb"></A>Setting the current color as a packed 32-bit integer using the <A HREF="cpack.html#A143X9284"><B>cpack</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B08EE462ceb"></A>Enabling and disabling the z-buffer for storing depth information with the <A HREF="zbuffer.html#A143X97b1"><B>zbuffer</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B08EE580ceb"></A>Clearing the z-buffer with the <A HREF="zclear.html#A143X97d3"><B>zclear</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B08EE687ceb"></A>Specifying the function used for depth comparison with the <A HREF="zfunction.html#A22f0MARJ"><B>zfunction</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B08EE795ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/glintro.html#A8G44310marj">Understanding the Hardware</A> Used by GL, <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/configframebuf.html#configframebuf.html">Configuring the Frame Buffer</A>, and Working in <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/workcolor.html#workcolor.html">Color Map and RGB Modes</A>.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B08EE903ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/clrrstintgl.html#clrrstintgl.html">Clearing, Resetting, and Initiliazing GL</A>, <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/writemasks.html#writemasks.html">Writemasks and Logical Operations</A>.</P><hr><center>

<a href="defbasis.html">Next</a>  |

 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
</center></BODY>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>

<A href="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A150X930"></A>defbasis Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX368" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX369" REL="I2" TITLE="wire frame curve and surface patch"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX370" REL="I3" TITLE="defbasis"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX371" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX372" REL="I2" TITLE="cubic spline basis matrix"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX373" REL="I3" TITLE="defining"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX374" REL="I1" TITLE="defbasis subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A150X932"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0911814ceb"></A>Defines a cubic spline basis matrix.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C1110"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0911963ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0912067ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A150X935"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A150X936"></A><B>void defbasis(Int32 </B><A HREF="defbasis.html#A150X93e"><I>id</I></A><B>, Matrix </B><A HREF="defbasis.html#A150X93f"><I>mat</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A150X9d"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A150X910"></A><B>SUBROUTINE DEFBAS(</B><I>id</I><B>,</B><I> mat</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>id</I>
<B>REAL </B><I>mat</I><B>(4,4)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A150X939"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0912437ceb"></A>The <B>defbasis</B> subroutine assigns a basis matrix identifier for use by subroutines that generate curves and patches. Use the basis matrix identifier in subsequent calls to the <A HREF="curvebasis.html#sTS23a0marj"><B>curvebasis</B></A> and <A HREF="patchbasis.html#A143X95d6"><B>patchbasis</B></A> subroutines. </P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9ce1"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A150X93d"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A150X93e"></A><I>id</I>  </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the basis identifier to assign to the matrix. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A150X93f"></A><I>mat</I>  </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the matrix to which to assign the basis identifier.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A150X942"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0912812ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="curve1_c.html#A16C0c804"><B>curve1.c</B></A> uses the <B>defbasis</B> subroutine to define three basis matrices for drawing curves.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A64C01658a"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0912973ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C1113"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C1114"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C1115"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="C41DC93930nqui"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0913292ceb"></A>Drawing a cubic spline curve with the <A HREF="crv.html#ZMS220marj"><B>crv</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0913399ceb"></A>Drawing a series of curve segments with the <A HREF="crvn.html#ESS22c0marj"><B>crvn</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0913506ceb"></A>Setting the current cubic spline curve basis matrix with the <A HREF="curvebasis.html#sTS23a0marj"><B>curvebasis</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0913613ceb"></A>Setting the number of line segments that draw a curve segment with the <A HREF="curveprecision.html#aUS2120marj"><B>curveprecision</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0913720ceb"></A>Drawing surface patches with the <A HREF="patch.html#A143X95b4"><B>patch</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0913827ceb"></A>Setting the current spline surface basis matrices with the <A HREF="patchbasis.html#A143X95d6"><B>patchbasis</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0913936ceb"></A>Setting the number of curves used to represent a patch with the <A HREF="patchcurves.html#A143X95f8"><B>patchcurves</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0914043ceb"></A>Setting the precision at which curves are drawn with the <A HREF="patchprecision.html#A143X961a"><B>patchprecision</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0914152ceb"></A>Drawing a rational curve with the <A HREF="rcrv.html#WRS2380marj"><B>rcrv</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0914259ceb"></A>Drawing a series of rational curve segments with the <A HREF="rcrvn.html#A1TS2220marj"><B>rcrvn</B></A> subroutine.</P>

</TITLE>
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>

 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A150X9444"></A>defcursor Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX375" REL="I1" TITLE="defcursor subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX376" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX377" REL="I2" TITLE="cursor"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX378" REL="I3" TITLE="defcursor"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX379" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX380" REL="I2" TITLE="cursor"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX381" REL="I3" TITLE="defining"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A150X9446"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0931824ceb"></A>Defines a cursor glyph.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C1d8"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0931971ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0932075ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A150X9449"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A150X944a"></A><B>void defcursor(Int32 </B><A HREF="defcursor.html#A150X9453"><I>index</I></A><B>, Uint16 *</B><A HREF="defcursor.html#A150X9454"><I>cursor</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A150X9421"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A150X9424"></A><B>SUBROUTINE DEFCUR(</B><I>index</I><B>,</B><I> cursor</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>index</I>
<B>INTEGER*2 </B><I>cursor</I><B>(</B><I>1</I><B>);</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A150X944d"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0932444ceb"></A>The <B>defcursor</B> subroutine defines a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A25P03ee">cursor glyph</A> with the specified name and bitmap.  Call the <A HREF="curstype.html#A150X93ee"><B>curstype</B></A> subroutine to set the type and size of cursor before calling the <B>defcursor </B>subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0932551ceb"></A>The bitmap can be 16x16 or 32x32 and one or two layers deep. If the cursor has been defined by the <B>curstype </B>subroutine as type C16X2 or C32X2, the bitmap array is two layers deep.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0932659ceb"></A>By default, the bitmap cursor origin is at (0,0), its lower-left corner. Use the <A HREF="curorigin.html#A150X9398"><B>curorigin</B></A> subroutine to reset the cursor origin (the position controlled by 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A79P07a">valuators</A> attached to the cursor and the position used for the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P06fb">picking region</A>).</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0932767ceb"></A>To replace the bitmap assigned to a cursor constant, call the <B>defcursor</B> subroutine again, keeping the <A HREF="defcursor.html#A150X9453"><I>index</I></A> parameter the same but changing the bitmap <A HREF="defcursor.html#A150X9454"><I>cursor</I></A> parameter. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0932883ceb"></A>By default, a cross-hair cursor origin is at (15,15), the intersection of its two lines.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0932991ceb"></A>By default, an arrow is defined as cursor 0 (zero) and cannot be redefined. </P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9cce"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<P><A NAME="E1B0933160ceb"></A>The ordering of the values in the <I>cursor</I> array is left-to-right, then bottom-to-top, low-order bit plane, then high-order bit plane. This format is the same as that used by the <B>defrasterfont </B>subroutine. In other words, the first 16-bit short word specifies the lower-left bits of the image. If the cursor is 32 bits wide, the next short word specifies the lower-right bits. For a 16-bit wide cursor, the second short word specifies the second row from the bottom, the third word specifies the third row, and so on. If the cursor is a three-color cursor, place the bitmap for the high bit after the data for the low bit. The four different cursor configurations make use of different array sizes, as follows:</P>

<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TH NOWRAP="NOWRAP">Cursor Type</TH>
<TH>  Array Size</TH></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A2D390C233ttay"></A>C16X1</TD>
<TD>  16</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="AB641C2853ttay"></A>C16X2</TD>
<TD>  32</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="AB641C2999ttay"></A>C32X1</TD>
<TD>  64</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="AB641C3145ttay"></A>C32X2</TD>
<TD>  128</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A150X9452"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A150X9453"></A><I>index</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies a number to identify a cursor to other cursor routines.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A150X9454"></A><I>cursor</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the bitmap for the cursor. For the cross-hair cursor type, this parameter is disregarded.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A64C01656e"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0933717ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C1db"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C1dc"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C1dd"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A150X9467"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0934035ceb"></A>Setting the origin of a cursor with the <A HREF="curorigin.html#A150X9398"><B>curorigin</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0934142ceb"></A>Controlling cursor visibility by window with the <A HREF="curson.html#ru1280nita"><B>curson</B> or <B>cursoff</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0934249ceb"></A>Defining the type and size of a cursor with the <A HREF="curstype.html#A150X93ee"><B>curstype</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0934355ceb"></A>Returning the cursor characteristics with the <A HREF="getcursor.html#sP1160nita"><B>getcursor</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0934464ceb"></A>Putting the system in picking mode with the <A HREF="pick.html#h632f0nita"><B>pick</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0934571ceb"></A>Setting the cursor characteristics with the <A HREF="setcursor.html#ZR1nita"><B>setcursor</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0934679ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A>, Creating and Managing <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/managewinds.html#managewinds.html">Windows</A>.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0934787ceb"></A> <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/cursorgl.html#cursorgl.html">Creating a Cursor</A>.</P><hr><center>

<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A143X9b1f"></A>deflinestyle Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX382" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX383" REL="I2" TITLE="attribute"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX384" REL="I3" TITLE="deflinestyle"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX385" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX386" REL="I2" TITLE="linestyle"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX387" REL="I3" TITLE="defining"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX388" REL="I1" TITLE="deflinestyle subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9b21"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0952961ceb"></A>Defines a linestyle.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A77C167"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0953110ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0953215ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9b25"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A143X9b26"></A><B>void deflinestyle(Int32 </B><A HREF="deflinestyle.html#A143X9b2b"><I>index</I></A><B>,</B> <B>Linestyle</B> <A HREF="deflinestyle.html#A143X9b2a"><I>linestyle</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A19C0e0e4"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A19C0e0e5"></A><B>SUBROUTINE DEFLIN(</B><I>index</I><B>, </B><I>linestyle</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>index</I><B>,</B><I> linestyle</I></PRE>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A77C16a"></A><B>Note: </B>For FORTRAN users, this subroutine accepts long integer parameters (INTEGER*4) when invoked from a FORTRAN program, although it accepts short integers when invoked from a C program. The C and FORTRAN syntax shown here reflect this difference.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A143X9b27"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0953639ceb"></A>The <B>deflinestyle</B> subroutine defines a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A172P1436">linestyle</A>, which is a write-enabled bit pattern that is applied when lines are drawn. The least significant bit of the linestyle is applied first.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0953748ceb"></A>You can define up to 2(16) (65536) linestyles. By default, index 0 contains the pattern <SAMP>0xFFFF</SAMP>, which draws solid lines. Index 0 cannot be redefined. A 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A172P1436">linestyle</A> can be redefined by reusing an index.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><B>Notes: </B>
<OL><LI><A NAME="A258C01c378"></A>The operation of this subroutine for the Supergraphics Processor Subsystem is modified. (See 
"<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/powerstation730.html#NITAXIO">Hardware Considerations</A>".)</LI>

<LI><A NAME="A258C01c379"></A>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</LI></OL></BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A143X9b29"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X9b2b"></A><I>index</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the index into a table of linestyles.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X9b2a"></A><I>linestyle</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies a 16-bit pattern stored in the linestyle table at <I>index</I>.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9b2f"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0954233ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="curved_c.html#A16C0c830"><B>curved.c</B></A> uses the <B>deflinestyle</B> subroutine to define a dashed line.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015c77"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>


<P><A NAME="E1B0954449ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0954556ceb"></A>On some display adapters, notably the High-Performance 3-D Graphics Processor, there is a performance penalty for drawing non-solid lines.</P>


<P><A NAME="E1B0954663ceb"></A>On the POWER GXT1000 adapter, the line stipple is reset for 
every line segment between a <B>bgnline</B> and <B>endline</B> subroutine pair and a 
<B>bgnclosedline</B> and <B>endclosedline</B> subroutine pair.</P>



<H3><A NAME="A11C0b4ca"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C16b"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C16c"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A258C01c37a"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0955019ceb"></A>Defining a cursor with the <A HREF="defcursor.html#A150X9444"><B>defcursor</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0955128ceb"></A>Defining a pattern with the <A HREF="defpattern.html#A143X9b41"><B>defpattern</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0955235ceb"></A>Defining bitmaps for a raster font with the <A HREF="defrasterfont.html#A143X9d3f"><B>defrasterfont</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0955341ceb"></A>Returning the current linestyle with the <A HREF="getlstyle.html#A143X9bc9"><B>getlstyle</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0955447ceb"></A>Setting the repeat factor for the current linestyle with the <A HREF="lsrepeat.html#DmN1110marj"><B>lsrepeat</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0955553ceb"></A>Selecting a linestyle with the <A HREF="setlinestyle.html#XFM1310marj"><B>setlinestyle</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0955663ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A>, 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawwfcvs.html#drawwfcvs.html">Drawing Wire Frame Curves and Surface Patches</A>, 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawnurbs.html#drawnurbs.html">Drawing NURBS Curves and Surfaces</A>, 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawbeg-end.html">Drawing with Begin-End Style Subroutines</A>, 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/move-draw.html">Drawing with Move-Draw Style Subroutines</A>, 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/setglattrib.html#setglattrib.html">Setting Drawing Attributes</A>, 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/glintro.html#A8G44310marj">Understanding the Hardware Used by GL</A>, and 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawpoly.html#drawpoly.html">Drawing Rectangles, Circles, Arcs, and Polygons</A>.</P><hr><center>

<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A143X9b41"></A>defpattern Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX389" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX390" REL="I2" TITLE="attribute"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX391" REL="I3" TITLE="defpattern"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX392" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX393" REL="I2" TITLE="pattern"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX394" REL="I3" TITLE="defining"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX395" REL="I1" TITLE="defpattern subroutine (GL)"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A143X9b43"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0975806ceb"></A>Defines patterns used in area fills.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A77C1a1"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0975956ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0976060ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9b47"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A143X9b48"></A><B>void defpattern</B>
<B>(Int32 </B><A HREF="defpattern.html#A143X9b4c"><I>index</I></A><B>, Int16 </B><A HREF="defpattern.html#A143X9b4e"><I>size</I></A><B>, Int16 *</B><A HREF="defpattern.html#A143X9b4d"><I>mask</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A19C0e0e6"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A19C0e0e7"></A><B>SUBROUTINE DEFPAT(</B><I>index</I><B>,</B> <I>size</I><B>,</B> <I>mask</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>index</I><B>,</B> <I>size</I>
<B>INTEGER*2 </B><I>mask</I><B>((</B><I>size</I><B>*</B><I>size</I><B>)/16)</B></PRE>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A77C1a4"></A><B>Note: </B>For FORTRAN users, this subroutine accepts long integer parameters (INTEGER*4) when invoked from a FORTRAN program, although it accepts short integers when invoked from a C program. The C and FORTRAN syntax shown here reflect this difference.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A143X9b49"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0976486ceb"></A>The <B>defpattern</B> subroutine defines patterns for filling areas such as <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawbeg-end.html#A364C992f5">polygons</A>, <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawpoly.html#A7C0a4bd">rectangles</A>, and <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawnurbs.html#drawnurbs.html">curves</A>. By default, pattern 0 is a 16x16-bit solid pattern. Index 0 cannot be changed. The system stores the pattern in a pattern table at <A HREF="defpattern.html#A143X9b4c"><I>index</I></A>. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0976596ceb"></A>The pattern is described from left to right and bottom to top, just as characters are described in a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P073b">raster font</A>. The <B>defpattern</B> subroutine allows you to define an arbitrary pattern and assign it an index identifier. You can later reference this pattern with the <A HREF="setpattern.html#WeM11c0marj"><B>setpattern</B></A> subroutine via this identifier. 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A13791abd">Patterns</A>, 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A263A93ae">cursors</A>, and 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A270A983b">fonts</A> are available to all windows when using multiple windows.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><B>Notes: </B>
<OL><LI><A NAME="A258C01c387"></A>The operation of this subroutine for the Supergraphics Processor Subsystem is modified. 
(See "<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/powerstation730.html#NITAXIO">Hardware Considerations</A>".) </LI>

<LI><A NAME="A258C01c388"></A>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</LI></OL></BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A143X9b4b"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X9b4c"></A><I>index</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the constant to use as an identifier for the pattern described by the 
<I>mask</I> parameter. This constant is used as an index into a table of patterns. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X9b4d"></A><I>mask</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the array of short integers that form the actual bit pattern. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X9b4e"></A><I>size</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the size of the pattern: for example, 16 specifies a 16x16-bit pattern.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015c79"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0977190ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0977316ceb"></A>On the High-Performance 3-D Graphics Processor, there is a performance penalty for non-solid patterns. The High-Performance 3-D Graphics Processor supports only 16x16-bit, 32x32-bit, or 64x64-bit patterns.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0977422ceb"></A>The POWER Gt4 and POWER Gt4x adapters support arbitrary-sized patterns, from 1x1 to 64x64 bits.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0977529ceb"></A>The Supergraphics Processor Subsystem and the POWER GXT1000 adapter support

The  Supergraphics Processor Subsystem supports

 only 16x16-bit and 32x32-bit patterns.The getgdesc(GD_MAX_PATTERN_SIZE) call can be used to determine the largest supported tile pattern.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A11C0b4cd"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C1a5"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C1a6"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A258C01c389"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0977845ceb"></A>Defining a cursor with the <A HREF="defcursor.html#A150X9444"><B>defcursor</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0977951ceb"></A>Defining bitmaps for a raster font with the <A HREF="defrasterfont.html#A143X9d3f"><B>defrasterfont</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0978058ceb"></A>Returning the index of the current fill pattern with the <A HREF="getpattern.html#A143X9b63"><B>getpattern</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0978166ceb"></A>Selecting a pattern for filling polygons and rectangles with the <A HREF="setpattern.html#WeM11c0marj"><B>setpattern</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0978274ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A>, 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawwfcvs.html#drawwfcvs.html">Drawing Wire Frame Curves and Surface Patches</A>, 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawnurbs.html#drawnurbs.html">Drawing NURBS Curves and Surfaces</A>, 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawbeg-end.html">Drawing with Begin-End Style Subroutines</A>, 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/move-draw.html">Drawing with Move-Draw Style Subroutines</A>, 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/setglattrib.html#setglattrib.html">Setting Drawing Attributes</A>, 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/glintro.html#A8G44310marj">Understanding the Hardware Used by GL</A>, and 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawpoly.html#drawpoly.html">Drawing Rectangles, Circles, Arcs, and Polygons</A>.</P><hr><center>

<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A142X910bf"></A>defpup Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX396" REL="I1" TITLE="defpup subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX397" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX398" REL="I2" TITLE="popp menus"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX399" REL="I3" TITLE="defining"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX400" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX401" REL="I2" TITLE="popp menu"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX402" REL="I3" TITLE="defpup"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A142X910c1"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0996365ceb"></A>Defines a pop-up menu.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1116"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0996514ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0996618ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A142X910c5"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X912170"></A><B>Int32 defpup(Char8</B> <B>*</B><A HREF="defpup.html#A213X912175"><I>string</I></A> [<B>, Int32</B> <A HREF="defpup.html#A213X91217d"><I>arguments</I></A> ...] <B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010b52"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010b53"></A>None: available only in C.</PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A142X910c7"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0996991ceb"></A>The <B>defpup </B>subroutine defines a pop-up menu and returns a menu identifier. </P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9ddd"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A142X910c9"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912175"></A><I>string</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the pointer to the text to add as a menu item. There are seven menu item type flags 
for optional pairing with each menu item: 


<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912176"></A><B>%t </B></TD>
<TD>  Marks item text as the menu title string. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912177"></A><B>%F </B></TD>
<TD>  Invokes a routine for every selection from this menu except those marked with a <B>%n</B> flag. You must specify the invoked routine in the <A HREF="defpup.html#A213X91217d"><I>arguments</I></A> parameter. The value of the menu item is used as a parameter of the executed routine. Thus, if you select the third menu item, the system passes 3 as a parameter to the function specified by the <B>%F</B> flag. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912178"></A><B>%f </B></TD>
<TD>  Invokes a routine when this particular menu item is selected. You must specify the invoked routine in the <A HREF="defpup.html#A213X91217d"><I>arguments</I></A> parameter. The value of the menu item is passed as a parameter of the routine. Thus, if you select the third menu item, the system passes 3 as a parameter to the routine specified by the <B>%f</B> flag. If you have also used the<B> %F</B> flag within this menu, then the result of the <B>%f </B>flag is passed as a parameter of the <B>%F</B> flag.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912179"></A><B>%l </B></TD>
<TD>  Adds a line under the current entry. This is useful in providing visual clues for grouping like entries together. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X91217a"></A><B>%m </B></TD>
<TD>  Pops up a menu whenever this menu item is selected. You must provide the menu identifier of the new menu in the <A HREF="defpup.html#A213X91217d"><I>arguments</I></A> parameter.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X91217b"></A><B>%n </B></TD>
<TD>  Like the <B>%f</B> flag, this flag invokes a routine when the user selects this menu item. However, the <B>%n</B> flag differs from the <B>%f</B> flag in that it ignores the routine (if any) specified by the <B>%F</B> flag. The value of the menu item is passed as a parameter of the executed routine. Thus, if you select the third menu item, the system passes 3 as a parameter to the function specified by the <B>%f</B> flag. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X91217c"></A><B>%x</B><I>n </I></TD>
<TD>  Assigns a numeric value to this menu item. This value overrides the default position-based value assigned to this menu item (third item=3). You must enter the numeric value as the part of the text string specified by the <I>n</I> parameter. Do not use the <A HREF="defpup.html#A213X91217d"><I>arguments</I></A> parameter to specify the numeric value.</TD></TR></TABLE></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X91217d"></A><I>arguments </I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies an optional set of arguments. Each argument expects the command or submenu to be assigned to this menu item. The <I>arguments</I> parameter can be used as many times as necessary. </TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A142X910cd"></A>Return Value</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0997826ceb"></A>The menu identifier of the menu just defined.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A30C011008"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0997980ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="curved_c.html#A16C0c830"><B>curved.c</B></A> uses the <B>defpup</B> subroutine to define a pop-up menu. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A64C0165bb"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0998141ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1119"></A>File</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C111a"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A142X910df"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0998417ceb"></A>Adding an item to an existing pop-up menu with the <A HREF="addtopup.html#A142X9109d"><B>addtopup</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0998533ceb"></A>Displaying a pop-up menu with the <A HREF="dopup.html#A142X910e1"><B>dopup</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0998649ceb"></A>Deallocating a pop-up menu and its data structures with the <A HREF="freepup.html#A142X91103"><B>freepup</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0998756ceb"></A>Allocating and initializing a structure for a new pop-up menu with the <A HREF="newpup.html#A142X91125"><B>newpup</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0998873ceb"></A>Enabling or disabling a given pop-up entry with the <A HREF="setpup.html#A5um1280marj"><B>setpup</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0998979ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A> and Creating and Managing <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/popupmenus.html#popupmenus.html">Pop-Up Menus</A>.</P><hr><center>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>

<a href="delobj.html">Next</a>  |

 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A143X9d3f"></A>defrasterfont Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX403" REL="I1" TITLE="defrasterfont subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX404" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX405" REL="I2" TITLE="text"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX406" REL="I3" TITLE="defrasterfont"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX407" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX408" REL="I2" TITLE="text"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX409" REL="I3" TITLE="defining raster font bitmaps"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A143X9d41"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B09B9995ceb"></A>Defines bitmaps for a raster font.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C121c"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B09BA145ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B09BA249ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9d45"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A143X9d46"></A><B>void defrasterfont</B>
<B>(Int32</B> <A HREF="defrasterfont.html#A213X912613"><I>index</I></A><B>, Int16</B> <A HREF="defrasterfont.html#A213X912614"><I>height</I></A><B>, </B>
<B>Int16</B> <A HREF="defrasterfont.html#A213X912615"><I>numchars</I></A><B>, Fontchar</B> <A HREF="defrasterfont.html#A213X912616"><I>chars</I></A><B> [&nbsp;], </B>
<B>Int16</B> <A HREF="defrasterfont.html#A213X91261d"><I>numraster</I></A><B>, Int16</B> <A HREF="defrasterfont.html#A213X91261e"><I>raster</I></A><B> [&nbsp;])</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010bf4"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B09BA519ceb"></A><B>SUBROUTINE DEFRAS(</B><I>index</I><B>,</B> <I>height</I><B>,</B> <I>numchars</I><B>,</B> <I>chars</I><B>,</B> <I>numraster</I><B>,</B> <I>raster</I><B>)</B></P>

<P><B>INTEGER *4 </B><I>index</I><B>,</B><I> height</I><B>,</B> <I>numchars</I><B>,</B> <I>numraster</I></P>

<P><B>INTEGER*2 </B><I>raster</I><B>(</B><I>numraster</I><B>),</B> <I>chars</I><B>(4*</B><I>numchars</I><B>)</B></P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A79C121f"></A><B>Note: </B>For FORTRAN users, this subroutine accepts long integer parameters (INTEGER*4) when invoked from a FORTRAN program, although it accepts short integers when invoked from a C program. The C and FORTRAN syntax shown here reflect this difference.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A143X9d47"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B09BA735ceb"></A>The <B>defrasterfont </B>subroutine defines a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P073b">raster font</A>.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B09BA844ceb"></A>To replace a raster font, specify the index of the previous font as the index for the new font. To delete a raster font, define a font with no characters. 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A13791abd">Patterns</A>, 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A172P1436">linestyles</A>, 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A263A93ae">cursors</A>, and 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A270A983b">fonts</A> are available to all windows when using multiple windows. The assumed code set table encoding is 
locale dependent. In most locales, this is an ISO8859 encoding.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><B>Notes: </B>
<OL><LI><A NAME="A62C015d86"></A>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</LI>

<LI><A NAME="A62C015d87"></A>The hardest part of creating a new raster font is generating a bitmap for each character. You may want to write a graphically oriented tool for creating the bitmaps expected by the <A HREF="defrasterfont.html#A213X91261e"><I>raster</I></A> parameter.</LI></OL></BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A143X9d49"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912613"></A><I>index</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies a constant to use as the identifier for this raster font. This constant is used as an index into a font table. The default font, 0, is a fixed-pitch font with a height of 16 and width of 9. Font 0 cannot be redefined. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912614"></A><I>height</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the maximum height (in pixels) for a character.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912615"></A><I>numchars</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the number of characters in this font.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912616"></A><I>chars</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies an array of character description structures of type <B>Fontchar</B>. The <B>Fontchar</B> structure is defined in the <B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B> file as: 

<PRE><A NAME="A139X91ecd"></A>typedef&nbsp;struct&nbsp;{
&nbsp;&nbsp;unsigned&nbsp;short&nbsp;offset;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Byte&nbsp;w,&nbsp;h;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;signed&nbsp;char&nbsp;xoff,&nbsp;yoff;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;short&nbsp;width;
}&nbsp;Fontchar;</PRE>




<P><A NAME="A232C13d"></A>The character description structures are as follows:</P>




<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912617"></A><B>offset</B> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the element of the <A HREF="defrasterfont.html#A213X91261e"><I>raster</I></A> array at which the bitmap for this character starts. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912618"></A><B>w</B></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the number of columns in the bitmap that contain set bits (character width).</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912619"></A><B>h</B> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the number of rows in the bitmap of the character (including ascender and descender).</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X91261a"></A><B>xoff</B> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the bitmap columns between the start of the character's bitmap and the start of the character. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X91261b"></A><B>yoff</B> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the number of rows between the character's baseline and the bottom of the bitmap. For characters with descenders (for example, g) this value is a negative number. For characters that rest entirely on the baseline, this value is zero.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X91261c"></A><B>width</B> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the pixel width for the character. This value tells the system how far to space after drawing the character. (This value is added to the character position.) </TD></TR></TABLE></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X91261d"></A><I>numraster</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the length of the <A HREF="defrasterfont.html#A213X91261e"><I>raster</I></A> parameter array.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X91261e"></A><I>raster</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies a one-dimensional array that contains all the bitmaps for the characters in the font. Each element of the array is a 16-bit integer and the elements are ordered left to right, bottom to top. When interpreting each element, the bits are left justified within the character's 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A255B966">bounding box</A>.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P><A NAME="E1B09BB969ceb"></A>Maximum row width for a single bitmap is not limited to the capacity of a single 16-bit integer array element. The rows of a bitmap may span more than one array element. However, each new row in the character bitmap must start with its own array element. Likewise, each new character bitmap must start with its own array element. The system reads the row width and starting location for a character bitmap from the structures records in the <A HREF="defrasterfont.html#A213X912616"><I>chars</I></A> array.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A30C011054"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B09BC124ceb"></A>The example C language programs <A HREF="curved_c.html#A16C0c830"><B>curved.c</B></A> and <A HREF="font3_c.html#A149C18a9"><B>font3.c</B></A> use the <B>defrasterfont</B> subroutine to define a new raster font. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015d88"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B09BC285ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B09BC392ceb"></A>This subroutine is not available for National Language Support.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1220"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1221"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1222"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9d5f"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B09BC762ceb"></A>Drawing a string of raster characters on the screen with the <A HREF="charstr.html#A143X9cfb"><B>charstr</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B09BC869ceb"></A>Updating the current character position with the <A HREF="cmov.html#A143X9d1d"><B>cmov</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B09BC976ceb"></A>Selecting a raster font with the <A HREF="font.html#A143X9d61"><B>font</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B09BD084ceb"></A>Returning the current character position with the <A HREF="getcpos.html#A144X9364"><B>getcpos</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B09BD192ceb"></A>Returning the baseline extent of the longest character descender with the <A HREF="getdescender.html#A144X9386"><B>getdescender</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B09BD300ceb"></A>Returning the current raster font number with the <A HREF="getfont.html#A144X93a8"><B>getfont</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B09BD407ceb"></A>Returning the maximum character height in the current raster font with the <A HREF="getheight.html#A144X93ca"><B>getheight</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B09BD514ceb"></A>Using an AIXwindows font to define a raster font with the <A HREF="loadXfont.html#vUO390nita"><B>loadXfont</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B09BD620ceb"></A>Returning the width of the specified text string with the <A HREF="strwidth.html#A144X93ec"><B>strwidth</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<H2><A NAME="A142X940a"></A>delobj Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX410" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX411" REL="I2" TITLE="object (display list)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX412" REL="I3" TITLE="delobj"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX413" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX414" REL="I2" TITLE="object (display list)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX415" REL="I3" TITLE="deleting"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX416" REL="I1" TITLE="delobj subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A142X940c"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B09E0178ceb"></A>Deletes an object.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C11f"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B09E0326ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B09E0429ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A142X9410"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A142X9411"></A><B>void delobj(Int32 </B><A HREF="delobj.html#A142X9415"><I>object</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010aa9"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010aaa"></A><B>SUBROUTINE DELOBJ(</B><I>object</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>object</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A142X9412"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B09E0791ceb"></A>The <B>delobj</B> subroutine deletes an entire object, freeing the entire display list and all associated tags. The object identifier becomes undefined and unused.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A4C09c69"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>. </BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A142X9414"></A>Parameter</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A142X9415"></A><I>object</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the identifier of the object to delete.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015d10"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B09E1113ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C122"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C123"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C124"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A142X942a"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B09E1433ceb"></A>Deleting tags from a display list with the <A HREF="deltag.html#A1N61210marj"><B>deltag</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B09E1540ceb"></A>Opening an object for editing with the <A HREF="editobj.html#A142X9360"><B>editobj</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B09E1647ceb"></A>Creating an object with the <A HREF="makeobj.html#A142X912d"><B>makeobj</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B09E1754ceb"></A>Deleting a routine from an object with the <A HREF="objdelete.html#A142X9afd"><B>objdelete</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<A NAME="INDEX417" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX418" REL="I2" TITLE="object (display list)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX419" REL="I3" TITLE="deltag"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX420" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX421" REL="I2" TITLE="object (display list)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX422" REL="I3" TITLE="deleting tags from"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX423" REL="I1" TITLE="deltag subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911fa8"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B09FE616ceb"></A>Deletes tags from objects.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C125"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B09FE769ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B09FE873ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911fab"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X911fac"></A><B>void deltag(Int32 </B><A HREF="deltag.html#QLQ2b0marj"><I>tag</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010a91"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010a92"></A><B>SUBROUTINE DELTAG(</B><I>tag</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>tag</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911faf"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B09FF234ceb"></A>The <B>deltag</B> subroutine removes the tag from the object currently open for editing. The <SAMP>STARTTAG</SAMP> and <SAMP>ENDTAG</SAMP> special tags cannot be deleted. </P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9d96"></A><B>Note: </B>This editing subroutine itself cannot be used to add to a
 <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A213X911fb2"></A>Parameter</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="QLQ2b0marj"></A><I>tag</I><B></B></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the tag to delete. </TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015d04"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B09FF559ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C128"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C129"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C12a"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911fbe"></A>Related Information</H3>

<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">
<HTML>
<HEAD>

<TITLE>depthcue.c Example C Language Program
</TITLE>
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="cylinder2_c.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="doily_c.html">Next</a>  |
<A HREF="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A16C0c8ff"></A>depthcue.c Example C Language Program
</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX2261" REL="I1" TITLE="depthcue.c example program (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2262" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2263" REL="I2" TITLE="example programs"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2264" REL="I3" TITLE="curve and surface patch"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2265" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2266" REL="I2" TITLE="drawing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2267" REL="I3" TITLE="cube"></A>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA35339ttay"></A>/* depthcue.c Example C Language Program 
 *
 * Draws a depthcue'd 3-d wireframe cube with lots of 
 * little points inside. Moving the mouse rotates the
 * cube.
 * NEAR and FAR (Z) clipplanes map to z values of
 * getgdesc(GD_ZMIN) and getgdesc(GD_ZMAX) respectively.
 * Points near NEAR are the brightest, those near FAR are
 * the dimmest. Give two hexadecimal values on the command
 * line to specify which zvalues are mapped to bright
 * and dark.
 *
 * Press the middle mouse to quit.
 */</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA35502ttay"></A>#include &lt;gl/gl.h>
#include &lt;gl/device.h>
#include &lt;math.h></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA35651ttay"></A>#define CUBE 9531</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA35799ttay"></A>float hrand();</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA35965ttay"></A>/*Hold the colormap values*/
static short *CarrayR, *CarrayG, *CarrayB;</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA37547ttay"></A>main (argc,argv)
int argc;
char **argv;
{
  int val, i;
  long near, far,           /*Z buffer and depth cueing*/
     nearest, farthest;     /*information*/
  float inc, c;
  short lo_end=128,         /*Low/High index of the colormap*/ 
     hi_end=255;            /*Used for the depth cueing*/</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA37728ttay"></A>  prefposition(200, 600, 200, 600);
  winopen("depthcue");
  winconstraints();
  doublebuffer();
  gconfig();</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA37914ttay"></A>  /*Find out the nearest and farthest values of the z mapping*/
  nearest   = getgdesc(GD_ZMIN);
  farthest  = getgdesc(GD_ZMAX);</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA38129ttay"></A>  if (argc == 5) {
    near = strtol(argv[1], (char **) NULL, 0);
    far = strtol(argv[2], (char **) NULL, 0);
    lo_end = strtol(argv[3], (char **) NULL, 0);
    hi_end = strtol(argv[4], (char **) NULL, 0);</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA38334ttay"></A>  }
  else if (argc == 3)  {
    near = strtol(argv[1], (char **) NULL, 0);
    far = strtol(argv[2], (char **) NULL, 0);
  }
  else {
    near = nearest;
    far  = farthest;
  }</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA38513ttay"></A>  if (near &lt; nearest)  near=nearest; /*Clamp to adapters constraints*/
  if (far  > farthest) far=farthest;</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA38926ttay"></A>  reshapeviewport();
  perspective(600, 1.0, 350.0, 1400.0);
  lookat(0.0, 0.0, 700.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0);
  qdevice(KEYBD);    
  makeobj(CUBE);              /* generate a bunch of random points */
  for (i = 0; i &lt; 100; i++)
    pnt(hrand(-200.0,200.0), hrand(-200.0,200.0), 
        hrand(-200.0,200.0)); /* and a cube */
  movei(-200, -200, -200);
  drawi( 200, -200, -200);
  drawi( 200,  200, -200);
  drawi(-200,  200, -200);
  drawi(-200, -200, -200);
  drawi(-200, -200,  200);
  drawi(-200,  200,  200);
  drawi(-200,  200, -200);
  movei(-200,  200,  200);
  drawi( 200,  200,  200);
  drawi( 200, -200,  200);
  drawi(-200, -200,  200);
  movei( 200,  200,  200);
  drawi( 200,  200, -200);
  movei( 200, -200, -200);
  drawi( 200, -200,  200);
  closeobj();</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA39103ttay"></A>  /*Save the current colormap so it can be reset when the program ends*/
  save_cmap(lo_end,hi_end); </PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA39280ttay"></A>  /* load the color map with a cyan ramp */
  /* starting at lo_end and going to hi_end inclusively */</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA39478ttay"></A>  inc = 255.0/((float)(hi_end-lo_end));
  c = 0.0;
  for (i = lo_end; i &lt;= hi_end; i++)
    {
      c += inc;
      mapcolor(i, 0,(Int16) c, (Int16) c);
    }</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA39735ttay"></A>  /*Print out the information about the color and z buffer*/
  printf (" near    = %ld, far      = %ld \n", near, far);
  printf (" nearest = %ld, farthest = %ld \n", nearest, farthest);
  printf (" low colormap = %d, high colormap = %d\n", lo_end, hi_end);
  printf (" number of colors in ramp = %d \n", 1+hi_end-lo_end);</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA39981ttay"></A>  /* Set the range of z values that will be stored in the  */
  /* bitplanes.  The percentage takes care of the error    */
  /* accumulation that occurs when the farthest limits are */
  /* used.                                                 */
  lsetdepth((long)(near*0.98), (long)(far*0.98));</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA3A202ttay"></A>  /* set up the mapping of z values to color map           */
  /* indexes: z value nearest is mapped to index lo_end    */
  /* and z value farthest is mapped to index hi_end        */
  lshaderange(lo_end,hi_end,nearest,farthest);</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA3A414ttay"></A>  /* turn on depthcue mode:  the color index of each       */
  /* pixel in points and lines is determined from the      */
  /* z value of the pixel                                  */
  depthcue(TRUE);</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA3A678ttay"></A>  /* until a key is pressed, rotate cube according to      */
  /* movement of the mouse                                 */
  while (!getbutton(MIDDLEMOUSE)) {
    pushmatrix();
    rotate(3*getvaluator(MOUSEY), 'x');
    rotate(3*getvaluator(MOUSEX), 'y');
    color(BLACK);
    clear();
    callobj(CUBE);
    popmatrix();
    swapbuffers();
  }</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA3A856ttay"></A>  /*Restore the colormap*/
  restore_cmap(lo_end,hi_end);
  /*Exit gracefully*/
  gexit();
  exit(1);
}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA3B097ttay"></A>/* this routine returns random numbers in the            */
/* specified range                                       */
float hrand(low,high)
float low,high;
{
  float val;    
  val = ((float)( (short)rand() &amp; 0xffff)) / ((float)0xffff);
  return( (2.0 * val * (high-low)) + low);
}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA3B266ttay"></A>/*This saves the colormap*/
save_cmap(lo_end,hi_end)
short lo_end,hi_end;
{</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA3B460ttay"></A>  CarrayR = calloc (lo_end+hi_end,sizeof(short));
  CarrayG = calloc (lo_end+hi_end,sizeof(short));
  CarrayB = calloc (lo_end+hi_end,sizeof(short));</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA3B633ttay"></A>  getmcolors ((Int16 const)lo_end,(Int16 const)hi_end,
     CarrayR, CarrayG, CarrayB);
}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA3B834ttay"></A>/*This restores the colormap*/
restore_cmap(lo_end,hi_end)
short lo_end,hi_end;
{
  mapcolors ((Int16 const)lo_end,(Int16 const)hi_end,
     CarrayR, CarrayG, CarrayB);
}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA3C214ttay"></A>/*Changes
    -  Put constants in the program for the colormap creation
    -  This program accept 2 arguments that are the nearest and
       farthest z values which are used for the depth cueing.
       This program called: lshaderange(128,255,-0x40000,0x3FFFFF);
       now:    lshaderange(lo_end,hi_end,nearest,farthest);
    -  Used a define for the object number (called CUBE)
    -  Save/restore the colormap
    -  The defaults of the near and far z mappings are no longer
       hard coded  ( near = -0x400000; far = 0x3fffff;), but are
       initialized with getgdesc.  Also the near and far mappings
       are clamped to there min and max values respectively.
*/</PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A200C116a"></A>Related Information</H3>

<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="PNK22d0marj"></A>depthcue Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX424" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX425" REL="I2" TITLE="depth-cue"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX426" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX427" REL="I2" TITLE="depth-cueing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX428" REL="I3" TITLE="turning on and off"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX429" REL="I1" TITLE="depthcue subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A60C015778"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0A1D071ceb"></A>Turns depth-cueing on and off.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C1147"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0A1D221ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0A1D326ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A60C01577c"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A60C01577d"></A><B>void depthcue(Int32 </B><A HREF="depthcue.html#T2K2marj"><I>mode</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A60C01577e"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A60C01577f"></A><B>SUBROUTINE DEPTHC(</B><I>mode</I><B>)</B>
<B>LOGICAL </B><I>mode</I><B>;</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A60C015780"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0A1D691ceb"></A>The <B>depthcue</B> subroutine turns 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A150P19d9">depth-cueing</A> on or off. If the value of the <A HREF="depthcue.html#T2K2marj"><I>mode</I></A> parameter is TRUE, depth-cueing is enabled, and all lines, points, characters, and polygons drawn by the system are depth-cued. This means that the color of the lines, points, characters, or polygons are determined by the <I>z</I> values and the range of color indexes specified by the <A HREF="lshaderange.html#fkk1d0marj"><B>lshaderange</B></A> or <A HREF="lRGBrange.html#A143X93d8"><B>lRGBrange</B></A> subroutine determines the color of the lines, points, characters, or polygons. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0A1D799ceb"></A>The <I>z</I> values, whose range is set by the <A HREF="lsetdepth.html#naR120marj"><B>lsetdepth</B></A> subroutine, are mapped linearly into the range of color indexes. In this mode, lines that vary greatly in <I>z</I> value span the range of colors specified by the <B>lshaderange</B> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0A1D917ceb"></A>For depth-cueing to work properly, the color map locations specified by the <A HREF="lshaderange.html#fkk1d0marj"><B>lshaderange</B></A> subroutine must be loaded with a series of colors that gradually increase or decrease in intensity. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A60C015784"></A>Parameter</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="T2K2marj"></A><I>mode</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies a value indicating OFF or ON state of depth-cueing. Values for the <I>mode</I> parameter are as follows:</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A60C015785"></A></TD>
<TD>  1 = True (ON)</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A60C015786"></A></TD>
<TD>  0 = False (OFF)</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A60C015787"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0A1E274ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="depthcue_c.html#A16C0c8ff"><B>depthcue.c</B></A> uses the <B>depthcue</B> subroutine to turn on depth-cueing. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A64C0165aa"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0A1E437ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the  AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C114a"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C114b"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C114c"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A60C01578b"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0A1E764ceb"></A>Indicating whether depth-cue mode is on or off with the <A HREF="getdcm.html#A5OK230marj"><B>getdcm</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0A1E871ceb"></A>Setting the range of RGB colors used for depth-cueing with the <A HREF="lRGBrange.html#A143X93d8"><B>lRGBrange</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0A1E978ceb"></A>Setting the viewport depth range with the <A HREF="lsetdepth.html#naR120marj"><B>lsetdepth</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0A1F086ceb"></A>Setting the range of color indexes used for depth-cueing with the <A HREF="lshaderange.html#fkk1d0marj"><B>lshaderange</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0A1F194ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A>, Performing <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/depth-cueing.html">Depth-Cueing</A>, and Working in <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/workcolor.html#workcolor.html">Color Map and RGB Modes</A>.</P><hr><center>

<H2><A NAME="A16C0c90f"></A>doily.c Example C Language Program
</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX2268" REL="I1" TITLE="doily.c example program (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2269" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2270" REL="I2" TITLE="example programs"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2271" REL="I3" TITLE="drawing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2272" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2273" REL="I2" TITLE="doily"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2274" REL="I3" TITLE="drawing"></A>

<A NAME="INDEX2276" REL="I2" TITLE="drawing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2277" REL="I3" TITLE="doily"></A>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA63093ttay"></A>/*
doily.c:</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA63299ttay"></A>Draws a doily depending on how many points you give
it (range is
currently set between 3..100).  point count is equivale
nt to how
many line segments make up the circle's edge.
*/</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA63462ttay"></A>#include &lt;gl/gl.h>
#include &lt;gl/device.h>
#include &lt;math.h></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA63612ttay"></A>#define PI 3.1415926535</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA63762ttay"></A>float points[100][2];</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA63918ttay"></A>main(argc, argv)
int argc;
char *argv[];
{</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA64131ttay"></A>  int val,dev;
  long numpts;            /* First figure out how many points there are. */</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA64303ttay"></A>  if (argc != 2) {
    printf("Usage: %s &lt;point_count>\n", argv[0]);
    exit(0);
  }</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA64518ttay"></A>  numpts = atoi(argv[1]); /* convert argument to internal format */
  if (numpts > 100) {
    printf("Too many points\n");
    exit(0);
  }
  else if (numpts &lt; 3) {
    printf("Too few points\n"); exit(0);
  }</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA64764ttay"></A>  initialize(numpts);    
  while (TRUE) {       
    if (qtest()) {           
      dev = qread(&amp;val);           
      if (dev == ESCKEY) {
        gexit();
        exit(0);
      }
      else if (dev == REDRAW) {
        reshapeviewport();
        drawdoily(numpts);
      }
    }
  }</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA64906ttay"></A>}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA65060ttay"></A>initialize(numpts)
long numpts;
{</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA65266ttay"></A>  int gid;
  long i;    /* Now get the x and y coordinates of numpts equally-
              * spaced points around the unit circle.
              */
  for (i = 0; i &lt; numpts; i++) {</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA66741ttay"></A>    points[i][0] = cos((i*2.0*PI)/numpts);
    points[i][1] = sin((i*2.0*PI)/numpts);
  }
  keepaspect(1,1);
  prefposition(XMAXSCREEN/4,XMAXSCREEN*3/4,YMAXSCREEN/4,
      YMAXSCREEN*3/4);
  gid = winopen("doily");    
  qdevice(ESCKEY);
  qdevice(REDRAW);
  qenter(REDRAW,gid);    
  ortho2(-1.2, 1.2, -1.2, 1.2);</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA66883ttay"></A>}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA67037ttay"></A>drawdoily(numpts)
long numpts;
{</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA67184ttay"></A>  long i,j;    </PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA67396ttay"></A>  color(BLACK);
  clear();
  color(RED);    
  for (i = 0; i &lt; numpts; i++)
    for (j = i+1; j &lt; numpts; j++) {
      move2(points[i][0], points[i][1]);
      draw2(points[j][0], points[j][1]);
    }</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA67538ttay"></A>}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA67694ttay"></A>/*
  Changes:
  - exit(); to exit(1);
*/</PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A200C116d"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D77FF465ceb"></A>The <A HREF="keepaspect.html#A142X91896"><B>keepaspect</B></A> subroutine<A HREF="A142X91896" REL="PAGENUM"></A>, <A HREF="prefposition.html#A142X9164f"><B>prefposition</B></A> subroutine<A HREF="A142X9164f" REL="PAGENUM"></A>.</P>

<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">

<TITLE>dopup Subroutine
</TITLE>
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="depthcue.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="doublebuffer.html">Next</a>  |
<A href="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A142X910e1"></A>dopup Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX430" REL="I1" TITLE="dopup subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX431" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX432" REL="I2" TITLE="popp menus"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX433" REL="I3" TITLE="displaying"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX434" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX435" REL="I2" TITLE="popp menu"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX436" REL="I3" TITLE="dopup"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A142X910e3"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0A3E355ceb"></A>Displays the specified pop-up menu.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C111d"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0A3E502ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0A3E607ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A142X910e7"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X91218e"></A><B>Int32 dopup(Int32</B> <A HREF="dopup.html#A213X912194"><I>popup</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010b56"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010b57"></A><B>INTEGER*4 FUNCTION DOPUP(</B><I>popup</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4</B> <I>popup</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A142X910e9"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0A3E969ceb"></A>The <B>dopup </B>subroutine displays the specified pop-up menu until the user makes a selection. If the calling program has the input focus, the specified menu is displayed and the system returns the value resulting from the item selection.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0A3F076ceb"></A>The value can be returned by a submenu, a function, or a number bound directly to an item. If no selection is made, the <B>dopup </B>subroutine returns a value of -1 (negative one).</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0A3F187ceb"></A>The <B>dopup</B> subroutine manipulates events in the event queue. If the <B>dopup</B> subroutine is called as a result of a left mouse or middle mouse button press event, the menu remains posted until the right mouse button is pressed to make a selection. The <B>dopup</B> subroutine removes a pair of right mouse press and release events from the event queue (if the right mouse was queued), and also removes the left mouse or middle mouse button release event.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0A3F295ceb"></A>If the <B>dopup</B> subroutine is called as a result of a right mouse button press event, the menu remains posted until the right mouse button is released. The menu entry selected is the entry that was highlighted when the right mouse button was released. The <B>dopup</B> subroutine removes the right mouse button release event from the event queue.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0A3F402ceb"></A>If no selection is made (that is, if the user releases the right mouse button off the pop-up menu) no menu entry selection is made, and the <B>dopup</B> subroutine returns a value of -1. The right mouse button release event is removed from the queue.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0A3F510ceb"></A>In more complicated event sequences, all mouse button-up events up to and including the first right mouse button-up event are removed. If the user accidently presses other mouse buttons before making a pop-up menu selection, <I>orphaned</I> button down events (button down events without matching button up events) may remain in the event queue.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0A3F617ceb"></A>When the menu is defined, the <A HREF="defpup.html#A142X910bf"><B>defpup</B></A> or <A HREF="addtopup.html#A142X9109d"><B>addtopup</B></A> subroutine specifies the list of menu entries and their corresponding actions.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9de0"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A142X910eb"></A>Parameter</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912194"></A><I>popup</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies which pop-up menu to display.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A30C01100a"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0A3F942ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="curved_c.html#A16C0c830"><B>curved.c</B></A> uses the <B>dopup</B> subroutine to display a pop-up menu.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A64C0165bf"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0A40101ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1120"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1121"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1122"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A142X91101"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0A40428ceb"></A>Adding an item to an existing pop-up menu with the <A HREF="addtopup.html#A142X9109d"><B>addtopup</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0A40544ceb"></A>Defining a pop-up menu with the <A HREF="defpup.html#A142X910bf"><B>defpup</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0A40660ceb"></A>Deallocating a pop-up menu and its data structures with the <A HREF="freepup.html#A142X91103"><B>freepup</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0A40768ceb"></A>Allocating and initializing a structure for a new pop-up menu with the <A HREF="newpup.html#A142X91125"><B>newpup</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0A40883ceb"></A>Enabling or disabling a given pop-up entry with the <A HREF="setpup.html#A5um1280marj"><B>setpup</B></A> subroutine.</P>
