```html
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A16C0c8ee"></A>doublebuff.c Example C Language Program
</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX2278" REL="I1" TITLE="doublebuff.c example program (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2279" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2280" REL="I2" TITLE="example programs"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2281" REL="I3" TITLE="frame buffer"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2282" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2283" REL="I2" TITLE="frame buffer"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2284" REL="I3" TITLE="animation"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2285" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2286" REL="I2" TITLE="double buffering"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2287" REL="I3" TITLE="animation"></A>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA26071ttay"></A>/* doublebuff.c:
 *
 * This program demonstrates double buffering.
 * Double buffering is a method for providing smooth,
 * flicker free animation of moving images. This example
 * draws two wireframe" cubes, one inside the other.
 * The cubes are connected to the mouse, and move as the
 * mouse is moved. Notice how the cubes move smoothly as
 * the mouse is moved.
 *
 * Holding down the shift key puts the system into 
 * singlebuffer mode. Notice how the image flickers.
 * This flickering occurs because you are watching the
 * window being cleared and the cube being redrawn.
 * Letting go of the shift key puts the system back into
 * doublebuffer mode. The motion is smooth because all
 * drawing is occurring in the back buffer, which is 
 * invisible. When the drawing is completed, the front
 * and back buffers are * exchanged.
 */</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA26229ttay"></A>#include &lt;gl/gl.h>
#include &lt;gl/device.h></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA26387ttay"></A>#define DOUBLE_BUFFER 1
#define SINGLE_BUFFER 0</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA26680ttay"></A>int buffer_mode=DOUBLE_BUFFER;         /* DOUBLE_BUFFER=doublebuffer, * 1=singlebuffer */
main()
{
  int x, y;                /*  current position of object */
  Device dev;
  short val;
  long event=0;
  x = 0;
  y = 0;
  initialize();
  while(TRUE) {
    if (qtest())           /*If there are any events in the queue*/
      dev = qread(&amp;val);   /*Read the queue*/
      /*This allows the program always move the cube*/</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA27108ttay"></A>    switch(dev) {
    case ESCKEY:           /*  exit program with ESC */
      gexit();
      exit(0);
      break;
    case REDRAW:           /* window was exposed. Redraw it. */
      reshapeviewport();
      drawcube(x,y);
      break; 
    case LEFTMOUSE:        /* LEFTMOUSE turns on double buffer*/
      if (buffer_mode == SINGLE_BUFFER){
        buffer_mode = DOUBLE_BUFFER;
        doublebuffer();    /* put system in doublebuffer mode */
        gconfig();
      }
      break;
    case RIGHTMOUSE:       /* RIGHTMOUSE turns on single buffer*/
      if (buffer_mode == DOUBLE_BUFFER) {
        buffer_mode = SINGLE_BUFFER;
        singlebuffer();    /* put system in singlebuffer mode */
        gconfig();
      }
      break;
    }                      /*End of the switch statement*/</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA27303ttay"></A>    y = getvaluator(MOUSEX); /*read the x,y value of the mouse*/
    x = getvaluator(MOUSEY); /*works outside of the window*/
    drawcube(x,y);
  }
}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA27560ttay"></A>initialize()
{
  /* open a window, 500 by 500 pixels */
  prefsize (500,500);
  winopen("doublebuffer"); /* put system into double buffer mode */
  winconstraints();
  doublebuffer();
  gconfig();               /* queue up the shift keys and the mouse */
  qdevice (ESCKEY);
  qdevice (LEFTMOUSE);
  qdevice (RIGHTMOUSE);</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA27730ttay"></A>  /* use perspective projection */
  perspective (400, 3.0/2.0, 0.001, 100000.0);</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA27934ttay"></A>  /* look at the origin from a distance of three units */
  translate (0.0, 0.0, -3.0);
  /* draw the first time, so that we don't stare
      * at a blank screen */
  drawcube();
}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA28246ttay"></A>drawcube(rotx,roty)
int rotx, roty;
{
  /* clear to background color */
  color(BLACK);
  clear();
  /* set the drawing color */
  color(WHITE);
  pushmatrix();
  /* rotate into the desired viewing position */
  rotate(rotx,'x');
  rotate(roty,'y');
  /* draw the big cube */
  cube();
  /* draw the small cube */
  scale(0.3,0.3,0.3);
  cube();
  popmatrix();</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA28428ttay"></A>  /* put up a message, instructions */
  cmov2 (-0.4,-1.0);
  charstr ("Left: double buffer |  Right: single buffer");</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA28651ttay"></A>  /* put up a message, showing buffering mode */
  cmov2 (-0.95, 0.95);
  if (buffer_mode == SINGLE_BUFFER) {
    charstr ("single-buffered, flickering image");
  }
  else {
    charstr ("double-buffered, smoothly animated image");
  }</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA28849ttay"></A>  /*If it is double buffered, exchange the front and back buffers */
  /*Otherwise if it is single buffered the library ignores*/
  /*this call*/
  swapbuffers();</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA28993ttay"></A>}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA29197ttay"></A>cube()
{
  /* make a cube out of 4 squares */
  pushmatrix();
  side();
  rotate(900,'x');
  side();
  rotate(900,'x');
  side();
  rotate(900,'x');
  side();
  popmatrix();
}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA29392ttay"></A>side()
{
  /* make a square translated 0.5 in the z direction */
  pushmatrix();
  translate(0.0,0.0,0.5);
  rect(-0.5,-0.5,0.5,0.5);
  popmatrix();
}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA29826ttay"></A>/*Changes:
  - The line once read buffer_mode = ; and now it reads:
        buffer_mode = 1; (Actually now it is SINGLE_BUFFER)
  - The qread and qdevice of MOUSEX and MOUSEY was removed.
    It is too choppy and it cannot read the mouse once the
    pointer's hot spot is outside of the window.  Now it is
    the getvaluator (MOUSE[X|Y]).
  - Put if (qtest) before the qread so the program does
    not stay in the qread command when the mouse's hot
    spot is outside of the window.
  - Added the defines for better programming style
      #define DOUBLE_BUFFER 1
      #define SINGLE_BUFFER 0
  - Made the left and right mouse buttons represent 
      double and single buffer animation respectively
  - Added the button instructions in the window (above) 
  - Added winconstraints so the window can be made larger
*/</PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A200C1167"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D780D198ceb"></A>The <A HREF="doublebuffer.html#A145X91a7"><B>doublebuffer</B></A> subroutine<A HREF="A145X91a7" REL="PAGENUM"></A>.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D780D224ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/animatescene.html#animatescene.html">Creating Animated Scenes</A> in<I> GL3.2 Version 4 for AIX: Programming Concepts</I>.</P>
```

```html
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A145X91a7"></A>doublebuffer Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX437" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX438" REL="I2" TITLE="animation"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX439" REL="I3" TITLE="doublebuffer"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX440" REL="I1" TITLE="doublebuffer subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX441" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX442" REL="I2" TITLE="display mode"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX443" REL="I3" TITLE="setting to double buffer mode"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX444" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX445" REL="I2" TITLE="frame buffer configuration"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX446" REL="I3" TITLE="doublebuffer"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A145X91a9"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0A5E021ceb"></A>Sets the display mode to double buffer mode. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A77C114"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0A5E170ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0A5E276ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A145X91ac"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A145X91ad"></A><B>void doublebuffer(&nbsp;)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A145X9185"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A145X9188"></A><B>SUBROUTINE DOUBLEBUFFER</B></PRE>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A145X91a3"></A><B>Note: </B>In using FORTRAN syntax, it is necessary to spell out DOUBLEBUFFER because the word <I>double</I> is a reserved word.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A145X91b0"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0A5E690ceb"></A>The <B>doublebuffer </B>subroutine reorganizes the frame buffer 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A3C0F2A3129mhay">bitplanes</A>
 into a pair of frame buffers, the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P051c">front buffer and the back buffer</A>. In 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0474">double buffer mode</A>, only the front buffer is displayed. Drawing routines normally update only the back bitplanes; the <A HREF="frontbuffer.html#A145X9a0"><B>frontbuffer</B></A> and <A HREF="backbuffer.html#A145X94a"><B>backbuffer</B></A> subroutines can override the default. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0A5E798ceb"></A>The actual repartitioning of the frame buffer into double buffer mode does not occur until the <A HREF="gconfig.html#hS4260nita"><B>gconfig</B></A> subroutine is called. The <A HREF="gconfig.html#hS4260nita"><B>gconfig</B></A> subroutine sets <B>frontbuffer</B> = False and <B>backbuffer</B> = True in double buffer mode.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0A5E905ceb"></A>To determine the number of bitplanes available in each buffer, use the <A HREF="getgdesc.html#t9311e0marj"><B>getgdesc</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9c5f"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A145X91b6"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0A5F119ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="doublebuff_c.html#A16C0c8ee"><B>doublebuff.c</B></A> sets the display mode for double buffering with the <B>doublebuffer</B> subroutine to allow smooth motion when moving and redrawing a cube. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015c95"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0A5F280ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A145X91a1"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C117"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C118"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A258C01c338"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0A5F599ceb"></A>Enabling updating in the back buffer with the <A HREF="backbuffer.html#A145X94a"><B>backbuffer</B></A> subroutine. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0A5F706ceb"></A>Reconfiguring the system with the <A HREF="gconfig.html#hS4260nita"><B>gconfig</B></A> subroutine.<B>    </B></P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0A5F813ceb"></A>Finding out which buffers are enabled for writing with the <A HREF="getbuffer.html#A145X9f6"><B>getbuffer</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0A5F920ceb"></A>Returning the current display mode with the <A HREF="getdisplaymode.html#A145X9206"><B>getdisplaymode</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0A60028ceb"></A>Returning the number of bitplanes available in each buffer with the <A HREF="getgdesc.html#t9311e0marj"><B>getgdesc</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0A60136ceb"></A>Enabling updating in the front buffer with the <A HREF="frontbuffer.html#A145X9a0"><B>frontbuffer</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0A60243ceb"></A>Writing to and displaying all bitplanes with the <A HREF="singlebuffer.html#A145X9259"><B>singlebuffer</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0A60350ceb"></A>Exchanging the font and back buffers with the <A HREF="swapbuffers.html#A145X9302"><B>swapbuffers</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0A60458ceb"></A>Understanding the <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/glintro.html#A8G44310marj">Hardware Used by GL</A> in<I> GL3.2 Version 4 for AIX: Programming Concepts</I>.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0A60565ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/configframebuf.html#configframebuf.html">Configuring the Frame Buffer</A>, <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/animatescene.html#animatescene.html">Creating Animated Scenes</A>.</P><hr><center>
```

```html
<H2><A NAME="A16C0c922"></A>draw.c Example C Language Program
</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX2288" REL="I1" TITLE="draw.c example program (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2289" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2290" REL="I2" TITLE="example programs"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2291" REL="I3" TITLE="drawing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2292" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2293" REL="I2" TITLE="drawing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2294" REL="I3" TITLE="line"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2295" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2296" REL="I2" TITLE="line"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2297" REL="I3" TITLE="drawing"></A>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA73254ttay"></A>/*
draw.c</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA73413ttay"></A>An absolutely minimal line drawing program.
*/</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA73569ttay"></A>#include &lt;gl/gl.h>
#include &lt;gl/device.h></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA73714ttay"></A>main()
{</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA73876ttay"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Device dev;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;short val;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;unsigned short xpos, ypos;    </PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA74283ttay"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;initialize();    
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;while(TRUE) {        
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;dev = qread(&amp;val);        
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;switch(dev) {               /* wait for mouse down */
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;case ESCKEY:                /* quit */
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;gexit();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;exit(0);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;case REDRAW:
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;reshapeviewport();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(BLACK);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;clear();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(RED);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;break;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;case MIDDLEMOUSE:           /* move */
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;qread(&amp;xpos);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;qread(&amp;ypos);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;move2i(xpos, ypos);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;qread(&amp;val);              /* these three reads clear out */
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;qread(&amp;val);              /* the queue */
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;qread(&amp;val);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;break;            
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;case LEFTMOUSE:             /* draw */
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;qread(&amp;xpos);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;qread(&amp;ypos);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;draw2i(xpos, ypos);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;qread(&amp;val);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;qread(&amp;val);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;qread(&amp;val);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;break;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;}
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA74425ttay"></A>}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA74572ttay"></A>initialize()
{</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA74725ttay"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;int gid;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;float xmax,ymax;   </PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA75011ttay"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;prefposition(XMAXSCREEN/4, XMAXSCREEN*3/4, YMAXSCREEN/4, 
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;    YMAXSCREEN*3/4);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;gid = winopen("draw");   
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;xmax = .5 + (float) XMAXSCREEN;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;ymax = .5 + (float) YMAXSCREEN;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;ortho2(xmax/4.0,xmax*3.0/4.0,ymax/4.0,ymax*3.0/4.0);   
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;qdevice(ESCKEY);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;qdevice(LEFTMOUSE);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;qdevice(MIDDLEMOUSE);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;tie(LEFTMOUSE, MOUSEX, MOUSEY);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;tie(MIDDLEMOUSE, MOUSEX, MOUSEY);   
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(BLACK);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;clear();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(RED);</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA75154ttay"></A>}</PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A200C1171"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D781C475ceb"></A>The <A HREF="getdrawmode.html#A143X9482"><B>getdrawmode</B></A> subroutine<A HREF="A143X9482" REL="PAGENUM"></A>.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D781C501ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/underframebuf.html#underframebuf.html">Understanding the Frame Buffer in GL</A> in<I> GL3.2 Version 4 for AIX: Programming Concepts</I> explains the use of different buffers.</P>
```

```html
<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">
<HTML>
<HEAD>
<META HTTP-EQUIV="Content-Type" CONTENT="text/html; charset=iso-8859-1">

<TITLE>draw Subroutine
</TITLE>
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="doublebuffer.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="drawmode.html">Next</a>  |
<A href="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="EYf2e0marj"></A>draw Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX447" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX448" REL="I2" TITLE="moveraw style"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX449" REL="I3" TITLE="draw"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX450" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX451" REL="I2" TITLE="line"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX452" REL="I3" TITLE="drawing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX453" REL="I1" TITLE="draw subroutine (GL)"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A213X912e47"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0A7E350ceb"></A>Draws a line.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C12e4"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0A7E499ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0A7E603ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912e4a"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X912e4b"></A><B>void draw</B>
<B>(Coord </B><A HREF="draw.html#A213X912e55"><I>x</I></A><B>, Coord</B> <A HREF="draw.html#A213X912e56"><I>y</I></A><B>, Coord</B> <A HREF="draw.html#A213X912e57"><I>z</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="jxJ170marj"></A><B>void drawi</B>
<B>(Icoord </B><A HREF="draw.html#A213X912e55"><I>x</I></A><B>, Icoord</B> <A HREF="draw.html#A213X912e56"><I>y</I></A><B>,</B> <B>Icoord</B> <A HREF="draw.html#A213X912e57"><I>z</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="QyJ230marj"></A><B>void draws</B>
<B>(Scoord </B><A HREF="draw.html#A213X912e55"><I>x</I></A><B>, Scoord</B> <A HREF="draw.html#A213X912e56"><I>y</I></A><B>,</B> <B>Scoord</B> <A HREF="draw.html#A213X912e57"><I>z</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="pzJ150marj"></A><B>void draw2</B>
<B>(Coord </B><A HREF="draw.html#A213X912e55"><I>x</I></A><B>, Coord</B> <A HREF="draw.html#A213X912e56"><I>y</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="qQJ150marj"></A><B>void draw2i</B>
<B>(Icoord </B><A HREF="draw.html#A213X912e55"><I>x</I></A><B>, Icoord</B> <A HREF="draw.html#A213X912e56"><I>y</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A7AJ90marj"></A><B>void draw2s</B>
<B>(Scoord </B><A HREF="draw.html#A213X912e55"><I>x</I></A><B>, Scoord</B> <A HREF="draw.html#A213X912e56"><I>y</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010ab3"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010ab4"></A><B>SUBROUTINE DRAW(</B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>, </B><I>z</I><B>)</B>
<B>REAL </B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>, </B><I>z</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010ab5"></A><B>SUBROUTINE DRAWI(</B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>, </B><I>z</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>, </B><I>z</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010ab6"></A><B>SUBROUTINE DRAWS(</B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>, </B><I>z</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*2 </B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>, </B><I>z</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010ab7"></A><B>SUBROUTINE DRAW2(</B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>)</B>
<B>REAL </B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010ab8"></A><B>SUBROUTINE DRAW2I(</B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010ab9"></A><B>SUBROUTINE DRAW2S(</B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*2 </B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I></PRE>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A78C12e7"></A><B>Note: </B>For FORTRAN users, the INTEGER*2 versions of this subroutine, <B>DRAWS</B> and <B>DRAW2S</B>, should not be called with integer constant parameters. For example, 2 is an integer constant; JJ is an integer variable. The XL FORTRAN compiler, invoked by the <B>xlf</B> command, stores all integer constants as long integers (INTEGER*4), not as short integers (INTEGER*2). Invoking one of the short versions of this subroutine with an integer constant will result in unexpected behavior.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A213X912e4e"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0A7F598ceb"></A>The <B>draw</B> subroutine connects the point specifies by the <A HREF="draw.html#A213X912e55"><I>x</I></A>, <A HREF="draw.html#A213X912e56"><I>y</I></A>, <A HREF="draw.html#A213X912e57"><I>z</I></A> parameters and the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A25P03eb">current graphics position</A> with a line segment. It uses the current line attributes: 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A172P1436">linestyle</A>, 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A172P1437">linewidth</A>, 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A31996bc">color</A> (if in 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A150P19d9">depth-cue mode</A>, the depth-cued color is used), and 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A3C0F2A4599mhay">writemask</A>. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0A7F704ceb"></A>The <B>draw</B> subroutine updates the current graphics position to the specified point.  </P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A213X912e51"></A><B>Note: </B>Do not place routines that invalidate the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A25P03eb">current graphics position</A> within sequences of moves and draws.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<P><A NAME="E1B0A7F870ceb"></A>The six different forms for the <B>draw</B> subroutine are as follows:</P>

<TABLE BORDER="2"><TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><BR></TD>

<TD><B>2-D</B></TD>

<TD><B>3-D</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>Int16</TD>

<TD>draw2s</TD>

<TD>draws</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>Int32</TD>

<TD>draw2i</TD>

<TD>drawi</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>float</TD>

<TD>draw2</TD>

<TD>draw</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P><A NAME="E1B0A80033ceb"></A>The syntax for each of the subroutine forms is the same except for the parameter type.  They differ only in that <A HREF="draw.html#A213X912e4b"><B>draw</B></A> expects real coordinates, <A HREF="draw.html#jxJ170marj"><B>drawi</B></A> expects integer coordinates, and <A HREF="draw.html#QyJ230marj"><B>draws</B></A> expects short integer coordinates. In addition, the <A HREF="draw.html#pzJ150marj"><B>draw2</B></A> routines assume a 2-D point instead of a 3-D point.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912e54"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912e55"></A><I>x</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>x</I> coordinate of the point to which to draw a line segment.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912e56"></A><I>y</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>y</I> coordinate of the point to which to draw a line segment.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912e57"></A><I>z</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>z</I> coordinate of the point to which to draw a line segment (not used by 2-D subroutines).  </TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A30C010ffa"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0A80409ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="depthcue_c.html#A16C0c8ff"><B>depthcue.c</B></A> uses the <B>drawi</B> subroutine to draw the edges of a cube. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015d14"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0A80570ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C12e8"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C12e9"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C12ea"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A258C01c5a4"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0A80890ceb"></A>Moving the current graphics position to a specified point with the <A HREF="move.html#pofmarj"><B>move</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0A80999ceb"></A>Drawing a point with the <A HREF="pnt.html#Ptf3a0marj"><B>pnt</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0A81106ceb"></A>Drawing a relative line with the <A HREF="rdr.html#gpf1c0marj"><B>rdr</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0A81215ceb"></A>Moving the current graphics position to a point relative to the current point with the <A HREF="rmv.html#kzf90marj"><B>rmv</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0A81323ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A>, Drawing with <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/move-draw.html">Move-Draw Style</A> Subroutines, <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/depth-cueing.html">Performing Depth-Cueing</A> in GL, <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/setglattrib.html#setglattrib.html">Setting Drawing Attributes</A>, and Working in <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/workcolor.html#workcolor.html">Color Map and RGB Modes</A>.</P><hr><center>
```

```html
<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">
<HTML>
<HEAD>
<META HTTP-EQUIV="Content-Type" CONTENT="text/html; charset=iso-8859-1">

<TITLE>drawmode Subroutine
</TITLE>
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="draw.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="editobj.html">Next</a>  |
<A href="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A143X9460"></A>drawmode Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX454" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX455" REL="I2" TITLE="frame buffer configuration"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX456" REL="I3" TITLE="drawmode"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX457" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX458" REL="I2" TITLE="bitplanes"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX459" REL="I3" TITLE="choosing a set for drawing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX460" REL="I1" TITLE="drawmode subroutine (GL)"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A143X9462"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0AA6938ceb"></A>Specifies the target frame buffer for the drawing subroutines.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C11b7"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0AA7086ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0AA7191ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9466"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A143X9467"></A><B>void drawmode(Int32 </B><A HREF="drawmode.html#A143X946b"><I>mode</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A28C010704"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A28C010705"></A><B>SUBROUTINE DRAWMO(</B><I>mode</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>mode</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9468"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0AA7555ceb"></A>The <B>drawmode</B> subroutine reconfigures the system and redirects the target of a number of GL drawing and attribute subroutines. The affected routines depend on the mode that the user chooses. Calls to the <A HREF="color.html#A146X9429"><B>color</B></A>, <A HREF="getcolor.html#A146X924b"><B>getcolor</B></A>, <A HREF="writemask.html#A143X9592"><B>writemask</B></A>, <A HREF="getwritemask.html#A143X94c6"><B>getwritemask</B></A>, <A HREF="mapcolor.html#A146X9535"><B>mapcolor</B></A>, and <A HREF="getmcolor.html#nXI1100marj"><B>getmcolor</B></A> subroutines affect only the current drawing mode. In cursor mode, only the <B>getmcolor </B>and <B>mapcolor</B> subroutines perform a function. </P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9c90"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a
 <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A143X946a"></A>Parameter</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X946b"></A><I>mode</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the drawing mode identifier. The mode constants for both C and FORTRAN and their functions are displayed in the following table:


<TABLE BORDER="2"><TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD COLSPAN="2"><B>Mode Constants</B></TD>

<TD><BR></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>C</B></TD>

<TD><B>FORTRAN</B></TD>

<TD><B>Description</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>UNDERDRAW</TD>

<TD>UNDRDR</TD>

<TD>Redirects drawing into the background (underlay) bitplanes.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>NORMALDRAW</TD>

<TD>NORMDR</TD>

<TD>Redirects all drawing into the mainframe buffer bitplanes.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>OVERDRAW</TD>

<TD>OVRDRW</TD>

<TD>Redirects drawing into the foreground (overlay) bitplanes.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>PUPDRAW</TD>

<TD>PUPDRW</TD>

<TD>Redirects <B>mapcolor</B> and <B>getmcolor</B> subroutines to affect only the pop-up menus.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>CURSORDRAW</TD>

<TD>CURSDR</TD>

<TD>Redirects <B>mapcolor</B> and <B>getmcolor</B> subroutines to affect only the cursor.</TD></TR></TABLE></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P><A NAME="E1B0AA7917ceb"></A>The following provides additional descriptions for the preceding modes:</P>

<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TH NOWRAP="NOWRAP">Mode</TH>
<TH>  Description</TH></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A10C0abd9"></A>UNDERDRAW</TD>
<TD>  The line drawing and polygon drawing routines (both <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawbeg-end.html">begin-end style</A> and <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/move-draw.html">move-draw style</A>) draw into the underlay planes rather than the main 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A270A984a">frame buffer</A>. The pixmap transfer subroutines (the <A HREF="rectread.html#A142X9c7c"><B>rectread</B></A>, <A HREF="rectwrite.html#A142X9c9e"><B>rectwrite</B></A>, and <A HREF="rectcopy.html#A142X9d04"><B>rectcopy</B></A> subroutines) also draw into the underlays. All of the current attributes are used during drawing, except the color and the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A3C0F2A4599mhay">writemask</A>. Each drawing mode has a separate current color and current writemask, which are saved and restored when that drawing mode is exited and entered.


<P>Drawing into the underlay planes can only be done in colorindex mode. The system automatically goes into colorindex mode when the UNDERDRAW mode is entered. Lighting and NURBS subroutines do not work correctly in UNDERDRAW mode. Because of the small number of bitplanes, only flat shading is possible; Gouraud shading does not work. The 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A154P1160a">z-buffer</A> is not updated when in UNDERDRAW mode.</P>




<P>The system must have been configured to contain underlay planes before the UNDERDRAW mode can be entered. Underlay planes may be configured by calling the <A HREF="underlay.html#Az5O370nita"><B>underlay</B></A> subroutine followed by the <A HREF="gconfig.html#hS4260nita"><B>gconfig</B></A> subroutine.</P></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A10C0abdc"></A>NORMALDRAW</TD>
<TD>  All drawing occurs in the main <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A270A984a">frame buffer</A>. NORMALDRAW is the default drawing mode.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A10C0abdd"></A>OVERDRAW</TD>
<TD>  The line drawing and polygon drawing routines (both begin-end style and move-draw style) draw into the overlay planes rather than the main frame buffer. The pixmap transfer subroutines (the <A HREF="rectread.html#A142X9c7c"><B>rectread</B></A>, <A HREF="rectwrite.html#A142X9c9e"><B>rectwrite</B></A>, and <A HREF="rectcopy.html#A142X9d04"><B>rectcopy</B></A> subroutines) also draw into the overlays. All of the current attributes are used during drawing, except the color and the writemask. Each draw mode has a separate current color and current 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A3C0F2A4599mhay">writemask</A>, which are saved and restored when that draw mode is exited and entered.


<P>Drawing into the overlay planes can only be done in colorindex mode. The system automatically goes into colorindex mode when the OVERDRAW mode is entered. Lighting and NURBS subroutines do not work correctly in OVERDRAW mode. Because of the small number of bitplanes, only flat shading is possible; Gouraud shading does not work. The 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A154P1160a">z-buffer</A> is not updated when in OVERDRAW mode.</P>




<P>The system must have been configured to contain overlay planes before the OVERDRAW mode can be entered. Overlay planes may be configured by calling the <A HREF="overlay.html#A143X950a"><B>overlay</B></A> subroutine followed by the <A HREF="gconfig.html#hS4260nita"><B>gconfig</B></A> subroutine.</P>




<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A6F1DB4132csol"></A><B>Note: </B>To z-buffer drawing into the overlay planes, enable z-buffering. If you do not want to z-buffer this type of drawing, disable z-buffering by calling the <B>zbuffer</B> subroutine with a value of False while drawing into the overlay planes. Unclear visual images may be the unintentional result when a drawing in the overlay becomes z-buffered.</BLOCKQUOTE>

</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A10C0abe0"></A>PUPDRAW</TD>
<TD>  Only the <A HREF="mapcolor.html#A146X9535"><B>mapcolor</B></A> subroutine and <A HREF="getmcolor.html#nXI1100marj"><B>getmcolor</B></A> subroutine are affected. Drawing subroutines cannot be used to draw into the pop-up menus. In particular, lines, polygons, and pixmaps cannot be drawn into the pop-up menus. Only the pop-up subroutines may be used to access the pop-up menus.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A10C0abe1"></A>CURSORDRAW</TD>
<TD>  Only the <A HREF="mapcolor.html#A146X9535"><B>mapcolor</B></A> and <A HREF="getmcolor.html#nXI1100marj"><B>getmcolor</B></A> subroutine are affected. Drawing subroutines cannot be used to draw into the cursor. Only the cursor subroutines access the cursor.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A30C010fc8"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0AA9030ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="prompt_c.html#A16C0c8de"><B>prompt.c</B></A> uses the <B>drawmode</B> subroutine with the PUPDRAW mode identifier to set the drawing mode for operations on the pop-up menus.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A64C01654e"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0AA9192ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3CFC5F7980janb"></A>Only the Color Graphics Processor has underlay planes. Neither the POWERgraphics Gt4 family of graphics adapters, nor the POWERgraphics GXT1000 posses underlay planes. The call drawmode(UNDERDRAW) is ignored on the GXT1000 and Gt4 family adapters.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3CFC5F7991janb"></A>The call drawmode(OVERDRAW) is ignored for windows that have been created with the <B>winX</B> subroutine, unless the <B>glcompat</B> GLC_CREATE_OVERLAY flag has been set.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3CFC5F8002janb"></A>When performing BLITs to and from the overlay planes on the GXT1000, note that the transparent pixel value on the GXT1000 is 255, not 0. That is, transparent pixels in a pixmap should have the value of 255. Ordinary drawing into the overlay planes still uses color 0 as the transparent color.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C11ba"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C11bb"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C11bc"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9480"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0AA9512ceb"></A>Enabling drawing into the back buffer with the <A HREF="backbuffer.html#A145X94a"><B>backbuffer</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0AA9620ceb"></A>Setting color map mode as the current mode with the <A HREF="cmode.html#A146X93d6"><B>cmode</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0AA9729ceb"></A>Setting the color index in the current mode with the <A HREF="color.html#A146X9429"><B>color</B></A> subroutine. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0AA9837ceb"></A>Setting the display mode to double buffer mode with the <A HREF="doublebuffer.html#A145X91a7"><B>doublebuffer</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0AA9943ceb"></A>Enabling or disabling drawing into the front buffer with the <A HREF="frontbuffer.html#A145X9a0"><B>frontbuffe</B></A>r subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0AAA050ceb"></A>Changing a color map entry to an RGB value with the <A HREF="mapcolor.html#A146X9535"><B>mapcolor</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0AAA158ceb"></A>Setting the number of bitplanes used for overlay colors with the <A HREF="overlay.html#A143X950a"><B>overlay</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0AAA265ceb"></A>Setting the current color in RGB mode with the <A HREF="RGBcolor.html#A143X9394"><B>RGBcolor</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0AAA377ceb"></A>Setting a display mode that bypasses the color map with the <A HREF="RGBmode.html#A143X93b6"><B>RGBmode</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0AAA484ceb"></A>Granting write access to a subset of available bitplanes with the <A HREF="RGBwritemask.html#A143X93fa"><B>RGBwritemask</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0AAA591ceb"></A>Setting the display mode to single buffer mode with the <A HREF="singlebuffer.html#A145X9259"><B>singlebuffer</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0AAA698ceb"></A>Setting the number of bitplanes used for underlay colors with the <A HREF="underlay.html#Az5O370nita"><B>underlay</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0AAA807ceb"></A>Granting write permission to a subset of available bitplanes with the <A HREF="writemask.html#A143X9592"><B>writemask</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0AAA922ceb"></A>Turning z-buffer mode on and off with the <A HREF="zbuffer.html#A143X97b1"><B>zbuffer</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0AAB039ceb"></A>Enabling drawing to the z-buffer with the <A HREF="zdraw.html#A143X97f5"><B>zdraw</B></A> subroutine.</P>
```

```html
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A142X9360"></A>editobj Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX461" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX462" REL="I2" TITLE="object (display list)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX463" REL="I3" TITLE="editobj"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX464" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX465" REL="I2" TITLE="object (display list)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX466" REL="I3" TITLE="opening for editing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX467" REL="I1" TITLE="editobj subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A142X9362"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0AC8224ceb"></A>Opens a display list for editing.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C12b"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0AC8377ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0AC8480ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A142X9366"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X911f5b"></A><B>void editobj(Int32 </B><A HREF="editobj.html#A142X936b"><I>object</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010a7c"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010a7d"></A><B>SUBROUTINE EDITOB(</B><I>object</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>object</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A142X9368"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0AC8846ceb"></A>The <B>editobj </B>subroutine opens a display list for editing. The system initializes an editing pointer to the end of the newly opened object. It appends all new routines at that pointer location until there is a call to the <A HREF="closeobj.html#A142X915b"><B>closeobj</B></A> subroutine or to one that repositions the editing pointer, such as the <A HREF="objdelete.html#A142X9afd"><B>objdelete</B></A>, <A HREF="objinsert.html#A142X9adb"><B>objinsert</B></A>, or <A HREF="objreplace.html#A142X9b50"><B>objreplace</B></A> subroutines.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0AC8953ceb"></A>Usually it is not necessary to be concerned about memory allocation. Objects grow and shrink automatically as routines are added and deleted. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0AC9061ceb"></A>A call for an undefined object identifier causes the system to display an error message.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9d87"></A><B>Note: </B>This editing subroutine itself cannot be added to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A142X936a"></A>Parameter</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A142X936b"></A><I>object</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies identifier for object definition to edit.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015cfa"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0AC9385ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C12e"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C12f"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C130"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A142X9380"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0AC9705ceb"></A>Specifying the amount of memory allocated for an object with the <A HREF="chunksize.html#A142X9c38"><B>chunksize</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0AC9812ceb"></A>Closing an object with the <A HREF="closeobj.html#A142X915b"><B>closeobj</B></A>  subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0AC9919ceb"></A>Compacting the  memory storage of an object with the <A HREF="compactify.html#A142X9c5a"><B>compactify</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0ACA029ceb"></A>Creating an object with the <A HREF="makeobj.html#A142X912d"><B>makeobj</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0ACA136ceb"></A>Inserting a routine into an object with the <A HREF="objinsert.html#A142X9adb"><B>objinsert</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0ACA244ceb"></A>Deleting a routine from an object with the <A HREF="objdelete.html#A142X9afd"><B>objdelete</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0ACA351ceb"></A>Replacing an existing display list routine with a new one with the <A HREF="objreplace.html#A142X9b50"><B>objreplace</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0ACA459ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A> and Creating <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/workobjects.html#workobjects.html">Objects (Display Lists)</A>.</P><hr><center>
```

```html
<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">

<HEAD>

<TITLE>endfullscrn Subroutine
</TITLE>
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="editobj.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="endpick.html">Next</a>  |
<A href="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="laa350marj"></A>endfullscrn Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX468" REL="I1" TITLE="endfullscrn subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX469" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX470" REL="I2" TITLE="window"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX471" REL="I3" TITLE="endfullscrn"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX472" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX473" REL="I2" TITLE="fullcreen mode"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX474" REL="I3" TITLE="ending"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A318C9ebd"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0AE7201ceb"></A>Ends full-screen mode.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C12bb"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0AE7350ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0AE7454ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A318C9ec0"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A318C9ec1"></A><B>void endfullscrn(&nbsp;)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010c4f"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010c50"></A><B>SUBROUTINE ENDFUL</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A318C9ec4"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0AE7821ceb"></A>The <B>endfullscrn</B> subroutine ends full-screen mode and returns the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A27P018">screenmask</A> and 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A27P039">viewport</A> to the boundaries of the current window. This subroutine leaves the current transformation unchanged.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9ec6"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>
```

```html
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A213X91185b"></A>endpick Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX475" REL="I1" TITLE="endpick subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX476" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX477" REL="I2" TITLE="picking and selecting"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX478" REL="I3" TITLE="turning off picking mode"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX479" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX480" REL="I2" TITLE="picking and selecting"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX481" REL="I3" TITLE="endpick"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX482" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX483" REL="I2" TITLE="selecting"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A213X91185d"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0B07490ceb"></A>Turns off picking mode.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C184"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0B07639ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0B07742ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911860"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X911861"></A><B>Int32 endpick(Int16 </B><A HREF="endpick.html#A213X91186b"><I>buffer</I></A><B>[&nbsp;])</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911839"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X91183c"></A><B>INTEGER*4 FUNCTION ENDPIC(</B><I>buffer</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*2 </B><I>buffer</I><B>(1)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911864"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0B08108ceb"></A>The <B>endpick</B> subroutine turns off 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P06fa">picking mode</A> and returns the number of 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P061e">hits</A>.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0B08215ceb"></A>When the system is in picking mode, and a subroutine draws in the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P06fb">picking region</A>, the contents of the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P06e3">name stack</A> are stored in a buffer, along with the number of names in the stack. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0B08324ceb"></A>If a drawing primitive overlaps or intrudes upon the picking volume, a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P061e">hit</A> has occurred. The hit is recorded only if the name stack has been touched since the last hit. Any of the subroutines <A HREF="loadname.html#A213X9119af"><B>loadname</B></A>, <A HREF="pushname.html#A213X911b48"><B>pushname</B></A>, or <A HREF="popname.html#A213X911af9"><B>popname</B></A> touch the name stack. The first hit after picking begins is always recorded.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0B08433ceb"></A>A hit is recorded by placing the depth of the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P06e3">name stack</A> into the next vacant slot in the buffer, followed by the entire contents of the name stack. The bottom of the name stack is transferred to the buffer first, followed by the second from the bottom entry of the name stack, and so forth. In other words, from bottom to top is mapped to from left to right.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9cf5"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A213X91186a"></A>Parameter</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X91186b"></A><I>buffer</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies a buffer in which to write the number of 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P061e">hits</A>.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X91186c"></A>Return Value</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0B08753ceb"></A>The number of times the name stack was written to the buffer. If the returned function value is negative, then the buffer was too small to contain all the readings from the name stack. The absolute value is the number of stacks actually recorded.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A30C010fe0"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0B08908ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="pick1_c.html#A13C0bd9f"><B>pick1.c</B></A> calls the <B>endpick</B> subroutine to turn off picking mode. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015cb4"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0B09069ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C187"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C188"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C189"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X91187e"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0B09389ceb"></A>Turning off selecting mode with the <A HREF="endselect.html#A213X91190c"><B>endselect</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0B09496ceb"></A>Putting the system in selecting mode with the <A HREF="gselect.html#A213X9118b2"><B>gselect</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0B09601ceb"></A>Initializing the name stack with the <A HREF="initnames.html#YlD250marj"><B>initnames</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0B09708ceb"></A>Loading the name on top of the name stack with the <A HREF="loadname.html#A213X9119af"><B>loadname</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0B09816ceb"></A>Putting the system in picking mode with the <A HREF="pick.html#h632f0nita"><B>pick</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0B09923ceb"></A>Popping a name off the name stack with the <A HREF="popname.html#A213X911af9"><B>popname</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0B0A029ceb"></A>Pushing a new name onto the name stack with the <A HREF="pushname.html#A213X911b48"><B>pushname</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0B0A149ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A>, Working with <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/workcoords.html#workcoords.html">Coordinate Systems</A>, and <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/picknselect.html#picknselect.html">Picking and Selecting</A> Overview.</P><hr><center>
```

```html
<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">
<HTML>
<HEAD>
<META HTTP-EQUIV="Content-Type" CONTENT="text/html; charset=iso-8859-1">

<TITLE>finish Subroutine
</TITLE>
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="endselect.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="font.html">Next</a>  |
<A href="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A9URSg3c3csol"></A>finish Subroutine</H2>


<H3><A NAME="A71BC6B971csol"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0B50130ceb"></A>Blocks until all buffers and first-in-first-out (FIFOs) queues are empty.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A71BC6C319csol"></A>Library</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0B50279ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0B50383ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A71BC6C800csol"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A71BC6C945csol"></A><B>void finish</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A71BC6D094csol"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A71BC6D242csol"></A><B>SUBROUTINE FINISH</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A71BC6D390csol"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0B50735ceb"></A>The <B>finish</B> subroutine blocks until all buffers and FIFOs that buffer up GL drawing commands are empty. The <B>finish</B> subroutine does not return to the user application until all drawings sent to a window are displayed on the screen.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0B50846ceb"></A>The amount of time that elapses before the <B>finish</B> subroutine returns can be highly variable. This timeframe depends on the depth of the FIFO, the nature of its contents (for example, lines or polygons), and the performance of the graphics adapter. Excessive use of the <B>finish</B> subroutine may adversely impact overall system performance.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A71BC6E200csol"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0B51006ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0B51116ceb"></A>GL implementations are not consistent in the use of buffers and/or FIFOs. The following list illustratrates the variety of ways FIFOs or buffers can be used in a GL implementation:</P>

<UL><LI><A NAME="A71BC6E763csol"></A>A separate FIFO for every window</LI>

<LI><A NAME="A71BC6E950csol"></A>One FIFO per process</LI>

<LI><A NAME="A71BC6F143csol"></A>A single FIFO for the entire system.</LI></UL>


<P><A NAME="E1B0B51387ceb"></A>Certain events, such as switching drawing from one window to another or using some <B>get</B> functions, can cause buffers and FIFOs to be drained.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0B51497ceb"></A>The POWER Gt4 and POWER Gt4x adapters implement one logical FIFO per window. The <B>finish</B> subroutine forces the draining of only the FIFO associated with the current window. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0B51604ceb"></A>The following adapters and processors have one graphics command FIFO for the entire system:</P>

<UL><LI><A NAME="A71BC70044csol"></A>3-D Color Graphics Processor</LI>

<LI><A NAME="A71BC70255csol"></A>POWERstation 730</LI>

<LI><A NAME="A71BC70429csol"></A>POWERgraphics GTO.</LI></UL>


<P><A NAME="E1B0B51875ceb"></A>This FIFO is automatically drained whenever a switch to a different window is initiated. That is, drawing in one window, and then drawing in another, implicitly drains the FIFO.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A71BC70885csol"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A71BC71118csol"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A71BC71305csol"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A71BC71547csol"></A><B>/usr/include/X11/Xlib.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for version X11 of Enhanced X-Windows.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A71BC72302csol"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0B52267ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/exhwindcalls.html#exhwindcalls.html">Using Enhanced X-Windows Calls with GL Subroutines</A> in<I> GL3.2 Version 4 for AIX: Programming Concepts</I>.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0B52385ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/enhxinterop.html#enhxinterop.html">Enhanced X-Windows and GL Interoperability</A> in<I> GL3.2 Version 4 for AIX: Programming Concepts</I></P><hr><center>
[  <a href="endselect.html">Previous</a>  |
```

```html
</TITLE>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">

<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A143X9d61"></A>font Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX491" REL="I1" TITLE="font subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX492" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX493" REL="I2" TITLE="text"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX494" REL="I3" TITLE="font"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX495" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX496" REL="I2" TITLE="text"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX497" REL="I3" TITLE="selecting a raster font"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A143X9d63"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0B75980ceb"></A>Selects a raster font for drawing text strings.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1224"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0B76128ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0B76232ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9d67"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X912629"></A><B>void font(Int32 </B><A HREF="font.html#A213X91262d"><I>fontnum</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010c13"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010c14"></A><B>SUBROUTINE FONT(</B><I>fontnum</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>fontnum</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9d69"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0B76595ceb"></A>The <B>font </B>subroutine selects the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P073b">raster font</A> that the <A HREF="charstr.html#A143X9cfb"><B>charstr</B></A> subroutine uses when it draws a text string. This font remains in effect until you call the <B>font</B> subroutine again. Font <SAMP>0</SAMP> (zero) is the default. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9d6b"></A>Parameter</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X91262d"></A><I>fontnum</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies a font identifier, an index into the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A270A983b">font</A> table built by the <A HREF="defrasterfont.html#A143X9d3f"><B>defrasterfont</B></A> subroutine. If you specify a font number that is not defined, the system selects font <SAMP>0</SAMP> (zero). </TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A30C011058"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0B76859ceb"></A>The example C language programs <A HREF="curved_c.html#A16C0c830"><B>curved.c</B></A> and <A HREF="font3_c.html#A149C18a9"><B>font3.c</B></A> use the <B>font</B> subroutine to select a raster font defined with the <A HREF="defrasterfont.html#A143X9d3f"><B>defrasterfont</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015d95"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0B77018ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1227"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1228"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1229"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9d81"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0B77337ceb"></A>Drawing a string of raster characters on the screen with the <A HREF="charstr.html#A143X9cfb"><B>charstr</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0B77444ceb"></A>Defining bitmaps for a raster font with the <A HREF="defrasterfont.html#A143X9d3f"><B>defrasterfont</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0B77552ceb"></A>Returning the baseline extent of the longest character descender with the <A HREF="getdescender.html#A144X9386"><B>getdescender</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0B77658ceb"></A>Returning the current raster font number with the <A HREF="getfont.html#A144X93a8"><B>getfont</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0B77766ceb"></A>Returning the maximum character height in the current raster font with the <A HREF="getheight.html#A144X93ca"><B>getheight</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0B77873ceb"></A>Returning the width of the specified text string with the <A HREF="strwidth.html#A144X93ec"><B>strwidth</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0B77981ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A> and Creating <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/textchars.html#textchars.html">Text Characters</A>.</P><hr><center>
```

```html
<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>

 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A149C18a9"></A>font3.c Example C Language Program
</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX2298" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2299" REL="I2" TITLE="example programs"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2300" REL="I3" TITLE="text"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2301" REL="I1" TITLE="font3.c example program (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2302" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2303" REL="I2" TITLE="text"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2304" REL="I3" TITLE="example program"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2305" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2306" REL="I2" TITLE="fonts"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2307" REL="I3" TITLE="example program"></A>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA94666ttay"></A>/* Examples: font3.c*/</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA94885ttay"></A>/* Define a font with three characters -- a lower-case j,
 * an arrow, and a Greek sigma. Use ASCII values 1 and 2
 * (\001 and \002) for the arrow and sigma. Use the
 * ASCII value of j (= \152) for the j character.
 */</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA95033ttay"></A>#include &lt;gl/gl.h></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA95204ttay"></A>#define EXAMPLEFONT        1
#define efont_ht        16
#define efont_nc        127</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA95488ttay"></A>unsigned short efont_bits[] = {
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;/* lower-case j */
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;0x7000, 0xd800, 0x8c00, 0x0c00, 0x0c00, 0x0c00, 0x0c00,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;0x0c00, 0x0c00, 0x1c00, 0x0000, 0x0000, 0x0c00, 0x0c00,
  /* arrow */
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;0x0200, 0x0300, 0x0380, 0xafc0, 0xafe0, 0xaff0, 0xafe0,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;0xafc0, 0x0380, 0x0300, 0x0200,
  /* sigma */
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;0xffc0, 0xc0c0, 0x6000, 0x3000, 0x1800, 0x0c00, 0x0600,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;0x0c00, 0x1800, 0x3000, 0x6000, 0xc180, 0xff80,
  };</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA95736ttay"></A>#define efont_nr (sizeof efont_bits)
#define ASSIGN(fontch, of, wi, he, xof, yof, wid) \
                fontch.offset = of; \
                fontch.w = wi; \
                fontch.h = he; \
                fontch.xoff = xof; \
                fontch.yoff = yof; \
                fontch.width = wid</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA95886ttay"></A>Fontchar efont_chars[127];</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA96035ttay"></A>main ()
{        </PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA96344ttay"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;ASSIGN(efont_chars['j'],        0, 6, 14, 0, -2,  8);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;ASSIGN(efont_chars['\001'],14, 12, 11, 0,  0, 14);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;ASSIGN(efont_chars['\002'],25, 10, 13, 0,  0, 12);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;prefsize (200,200);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;winopen("font");
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(BLACK);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;clear();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;defrasterfont (EXAMPLEFONT, efont_ht, efont_nc, efont_chars,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;    efont_nr, efont_bits);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;font (EXAMPLEFONT);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(RED);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;cmov2i(100, 100);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;charstr ("j\001\002\001jj\002");
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;cmov2i(100, 84);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;charstr("ajb\001c\002d");
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;sleep(10);</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EA96487ttay"></A>}</PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A200C1174"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7829614ceb"></A>The <A HREF="charstr.html#A143X9cfb"><B>charstr</B></A> subroutine<A HREF="A143X9cfb" REL="PAGENUM"></A>, <A HREF="defrasterfont.html#A143X9d3f"><B>defrasterfont</B></A> subroutine<A HREF="A143X9d3f" REL="PAGENUM"></A>, <A HREF="font.html#A143X9d61"><B>font</B></A> subroutine<A HREF="A143X9d61" REL="PAGENUM"></A>.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7829640ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/textchars.html#Qi62180nita">Fonts</A> in<I> GL3.2 Version 4 for AIX: Programming Concepts</I> describes font assignment in GL, and discusses relevant subroutines.</P>
```

```html
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A142X91103"></A>freepup Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX498" REL="I1" TITLE="freepup subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX499" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX500" REL="I2" TITLE="popp menus"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX501" REL="I3" TITLE="deallocating"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX502" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX503" REL="I2" TITLE="popp menu"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX504" REL="I3" TITLE="freepup"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A142X91105"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0B94454ceb"></A>Deallocates a menu.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1126"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0B94603ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0B94707ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A142X91109"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X91219c"></A><B>void freepup(Int32 </B><A HREF="freepup.html#A213X9121a1"><I>popup</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A27C010425"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A27C010426"></A><B>SUBROUTINE FREEPU(</B><I>popup</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4</B> <I>popup</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A142X9110b"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0B95070ceb"></A>The <B>freepup </B>subroutine deallocates a pop-up menu, freeing the memory reserved for its data structures. </P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9de3"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A142X9110d"></A>Parameter</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X9121a1"></A><I>popup</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the pop-up menu to deallocate.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A64C0165c2"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0B95401ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1129"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C112a"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C112b"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A142X91123"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0B95728ceb"></A>Adding an item to an existing pop-up menu with the <A HREF="addtopup.html#A142X9109d"><B>addtopup</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0B95846ceb"></A>Defining a pop-up menu with the <A HREF="defpup.html#A142X910bf"><B>defpup</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0B95962ceb"></A>Displaying a pop-up menu with the <A HREF="dopup.html#A142X910e1"><B>dopup</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0B96071ceb"></A>Allocating and initializing a structure for a new pop-up menu with the <A HREF="newpup.html#A142X91125"><B>newpup</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0B96188ceb"></A>Enabling or disabling a given pop-up entry with the <A HREF="setpup.html#A5um1280marj"><B>setpup</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0B96296ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A> and Creating and Managing <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/popupmenus.html#popupmenus.html">Pop-Up Menus</A>.</P><hr><center>
```

```html
<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">

<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A145X9a0"></A>frontbuffer Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX505" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX506" REL="I2" TITLE="animation"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX507" REL="I3" TITLE="frontbuffer"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX508" REL="I1" TITLE="frontbuffer subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX509" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX510" REL="I2" TITLE="drawing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX511" REL="I3" TITLE="into front buffer"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX512" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX513" REL="I2" TITLE="front buffer"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX514" REL="I3" TITLE="drawing into"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX515" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX516" REL="I2" TITLE="frame buffer configuration"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX517" REL="I3" TITLE="frontbuffer"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A145X9a4"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0BB3367ceb"></A>Enables or disables drawing into the front buffer.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A77C11a"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0BB3516ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0BB3620ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A145X9a7"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A145X9a8"></A><B>void frontbuffer(Int32 </B><A HREF="frontbuffer.html#A145X996"><I>bool</I></A><B>&nbsp;)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A145X97e"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A145X981"></A><B>SUBROUTINE FRONTB(</B><I>bool</I><B>)</B>
<B>LOGICAL </B><I>bool</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A145X9ab"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0BB3986ceb"></A>The <B>frontbuffer</B> subroutine enables drawing into the 
 <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P051c">front frame buffer</A>. In common usage, drawing is done to the back buffer, after which a call to the <A HREF="swapbuffers.html#A145X9302"><B>swapbuffers</B></A> subroutine is made to exchange buffers. The <B>frontbuffer</B> subroutine can be used to override this default.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0BB4094ceb"></A>This routine is useful only in 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0474">double buffer mode</A> and is ignored in 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A27P01c">single buffer mode</A>.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A145X99b"></A>Parameter</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A145X996"></A><I>bool</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the value for the state of the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P051c">front frame buffer</A>. The settings for the <I>bool</I> parameter are:</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A145X9ae"></A></TD>
<TD>  True = drawing into the front buffer is enabled.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A145X9af"></A></TD>
<TD>  False = drawing into the front buffer is disabled.


<P>The <A HREF="gconfig.html#hS4260nita"><B>gconfig</B></A> subroutine sets the front buffer to FALSE.</P></TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015c97"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0BB4583ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A11C0b495"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C11d"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C11e"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A258C01c33d"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0BB4903ceb"></A>Enabling drawing into the back buffer with the <A HREF="backbuffer.html#A145X94a"><B>backbuffer</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0BB5010ceb"></A>Setting the display mode to double buffer mode with the <A HREF="doublebuffer.html#A145X91a7"><B>doublebuffer</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0BB5119ceb"></A>Finding out which buffers are enabled for writing with the <A HREF="getbuffer.html#A145X9f6"><B>getbuffer</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0BB5226ceb"></A>Exchanging the front and back buffers with the <A HREF="swapbuffers.html#A145X9302"><B>swapbuffers</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0BB5334ceb"></A>Understanding the <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/glintro.html#A8G44310marj">Hardware Used by GL</A> in<I> GL3.2 Version 4 for AIX: Programming Concepts</I>.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0BB5442ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/configframebuf.html#configframebuf.html">Configuring the Frame Buffer</A>, <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/animatescene.html#animatescene.html">Creating Animated Scenes</A>.</P><hr><center>
```

```html
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A74C12"></A>frontface Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX518" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX519" REL="I2" TITLE="removing surface"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX520" REL="I3" TITLE="frontface"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX521" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX522" REL="I2" TITLE="frontfacing polygons"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX523" REL="I3" TITLE="display"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX524" REL="I1" TITLE="frontface subroutine (GL)"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A74C13"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0BD4999ceb"></A>Controls frontfacing polygon removal.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A74C15"></A>Library</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0BD5148ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0BD5251ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A74C18"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A74C19"></A><B>void frontface (Int32 </B><I>mode</I><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A74C1a"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A74C1b"></A><B>SUBROUTINE FRONTF(</B><I>mode</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>mode</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A74C1c"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0BD5616ceb"></A>The <B>frontface </B>subroutine allows or suppresses the display of frontfacing filled polygons. With the <A HREF="backface.html#A143X974b"><B>backface</B></A> subroutine, it is useful for drawing polygons that have different colors on each side. The <B>frontface</B> subroutine can also be useful for performing a primitive kind of 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P061d">hidden surface</A> removal.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0BD5725ceb"></A>A frontfacing polygon is defined as a polygon whose vertices are in counterclockwise order in screen coordinates. When frontfacing polygon removal is on, the system displays only polygons whose vertices are in clockwise order.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0BD5834ceb"></A>If both frontfacing and backfacing polygon removal is enabled, no filled polygons are displayed. (An exception is made if the graphics pipeline cannot determine if a polygon is front- or backfacing because it is degenerate or otherwise exceptional.)</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><B>Notes: </B>
<OL><LI><A NAME="A108C13"></A>Matrices that negate coordinates, such as <SAMP>scale(-1.0,&nbsp;1.0,&nbsp;1.0)</SAMP>, reverse the directional order of a polygon's points and can cause the <B>frontface</B> subroutine to do the opposite of what is intended.</LI>

<LI><A NAME="A98C1e"></A>If a polygon is extremely small or has degenerate vertices, the graphics pipeline cannot determine if the polygon is frontfacing. In such cases, the polygon is rendered by default.</LI></OL></BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A74C1e"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A74C1f"></A><I>mode</I></TD>
<TD>  Sets action of subroutine:</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A74C110"></A></TD>
<TD>  True = Enables frontfacing polygon removal.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A74C111"></A></TD>
<TD>  False = Disables frontfacing polygon removal.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A74C113"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0BD6371ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0BD6490ceb"></A>The 3-D Color Graphics Processor does not support this subroutine. It has no effect and is ignored.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0BD6599ceb"></A>
On the POWERgraphics GTO adapter
On the POWERgraphics GTO and POWER GXT1000 adapters, either frontfacing polygon removal or backfacing polygon removal can be specified, but not both simultaneously. Enabling frontfacing culling disables backfacing culling.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A74C115"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A74C116"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A74C117"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A74C118"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B0BD6917ceb"></A>Enabling or disabling backfacing polygon removal with the <A HREF="backface.html#A143X974b"><B>backface</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B0BD7023ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A> and Removing <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/remhidden.html#remhidden.html">Hidden Surfaces</A>.</P><hr><center>
```
