<H2><A NAME="A143X945"></A>getvaluator Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX850" REL="I1" TITLE="getvaluator subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX851" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX852" REL="I2" TITLE="query"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX853" REL="I3" TITLE="getvaluator"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX854" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX855" REL="I2" TITLE="device"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX856" REL="I3" TITLE="returning valuator state"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX857" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX858" REL="I2" TITLE="queue and device"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX859" REL="I3" TITLE="getvaluator"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A143X947"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B116F835ceb"></A>Returns the current state of a valuator.</P>

<H3><A NAME="C41DF3F703nqui"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B116F983ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1170087ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912c07"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X912c08"></A><B>Int32 getvaluator(Device </B><A HREF="getvaluator.html#A143X950"><I>device</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010c5f"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010c60"></A><B>INTEGER*4 FUNCTION GETVAL(</B><I>device</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4</B> <I>device</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X94d"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1170456ceb"></A>The <B>getvaluator</B> subroutine returns the current value (an integer) of the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A79P07a">valuator</A> specified in the <A HREF="getvaluator.html#A143X950"><I>device</I></A> parameter. </P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9f78"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A143X94f"></A>Parameter</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X950"></A><I>device</I></TD>
<TD>  Identifier of the valuator (such as MOUSEX or BPADX) to be read.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X953"></A>Return Value</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1170772ceb"></A>The value stored at the device named by the <I>device</I> parameter.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A30C011060"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1170928ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="select1_c.html#A16C0c970"><B>select1.c</B></A> uses the <B>getvaluator</B> subroutine to obtain the mouse coordinates whenever the left mouse button is pressed.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A109C01a710"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1171091ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X961"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="C41DF40769nqui"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="C41DF40845nqui"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="C41DF40921nqui"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/device.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="C41DF40997nqui"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fdevice.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X965"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1171527ceb"></A>Reading a list of valuators with the <A HREF="getdev.html#A143X923"><B>getdev</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1171634ceb"></A>Assigning initial, minimum, and maximum values to a valuator with the <A HREF="setvaluator.html#A143X921e"><B>setvaluator</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A142X9107"></A>getviewport Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX860" REL="I1" TITLE="getviewport subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX861" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX862" REL="I2" TITLE="viewport"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX863" REL="I3" TITLE="getviewport"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX864" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX865" REL="I2" TITLE="query"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX866" REL="I3" TITLE="getviewport"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX867" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX868" REL="I2" TITLE="viewport"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX869" REL="I3" TITLE="returning dimensions"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A142X9109"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1191848ceb"></A>Returns the dimensions of the current viewport.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C125e"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1191997ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1192101ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A142X910d"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1192257ceb"></A><B>void getviewport(Screencoord *</B><A HREF="getviewport.html#A142X9112"><I>left</I></A><B>, Screencoord *</B><A HREF="getviewport.html#A142X9113"><I>right</I></A><B>, </B></P>

<P><B>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Screencoord *</B><A HREF="getviewport.html#A142X9114"><I>bottom</I></A><B>, Screencoord *</B><A HREF="getviewport.html#A142X9fd"><I>top</I></A><B>)</B></P>

<H3><A NAME="A142X9f8"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A142X9f9"></A><B>SUBROUTINE GETVIE(</B><I>left</I><B>,</B> <I>right</I><B>,</B> <I>bottom</I><B>,</B> <I>top</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*2 </B><I>left</I><B>,</B> <I>right</I><B>,</B> <I>bottom</I><B>,</B> <I>top</I> </PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A142X910f"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1192523ceb"></A>The <B>getviewport</B> subroutine returns the dimensions of the current 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A27P039">viewport</A>
 (the top of the viewport stack) and copies these dimensions to the location variables specified as parameters. The <A HREF="getviewport.html#A142X9112"><I>left</I></A>, <A HREF="getviewport.html#A142X9113"><I>right</I></A>, <A HREF="getviewport.html#A142X9114"><I>bottom</I></A>, and <A HREF="getviewport.html#A142X9fd"><I>top</I></A> parameters are the addresses of four memory locations assigned the left, right bottom, and top coordinates of the viewport.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A319C92609"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A142X9111"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A142X9112"></A><I>left</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the memory location in which to return the <I>x</I> coordinate (in pixels) of the left side of the viewport.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A142X9113"></A> <I>right</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the memory location in which to return the <I>x </I>coordinate (in pixels) of the right side of the viewport.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A142X9114"></A> <I>bottom</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the memory location in which to return the <I>y </I>coordinate (in pixels) of the bottom side of the viewport.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A142X9fd"></A> <I>top</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the memory location in which to return the <I>y </I>coordinate (in pixels) of the top side of the viewport.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015d56"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1193017ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1261"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1262"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1263"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A142X9127"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1193339ceb"></A>Popping the viewport stack with the <A HREF="popviewport.html#A213X911d3c"><B>popviewport</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1193447ceb"></A>Pushing the viewport onto the viewport stack with the <A HREF="pushviewport.html#A213X911bee"><B>pushviewport</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1193555ceb"></A>Setting the viewport to the dimensions of the current window with the <A HREF="reshapeviewport.html#A7LQ3b0marj"><B>reshapeviewport</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1193662ceb"></A>Setting the area of the window used for all drawing with the <A HREF="viewport.html#qrY270marj"><B>viewport</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1193769ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A>, <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/querysys.html#querysys.html">Querying</A> the System, 
and Using <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/useviewprts.html#useviewprts.html">Viewports and Screenmasks</A>.</P><hr><center>

<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A143X94c6"></A>getwritemask Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX877" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX878" REL="I2" TITLE="frame buffer update control"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX879" REL="I3" TITLE="getwritemask"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX880" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX881" REL="I2" TITLE="writemask"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX882" REL="I3" TITLE="returning current"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX883" REL="I1" TITLE="getwritemask subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A143X94c8"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B11D9665ceb"></A>Returns the current writemask.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C11e6"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B11D9813ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B11D9917ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X94cc"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A143X94cd"></A><B>Int32 getwritemask(&nbsp;)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A28C010765"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A28C010766"></A><B>INTEGER*4 FUNCTION GETWRI</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X94ce"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B11DA276ceb"></A>The <B>getwritemask</B> subroutine returns the color map mode 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A3C0F2A4599mhay">writemask</A>. Independently settable writemasks exist for the overlay, underlay, and main frame buffers.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B11DA384ceb"></A>The returned value of this function is an integer with up to 12 significant bits, one for each available bitplane. When a bit is set to zero in the writemask, the corresponding bitplane is read only. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B11DA491ceb"></A>This subroutine is intended for user in color map mode only. To get the RGB mode writemask, use the <A HREF="gRGBmask.html#A143X94e8"><B>gRGBmask</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9e06"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a
 <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A143X94d4"></A>Return Value</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B11DA704ceb"></A>The writemask for the current drawing mode.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A64C0165ce"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B11DA864ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C11e9"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C11ea"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C11eb"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X94e6"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B11DB185ceb"></A>Specifying the target frame buffer for the drawing subroutines with the <A HREF="drawmode.html#A143X9460"><B>drawmode</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B11DB293ceb"></A>Returning the current RGB writemask with the <A HREF="gRGBmask.html#A143X94e8"><B>gRGBmask</B></A> subroutine. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B11DB399ceb"></A>Granting write access to a subset of available bitplanes with the <A HREF="RGBwritemask.html#A143X93fa"><B>RGBwritemask</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B11DB507ceb"></A>Granting write permission to a subset of available bitplanes with the <A HREF="writemask.html#A143X9592"><B>writemask</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B11DB614ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/configframebuf.html#configframebuf.html">Configuring the Frame Buffer</A>
 and <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/querysys.html#querysys.html">Querying</A> the System.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B11DB723ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/writemasks.html#writemasks.html">Writemasks and Logical Operations</A>
 and Working in <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/workcolor.html#workcolor.html">Color Map and RGB Modes</A>.</P><hr><center>

<HEAD>

<TITLE>getXdpy or getXwid Subroutine
</TITLE>
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="getviewport.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="getwritemask.html">Next</a>  |
<A href="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A114C13c"></A>getXdpy or getXwid Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX870" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX871" REL="I2" TITLE="Windows"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX872" REL="I3" TITLE="getXdpy"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX873" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX874" REL="I2" TITLE="Windows"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX875" REL="I3" TITLE="getXwid"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX876" REL="I1" TITLE="getXdpy subroutine (GL)"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A114C13d"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B11B6854ceb"></A>Returns the Enhanced X-Windows connection for the given GL session, or the window ID of the current GL window.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A114C13f"></A>Library</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B11B7004ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B11B7110ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A114C142"></A>C Syntax</H3>

<PRE><A NAME="A114C143"></A><B>Display *getXdpy()</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A114C144"></A><B>Window getXwid()</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A114C145"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>

<PRE><A NAME="A114C146"></A><B>INTEGER *4 FUNCTION GETXDPY()</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A114C147"></A><B>INTEGER *4 FUNCTION GETXWID()</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A114C148"></A>Description</H3>

<P><A NAME="E1B11B7576ceb"></A>The <B>getXdpy</B> subroutine returns a pointer to a data structure that 
describes the Enhanced X-Windows connection being used by the GL library to communicate with the X server.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B11B7682ceb"></A>The <B>getXwid</B> subroutine returns the Enhanced X-Windows window ID of the 
current GL <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A13791dc4">window</A>.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B11B7799ceb"></A>The Enhanced X-Windows display connection, with the Enhanced X-Windows window ID, enables applications programs to use Enhanced X-Windows routines to modify a GL window. With this ability, application programs can do several things, including the following:</P>

<UL><LI><A NAME="A161C1294"></A><!--:libs:x11tr:--><A HREF="../x11tr/pdf/XReparWin.pdf.html">Reparent a window</A></LI>

<LI><A NAME="A161C1295"></A>Manipulate properties</LI>

<LI><A NAME="A3CFC99F307janb"></A>Work with resources</LI>

<LI><A NAME="A3CFC99F325janb"></A>Process events</LI>

<LI><A NAME="A3CFC99F344janb"></A>Develop widgets.</LI></UL>


<P><A NAME="E1B11B8168ceb"></A>Not all possible combinations of GL and Enhanced X-Windows calls result in defined behavior, however. In particular, avoid the following usages:</P>

<UL><LI><A NAME="A144C1c9e"></A>Do not use Enhanced X-Windows drawing routines to draw into a GL window. The screen results are undefined. Use Enhanced X-Windows drawing routines to draw into Enhanced X-Windows only.</LI>

<LI><A NAME="A144C1ca0"></A>Use only the GL <A HREF="loadXfont.html#vUO390nita"><B>loadXfont</B></A> subroutine to load X fonts for use with the GL <A HREF="charstr.html#A143X9cfb"><B>charstr</B></A> subroutine. Use the <!--:libs:x11tr:--><A HREF="../x11tr/pdf/XLoadFont.pdf.html"><B>XLoadFont</B></A> or <!--:libs:x11tr:--><A HREF="../x11tr/pdf/XLoadFont.pdf.html"><B>XLoadQueryFont</B></A> subroutine only if you plan to use X text-rendering routines to draw into an Enhanced X-Windows window.</LI>

<LI><A NAME="A144C1ca1"></A>Do not change, modify, or delete GL internal properties associated with GL windows. Doing so causes unpredictable behavior.</LI>

<LI><A NAME="A144C1ca2"></A>Do not grab or ungrab pointers, keyboards, or the server while in GL fullscreen mode. Doing so causes unpredictable behavior.</LI>

<LI><A NAME="A144C1ca3"></A>Events associated with GL windows can be obtained through the Enhanced X-Windows event queue. However, if you choose to obtain events in this manner, do not also use the GL event queue. Doing so causes unpredictable results. An application can use both the GL and Enhanced X-Windows event queues within the same executable if the GL queue is used only for GL events and the Enhanced X-Windows event queue is used only for Enhanced X-Windows events.</LI></UL>


<P><A NAME="E1B11B8641ceb"></A>The previous brief restrictions are explained more fully in <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/exhwindcalls.html#exhwindcalls.html">"Using Enhanced X-Windows Calls with GL Subroutines"</A> in<I> GL3.2 Version 4 for AIX: Programming Concepts</I>.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B11B8749ceb"></A>All GL windows opened by a client normally share one Enhanced X-Windows connection. GL rendering can be performed only locally; that is, a GL application must execute on the same physical machine as that which contains the display adapter. GL does not support a client-server model of network graphics programming.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A114C155"></A>Return Values</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A114C156"></A><B>getXdpy</B></TD>
<TD>  Returns a pointer to the Enhanced X-Windows Display structure.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A114C157"></A><B>getXwid</B></TD>
<TD>  Returns the Enhanced X-Windows window ID.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="BD9BB84952vbia"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B11B9078ceb"></A>Example programs showing the usage of the <B>getXdpy</B> and <B>getXwid</B> subroutines can be found in the <B>/usr/lpp/GL/examples</B> directory.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A114C158"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B11B9240ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature. </P>

<P><A NAME="A3CFC99F380janb"></A>The POWERgraphics GXT1000 supports RGB and color index modes by creating separate separate X11 windows--one window is permanently in RGB mode, and the other is permanently in color index mode. Both of these windows are wrapped in a single parent window. The <B>getXwid</B> subroutine returns the X11 window handle of that parent window.  Standard X11 interfaces can be used to determine the child windows of the parent.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A114C15a"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A114C15b"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A114C15c"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A114C15d"></A><B>/usr/include/X11/Xlib.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for version X11 of Enhanced X-Windows.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A114C161"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B11B9619ceb"></A>The <A HREF="loadXfont.html#vUO390nita"><B>loadXfont</B></A> subroutine, <A HREF="charstr.html#A143X9cfb"><B>charstr</B></A> subroutine, <!--:libs:x11tr:--><A HREF="../x11tr/pdf/XReparWin.pdf.html"><B>XReparentWindow</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B11BA178ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/exhwindcalls.html#exhwindcalls.html">Using Enhanced X-Windows Calls with GL Subroutines</A> in<I> GL3.2 Version 4 for AIX: Programming Concepts</I>.</P><hr><center>
[  <a href="getviewport.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="getwritemask.html">Next</a>  |
<A href="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
</center></BODY>

</HTML>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">

<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A9SR350marj"></A>getzbuffer Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX884" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX885" REL="I2" TITLE="frame buffer configuration"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX886" REL="I3" TITLE="zbuffer"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX887" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX888" REL="I2" TITLE="hidden surface"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX889" REL="I3" TITLE="getzbuffer"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX890" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX891" REL="I2" TITLE="z buffer"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX892" REL="I3" TITLE="finding out whether off or on"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX893" REL="I1" TITLE="getzbuffer subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912324"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B11FC813ceb"></A>Determines whether z-buffering is on or off.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C1223"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B11FC961ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B11FD065ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912327"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X912328"></A><B>Int32 getzbuffer(&nbsp;)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A28C010788"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A28C010789"></A><B>INTEGER*4 FUNCTION GETZBU</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X91232b"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B11FD423ceb"></A>The <B>getzbuffer</B> subroutine returns the status of the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A154P1160a">z-buffer</A>. The z-buffer option to the High-Performance 3-D Color Graphics Processor must be installed before the z-buffer can be turned on.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9e64"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A></BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A213X91232e"></A>Return Values</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X91232f"></A>False(0)<B></B></TD>
<TD>  Z-buffering off (the default value).</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A139X91ec9"></A>True(1)<B></B></TD>
<TD>  Z-buffering on.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A64C0165e6"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B11FD814ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C1226"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C1227"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C1228"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X91233b"></A>Related Information</H3>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>

<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="xT41a0nita"></A>gexit Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX894" REL="I1" TITLE="gexit subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX895" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX896" REL="I2" TITLE="initializing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX897" REL="I3" TITLE="gexit"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX898" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX899" REL="I2" TITLE="initializing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX900" REL="I3" TITLE="terminating a graphics program"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A213X91244f"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1220247ceb"></A>Terminates a graphics program.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C11d0"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1220398ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1220502ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912452"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X912453"></A><B>void gexit(&nbsp;)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010ba4"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912456"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1220854ceb"></A>The <B>gexit</B> subroutine is the final graphics routine in a program. This subroutine waits for the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0612">graphics pipeline</A> to empty, then frees all GL data structures.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1220963ceb"></A>After the <B>gexit</B> subroutine, a process can no longer call any routines that require the graphics to be initialized.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9e8d"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<P><A NAME="E1B1221129ceb"></A>The <B>gexit</B> subroutine unmaps and eliminates all windows, closes the display connection,  detaches all GL shared memory segments, cleans up and closes all GL graphics hardware resources, and eliminates GL processes and kernel context.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1221238ceb"></A>The <B>gexit</B> subroutine leaves the calling process in a state similar to that in which it would have been if no GL routine had ever been callled.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A30C011040"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1221394ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="scrn_rotate_c.html#A16C0c92f"><B>scrn_rotate.c</B></A> uses the <B>gexit</B> subroutine to end graphics processing. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A64C0165f5"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1221554ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C11d3"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C11d4"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C11d5"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912465"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1221883ceb"></A>Resetting all global state attributes to their initial values with the <A HREF="greset.html#xW42e0nita"><B>greset</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1221994ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/glintro.html#A8G44310marj">Understanding the Hardware</A> Used by GL in<I> GL3.2 Version 4 for AIX: Programming Concepts</I>.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1222102ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/clrrstintgl.html#clrrstintgl.html">Clearing, Resetting, and Initializing GL</A> in<I> GL3.2 Version 4 for AIX: Programming Concepts</I>.</P><hr><center>

<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="LDg21c0marj"></A>ginit Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX901" REL="I1" TITLE="ginit subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX902" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX903" REL="I2" TITLE="initializing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX904" REL="I3" TITLE="ginit"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX905" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX906" REL="I2" TITLE="initializing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX907" REL="I3" TITLE="graphics system"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A213X91249a"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1243662ceb"></A>Initializes the graphics system. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X91249c"></A>Library</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1243814ceb"></A>Graphics Library (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X91249d"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X91249e"></A><B>void ginit(&nbsp;)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010ba8"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010ba9"></A><B>SUBROUTINE GINIT</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X9124a1"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1244170ceb"></A>The <B>ginit</B> subroutine initializes the graphics environment to its default values for the global state 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A78P0561">attributes</A> and creates a window that covers the screen. The <B>ginit</B> subroutine queues the 
REDRAW
 window manager device.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1244278ceb"></A>Call the <B>ginit </B>subroutine once, before any other GL subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1244386ceb"></A>The recommendation is to use the <A HREF="winopen.html#A142X91549"><B>winopen</B></A> subroutine for initialization functions to take advantage of the window manager and to avoid unexpected events in the <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/cntrlques.html#A29C0109de">event queue</A>.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9e90"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A30C011042"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1244629ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="prompt_c.html#A16C0c8de"><B>prompt.c</B></A> uses the <B>ginit</B> subroutine to do a basic graphics setup.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A64C0165f8"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1244793ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C11d7"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C11d8"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C11d9"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X9124b1"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1245113ceb"></A>Initializing the graphics system without changing the color map with the <A HREF="gbegin.html#JS4380nita"><B>gbegin</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1245222ceb"></A>Terminating a graphics program with the <A HREF="gexit.html#xT41a0nita"><B>gexit</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1245330ceb"></A>Resetting all global state attributes to their initial values with the <A HREF="greset.html#xW42e0nita"><B>greset</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1245437ceb"></A>Creating a new window with the <A HREF="winopen.html#A142X91549"><B>winopen</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1245545ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/setglattrib.html#setglattrib.html">Setting Drawing Attributes</A>
 and <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/cntrlques.html#cntrlques.html">Controlling Queues and Devices</A>.</P>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">

<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A3CFC9E2687janb"></A>glcompat Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX908" REL="I1" TITLE="glcompat subroutine (GL)"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A3CFC9E2698janb"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="A3CFC9E2708janb"></A>Controls backwards compatibility modes.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A3CFC9E2719janb"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A3CFC9E2729janb"></A><B>void glcompat (Int32</B> <I>mode</I>, <B>Int32</B> <I>value</I>)</PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A3CFC9E2740janb"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A3CFC9E2751janb"></A><B>SUBROUTINE GLCOMPAT</B> (<I>mode, value</I>)
<B>INTEGER*4</B> <I>mode, value</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A3CFC9E2761janb"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A3CFC9E2772janb"></A><I>mode</I></TD>
<TD>  Token representing the compatibility mode to be changed.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A3CFC9E2783janb"></A><I>value</I></TD>
<TD>  The value that the compatibility mode should have.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A3CFC9E2794janb"></A>Functional Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="A3CFC9E2805janb"></A>This subroutine governs various compatibility modes for the GL subsystem. Applications should use this subroutine judiciously to minimize porting headaches while maximizing useful function. The following <B>glcompat</B> modes can also be set with environment variables with the same corresponding names.  </P>

<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A3CFC9E2815janb"></A><B>Mode</B></TD>
<TD>  GLC_CREATE_OVERLAY</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A3CFC9E2826janb"></A><B>Default</B></TD>
<TD>  FALSE</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A3CFC9E2838janb"></A><B>Function</B></TD>
<TD>  On the POWERgraphics GXT1000 adapter, this mode controls whether the <B>winX</B> subroutine will automatically create an overlay window. When this mode is set to TRUE, and the XID passed to <B>winX</B> is not an overlay window, then the <B>winX</B> routine will create an overlay window and make it a child of the indicted X window. Although the overlay window will be a distinct X11 window, internally, it will be used to emulate overlay plane functions. It can be accessed via the <B>drawmode</B> subroutine and can be drawn into with the usual GL functions.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A3CFC9E2849janb"></A></TD>
<TD>  When this mode is set to FALSE, the <B>winX</B> routine will simply accept the indicated X Window, and create and attach a GL context to that window. The <B>drawmode</B> subroutine should not be used with windows created by <B>winX</B> when this mode is FALSE.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A3CFC9E2859janb"></A></TD>
<TD>  This mode has no effect on graphics adapters other than the  POWERgraphics GXT1000.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A3CFC9E2870janb"></A><B>Mode</B></TD>
<TD>  GLC_ISSUE_OVERDRAW</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A3CFC9E2881janb"></A><B>Default</B></TD>
<TD>  FALSE</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A3CFC9E2892janb"></A><B>Function</B></TD>
<TD>  On the POWERgraphics GXT1000 adapter, this mode controls how exposure events for the overlay planes are handled. When the mode is TRUE, the REDRAW_OVERLAY event will be issued whenever the overlay planes are uncovered and need redrawing. The REDRAW event will not be issued if the main frame buffer window has not been damaged.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A3CFC9E2903janb"></A></TD>
<TD>  When the mode is FALSE, damage to the overlay planes will be reported with the REDRAW event. Note that if the main frame buffer has also been damaged, it may happen that two REDRAW events are reported for the window.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A3CFC9E2914janb"></A></TD>
<TD>  Set this mode to FALSE if your application does not handle REDRAW_OVERLAY events, but needs to find out when the overlays need to be redrawn.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A3CFC9E2924janb"></A></TD>
<TD>  This mode has no effect on graphics adapters other than the POWERgraphics GXT1000.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A3CFC9E2935janb"></A><B>Mode</B></TD>
<TD>  GLC_FB_FULLSCREEN</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A3CFC9E2946janb"></A><B>Default</B></TD>
<TD>  FALSE</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A3CFC9E2956janb"></A><B>Function</B></TD>
<TD>  On the POWERgraphics GXT1000 adapter, this mode enables the <B>fullscrn</B> routine to affect the main frame buffer. By default, the <B>fullscrn</B> subroutine applies only to the overlay bit-planes. </TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A3CFC9E2967janb"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="A3CFC9E2978janb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A3CFC9E2988janb"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A3CFC9E2999janb"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A3CFC9E3010janb"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE><hr><center>

<H1><A NAME="A3CFD921658janb"></A>Chapter 2. GL Example Programs</H1>
<H3><A NAME="A26C0fdf1"></A>Functional List of GL Example Programs</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7733275ceb"></A>Select an example program from the following list:</P>

<DL><DT><A NAME="A65C01683e"></A><A HREF="backface_c.html#A16C0c7a2"><B>backface.c</B></A> Example C Language program draws a cube</DT>

<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">

<TITLE>greset Subroutine
</TITLE>
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="glcompat.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="gRGBcolor.html">Next</a>  |
<A href="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="xW42e0nita"></A>greset Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX909" REL="I1" TITLE="greset subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX910" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX911" REL="I2" TITLE="initializing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX912" REL="I3" TITLE="greset"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX913" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX914" REL="I2" TITLE="initializing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX915" REL="I3" TITLE="resetting all global state attributes"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A213X9124b8"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1330291ceb"></A>Resets all global state attributes to their initial values.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A75C11"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1330440ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1330543ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X9124bb"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X9124bc"></A><B>void greset(&nbsp;)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010bb5"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010bb6"></A><B>SUBROUTINE GRESET</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X9124bf"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1330895ceb"></A>The <B>greset</B> subroutine resets all global state attributes to their initial values. This subroutine can be called at any time to reset the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A78P0561">attributes</A>.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1331003ceb"></A>The following table lists the global state attributes:</P>

<TABLE BORDER="2"><TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD COLSPAN="2"><B>Global State Attributes</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>Attribute</B></TD>

<TD><B>Initial Value</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>backface mode</TD>

<TD>off</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>blinking</TD>

<TD>off</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>buffer mode</TD>

<TD>single</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>color</TD>

<TD>undefined</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>color map mode</TD>

<TD>one map</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>concave</TD>

<TD>off</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>cursor</TD>

<TD>0 (arrow)</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>depth range</TD>

<TD>-0x800000,+0x7FFFFF (On Supergraphics Processor Subsystem: 0x0,0x1FFFFF)</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>depthcue mode</TD>

<TD>off</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>display mode</TD>

<TD>color map</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>drawmode</TD>

<TD>NORMALDRAW</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>font</TD>

<TD>0</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>linestyle</TD>

<TD>0 (solid)</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>linewidth</TD>

<TD>1 pixel</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>logical operation</TD>

<TD>LO_SRC</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>lsrepeat</TD>

<TD>1</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>pattern</TD>

<TD>0 (solid)</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>picking size</TD>

<TD>10x10 pixels</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>RGB color</TD>

<TD>undefined</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>RGB shaderange</TD>

<TD>undefined</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>RGB writemask</TD>

<TD>undefined</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>shademodel</TD>

<TD>GOURAUD</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>shaderange</TD>

<TD>0,7,-0x800000,+0x7FFFFF (On Supergraphics Processor Subsystem: 0x0,0x1FFFFF)</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>viewport</TD>

<TD>entire window</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>writemask</TD>

<TD>all planes enabled</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>z-buffer mode</TD>

<TD>off</TD></TR></TABLE>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A213X9124b6"></A><B>Note: </B>Font 0 (zero) is a Helvetica-like font.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<P><A NAME="E1B1331557ceb"></A>The <B>greset </B>subroutine puts a 2-D orthographic <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/coordtransfrms.html#A264X9141">projection transformation</A> on the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P06dd">matrix stack</A> with left, right, bottom, and top set to the boundaries of the screen. The subroutine also turns on the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A263A93ae">cursor</A> and ties it to MOUSEX and MOUSEY. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1331667ceb"></A>The <B>greset</B> subroutine removes all 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A1819349">button</A>, 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A79P07a">valuator</A>, and keyboard entries from the event queue and discards them. Each button is set to FALSE and untied from valuators. Each valuator (and in particular MOUSEX) is set to XMAXSCREEN/2 with range 0 to XMAXSCREEN. MOUSEY is set to YMAXSCREEN/2 and has range 0 to YMAXSCREEN.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1331774ceb"></A>The <B>greset </B>subroutine also defines certain entries in the color map, as follows:</P>

<TABLE BORDER="2"><TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD COLSPAN="4"><B>Color Map Entries</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><BR></TD>

<TD COLSPAN="3"><B>RGB Value</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>Name</B></TD>

<TD><B>Red</B></TD>

<TD><B>Green</B></TD>

<TD><B>Blue</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>BLACK</TD>

<TD>    0</TD>

<TD>    0</TD>

<TD>    0</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>RED</TD>

<TD>255</TD>

<TD>    0</TD>

<TD>    0</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GREEN</TD>

<TD>    0</TD>

<TD>255</TD>

<TD>    0</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>YELLOW</TD>

<TD>255</TD>

<TD>255</TD>

<TD>    0</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>BLUE</TD>

<TD>    0</TD>

<TD>    0</TD>

<TD>255</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>MAGENTA</TD>

<TD>255</TD>

<TD>    0</TD>

<TD>255</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>CYAN</TD>

<TD>    0</TD>

<TD>255</TD>

<TD>255</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>WHITE</TD>

<TD>255</TD>

<TD>255</TD>

<TD>255</TD></TR></TABLE>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9e96"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A30C011044"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1332132ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="vlsi_c.html#A16C0c9fd"><B>vlsi.c</B></A> uses the <B>greset</B> subroutine to reset all global attributes on any keyboard event.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A64C0165fc"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1332293ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="C418D23215root"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="C418D23745root"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="C418D24010root"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="C418D24931root"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1332611ceb"></A>Reconfiguring the graphics system with the <A HREF="gconfig.html#hS4260nita"><B>gconfig</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1332718ceb"></A>Initializing the graphics system with the <A HREF="ginit.html#LDg21c0marj"><B>ginit</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/glintro.html#A8G44310marj">Understanding the Hardware Used by GL</A>, <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/setglattrib.html#setglattrib.html">Setting Drawing Attributes</A>, <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/underwininput.html#underwininput.html">Windows and Input Control Overview</A>, <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/workcoords.html#workcoords.html">Working with Coordinate Systems</A>.</P>

<H2><A NAME="ESL13a0marj"></A>gRGBcolor Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX916" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX917" REL="I2" TITLE="attribute"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX918" REL="I3" TITLE="gRGBcolor"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX919" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX920" REL="I2" TITLE="color, current"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX921" REL="I3" TITLE="returning in RGB mode"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX922" REL="I1" TITLE="gRGBcolor subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="C7540A2146vbia"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1352858ceb"></A>Gets the current RGB color values.</P>

<H3><A NAME="C7540A2308vbia"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1353008ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1353112ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="C7540A2541vbia"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1353270ceb"></A><B>void gRGBcolor</B></P>

<P><B>(Int16 </B><A HREF="gRGBcolor.html#D8HTi5bvbia"><I>red</I></A><B>, Int16</B> <A HREF="gRGBcolor.html#O8HTi3a8vbia"><I>green</I></A><B>, Int16</B> <A HREF="gRGBcolor.html#b8HTi15vbia"><I>blue</I></A><B>)</B></P>

<H3><A NAME="C7540A2691vbia"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1353453ceb"></A><B>SUBROUTINE GRGBCO(</B><I>red</I><B>,</B> <I>green</I><B>,</B> <I>blue</I><B>)</B></P>

<P><B>INTEGER*2 </B><I>red</I><B>, </B><I>green</I><B>, </B><I>blue</I></P>

<H3><A NAME="C7540A2837vbia"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1353613ceb"></A>The <B>gRGBcolor</B> subroutine gets the current RGB color values and copies them into the parameters.</P>

<OL><LI><A NAME="C7540A3086vbia"></A>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a display list.</LI>

<LI><A NAME="C7540A3162vbia"></A>This subroutine is available in RGB mode. It will not function in color map mode.</LI></OL>

<H3><A NAME="C7540A3230vbia"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="D8HTi5bvbia"></A><I>red</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the pointer to the location into which to copy the current red value.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="O8HTi3a8vbia"></A><I>green</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the pointer to the location into which to copy the current green value.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="b8HTi15vbia"></A><I>blue</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the pointer to the location into which to copy the current blue value.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="C7540A3477vbia"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1354151ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature. </P>

<H3><A NAME="C7540A3621vbia"></A>Files</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1354308ceb"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</B>Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1354416ceb"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</B>Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</P>

<H3><A NAME="C7E4C06383bett"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1354574ceb"></A>Returning the current color with the <A HREF="getcolor.html#A146X924b"><B>getcolor</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1354682ceb"></A>Getting a copy of the RGB values for a color map entry with the <A HREF="getmcolor.html#nXI1100marj"><B>getmcolor</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1354790ceb"></A>Setting the current color in RGB mode with the <A HREF="RGBcolor.html#A143X9394"><B>RGBcolor</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1354901ceb"></A>Setting a display mode that bypasses the color map with the <A HREF="RGBmode.html#A143X93b6"><B>RGBmode</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/querysys.html#querysys.html">Querying the System</A>.</P><hr><center>

<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A143X94e8"></A>gRGBmask Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX923" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX924" REL="I2" TITLE="frame buffer update control"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX925" REL="I3" TITLE="gRGBmask"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX926" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX927" REL="I2" TITLE="RGB writemask"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX928" REL="I3" TITLE="returning current"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX929" REL="I1" TITLE="gRGBmask subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A143X94ea"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1376579ceb"></A>Returns the current RGB writemask.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C11ed"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1376731ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1376835ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X94ee"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A143X94ef"></A><B>void gRGBmask</B>
<B>(Int16 *</B><A HREF="gRGBmask.html#A143X94f3"><I>redmask</I></A><B>, Int16 *</B><A HREF="gRGBmask.html#A143X94f4"><I>greenmask</I></A><B>, Int16 *</B><A HREF="gRGBmask.html#A143X94f5"><I>bluemask</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A28C010771"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A28C010772"></A><B>SUBROUTINE GRGBMA(</B><I>redmask</I><B>,</B> <I>greenmask</I><B>,</B> <I>bluemask</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*2 </B><I>redmask</I><B>,</B> <I>greenmask</I><B>,</B> <I>bluemask</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X94f0"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1377204ceb"></A>The <B>gRGBmask</B> subroutine gets the current RGB 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A3C0F2A4599mhay">writemask</A> as three 8-bit masks and copies them into the parameters. The subroutine places masks in the low order 8-bits of the locations <A HREF="gRGBmask.html#A143X94f3"><I>redmask</I></A>, <A HREF="gRGBmask.html#A143X94f4"><I>greenmask</I></A>, and <A HREF="gRGBmask.html#A143X94f5"><I>bluemask</I></A>. The system must be in 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0743">RGB mode</A> when this routine executes. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1377312ceb"></A>This subroutine is intended for use in RGB mode only. To get the writemask when in color map mode, use the <A HREF="getwritemask.html#A143X94c6"><B>getwritemask</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9e0b"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a
 <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A143X94f2"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X94f3"></A><I>redmask</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the pointer to the location into which the system is to copy the current red writemask value.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X94f4"></A><I>greenmask</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the pointer to the location into which the system is to copy the current green writemask value.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X94f5"></A><I>bluemask</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the pointer to the location into which the system is to copy the current blue writemask value.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A64C0165d2"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1377758ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C11f0"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C11f1"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C11f2"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9508"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1378092ceb"></A>Returning the current writemask with the <A HREF="getwritemask.html#A143X94c6"><B>getwritemask</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1378202ceb"></A>Granting write access to a subset of available bitplanes with the <A HREF="RGBwritemask.html#A143X93fa"><B>RGBwritemask</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1378312ceb"></A>Specifying the RGBA writemask with a single packed integer with the <A HREF="wmpack.html#A143X9570"><B>wmpack</B></A> subroutine. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1378420ceb"></A>Granting write permission to available bitplanes with the <A HREF="writemask.html#A143X9592"><B>writemask</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1378528ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/configframebuf.html#configframebuf.html">Configuring the Frame Buffer</A>, <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/querysys.html#querysys.html">Querying</A> the System, and Working in <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/workcolor.html#workcolor.html">Color Map and RGB Modes</A>.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1378651ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/writemasks.html#writemasks.html">Writemasks and Logical Operations</A>
 and Working in <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/workcolor.html#workcolor.html">Color Map and RGB Modes</A>.</P><hr><center>

</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="gRGBmask.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="gsync.html">Next</a>  |
<A href="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A213X9118b2"></A>gselect Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX930" REL="I1" TITLE="gselect subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX931" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX932" REL="I2" TITLE="picking and selecting"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX933" REL="I3" TITLE="putting system in selecting mode"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX934" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX935" REL="I2" TITLE="picking and selecting"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX936" REL="I3" TITLE="gselect"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A213X9118b4"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B139D448ceb"></A>Puts the system in selecting mode.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C197"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B139D598ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B139D703ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X9118b7"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X9118b8"></A><B>Int32 gselect(Int16 </B><A HREF="gselect.html#A213X9118c1"><I>buffer</I></A><B>[&nbsp;], Int32</B> <A HREF="gselect.html#A213X9118c2"><I>numnames</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911890"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X911893"></A><B>SUBROUTINE GSELEC(</B><I>buffer</I><B>, </B><I>numnames</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>numnames</I>
<B>INTEGER*2 </B><I>buffer</I><B>(</B><I>numnames</I><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X9118bb"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B139E072ceb"></A>The <B>gselect</B> subroutine puts the system in 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A27P019">selecting mode</A>. In this mode, the system notes when a drawing routine intersects the selecting volume and writes the contents of the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P06e3">name stack</A> to the specified buffer. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B139E180ceb"></A>If you push a name onto the name stack just before you call each drawing routine, you can record which drawing routines intersected the selecting region. Use the current viewing matrix to define the selecting region.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B139E292ceb"></A>The <B>gselect </B>and <A HREF="pick.html#h632f0nita"><B>pick</B></A> subroutines differ only in the manner in which the pick or select volume is specified. The <A HREF="pick.html#h632f0nita"><B>pick</B></A> subroutine uses a volume (default 10x10 pixels) centered on the current cursor location, while the <B>gselect</B> subroutine uses the unit cube (1x1x1) in modeling coordinates, thus employing the current viewing matrix in determining the selecting volume.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B139E400ceb"></A>Nothing is drawn to the screen when the system is in selecting mode. Instead, drawing commands are piped to the select mechanism and used to determine the pick or select region hits.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B139E508ceb"></A>With one exception, all drawing routines cause hits, including clear, points, lines, polygons, arcs, circles, curves, patches, and NURBS. The <B>charstr</B> subroutine does not cause a hit, although <B>cmov</B> and <B>cmov2</B> do cause hits.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B139E615ceb"></A>To end selecting mode, call the <A HREF="endselect.html#A213X91190c"><B>endselect</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9cf8"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A213X9118c0"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X9118c1"></A><I>buffer</I><B></B></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the buffer into which the system is to save the contents of the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P06e3">name stack</A>.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X9118c2"></A><I>numnames</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the maximum number of names to be saved.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A30C010fe2"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B139E988ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="select1_c.html#A16C0c970"><B>select1.c</B></A> uses the <B>gselect</B> subroutine to enter selecting mode.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015cb6"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B139F152ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C19a"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C19b"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C19c"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X9118d5"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B139F470ceb"></A>Turning off picking mode with the <A HREF="endpick.html#A213X91185b"><B>endpick</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B139F576ceb"></A>Turning off selecting mode with the <A HREF="endselect.html#A213X91190c"><B>endselect</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B139F684ceb"></A>Initializing the name stack with the <A HREF="initnames.html#YlD250marj"><B>initnames</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B139F792ceb"></A>Loading the name on top of the name stack with the <A HREF="loadname.html#A213X9119af"><B>loadname</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B139F899ceb"></A>Putting the system in picking mode with the <A HREF="pick.html#h632f0nita"><B>pick</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B13A0006ceb"></A>Setting the dimensions of the picking region with the <A HREF="picksize.html#A6cv180marj"><B>picksize</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B13A0115ceb"></A>Popping a name off the name stack with the <A HREF="popname.html#A213X911af9"><B>popname</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B13A0222ceb"></A>Pushing a new name onto the name stack with the <A HREF="pushname.html#A213X911b48"><B>pushname</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B13A0331ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A>, <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/picknselect.html#picknselect.html">Picking and Selecting</A> Overview, and Working with <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/workcoords.html#workcoords.html">Coordinate Systems</A>.</P><hr><center>

<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A4h41120marj"></A>gsync  Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX937" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX938" REL="I2" TITLE="animation"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX939" REL="I3" TITLE="gsync"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX940" REL="I1" TITLE="gsync subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX941" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX942" REL="I2" TITLE="vertical retrace"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX943" REL="I3" TITLE="waiting for next"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A318C9c83"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B13BE788ceb"></A>Waits for a vertical retrace period.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A77C12b"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B13BE936ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B13BF041ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A318C9c87"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A318C9c88"></A><B>void gsync(&nbsp;)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A17C0d9b3"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A17C0d9b4"></A><B>SUBROUTINE GSYNC</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A318C9c89"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B13BF394ceb"></A>The <B>gsync</B> subroutine waits for the next 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A27P031">vertical retrace</A>. Because this subroutine does not return until vertical retrace begins, the calling process is effectively blocked until that time.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B13BF502ceb"></A>This subroutine is useful for pacing the drawing when in single buffer mode. If the amount of drawing to be done is small, this subroutine can be used to achieve a limited amount of smooth animation in single buffer mode. For high-quality, smooth-animation, double-buffer mode should be used with the <A HREF="swapbuffers.html#A145X9302"><B>swapbuffers</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9c8b"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A11C0b4a4"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B13BF712ceb"></A>The <A HREF="worms_c.html#A16C0ca03"><B>worms.c</B></A> example C language program uses the <B>gsync</B> subroutine to help smooth the display while it is changing the frame buffer.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015cad"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B13BF873ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3CFCA5D361janb"></A>The POWERgraphics GXT1000 does not support the <B>gsync</B> subroutine.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A11C0b4a6"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C12e"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C12f"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A258C01c34c"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B13C0191ceb"></A>Setting the display mode to double buffer mode with the <A HREF="doublebuffer.html#A145X91a7"><B>doublebuffer</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B13C0300ceb"></A>Setting the display mode to single buffer mode with the <A HREF="singlebuffer.html#A145X9259"><B>singlebuffer</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B13C0407ceb"></A>Exchanging the front and back buffers in double buffer mode with the <A HREF="swapbuffers.html#A145X9302"><B>swapbuffers</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B13C0515ceb"></A>Understanding the <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/glintro.html#A8G44310marj">Hardware Used by GL</A> and Working in <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/workcolor.html#workcolor.html">Color Map and RGB Modes</A>.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B13C0621ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/animatescene.html#animatescene.html">Creating Animated Scenes</A>.</P><hr><center>

<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A237X9480e"></A>gversion Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX944" REL="I1" TITLE="gversion subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX945" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX946" REL="I2" TITLE="initializing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX947" REL="I3" TITLE="gversion"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX948" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX949" REL="I2" TITLE="query"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX950" REL="I3" TITLE="gversion"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX951" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX952" REL="I2" TITLE="initializing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX953" REL="I3" TITLE="returning graphics hardware, library information"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A237X94810"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B13E0544ceb"></A>Returns graphics hardware and library version information.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C11dc"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B13E0696ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B13E0799ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A237X94814"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X91134f"></A><B>Int32 gversion(Char8 *</B><A HREF="gversion.html#A213X911344"><I>v</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X91134c"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A52C0142ce"></A><B>INTEGER*4 GVERSI(</B><I>v</I><B>, </B><A HREF="gversion.html#A237X9481b"><I>length</I></A><B>)</B>
<B>CHARACTER*(*) </B><I>v</I>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>length</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A237X94816"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B13E1164ceb"></A>The <B>gversion</B> subroutine fills the buffer, identified by the <I>v</I> parameter, with a null-terminated string that specifies the graphics hardware type and the version number of GL. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B13E1272ceb"></A>It is not necessary to open a GL window or to call the <B>ginit</B> subroutine before using the <B>getdesc</B> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B13E1379ceb"></A>The <B>gversion</B> subroutine returns a value of -1 if GL is not supported on this particular hardware configuration.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A325C93ba0"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A5DB26C823bett"></A><B>Attention: </B>Calling the <B>gversion</B> subroutine before calling the <B>winopen</B> subroutine on the POWERgraphics GTO and the POWERstation 730, results in a core dump when the initial <B>winopen</B> subroutine call is made.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A237X94828"></A>Return Value</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B13E1647ceb"></A>In the following values table, <I>m</I> and <I>n</I> indicate the major and minor release numbers of the installed software libraries:</P>

<TABLE BORDER="2"><TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>Installed Adapter</B></TD>

<TD><B>String Returned</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>3-D Color Graphics Processor</TD>

<TD>GL:CGP-<I>m.n</I></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>Supergraphics Processor</TD>

<TD>GL:GTO-<I>m.n</I></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>POWER GTO adapter</TD>

<TD>GL:GTO-<I>m.n</I></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>POWER Gt4 adapter</TD>

<TD>GL:GT4-<I>m.n</I></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>POWER Gt4x adapter</TD>

<TD>GL:GT4-<I>m.n</I></TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A237X94818"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X911344"></A><I>v</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies a buffer into which you can copy a string. Reserve at least a 12-character buffer. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A237X9481b"></A><I>length</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the length of the string.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A64C01660a"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B13E2049ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C11df"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C11e0"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C11e1"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A237X9482e"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B13E2369ceb"></A>Creating a new window with the <A HREF="winopen.html#A142X91549"><B>winopen</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B13E2475ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/glintro.html#A8G44310marj">Understanding the Hardware</A> Used by GL and <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/clrrstintgl.html#clrrstintgl.html">Clearing, Resetting, and Initializing GL</A> in<I> GL3.2 Version 4 for AIX: Programming Concepts</I>.</P><hr><center>

<TITLE>iconsize Subroutine
</TITLE>
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="gversion.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="icontitle.html">Next</a>  |
<A href="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="LA13e0marj"></A>iconsize Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX954" REL="I1" TITLE="iconsize subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX955" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX956" REL="I2" TITLE="window"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX957" REL="I3" TITLE="iconsize"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX958" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX959" REL="I2" TITLE="window icons"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX960" REL="I3" TITLE="specifying"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912b43"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1404792ceb"></A>Specifies the icon size of a window.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C12de"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1404961ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1405065ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912b46"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X912b47"></A><B>void iconsize(Int32 </B><A HREF="iconsize.html#AzS232f0marj"><I>x</I></A><B>, Int32 </B><A HREF="iconsize.html#BT23130marj"><I>y</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010c3b"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010c3c"></A><B>SUBROUTINE ICONSI(</B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>)</B>
<B>integer*4 </B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912b4a"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1405469ceb"></A>The <B>iconsize </B>subroutine specifies the size of a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A13791dc4">window</A> icon as <A HREF="iconsize.html#AzS232f0marj"><I>x</I></A> pixels by <A HREF="iconsize.html#BT23130marj"><I>y</I></A> pixels. If a window has an icon size, the window manager reshapes the window to be that size and sends a REDRAWICONIC token to the graphics queue when the user stores that window. Windows without an icon size are handled by the window manager with the appropriate default behavior.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1405578ceb"></A>To assign a new window an icon size, call the <B>iconsize</B> subroutine before opening the window. To give an existing window an icon size, use the <B>iconsize </B>subroutine with the <A HREF="winconstraints.html#A142X914c1"><B>winconstraints</B></A> subroutine. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1405687ceb"></A>Any application using the <B>iconsize </B>subroutine should also call the <A HREF="qdevice.html#A143X967"><B>qdevice</B></A> subroutine to queue the tokens WINFREEZE and WINTHAW after opening the window. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1405794ceb"></A>In the current implementation, the <B>iconsize</B> subroutine does not set the size of the icon.  The actual size and shape of the icon are controlled by the window manager application.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9f58"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A213X912b4f"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="AzS232f0marj"></A><I>x</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the width of the window icon in pixels.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="BT23130marj"></A><I>y</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the height of the window icon in pixels.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A61C0159ee"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1406190ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C12e1"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C12e2"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C12e3"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="sH13240marj"></A>icontitle Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX961" REL="I1" TITLE="icontitle subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX962" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX963" REL="I2" TITLE="window"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX964" REL="I3" TITLE="icontitle"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX965" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX966" REL="I2" TITLE="window icons"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX967" REL="I3" TITLE="specifying"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912b96"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1427778ceb"></A>Specifies the icon title for the current window.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C12e5"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1427926ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1428029ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912b99"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X912b9a"></A><B>void icontitle(Char8 *</B><A HREF="icontitle.html#A4e233b0marj"><I>name</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010c49"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010c4a"></A><B>SUBROUTINE ICONTI(</B><A HREF="icontitle.html#A4e233b0marj"><I>name</I></A><B>,</B> <A HREF="icontitle.html#A4f23350marj"><I>length</I></A><B>)</B>
<B>CHARACTER *(*) </B><I>name</I>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>length</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912b9d"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1428393ceb"></A>The <B>icontitle </B>subroutine specifies the string displayed on an icon if the window manager draws that window's icon. </P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A81C11f1"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A213X912b9f"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A4e233b0marj"></A><I>name</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies a pointer to the string containing the icon title.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A4f23350marj"></A><I>length</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the length of the string containing the icon title.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A61C0159fc"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1428775ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C12e8"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C12e9"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C12ea"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912ba5"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1429092ceb"></A>Specifying the size of a window icon with the <A HREF="iconsize.html#LA13e0marj"><B>iconsize</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1429200ceb"></A>Adding a title bar to the current window with the <A HREF="wintitle.html#A142X915f3"><B>wintitle</B></A> subroutine.</P>
