```html
<A NAME="INDEX968" REL="I1" TITLE="initnames subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX969" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX970" REL="I2" TITLE="picking and selecting"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX971" REL="I3" TITLE="initializing name stack"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX972" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX973" REL="I2" TITLE="picking and selecting"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX974" REL="I3" TITLE="initnames"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A237X94591"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B144C802ceb"></A>Initializes the name stack.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C19d"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B144C952ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B144D055ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A237X94594"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A237X94595"></A><B>void initnames(&nbsp;)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A237X94573"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A237X94576"></A><B>SUBROUTINE INITNA</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A237X94598"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B144D411ceb"></A>The <B>initnames</B> subroutines initializes the name stack for use during 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P06fa">picking</A> or 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A27P019">selecting</A>.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A30C010fe6"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B144D565ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="pick1_c.html#A13C0bd9f"><B>pick1.c</B></A> calls the <B>initnames</B> subroutine to clear all of the names from the name stack. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015cba"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B144D727ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1a0"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1a1"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1a2"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A237X9459e"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B144E097ceb"></A>Putting the system in selecting mode with the <A HREF="gselect.html#A213X9118b2"><B>gselect</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B144E205ceb"></A>Loading a name onto the top of the name stack with the <A HREF="loadname.html#A213X9119af"><B>loadname</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B144E313ceb"></A>Putting the system in picking mode with the <A HREF="pick.html#h632f0nita"><B>pick</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B144E423ceb"></A>Popping a name off the name stack with the <A HREF="popname.html#A213X911af9"><B>popname</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B144E530ceb"></A>Pushing a new name onto the name stack with the <A HREF="pushname.html#A213X911b48"><B>pushname</B></A> subroutine.</P>
```

```html
<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">
<HTML>
<HEAD>
<META HTTP-EQUIV="Content-Type" CONTENT="text/html; charset=iso-8859-1">

<TITLE>iobounce.c Example C Language Program
</TITLE>
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="gamma_c.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="localatten_c.html">Next</a>  |
<A HREF="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A16C0c8ae"></A>iobounce.c Example C Language Program
</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX2318" REL="I1" TITLE="iobounce.c example program (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2319" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2320" REL="I2" TITLE="example programs"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2321" REL="I3" TITLE="drawing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2322" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2323" REL="I2" TITLE="sphere"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2324" REL="I3" TITLE="drawing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2325" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2326" REL="I2" TITLE="drawing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2327" REL="I3" TITLE="sphere"></A>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EAB0276ttay"></A>/*
iobounce.c:</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EAB0470ttay"></A>  A "pool" ball that "bounces" around a 2-d "surface".
  RIGHTMOUSE stops ball
  MIDDLEMOUSE increases y velocity
  LEFTMOUSE increases x velocity
*/</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EAB0626ttay"></A>#include &lt;gl/gl.h>
#include &lt;gl/device.h></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EAB0792ttay"></A>#define XMIN 100
#define YMIN 100
#define XMAX 900
#define YMAX 700</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EAB0945ttay"></A>long xvelocity = 0, yvelocity = 0;</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EAB1091ttay"></A>main()
{</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EAB1245ttay"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Device dev;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;short val;    </PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EAB1609ttay"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;initialize();    
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;while (TRUE) {       
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;while (qtest()) {          
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;dev = qread(&amp;val);          
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;switch (dev) {
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;case LEFTMOUSE:          /* increase xvelocity */
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;if (xvelocity >= 0)
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;xvelocity++;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;else
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;xvelocity--;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;break;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;case MIDDLEMOUSE:        /* increase yvelocity */
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;if (yvelocity >= 0)
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;yvelocity++;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;else
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;yvelocity--;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;break;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;case RIGHTMOUSE:         /* stop ball */
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;xvelocity = yvelocity = 0;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;break;                
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;case ESCKEY:
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;gexit();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;exit(0);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;}
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;}
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;drawball();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EAB1751ttay"></A>}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EAB1898ttay"></A>initialize()
{</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EAB2046ttay"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;int gid;    </PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EAB2314ttay"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;prefposition(XMAXSCREEN/4, XMAXSCREEN*3/4, YMAXSCREEN/4, 
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;    YMAXSCREEN*3/4);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;gid = winopen("iobounce");    
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;doublebuffer();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;gconfig();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;shademodel(FLAT);    
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;ortho2(XMIN - 0.5, XMAX + 0.5, YMIN - 0.5, YMAX + 0.5);    
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;qdevice(ESCKEY);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;qdevice(REDRAW);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;qdevice(LEFTMOUSE);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;qdevice(MIDDLEMOUSE);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;qdevice(RIGHTMOUSE);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;qenter(REDRAW,gid);</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EAB2457ttay"></A>}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EAB2604ttay"></A>drawball()
{</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EAB2764ttay"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;static xpos = 500,ypos = 500;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;long radius = 10;    </PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EAB3012ttay"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(BLACK);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;clear();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;xpos += xvelocity;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;ypos += yvelocity;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;if (xpos > XMAX - radius ||
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;    xpos &lt; XMIN + radius) {
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;xpos -= xvelocity;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;xvelocity = -xvelocity;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;}
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;if (ypos > YMAX - radius ||
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;    ypos &lt; YMIN + radius) {
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;ypos -= yvelocity;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;yvelocity = -yvelocity;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EAB3176ttay"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(YELLOW);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;circfi(xpos, ypos, radius);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;swapbuffers();</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EAB3319ttay"></A>}</PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A200C117c"></A>Related Information</H3><hr><center>
```

```html
<hr>

<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A142X920c"></A>isobj Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX975" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX976" REL="I2" TITLE="object (display list)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX977" REL="I3" TITLE="isobj"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX978" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX979" REL="I2" TITLE="object (display list)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX980" REL="I3" TITLE="checking number for accuracy"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX981" REL="I1" TITLE="isobj subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A142X920e"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B146E873ceb"></A>Indicates whether a given object number actually identifies an object.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C143"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B146F021ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B146F124ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A142X9212"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A142X9213"></A><B>Int32 isobj(Int32 </B><A HREF="isobj.html#A142X9217"><I>object</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010a71"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010a72"></A><B>LOGICAL FUNCTION ISOBJ(</B><I>object</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>object</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A142X9214"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B146F488ceb"></A>The <B>isobj</B> subroutine indicates whether a given object number actually identifies an 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A255B9bc">object</A>. The returned value is either True, if the object number is already in use, or False, if it is not.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9d81"></A><B>Note: </B>This editing subroutine itself cannot be added to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A142X9216"></A>Parameter</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A142X9217"></A><I>object</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the object identifier to test.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A142X921a"></A>Return Values</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A142X921b"></A>True</TD>
<TD>  Object number is already in use.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C146"></A>False</TD>
<TD>  Object number is not in use.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015cf6"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B146F970ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>
```

```html
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A143X91da"></A>isqueued Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX982" REL="I1" TITLE="isqueued subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX983" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX984" REL="I2" TITLE="device"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX985" REL="I3" TITLE="indicating whether enabled"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX986" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX987" REL="I2" TITLE="queue and device"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX988" REL="I3" TITLE="isqueued"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A143X91dc"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1492050ceb"></A>Indicates whether the specified device is enabled for queuing.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1150"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1492199ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1492303ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X91e0"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A143X91e1"></A><B>Int32 isqueued(Int16 </B><A HREF="isqueued.html#A143X91e5"><I>device</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010c8e"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010c8f"></A><B>LOGICAL FUNCTION ISQUEU(</B><I>device</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>device</I></PRE>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A79C1153"></A><B>Note: </B>For FORTRAN users, this function accepts long integer parameters (INTEGER*4) when invoked from a FORTRAN program, although it accepts short integers when invoked from a C program. The C and FORTRAN syntax shown here reflect this difference.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A143X91e2"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1492730ceb"></A>The <B>isqueued</B> subroutine indicates whether the specified device is enabled for queuing.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A81C11f4"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A143X91e4"></A>Parameter</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X91e5"></A><I>device</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the identifier for the device you want to test (for example, MOUSEX or BPADX).</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X91e8"></A>Return Values</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912c52"></A>True<I></I></TD>
<TD>  Enabled for queuing. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912c53"></A>False</TD>
<TD>  Not enabled for queuing.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A30C011070"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1493200ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="prompt_c.html#A16C0c8de"><B>prompt.c</B></A> uses the <B>isqueued</B> subroutine to determine whether the keyboard is enabled.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A64C016631"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1493361ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X91f6"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1154"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1155"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1156"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/device.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1157"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fdevice.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X91fa"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1493793ceb"></A>Enabling an input device for event queuing with the <A HREF="qdevice.html#A143X967"><B>qdevice</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1493900ceb"></A>Reading the first entry in the event queue with the <A HREF="qread.html#A143X989"><B>qread</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1494007ceb"></A>Disabling an input device for event queuing with the <A HREF="unqdevice.html#A143X91b8"><B>unqdevice</B></A> subroutine.</P>
```

```html
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="JXw220marj"></A>istag Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX989" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX990" REL="I2" TITLE="object (display list)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX991" REL="I3" TITLE="istag"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX992" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX993" REL="I2" TITLE="object (display list)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX994" REL="I3" TITLE="checking tag presence in current open object"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX995" REL="I1" TITLE="istag subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911f71"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B14B8443ceb"></A>Indicates whether a given tag is used within the current open object.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C14a"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B14B8624ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B14B8761ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911f74"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X911f75"></A><B>Int32 istag(Int32 </B><A HREF="istag.html#DfA2e0marj"><I>tag</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010a89"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010a8a"></A><B>LOGICAL FUNCTION ISTAG(</B><I>tag</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>tag</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911f78"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B14B9177ceb"></A>The <B>istag</B> subroutine indicates whether a given tag number actually identifies an existing tag. The returned value is either True (1), if the tag is already in use, or False (0), if it is not. If there is no current open 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A255B9bc">object</A>, the result is undefined.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9d90"></A><B>Note: </B>This editing subroutine, itself, cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A213X911f7b"></A>Parameter</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="DfA2e0marj"></A><I>tag</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the tag to test.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911f7c"></A>Return Values</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X911f7d"></A>True</TD>
<TD>  Tag number is already in use.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C14d"></A>False</TD>
<TD>  Tag number is not in use.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015d00"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B14B9660ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C14e"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C14f"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C150"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911f89"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B14B9987ceb"></A>Returning a unique integer for use as a tag number with the <A HREF="gentag.html#A48x2120marj"><B>gentag</B></A> subroutine.</P>
```

```html
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A142X91896"></A>keepaspect Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX996" REL="I1" TITLE="keepaspect subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX997" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX998" REL="I2" TITLE="window"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX999" REL="I3" TITLE="keepaspect"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1000" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1001" REL="I2" TITLE="windows"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1002" REL="I3" TITLE="specifying"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A142X91898"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B14DE080ceb"></A>Specifies the aspect ratio of a window.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C12f9"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B14DE229ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B14DE336ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A142X9189c"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X912b80"></A><B>void keepaspect(Int32 </B><A HREF="keepaspect.html#GZ3350marj"><I>x</I></A><B>, Int32 </B><A HREF="keepaspect.html#VZ33190marj"><I>y</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010c43"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010c44"></A><B>SUBROUTINE KEEPAS(</B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A142X9189e"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B14DE706ceb"></A>The<B> keepaspect </B>subroutine specifies the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A78P0547">aspect ratio</A> of a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A13791dc4">window</A>. It is called at the beginning of a graphics program, but only takes effect when the <A HREF="winopen.html#A142X91549"><B>winopen</B></A> subroutine is called. The resulting window maintains the aspect ratio specified in the<B> keepaspect </B>subroutine, even if the window changes size. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B14DE819ceb"></A>For example, <SAMP>keepaspect(1,1)</SAMP> always results in a square window. The<B> keepaspect </B>subroutine can also be called in conjunction with the <A HREF="winconstraints.html#A142X914c1"><B>winconstraints</B></A> subroutine to modify the enforced aspect ratio after the window is created. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B14DE929ceb"></A>With the <B>keepaspect</B> subroutine, the programmer can prevent the user from resizing a window to an aspect ratio that is different from the specified ratio.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9f64"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A142X918a0"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="GZ3350marj"></A><I>x</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the horizontal proportion of the aspect ratio.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="VZ33190marj"></A><I>y</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the vertical proportion of the aspect ratio.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A142X918a6"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B14DF310ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="colored_c.html"><B>colored.c</B></A> uses the <B>keepaspect</B> subroutine to restrict a window to a specific aspect ratio.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A61C0159f6"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B14DF471ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C12fc"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C12fd"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C12fe"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A142X918b6"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B14DF798ceb"></A>Specifying pixel values to be added to a window with the <A HREF="fudge.html#A142X917a6"><B>fudge</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B14DF905ceb"></A>Constraining the location and size of a window with the <A HREF="prefposition.html#A142X9164f"><B>prefposition</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B14E0015ceb"></A>Constraining the size of a window with the <A HREF="prefsize.html#A142X91671"><B>prefsize</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B14E0123ceb"></A>Binding window constraints to the current window with the <A HREF="winconstraints.html#A142X914c1"><B>winconstraints</B></A> subroutine. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B14E0230ceb"></A>Creating a window with the <A HREF="winopen.html#A142X91549"><B>winopen</B></A> subroutine. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B14E0342ceb"></A>Creating and Managing <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/managewinds.html#managewinds.html">Windows</A>.</P><hr><center>
```

```html
<H2><A NAME="A213X9113bc"></A>lampoff or lampon Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1003" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1004" REL="I2" TITLE="keyboard control"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1005" REL="I3" TITLE="lampon"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1006" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1007" REL="I2" TITLE="keyboard control"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1008" REL="I3" TITLE="lampoff"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1009" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1010" REL="I2" TITLE="keyboard display lights"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1011" REL="I3" TITLE="turning off or on"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1012" REL="I1" TITLE="lampoff subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1013" REL="I1" TITLE="lampon subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A213X9113be"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1501641ceb"></A>Turns the keyboard display lights off or on.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C12ab"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1501795ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1501898ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X9113c1"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X9113c2"></A><B>void lampoff(Int8 </B><A HREF="lampoff.html#A213X9113c9"><I>lamps</I></A><B>);</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A339C96461"></A><B>void lampon(Int8 </B><A HREF="lampoff.html#A213X9113c9"><I>lamps</I></A><B>);</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X91139a"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X91139d"></A><B>SUBROUTINE LAMPOF(</B><I>lamps</I><B>)</B>
<B>CHARACTER*1 </B><I>lamps</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A28C01078f"></A><B>SUBROUTINE LAMPON(</B><I>lamps</I><B>)</B>
<B>CHARACTER*1 </B><I>lamps</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X9113c5"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1502376ceb"></A>The <B>lampon</B> subroutine turns on any combination of the four user-controlled lamps on the keyboard. The <B>lampoff</B> subroutine turns them off. The four low-order bits of the <A HREF="lampoff.html#A213X9113c9"><I>lamps</I></A>  parameter control lamps 1 through 4.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9e76"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A213X9113c8"></A>Parameter</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X9113c9"></A><I>lamps</I></TD>
<TD>  Indicates the mask that specifies which lamps to manipulate. If a bit is set, then the corresponding keyboard lamp is either on or off.  </TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015d5a"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1502705ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C12ae"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C12af"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C12b0"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X9113dc"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1503051ceb"></A>Turning on or off the keyboard click with the <A HREF="clkoff.html#A213X9112de"><B>clkon</B> or <B>clkoff</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1503158ceb"></A>Ringing the keyboard bell with the <A HREF="ringbell.html#A213X911463"><B>ringbell</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1503269ceb"></A>Setting the duration of the keyboard bell sound with the <A HREF="setbell.html#A213X9114ae"><B>setbell</B></A> subroutine.</P>
```

```html
<H2><A NAME="qTc320marj"></A>lgetdepth Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1014" REL="I1" TITLE="lgetdepth subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1015" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1016" REL="I2" TITLE="viewport"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1017" REL="I3" TITLE="lgetdepth"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1018" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1019" REL="I2" TITLE="query"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1020" REL="I3" TITLE="lgetdepth"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1021" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1022" REL="I2" TITLE="viewport"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1023" REL="I3" TITLE="getting clipping plane distances"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A318C9e45"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1524108ceb"></A>Gets the distance of the near and far clipping planes.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C126a"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1524261ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1524367ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A318C9e48"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A318C9e49"></A><B>void lgetdepth(Int32 *</B><A HREF="lgetdepth.html#wm412e0marj"><I>near</I></A><B>, Int32</B> <B>*</B><A HREF="lgetdepth.html#Cn41c0marj"><I>far</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010b70"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010b71"></A><B>SUBROUTINE LGETDE(</B><I>near</I><B>,</B> <I>far</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4</B> <I>near</I><B>,</B> <I>far</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A318C9e4c"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1524740ceb"></A>The <B>lgetdepth</B> subroutine gets the distance of the near and far clipping planes and writes them into the <A HREF="lgetdepth.html#wm412e0marj"><I>near</I></A> and <A HREF="lgetdepth.html#Cn41c0marj"><I>far</I></A> parameters. Set these distances using the <A HREF="lsetdepth.html#naR120marj"><B>lsetdepth</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9e4e"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A318C9e4f"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="wm412e0marj"></A><I>near</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies a pointer to the location into which to write the distance of the near clipping plane.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="Cn41c0marj"></A><I>far</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies a pointer to the location into which to write the distance of the far clipping plane.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015d54"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1525126ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C126d"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C126e"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C126f"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A318C9e56"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1525451ceb"></A>Setting the viewport depth range with the <A HREF="lsetdepth.html#naR120marj"><B>lsetdepth</B></A> subroutine.</P>
```

```html
<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">
<HTML>
<HEAD>

<TITLE>linesmooth Subroutine
</TITLE>
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="lgetdepth.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="linewidth.html">Next</a>  |
<A href="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="Ew1f0marj"></A>linesmooth Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1024" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1025" REL="I2" TITLE="antialiasing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1026" REL="I3" TITLE="linesmooth"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1027" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1028" REL="I2" TITLE="antialiasing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1029" REL="I3" TITLE="of lines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1030" REL="I1" TITLE="linesmooth subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912942"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1547433ceb"></A>Turns line antialiasing on and off.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A75C1164"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1547596ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1547737ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912945"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X912946"></A><B>void linesmooth(Int32 </B><A HREF="linesmooth.html#A213X912953"><I>mode</I></A><B>&nbsp;)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X91291f"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X912922"></A><B>SUBROUTINE LINESM(</B><I>mode</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>mode</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912949"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1548162ceb"></A>The <B>linesmooth</B> subroutine allows the drawing of 
antialiased lines
 in color map and RGB modes. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1548279ceb"></A>In RGB mode, the current color is blended with the contents of the frame buffer in a read-modify-write operation. That is, the new pixel color is a calculated blend of the old pixel color and the current color, based on the percentage of overlap of the line with the pixel.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1548399ceb"></A>In color map mode, the low-order 4 bits of the current color index are replaced with a value representing the pixel coverage. Therefore, a color ramp must be loaded, with the low-order 4 bits of the color ramp blending between the foreground and background colors.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1548563ceb"></A>This type of color-index antialiasing hardware design allows the user to implement one of several antialiasing algorithms. One algorithm draws monocolored lines on a multicolored background; the other draws multicolored lines on a monochrome background. Refer to the section on <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/smjaglines.html#A8k32380nita">"Smoothing Jagged Lines with Antialiasing"</A> in<I> GL3.2 Version 4 for AIX: Programming Concepts</I> for examples and further detail. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1548693ceb"></A>Only solid (nonpatterned), unit-width lines are supported. That is, for antialiased lines to be drawn correctly, set <SAMP>linewidth=1</SAMP> using the <A HREF="linewidth.html#A3mM11b0marj"><B>linewidth</B></A> subroutine, <SAMP>linestyle=0xffff</SAMP> using the <A HREF="deflinestyle.html#A143X9b1f"><B>deflinestyle</B></A> subroutine, and <SAMP>lsrepeat=1</SAMP> using the <A HREF="lsrepeat.html#DmN1110marj"><B>lsrepeat</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<OL><LI><A NAME="A5FB6F9522ttay"></A>In order for antialiased lines and points to be displayed as visually smooth, gamma correction <I>must</I> be performed. A gamma correction factor in the range of 2.4 to 2.7 is suggested. If gamma correction is not performed, lines are not displayed as smooth, but exhibit a <I>roping</I> or <I>braiding</I> effect, as if the line were composed of separate, intertwining strands. For more information on gamma-correcting antialiased lines, see <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/smjaglines.html#A8k32380nita">"Smoothing Jagged Lines with Antialiasing"</A> in<I> GL3.2 Version 4 for AIX: Programming Concepts</I>.</LI>

<LI><A NAME="A5FB6F9746ttay"></A>Only solid, single, pixel-wide lines can be antialiased, and they cannot be used in conjunction with shading processor functions such as z-buffer, light, shade, and depth cue.</LI></OL>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912952"></A>Parameter</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912953"></A><I>mode</I></TD>
<TD>  Sets line-drawing mode as follows:


<TABLE BORDER="2"><TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD COLSPAN="3"><B>Mode Constants</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>C</B></TD>

<TD><B>FORTRAN</B></TD>

<TD><B>Description</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>SML_ON</TD>

<TD>SMLON</TD>

<TD>Enables smooth lines.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>SML_OFF</TD>

<TD>SMLOFF</TD>

<TD>Disables smooth lines.</TD></TR></TABLE></TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A75C1167"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1549298ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="alias_c.html#JBm90nita"><B>alias.c</B></A> uses the <B>linesmooth</B> subroutine to draw antialiased lines. Other examples that use the <B>linesmooth</B> subroutine include the <A HREF="alias_fore_c.html#A114C19e6"><B>alias_fore.c</B></A> and <A HREF="alias_back_c.html#A114C19c9"><B>alias_back.c</B></A> example programs.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A258C01c35f"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1549484ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<OL><LI><A NAME="A258C01c360"></A>The 3-D Color Graphics Processor supports antialiased lines only in color map mode. Only solid (nonpatterned) unit width lines are supported. On this adapter, the value <SAMP>0xf</SAMP> represents maximum pixel coverage, and <SAMP>0x0</SAMP> represents minimum pixel coverage. That is, the following color ramp should be loaded:


<TABLE BORDER="2"><TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD COLSPAN="2"><B>3-D Display Graphics Processor Color Ramp</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>Low-Order </B><B>4 Bits</B></TD>

<TD><B>Ramp</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>0000</TD>

<TD>(1/16) * foreground color + (15/16) * background color</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>0001</TD>

<TD>(2/16) * foreground color + (14/16) * background color</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>0010</TD>

<TD>(3/16) * foreground color + (13/16) * background color</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD> . . . .</TD>

<TD> . . . . . .</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>1111</TD>

<TD>(16/16) * foreground color + (0/16) * background color</TD></TR></TABLE>

For the 3-D Color Graphics Processor, the appearance of the intersections of color-index-mode antialiased lines and points can be significantly improved by setting the value of the <A HREF="zsource.html#A143X96d6"><B>zsource</B></A> subroutine to ZSRC_COLOR and the value of the <A HREF="zfunction.html#A22f0MARJ"><B>zfunction</B></A> subroutine to ZF_GREATER. Refer to the subsection on <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/smjaglines.html#A8k32380nita">improving intersections</A> within <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/smjaglines.html#A8k32380nita">"Smoothing Jagged Lines with Antialiasing"</A> in<I> GL3.2 Version 4 for AIX: Programming Concepts</I> for more details.</LI>

<LI><A NAME="A258C01c361"></A>The Supergraphics Processor supports antialiased lines in RGB mode only. Only solid (nonpatterned) unit width lines are supported.</LI>

<LI><A NAME="A94C122fd"></A>The POWER Gt4 and POWER Gt4x adapters support antialiasing in both RGB and color index modes. For these adapters, RGB-mode antialiased lines are drawn significantly slower than normal lines. For these adapters, the appearance of the intersections of color-index-mode antialiased lines can be improved significantly by setting the value of the <A HREF="logicop.html#iM521a0marj"><B>logicops</B></A> subroutine to LO_MAX.</LI>

<LI><A NAME="E1B154A113ceb"></A>The 8-bit POWERstation 730 and the 8-bit POWERgraphics GTO adapter do not support the drawing of antialiased lines. The 24-bit option must be installed for antialiased line support.</LI>

<LI><A NAME="A3CFCB36947janb"></A>When anti-aliased lines and points are drawn in RGB mode, a coverage factor (alpha value) for pixels on and near the anti-aliased objects is computed. This coverage factor is used to blend the color of the anti-aliased point or line with the contents of the frame buffer. The way in which the blending occurs is controlled by the <B>blendfunctio</B>n subroutine. When rendering anti-aliased objects in RGB mode, set the blendfunction to an appropriate value.</LI>

<LI><A NAME="A3CFCB36966janb"></A>The POWERgraphics GXT1000 supports anti-aliased line rendering in both color-index and RGB rendering modes. </LI></OL>

<H3><A NAME="A213X91293b"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A75C1169"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A75C116a"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A258C01c367"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B154A522ceb"></A>Specifying antialiasing of points with the <A HREF="pntsmooth.html#W3o220marj"><B>pntsmooth</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B154A648ceb"></A>Controlling the placement of point, line, and polygon vertices with the <A HREF="subpixel.html#jIZ1120marj"><B>subpixel</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B154A762ceb"></A>Smoothing Jagged Lines with <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/smjaglines.html#smjaglines.html">Antialiasing</A>, Understanding the <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/glintro.html#A8G44310marj">Hardware Used by GL</A>, Working in <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/workcolor.html#workcolor.html">Color Map and RGB Modes</A>, <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/setglattrib.html#setglattrib.html">Setting Drawing Attributes</A>.</P><hr><center>
```

```html
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A3mM11b0marj"></A>linewidth Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1031" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1032" REL="I2" TITLE="attribute"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1033" REL="I3" TITLE="linewidth"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1034" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1035" REL="I2" TITLE="linewidth"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1036" REL="I3" TITLE="specifying"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1037" REL="I1" TITLE="linewidth subroutine (GL)"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A213X912981"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B156F355ceb"></A>Specifies the linewidth.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A77C1108"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B156F507ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B156F626ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912984"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X912985"></A><B>void linewidth(Int16 </B><A HREF="linewidth.html#A213X91298c"><I>number</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A19C0e0e8"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A19C0e0e9"></A><B>SUBROUTINE LINEWI(</B><I>number</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>number</I></PRE>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A77C110b"></A><B>Note: </B>For FORTRAN users, this subroutine accepts long integer parameters (INTEGER*4) when invoked from a FORTRAN program, although it accepts short integers when invoked from a C program. The C and FORTRAN syntax shown here reflect this difference.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A213X912988"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1570091ceb"></A>The <B>linewidth</B> subroutine specifies the width of a line. The default width is one 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P06fd">pixel</A>. Wide lines are centered as nearly as possible on the infinitely thin mathematical line.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9d26"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A213X91298b"></A>Parameter</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X91298c"></A><I>number</I></TD>
<TD>  Width of the line in pixels.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X91298f"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1570446ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="prompt_c.html#A16C0c8de"><B>prompt.c</B></A> uses the <B>linewidth</B> subroutine to draw a two-pixel thick border around a prompt string.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015c7b"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1570641ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3CFCB4C307janb"></A>The POWERgraphics GXT1000 supports line widths from 1 to 255.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A77C110c"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C110d"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C110e"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912998"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1571011ceb"></A>Defining a linestyle with the <A HREF="deflinestyle.html#A143X9b1f"><B>deflinestyle</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1571138ceb"></A>Returning the current linewidth with the <A HREF="getlwidth.html#A213X91299c"><B>getlwidth</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1571266ceb"></A>Selecting a linestyle with the <A HREF="setlinestyle.html#XFM1310marj"><B>setlinestyle</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawnurbs.html#drawnurbs.html">Drawing NURBS Curves and Surfaces</A>, <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawwfcvs.html#drawwfcvs.html">Drawing Wire Frame Curves and Surface Patches</A>, <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/setglattrib.html#setglattrib.html">Setting Drawing Attributes</A>, 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/glintro.html#A8G44310marj">Understanding the Hardware Used by GL</A>, and <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawpoly.html#drawpoly.html">Drawing Rectangles, Circles, Arcs, and Polygons</A>.</P><hr><center>
```

```html
<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">
<HTML>
<HEAD>
<META HTTP-EQUIV="Content-Type" CONTENT="text/html; charset=iso-8859-1">

<TITLE>lmbind Subroutine
</TITLE>
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="linewidth.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="lmcolor.html">Next</a>  |
<A href="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="XeZ2340marj"></A>lmbind Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1038" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1039" REL="I2" TITLE="lighting"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1040" REL="I3" TITLE="lmbind"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1041" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1042" REL="I2" TITLE="lighting model, light source, or material"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1043" REL="I3" TITLE="binding"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1044" REL="I1" TITLE="lmbind subroutine (GL)"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A213X911dff"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1596893ceb"></A>Makes a material, light, or lighting model definition active.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C12cd"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1597053ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1597161ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911e02"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X911e03"></A><B>void lmbind(Int16 </B><A HREF="lmbind.html#QOa2300marj"><I>target</I></A><B>, Int32 </B><A HREF="lmbind.html#A5Oa2e0marj"><I>index</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911dde"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X911de1"></A><B>SUBROUTINE LMBIND(</B><I>target</I><B>, </B><I>index</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>target</I><B>,</B><I> index</I></PRE>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A78C12d0"></A><B>Note: </B>For FORTRAN users, this subroutine accepts long integer parameters (INTEGER*4) when invoked from a FORTRAN program, although it accepts short integers when invoked from a C program. The C and FORTRAN syntax shown here reflect this difference.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A213X911e06"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1597612ceb"></A>The <B>lmbind</B> subroutine takes a previously defined material, light, or lighting model and makes it active. Up to eight lights can be active (turned on) at the same time, but only one lighting model or material can be turned on at any time. Therefore, binding a material or lighting model automatically unbinds (deactivates) the previous lighting model or material. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1597739ceb"></A>The definition of a light, lighting model, or material (created previously with the <A HREF="lmdef.html#rgZ2250marj"><B>lmdef</B></A> subroutine) is not destroyed when one of these is unbound. The definition remains and can be rebound at a later time.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><B>Notes: </B>
<OL><LI><A NAME="A213X911de4"></A>Some of the properties of the currently bound material can be changed on the fly with the <A HREF="lmcolor.html#ofZ220marj"><B>lmcolor</B></A> subroutine, which provides a highly efficient path for temporarily changing material properties. Using the <B>lmcolor</B> subroutine is much more efficient than employing a combination of the <B>lmdef</B> and <B>lmbind</B> subroutines.</LI>

<LI><A NAME="A213X911dfc"></A>Lighting cannot be turned on and does not work if the matrix mode is not set to MVIEWING. The matrix mode can be changed with the <A HREF="mmode.html#XhZ2370marj"><B>mmode</B></A> subroutine.</LI>

<LI><A NAME="A258C01c58f"></A>The operation of this subroutine for the Supergraphics Processor Subsystem is modified. (See <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/powerstation730.html#NITAXIO">"Hardware Considerations"</A> in<I> GL3.2 Version 4 for AIX: Programming Concepts</I>.)</LI></OL></BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A213X911e09"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A5Oa2e0marj"></A><I>index</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the index into the table of previously defined materials, lights, or lighting models. Created with the <A HREF="lmdef.html#rgZ2250marj"><B>lmdef</B></A> subroutine.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="QOa2300marj"></A><I>target</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the target of the bind. There are 10 valid constants tokens that can be used for this parameter:


<TABLE BORDER="2"><TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD COLSPAN="2"><B>Constants</B></TD>

<TD><BR></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>C</B></TD>

<TD><B>FORTRAN</B></TD>

<TD><B>Description</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>MATERIAL</TD>

<TD>MATERI</TD>

<TD>Indicates that the material definition passed by the <I>index</I> parameter should become the currently active material. Lighting can be turned off by binding index 0 to a material.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>LIGHT0, LIGHT1, LIGHT2, LIGHT3, LIGHT4, LIGHT5, LIGHT6, LIGHT7</TD>

<TD>LIGHT0, LIGHT1, LIGHT2, LIGHT3, LIGHT4, LIGHT5, LIGHT6, LIGHT7</TD>

<TD>Indicate that the light definition passed by the <I>index</I> parameter should be bound to the respective light. Each light is distinct from the others and can be on or off. A light can be turned off by binding index 0 to it.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>LMODEL</TD>

<TD>LMODEL</TD>

<TD>Indicates that the lighting model definition passed by the <I>index</I> parameter is the current lighting model. There can be only one current lighting model.</TD></TR></TABLE></TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A30C010ff0"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1598406ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="cylinder2_c.html#A16C0c87c"><B>cylinder2.c</B></A> uses the <B>lmbind</B> subroutine to use the materials, lights, and lighting model defined with the <A HREF="lmdef.html#rgZ2250marj"><B>lmdef</B></A> subroutine. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015ce4"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1598586ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3CFCB71056janb"></A>Materials with different material properties on each side are now supported on the Gt4 class of graphics adapters and the GXT1000. Support for two-sided lighting is accomplished with the following token:</P>

<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A3CFCB71067janb"></A><B>Target</B></TD>
<TD>  BACKMATERIAL</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A3CFCB71079janb"></A><B>Function</B></TD>
<TD>  Indicates that the material definition passed by the index parameter should be used as the active material for back-facing polygons. Two-sided lighting must be enabled in order for this material definition to be used. </TD></TR></TABLE>

<P><A NAME="A3CFCB71097janb"></A>If two-sided lighting is enabled, and BACKMATERIAL is bound to a non-zero index, then the BACKMATERIAL properties are used for back-facing polygons, and MATERIAL properties are used for front-facing polygons. If two-sided lighting is enabled, and a zero index is bound to BACKMATERIAL, then the MATERIAL properties are used for both sides. If two-sided lighting is disabled, the material bound to BACKMATERIAL is not used.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3CFCB71110janb"></A>Two-sided lighting applies only to polygons and triangles; it does not apply to points, lines and characters, where only the MATERIAL properties are used.</P>

<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A3CFCB71121janb"></A><B>Target</B></TD>
<TD>  LIGHT0</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A3CFCB71132janb"></A><B>Function</B></TD>
<TD>  The light position is transformed by the current matrix at the time the the light is bound. That is, the actual position that the light will have in world coordinates is determined by its defined position and the current matrix when it is bound. Subsequent changes to the matrix do not affect the light position. The position value stored in the light definition (as defined with the <B>lmdef</B> subroutine) is not affected or changed.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A3CFCB71143janb"></A><B>Description</B></TD>
<TD>  Lighting is disabled when index 0 (zero) is bound to either the MATERIAL or to the LMODEL (or both). Both the material and the lighting model must be bound to a non-zero index for lighting to be enabled. Even if all lights are off, lighting is still enabled, although only the emmisive material properties contribute to the lit color.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A3CFCB71154janb"></A><B>Note: </B>If a light does not appear to be in the correct location, be sure that the current matrix had an appropriate value when the light was bound. The light position is transformed by the current matrix when the light is bound.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A78C12d1"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C12d2"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C12d3"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911e18"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1598930ceb"></A>Specifying RGBA colors with a single packed 32-bit integer using the <A HREF="cpack.html#A143X9284"><B>cpack</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1599043ceb"></A>Changing the target of the color commands with the <A HREF="lmcolor.html#ofZ220marj"><B>lmcolor</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1599164ceb"></A>Making a new material, light source, or lighting model active with the <A HREF="lmdef.html#rgZ2250marj"><B>lmdef</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1599286ceb"></A>Setting the current matrix mode with the <A HREF="mmode.html#XhZ2370marj"><B>mmode</B></A> subroutine. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1599404ceb"></A>Specifying a normal vector with the <A HREF="n3f.html#A139X91ef3"><B>n3f</B></A> subroutine. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1599514ceb"></A>Updating the current normal vector with the <A HREF="normal.html#A142X9b7"><B>normal</B></A> subroutine. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1599716ceb"></A>Setting the current color in RGB mode with the <A HREF="RGBcolor.html#A143X9394"><B>RGBcolor</B></A> subroutine. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1599824ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A>, Creating <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/crlighteff.html#crlighteff.html">Lighting Effects</A>, and Setting <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/setglpipeops.html#setglpipeops.html">Pipeline Options</A>.</P><hr><center>
```

```html
<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">
<HTML>

<META HTTP-EQUIV="Content-Type" CONTENT="text/html; charset=iso-8859-1">

<TITLE>lmcolor Subroutine
</TITLE>
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="lmbind.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="lmdef.html">Next</a>  |
<A href="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="ofZ220marj"></A>lmcolor Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1045" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1046" REL="I2" TITLE="lighting"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1047" REL="I3" TITLE="lmcolor"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1048" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1049" REL="I2" TITLE="color commands"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1050" REL="I3" TITLE="changing target of"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1051" REL="I1" TITLE="lmcolor subroutine (GL)"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A213X911e80"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B15C2702ceb"></A>Changes the target of the color commands while lighting is active.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C12d4"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B15C2851ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B15C2958ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911e83"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X911e84"></A><B>void lmcolor(Int32 </B><A HREF="lmcolor.html#K2b2350marj"><I>mode</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010a54"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010a55"></A><B>SUBROUTINE LMCOLO(</B><I>mode</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>mode</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911e87"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B15C3324ceb"></A>The <B>lmcolor</B> subroutine changes the target of the RGB color subroutines while lighting is active.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B15C3436ceb"></A>Properties of the currently bound material can be changed by calls to the <A HREF="lmdef.html#rgZ2250marj"><B>lmdef</B></A> subroutine, but that subroutine is relatively slow to execute. The <B>lmcolor</B> subroutine is provided to support fast and efficient changes to the current material as maintained in the graphics hardware without changing the definition of the currently bound material. Changes made by the <B>lmcolor</B> subroutine are lost when a new material is bound. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B15C3544ceb"></A>The standard RGB color subroutines (<A HREF="RGBcolor.html#A143X9394"><B>RGBcolor</B></A>, <A HREF="c.html#A143X9262"><B>c</B></A>, <A HREF="cpack.html#A143X9284"><B>cpack</B></A>) are used to change material properties efficiently. The <B>lmcolor </B>subroutine specifies which material property is to be affected by these subroutines. Because the <B>lmcolor</B> subroutine is effective only when lighting is active, the standard color subroutines are used to change the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A3C0F2A3323mhay">current color</A> when lighting is off.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A258C01c594"></A><B>Note: </B>The operation of this subroutine for the Supergraphics Processor Subsystem is modified. (See "<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/powerstation730.html#NITAXIO">Hardware Considerations</A>".)</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A213X911e8c"></A>Parameter</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="K2b2350marj"></A><I>mode</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the name of the mode to be used in conjunction with RGB color subroutines. Possible modes are: 


<TABLE BORDER="2"><TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD COLSPAN="2"><B>Mode Constants</B></TD>

<TD><BR></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>C</B></TD>

<TD><B>FORTRAN</B></TD>

<TD><B>Description</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>LMC_COLOR</TD>

<TD>LMCCOL</TD>

<TD>Color subroutines set the current color. If a color is the last thing sent before a vertex, the vertex will be colored. If a normal is the last thing sent before a vertex, the vertex is lighted. <B>LMC_COLOR </B>is the default mode. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>LMC_EMISSION</TD>

<TD>LMCEMI</TD>

<TD>Color subroutines set the current EMISSION color property of the current material. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>LMC_AMBIENT</TD>

<TD>LMCAMB</TD>

<TD>Color subroutines set the current AMBIENT color property of the current material. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>LMC_DIFFUSE</TD>

<TD>LMCDIF</TD>

<TD>Color subroutines set the current DIFFUSE color property of the current material. Alpha, the fourth color component specified by RGB color subroutines, sets the ALPHA property of the current material.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>LMC_SPECULAR</TD>

<TD>LMCSPE</TD>

<TD>Color subroutines set the current SPECULAR color property of the current material.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>LMC_AD</TD>

<TD>LMCAD</TD>

<TD>Color subroutines set the current DIFFUSE and AMBIENT color properties of the current material. Alpha, the fourth color component specified by RGB color subroutines, sets the ALPHA property of the current material.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>LMC_NULL</TD>

<TD>LMCNUL</TD>

<TD>RGB subroutines are ignored.</TD></TR></TABLE></TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015cea"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B15C3992ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C12d7"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C12d8"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C12d9"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911e9e"></A>Related Information</H3>
```

```html
</TITLE>
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="lmcolor.html">Previous</a>  |
```
