```html
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="DmN1110marj"></A>lsrepeat Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1113" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1114" REL="I2" TITLE="attribute"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1115" REL="I3" TITLE="lsrepeat"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1116" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1117" REL="I2" TITLE="linestyle repeat"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1118" REL="I3" TITLE="setting"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1119" REL="I1" TITLE="lsrepeat subroutine (GL)"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A213X9129dc"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B176D918ceb"></A>Sets the repeat factor for the current linestyle.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A77C110f"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B176E088ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B176E210ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X9129df"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X9129e0"></A><B>void lsrepeat(Int32</B> <A HREF="lsrepeat.html#A213X9129e8"><I>factor</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A19C0e0ea"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A26C0fdef"></A><B>SUBROUTINE LSREPE(</B><I>factor</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>factor</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X9129e3"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B176E935ceb"></A>The <B>lsrepeat</B> subroutine sets the repeat factor for the current 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A172P1436">linestyle</A>.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B176F065ceb"></A>This subroutine is used to create linestyles that are longer than 16 bits by multiplying each bit in the pattern by the value of the <A HREF="lsrepeat.html#A213X9129e8"><I>factor</I></A> parameter. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B176F188ceb"></A>Each bit in the pattern is multiplied successively. For example, if the line pattern is <SAMP>0000000111111111&nbsp;</SAMP>and the <I>factor </I>parameter equals <SAMP>3</SAMP>, the resulting linestyle is <SAMP>27</SAMP> bits on followed by <SAMP>21</SAMP> bits off. Line patterns start from the least significant bit.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B176F323ceb"></A>When a line is drawn, pixels are turned on if there is a 1 (one) in the corresponding position of the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A172P1436">linestyle</A> mask and turned off if there is a 0 (zero) in the corresponding position. The valid range of the repeat factor is from 1 to 255. </P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A258C01c3ad"></A><B>Note: </B>The operation of this subroutine for the Supergraphics Processor Subsystem is modified. (See <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/powerstation730.html#NITAXIO">"Hardware Considerations"</A> in<I> GL3.2 Version 4 for AIX: Programming Concepts</I>.) </BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A213X9129e7"></A>Parameter</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X9129e8"></A><I>factor</I></TD>
<TD>  Multiplier of the linestyle pattern.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015c7d"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B176F709ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B176F820ceb"></A>On the POWER Gt4 and POWER Gt4x adapters, the valid range for the repeat factor is from 1 to 64.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B176F930ceb"></A>On the POWERstation 730 and POWERgraphics GTO, linestyle repeat factors must be a multiple of 4. The valid range is from 4 to 252 in multiples of 4 with a lowest possible repeat factor of 4. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1770041ceb"></A>On the Supergraphics Processor Subsystem, the valid range for the repeat factor is 4 to 252 in multiples of 4. Any other value specified is rounded to the nearest multiple of 4.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1771192ceb"></A>On the POWER GXT1000, the valid range for the repeat factor is 1 to 255.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A77C1112"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C1113"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C1114"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X9129f4"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1B1771853ceb"></A>Defining a linestyle with the <A HREF="deflinestyle.html#A143X9b1f"><B>deflinestyle</B></A> subroutine. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1771981ceb"></A>Returning the linestyle repeat count with the <A HREF="getlsrepeat.html#A143X9ba7"><B>getlsrepeat</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1772097ceb"></A>Selecting a linestyle with the <A HREF="setlinestyle.html#XFM1310marj"><B>setlinestyle</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1B1772209ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A>, <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawbeg-end.html">Drawing with Begin-End Style Subroutines</A>, <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/move-draw.html">Drawing with Move-Draw Style Subroutines</A>, <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawnurbs.html#drawnurbs.html">Drawing NURBS Curves and Surfaces</A>, <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawwfcvs.html#drawwfcvs.html">Drawing Wire Frame Curves and Surface Patches</A>, 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/setglattrib.html#setglattrib.html">Setting Drawing Attributes</A>, <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/glintro.html#A8G44310marj">Understanding the Hardware Used by GL</A>, and <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawpoly.html#drawpoly.html">Drawing Rectangles, Circles, Arcs, and Polygons</A>.</P><hr><center>
```

```html
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A142X912d"></A>makeobj Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1120" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1121" REL="I2" TITLE="object (display list)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1122" REL="I3" TITLE="makeobj"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1123" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1124" REL="I2" TITLE="object (display list)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1125" REL="I3" TITLE="creating"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1126" REL="I1" TITLE="makeobj subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A142X912f"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F26498ceb"></A>Creates an object (display list).</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C151"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F26537ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F26561ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A142X9133"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A142X9134"></A><B>void makeobj(Int32 </B><A HREF="makeobj.html#A142X9138"><I>object</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010a5a"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010a5b"></A><B>SUBROUTINE MAKEOB(</B><I>object</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>object</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A142X9135"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F26674ceb"></A>The <B>makeobj</B> subroutine creates and names a new 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A> (object). If the <A HREF="makeobj.html#A142X9138"><I>object</I></A> parameter is the number of an existing object, the contents of that object are deleted. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F26700ceb"></A>When the <B>makeobj</B> subroutine executes, the object number is entered into a symbol table and memory is allocated for a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>. Subsequent graphics routines are then compiled into the display list instead of executing. Compilation continues until the <A HREF="closeobj.html#A142X915b"><B>closeobj</B></A> subroutine is called.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><B>Notes: </B>
<OL><LI><A NAME="A55C014c4d"></A>This editing subroutine itself cannot be added to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>. </LI>

<LI><A NAME="A139X91ed6"></A>The <B>makeobj</B> subroutine cannot be called within an object; that is, an existing object cannot be used to create a new object.</LI></OL></BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A142X9137"></A>Parameter</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A142X9138"></A><I>object</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the numeric identifier for the object being defined.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A30C010ff4"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F26832ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="depthcue_c.html#A16C0c8ff"><B>depthcue.c</B></A> uses the <B>makeobj</B> subroutine to specify the beginning of a display list defining a graphical object. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015cec"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F26875ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C154"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C155"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C156"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A142X914d"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F26972ceb"></A>Drawing an instance of an object with the <A HREF="callobj.html#A142X91c8"><B>callobj</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F26999ceb"></A>Specifying the amount of memory allocated for an object with the <A HREF="chunksize.html#A142X9c38"><B>chunksize</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F27024ceb"></A>Closing an object with the <A HREF="closeobj.html#A142X915b"><B>closeobj</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F27050ceb"></A>Opening an object for editing with the <A HREF="editobj.html#A142X9360"><B>editobj</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F27075ceb"></A>Returning a unique integer for use as an object identifier with the <A HREF="genobj.html#A142X91ea"><B>genobj</B></A> subroutine. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F27101ceb"></A>Establishing the uniqueness of an object number with the <A HREF="isobj.html#A142X920c"><B>isobj</B></A> subroutine. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F27127ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A> and Creating <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/workobjects.html#workobjects.html">Objects (Display Lists)</A>.</P><hr><center>
```

```html
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A142X942c"></A>maketag Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1127" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1128" REL="I2" TITLE="object (display list)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1129" REL="I3" TITLE="maketag"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1130" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1131" REL="I2" TITLE="object (display list)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1132" REL="I3" TITLE="inserting marker tag into"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1133" REL="I1" TITLE="maketag subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A142X942e"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F34967ceb"></A>Inserts a marker tag into a display list.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C157"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F35012ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F35040ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A142X9432"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A142X9433"></A><B>void maketag(Int32 </B><A HREF="maketag.html#A142X9437"><I>tag</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010a69"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010a6a"></A><B>SUBROUTINE MAKETA(</B><I>tag</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>tag</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A142X9434"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F35152ceb"></A>The <B>maketag</B> subroutine inserts a marker, or tag, at the current editing location of the currently open 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>. The current editing position is usually at the end of the display list, if the display list was recently opened with the <A HREF="makeobj.html#A142X912d"><B>makeobj</B></A> subroutine or <A HREF="editobj.html#A142X9360"><B>editobj</B></A> subroutine. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F35177ceb"></A>The current position can be maneuvered with the <A HREF="objdelete.html#A142X9afd"><B>objdelete</B></A>, <A HREF="objinsert.html#A142X9adb"><B>objinsert</B></A>, and <A HREF="objreplace.html#A142X9b50"><B>objreplace</B></A> subroutines. Tags can be used to help in the maneuvering through and editing of display lists.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F35204ceb"></A>There are two predefined tags, <SAMP>STARTTAG</SAMP> and <SAMP>ENDTAG</SAMP>, which mark the beginning and end of the display list. Tags should be unique within a single object; however, there is no restriction regarding uniqueness across different objects. Unique tags can be generated with the <A HREF="gentag.html#A48x2120marj"><B>gentag</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A31C011285"></A><B>Note: </B>This editing subroutine itself cannot be added to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A142X9436"></A>Parameter</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A142X9437"></A><I>tag</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies a 31-bit numeric identifier assigned to a routine in the display list.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015cf2"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F35305ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C15a"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C15b"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C15c"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A142X944c"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F35403ceb"></A>Deleting tags from a display list with the <A HREF="deltag.html#A1N61210marj"><B>deltag</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F35429ceb"></A>Returning a unique integer for use as a tag number with the <A HREF="gentag.html#A48x2120marj"><B>gentag</B></A> subroutine. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F35454ceb"></A>Establishing the uniqueness of a tag number with the <A HREF="istag.html#JXw220marj"><B>istag</B></A> subroutine. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F35480ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A> and Creating <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/workobjects.html#workobjects.html">Objects (Display Lists)</A>.</P><hr><center>
```

```html
<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">

</TITLE>
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>

<A href="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>

<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A146X9535"></A>mapcolor Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1134" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1135" REL="I2" TITLE="color map and RGB mode"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1136" REL="I3" TITLE="mapcolor"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1137" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1138" REL="I2" TITLE="color map entry"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1139" REL="I3" TITLE="changing to RGB value"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1140" REL="I1" TITLE="mapcolor subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A146X9537"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F42470ceb"></A>Changes a color map entry to a specified RGB value.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C14d"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F42509ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F42534ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A146X953a"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A146X953b"></A><B>void mapcolor</B>
<B>(Colorindex </B><A HREF="mapcolor.html#A146X9546"><I>index</I></A><B>,</B>
<B>Int16</B> <A HREF="mapcolor.html#A146X9547"><I>red</I></A><B>, Int16</B> <A HREF="mapcolor.html#A146X9548"><I>green</I></A><B>, Int16</B> <A HREF="mapcolor.html#A146X9549"><I>blue</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A146X9512"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A146X9515"></A><B>SUBROUTINE MAPCOL (</B><I>index</I><B>,</B> <I>red</I><B>,</B> <I>green</I><B>,</B> <I>blue</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>index</I><B>, </B><I>red</I><B>, </B><I>green</I><B>, </B><I>blue</I></PRE>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A78C150"></A><B>Note: </B>For FORTRAN users: this subroutine accepts long integer parameters (INTEGER*4) when invoked from a FORTRAN program, although it accepts short integers when invoked from a C program. The C and FORTRAN syntax shown here reflect this difference.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A146X953e"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F42672ceb"></A>The <B>mapcolor</B> subroutine changes a single color map entry for the current drawing mode to a specified 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A255B9de">RGB value</A>. The <A HREF="mapcolor.html#A146X9546"><I>index</I></A> parameter loads the color map entry that corresponds with the specified RGB intensities. The valid range for the <I>index</I> parameter depends on the drawing mode:</P>

<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A146X950a"></A>NORMALDRAW</TD>
<TD>  0 to 4095, or 0 to 255 if the system has only eight color bitplanes or is in multimap mode. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X910d91"></A>OVERDRAW</TD>
<TD>  1 to 3 if the <B>overlay(2) </B>subroutine has been called, or 1 to 15 if the  <B>overlay(4) </B>subroutine has been called. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X910d92"></A>UNDERDRAW</TD>
<TD>  0 to 3 if the <B>underlay(2) </B>subroutine has been called, or 0 to 15 if the <B>underlay(4) </B>subroutine has been called. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X910d93"></A>PUPDRAW</TD>
<TD>  1 to 3.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X910d94"></A>CURSORDRAW</TD>
<TD>  1 to 3.  </TD></TR></TABLE>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F42789ceb"></A>In <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/workcolor.html#a3P1390marj">multimap mode</A>, the <B>mapcolor </B>subroutine updates only the small color map currently selected by the <A HREF="setmap.html#A146X9646"><B>setmap</B></A> subroutine. The system ignores invalid indexes.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F42815ceb"></A>On most systems, this subroutine does not set the current drawing color, and so should not be used for this purpose. To set the current drawing color, use the  <A HREF="c.html#A143X9262"><B>c</B></A>, <A HREF="color.html#A146X9429"><B>color</B></A>, <A HREF="cpack.html#A143X9284"><B>cpack</B></A>, or <A HREF="RGBcolor.html#A143X9394"><B>RGBcolor</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F42845ceb"></A>Instead of the <B>mapcolor</B> subroutine, it is suggested that you use the <B>mapcolors</B> subroutine for new development, because of its significantly improved performance.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9cbd"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A146X9545"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A146X9546"></A><I>index</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the index into the color map.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A146X9547"></A><I>red</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the intensity of red associated with the index.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A146X9548"></A><I>green</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the intensity of green associated with the index.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A146X9549"></A><I>blue</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the intensity of blue associated with the index.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A146X954c"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F43004ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="colored_c.html"><B>colored.c</B></A> uses the <B>mapcolor</B> subroutine to edit the color map.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A64C016560"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F43048ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature. </P>

<P><A NAME="A3CFCCE1600janb"></A>The POWERgraphics GXT1000 supports a 12-bit colorindex frame buffer.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C151"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C152"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C153"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A146X955c"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F43149ceb"></A>Choosing a set of bitplanes for drawing with the <A HREF="drawmode.html#A143X9460"><B>drawmode</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F43175ceb"></A>Defining a color map ramp for gamma correction with the <A HREF="gammaramp.html#Kz4nita"><B>gammaramp</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F43200ceb"></A>Getting a copy of the RGB values for a color map entry with the <A HREF="getmcolor.html#nXI1100marj"><B>getmcolor</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F43226ceb"></A>Organizing the color map as one large map with the <A HREF="onemap.html#A146X95ef"><B>onemap</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F43252ceb"></A>Organizing the color map as 16 small maps with the <A HREF="multimap.html#A146X9593"><B>multimap</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F43278ceb"></A>Setting the number of bitplanes used for overlay colors with the <A HREF="overlay.html#A143X950a"><B>overlay</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F43303ceb"></A>Selecting one of 16 small color maps with the <A HREF="setmap.html#A146X9646"><B>setmap</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F43329ceb"></A>Setting the number of bitplanes used for underlay colors with the <A HREF="underlay.html#Az5O370nita"><B>underlay</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F43354ceb"></A>Working in <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/workcolor.html#workcolor.html">Color Map and RGB Modes</A>.</P><hr><center>
[  <a href="maketag.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="mapcolors.html">Next</a>  |
<A href="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
</center></BODY>

</HTML>
```

```html
<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>

<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="cv2170marj"></A>mapcolors Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1141" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1142" REL="I2" TITLE="color map and RGB mode"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1143" REL="I3" TITLE="mapcolors"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1144" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1145" REL="I2" TITLE="color map entries"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1146" REL="I3" TITLE="loading a range of"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1147" REL="I1" TITLE="mapcolors subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A58C0153d5"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F50276ceb"></A>Loads a range of the color map.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A74C1150"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F50316ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F50341ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A58C0153d9"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F50383ceb"></A><B>void mapcolors(Int16 </B><A HREF="mapcolors.html#DS2290marj"><I>start_idx</I></A><B>, Int16</B> <A HREF="mapcolors.html#ST250marj"><I>end_idx</I></A><B>, Int16</B> <A HREF="mapcolors.html#U2b0marj"><I>r</I></A><B>&nbsp;[&nbsp;], Int16</B> <A HREF="mapcolors.html#cV2b0marj"><I>g</I></A><B>&nbsp;[&nbsp;], Int16</B> <A HREF="mapcolors.html#yV210marj"><I>b</I></A><B>&nbsp;[&nbsp;]&nbsp;)</B></P>

<H3><A NAME="A58C0153db"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A58C0153dc"></A><B>SUBROUTINE MAPCOLORS (</B><I>start_idx</I><B>,</B> <I>end_idx</I><B>,</B> <I>r</I><B>,</B> <I>g</I><B>,</B> <I>b</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>start_idx</I><B>, </B><I>end_idx</I>
<B>INTEGER*2</B><I> r</I><B>(</B><I>1</I><B>), </B><I>g</I><B>(</B><I>1</I><B>), </B><I>b</I><B>(</B><I>1</I><B>)</B></PRE>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A74C1153"></A><B>Note: </B>For FORTRAN users, this subroutine accepts long integer parameters (INTEGER*4) when invoked from a FORTRAN program, although it accepts short integers when invoked from a C program. The C and FORTRAN syntax shown here reflect this difference.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A58C0153dd"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F50512ceb"></A>The <B>mapcolors</B> subroutine loads a range of color map table entries. The range that is loaded begins with <A HREF="mapcolors.html#DS2290marj"><I>start_idx</I></A> and ends with <A HREF="mapcolors.html#ST250marj"><I>end_idx</I></A>, inclusive. The length of the array must be equal to <I>end_idx</I> - <I>start_idx</I> + 1. For instance to load only one color map entry, set <I>start_idx</I> and <I>end_idx</I> to the same number. To load two entries, set <I>end_idx</I> to <I>start_idx</I> + 1.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F50538ceb"></A>The <B>mapcolors</B> subroutine is functionally equivalent to the C code shown in the following fragment, although it will execute considerably faster.</P>
<PRE><A NAME="A58C0153df"></A>&nbsp;{
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;int&nbsp;i;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;for&nbsp;(i=0;&nbsp;i&lt;&nbsp;(end_idx&nbsp;-&nbsp;start_idx&nbsp;+&nbsp;1);&nbsp;i++)
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;mapcolor&nbsp;(start_idx+i,&nbsp;r[i],g[i],b[i]);
&nbsp;}</PRE>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F50588ceb"></A>The <B>mapcolors</B> subroutine can be used to load the underlay, overlay, cursor, popup, or main frame buffer color map. Which map is loaded depends on the current drawing mode (as set by the <A HREF="drawmode.html#A143X9460"><B>drawmode</B></A> subroutine).</P>

<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A58C0153e1"></A>NORMALDRAW</TD>
<TD>  0 to 4095, or 0 to 255 if the system has only eight color bitplanes or is in multimap mode. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A58C0153e2"></A>OVERDRAW</TD>
<TD>  1 to 3 if the <B>overlay(2) </B>subroutine has been called, or 1 to 15 if the  <B>overlay(4) </B>subroutine has been called. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A58C0153e3"></A>UNDERDRAW</TD>
<TD>  0 to 3 if the <B>underlay(2) </B>subroutine has been called, or 0 to 15 if the <B>underlay(4) </B>subroutine has been called. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A58C0153e4"></A>PUPDRAW</TD>
<TD>  1 to 3.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A58C0153e5"></A>CURSORDRAW</TD>
<TD>  1 to 3.  </TD></TR></TABLE>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F50738ceb"></A>In <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/workcolor.html#a3P1390marj">multimap mode</A>, the <B>mapcolors </B>subroutine updates only the small color map currently selected by the <A HREF="setmap.html#A146X9646"><B>setmap</B></A> subroutine. The system ignores invalid indexes.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A58C0153e7"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A58C0153e8"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="DS2290marj"></A><I>start_idx</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the starting index in the color map to be loaded.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="ST250marj"></A><I>end_idx</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the ending index in the color map to be loaded.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="U2b0marj"></A><I>r</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies an array containing the intensity of the red component.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="cV2b0marj"></A><I>g</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies an array containing the intensity of the green component.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="yV210marj"></A><I>b</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies an array containing the intensity of the blue component.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A64C016564"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F51027ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature. </P>

<P><A NAME="A3CFCCF6041janb"></A>The POWERgraphics GXT1000 supports a 12-bit colorindex frame buffer.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A74C1154"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A74C1155"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A74C1156"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A58C0153ed"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F51204ceb"></A>Choosing a set of bitplanes for drawing with the <A HREF="drawmode.html#A143X9460"><B>drawmode</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F51246ceb"></A>Defining a color map ramp for gamma correction with the <A HREF="gammaramp.html#Kz4nita"><B>gammaramp</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F51299ceb"></A>Getting a range of color map RGB entries with the <A HREF="getmcolors.html#UI2f0marj"><B>getmcolors</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F51339ceb"></A>Organizing the color map as one large map with the <A HREF="onemap.html#A146X95ef"><B>onemap</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F51414ceb"></A>Organizing the color map as 16 small maps with the <A HREF="multimap.html#A146X9593"><B>multimap</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F51445ceb"></A>Setting the number of bitplanes used for overlay colors with the <A HREF="overlay.html#A143X950a"><B>overlay</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F51470ceb"></A>Selecting one of 16 small color maps with the <A HREF="setmap.html#A146X9646"><B>setmap</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F51496ceb"></A>Setting the number of bitplanes used for underlay colors with the <A HREF="underlay.html#Az5O370nita"><B>underlay</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F51521ceb"></A>Working in <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/workcolor.html#workcolor.html">Color Map and RGB Modes</A>.</P><hr><center>
```

```html
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>

<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A213X9119fe"></A>mapw Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1148" REL="I1" TITLE="mapw subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1149" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1150" REL="I2" TITLE="picking and selecting"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1151" REL="I3" TITLE="screen coordinates to modeling coordinates"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1152" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1153" REL="I2" TITLE="picking and selecting"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1154" REL="I3" TITLE="mapw"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1155" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1156" REL="I2" TITLE="coordinate transformation"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1157" REL="I3" TITLE="mapw"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911a00"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F61742ceb"></A>Computes the inverse mapping from screen coordinates to modeling coordinates.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C15d"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F61782ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F61806ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911a03"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X911a04"></A><B>void mapw</B>
<B>(Int32 </B><A HREF="mapw.html#A213X911a0d"><I>viewobj</I></A><B>, </B>
<B>Screencoord</B> <A HREF="mapw.html#A213X911a0b"><I>screenx</I></A><B>, Screencoord</B> <A HREF="mapw.html#A213X911a0c"><I>screeny</I></A><B>, </B>
<B>Coord *</B><A HREF="mapw.html#A213X911a0e"><I>modelx1</I></A><B>, Coord *</B><A HREF="mapw.html#A213X911a0f"><I>modely1</I></A><B>, Coord *</B><A HREF="mapw.html#A213X911a10"><I>modelz1</I></A><B>, </B>
<B>Coord *</B><A HREF="mapw.html#A213X911a11"><I>modelx2</I></A><B>, Coord *</B><A HREF="mapw.html#A213X911a12"><I>modely2</I></A><B>, Coord *</B> <A HREF="mapw.html#A213X911a13"><I>modelz2</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X9119dc"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F61884ceb"></A><B>SUBROUTINE MAPW(</B><I>viewobj</I><B>, </B><I>screenx</I><B>, </B><I>screeny</I><B>, </B><I>modelx1</I><B>, </B><I>modely1</I><B>, </B><I>modelz1</I><B>, </B><I>modelx2</I><B>, </B><I>modely2</I><B>, </B><I>modelz2</I><B>)</B></P>

<P><B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>viewobj</I><B>,</B><I> screenx</I><B>, </B><I>screeny</I></P>

<P><B>REAL </B><I>modelx1</I><B>, </B><I>modely1</I><B>, </B><I>modelz1</I><B>, </B><I>modelx2</I><B>, </B><I>modely2</I><B>, </B><I>modelz2</I> </P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A79C160"></A><B>Note: </B>For FORTRAN users, this subroutine accepts long integer parameters (INTEGER*4) when invoked from a FORTRAN program, although it accepts short integers when invoked from a C program. The C and FORTRAN syntax shown here reflect this difference.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A213X911a07"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F61949ceb"></A>The <B>mapw</B> subroutine takes a pair of 2-D 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A27P017">screen coordinates</A> and maps them into 3-D 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P06el">modeling coordinates</A>. Because the z coordinate is missing from the screen coordinate system, the point becomes a line in modeling space. The <B>mapw</B> subroutine computes the inverse mapping from the viewing object.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F61975ceb"></A>The system returns a modeling coordinate line, which is computed from the (<A HREF="mapw.html#A213X911a0b"><I>screenx</I></A><B>,</B> <A HREF="mapw.html#A213X911a0c"><I>screeny</I></A>) parameters and the <A HREF="mapw.html#A213X911a0d"><I>viewobj</I></A> parameter as two points and stored in the locations addressed by the <A HREF="mapw.html#A213X911a0e"><I>modelx1</I></A><B>,</B> <A HREF="mapw.html#A213X911a0f"><I>modely1</I></A><B>,</B> <A HREF="mapw.html#A213X911a10"><I>modelz1</I></A> parameters and the <A HREF="mapw.html#A213X911a11"><I>modelx2</I></A><B>,</B> <A HREF="mapw.html#A213X911a12"><I>modely2</I></A><B>,</B>  <A HREF="mapw.html#A213X911a13"><I>modelz2</I></A> parameters. </P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9d02"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A213X911a0a"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X911a0d"></A><I>viewobj</I><B></B></TD>
<TD>  Specifies a viewing object containing the transformations that map the current displayed objects to the screen.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X911a0b"></A><I>screenx</I><B></B></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>x</I> coordinate of the screen point to be mapped.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X911a0c"></A><I>screeny</I><B></B></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>y</I> coordinate of the screen point to be mapped.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X911a0e"></A><I>modelx1</I><B></B></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>x</I> <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A27P03d">model coordinate</A> of one endpoint of a line. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X911a0f"></A><I>modely1</I><B></B></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>y</I> model coordinate of one endpoint of a line.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X911a10"></A><I>modelz1</I><B></B></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>z</I> model coordinate of one endpoint of a line.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X911a11"></A><I>modelx2</I><B></B></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>x</I> model coordinate of the remaining endpoint of a line. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X911a12"></A><I>modely2</I><B></B></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>y</I> model coordinate of the remaining endpoint of a line. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X911a13"></A><I>modelz2</I><B></B></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>z</I> model coordinate of the remaining endpoint of a line.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015cbe"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F62226ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C161"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C162"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C163"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911a26"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F62323ceb"></A>Creating a new object in the display list with the <A HREF="makeobj.html#A142X912d"><B>makeobj</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F62348ceb"></A>Computing the inverse mapping from screen coordinates to 2-D modeling coordinates with the <A HREF="mapw2.html#A213X911a56"><B>mapw2</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F62374ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A>, <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/picknselect.html#picknselect.html">Picking and Selecting</A> Overview, and Working with <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/workcoords.html#workcoords.html">Coordinate Systems</A>.</P><hr><center>

</center></BODY>

</HTML>
```

```html
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A213X911a56"></A>mapw2 Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1158" REL="I1" TITLE="mapw2 subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1159" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1160" REL="I2" TITLE="picking and selecting"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1161" REL="I3" TITLE="screen coordinates to 2 modeling coordinates"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1162" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1163" REL="I2" TITLE="picking and selecting"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1164" REL="I3" TITLE="mapw2"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1165" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1166" REL="I2" TITLE="coordinate transformation"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1167" REL="I3" TITLE="mapw2"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911a58"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F6F148ceb"></A>Computes the inverse mapping from screen coordinates to 2-D modeling coordinates.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C164"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F6F186ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F6F210ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911a5b"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X911a5c"></A><B>void mapw2</B>
<B>(Int32 </B><A HREF="mapw2.html#A213X911a65"><I>viewobj</I></A><B>, </B>
<B>Screencoord</B> <A HREF="mapw2.html#A213X911a63"><I>screenx</I></A><B>, Screencoord</B> <A HREF="mapw2.html#A213X911a64"><I>screeny</I></A><B>, </B>
<B>Coord *</B><A HREF="mapw2.html#A213X911a66"><I>modelx</I></A><B>, Coord *</B><A HREF="mapw2.html#A213X911a67"><I>modely</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911a34"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X911a37"></A><B>SUBROUTINE MAPW2(</B><I>viewobj</I><B>, </B><I>screenx</I><B>, </B><I>screeny</I><B>, </B><I>modelx</I><B>, </B><I>modely</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>viewobj</I><B>,</B><I> screenx</I><B>, </B><I>screeny</I>
<B>REAL </B><I>modelx</I><B>, </B><I>modely</I></PRE>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A79C167"></A><B>Note: </B>For FORTRAN users, this subroutine accepts long integer parameters (INTEGER*4) when invoked from a FORTRAN program, although it accepts short integers when invoked from a C program. The C and FORTRAN syntax shown here reflect this difference.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A213X911a5f"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F6F343ceb"></A>The <B>mapw2</B> subroutine maps a point on the screen into 2-D 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P06el">modeling coordinates</A>. This subroutine is the 2-D version of the <A HREF="mapw.html#A213X9119fe"><B>mapw</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9d05"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A213X911a62"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X911a65"></A><I>viewobj</I><B></B></TD>
<TD>  Specifies a primitive containing the viewport, projection, viewing, and modeling 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A27P021">transformations</A> that define modeling space.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X911a63"></A><I>screenx</I><B></B></TD>
<TD>  Specifies a point in screen coordinates.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X911a64"></A><I>screeny</I><B></B></TD>
<TD>  Specifies a point in screen coordinates.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X911a66"></A><I>modelx</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the corresponding <I>x</I> model coordinate.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X911a67"></A><I>modely</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the corresponding <I>y</I> model coordinate.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015cc0"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F6F517ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>
```

```html
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A142X916d6"></A>maxsize Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1168" REL="I1" TITLE="maxsize subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1169" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1170" REL="I2" TITLE="window"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1171" REL="I3" TITLE="maxsize"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1172" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1173" REL="I2" TITLE="window sizes"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1174" REL="I3" TITLE="specifying maximum"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A142X916d8"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F7D159ceb"></A>Specifies the maximum size of a window.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C12ff"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F7D198ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F7D222ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912b62"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X912b63"></A><B>void maxsize(Int32 </B><A HREF="maxsize.html#kJ43d0marj"><I>x</I></A><B>, Int32 </B><A HREF="maxsize.html#AzJ43230marj"><I>y</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010c3f"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010c40"></A><B>SUBROUTINE MAXSIZ(</B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A142X916de"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F7D339ceb"></A>The <B>maxsize </B>subroutine specifies the maximum size (in pixels) of a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A13791dc4">window</A>. It is called at the beginning of a graphics program, but only takes effect when the <A HREF="winopen.html#A142X91549"><B>winopen</B></A> subroutine is called. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F7D369ceb"></A>The <B>maxsize </B>subroutine can also be called in conjunction with the <A HREF="winconstraints.html#A142X914c1"><B>winconstraints</B></A> subroutine to modify the enforced maximum size after the window is created. The default maximum size is 1280 pixels wide and 1024 pixels high. The window can be reshaped, but cannot become larger than the specified maximum size. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F7D396ceb"></A>With the <B>maxsize</B> subroutine, the programmer can prevent the user from resizing a window to a size larger than the specified size.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9f5e"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A142X916e0"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="kJ43d0marj"></A><I>x</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the maximum width in pixels of a window.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="AzJ43230marj"></A><I>y</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the maximum height in pixels of a window.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A61C0159f2"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F7D518ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1302"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1303"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1304"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A142X916f6"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F7D615ceb"></A>Specifying pixel values to be added to a window with the <A HREF="fudge.html#A142X917a6"><B>fudge</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F7D641ceb"></A>Obtaining the size of the window with the <A HREF="getsize.html#X513200marj"><B>getsize</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F7D667ceb"></A>Specifying the size of a window icon with the <A HREF="iconsize.html#LA13e0marj"><B>iconsize</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F7D692ceb"></A>Specifying the minimum size of a window with the <A HREF="minsize.html#MJ13260marj"><B>minsize</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F7D718ceb"></A>Constraining the size of a window with the <A HREF="prefsize.html#A142X91671"><B>prefsize</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F7D743ceb"></A>Specifying a window size change in discrete steps with the <A HREF="stepunit.html#A142X91bd2"><B>stepunit</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F7D768ceb"></A>Binding window constraints to the current window with the <A HREF="winconstraints.html#A142X914c1"><B>winconstraints</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F7D794ceb"></A>Creating a window with the <A HREF="winopen.html#A142X91549"><B>winopen</B></A> subroutine. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F7D819ceb"></A>Creating and Managing <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/managewinds.html#managewinds.html">Windows</A>.</P><hr><center>
```

```html
<H3><A NAME="A213X912b6b"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F8B586ceb"></A>Specifies the minimum size of a window.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1305"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F8B630ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F8B659ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912b6e"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X912b6f"></A><B>void minsize(Int32 </B><A HREF="minsize.html#Ce43290marj"><I>x</I></A><B>, Int32 </B><A HREF="minsize.html#Te4390marj"><I>y</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010c41"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010c42"></A><B>SUBROUTINE MINSIZ(</B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912b72"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F8B787ceb"></A>The <B>minsize </B>subroutine specifies the minimum size (in pixels) of a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A13791dc4">window</A>. It is called at the beginning of a graphics program, but only takes effect when the <A HREF="winopen.html#A142X91549"><B>winopen</B></A> subroutine is called. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F8B817ceb"></A>The <B>minsize </B>subroutine can also be called in conjunction with the <A HREF="winconstraints.html#A142X914c1"><B>winconstraints</B></A> subroutine to modify the enforced minimum size after the window is created. The default minimum size is 40 pixels wide and 30 pixels high. The window can be reshaped, but cannot become smaller than the specified minimum size. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F8B847ceb"></A>With the <B>minsize</B> subroutine, the programmer can prevent the user from resizing a window to a size smaller than the specified size.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9f61"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A213X912b76"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="Ce43290marj"></A><I>x</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the minimum width in pixels of a window. The lowest legal value for this parameter is 21.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="Te4390marj"></A><I>y</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the minimum height in pixels of a window. The lowest legal value for this parameter is 21.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A61C0159f4"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F8B978ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C130a"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912b7c"></A>Related Information</H3>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F8C139ceb"></A>Specifying the size of a window icon with the <A HREF="iconsize.html#LA13e0marj"><B>iconsize</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F8C168ceb"></A>Specifying the maximum size of a window with the <A HREF="maxsize.html#A142X916d6"><B>maxsize</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F8C194ceb"></A>Constraining the size of a window with the <A HREF="prefsize.html#A142X91671"><B>prefsize</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F8C223ceb"></A>Specifying a window size change in discrete steps with the <A HREF="stepunit.html#A142X91bd2"><B>stepunit</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F8C252ceb"></A>Binding window constraints to the current window with the <A HREF="winconstraints.html#A142X914c1"><B>winconstraints</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F8C279ceb"></A>Creating a window with the <A HREF="winopen.html#A142X91549"><B>winopen</B></A> subroutine. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F8C309ceb"></A>Creating and Managing <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/managewinds.html#managewinds.html">Windows</A>.</P><hr><center>
```

```html
<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">

<TITLE>mmode Subroutine
</TITLE>
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="minsize.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="move.html">Next</a>  |
<A href="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="XhZ2370marj"></A>mmode Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1182" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1183" REL="I2" TITLE="pipeline optionetting"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1184" REL="I3" TITLE="mmode"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1185" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1186" REL="I2" TITLE="matrix mode"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1187" REL="I3" TITLE="setting current"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1188" REL="I1" TITLE="mmode subroutine (GL)"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A213X911e4a"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F9B559ceb"></A>Sets the current matrix mode.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C12da"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F9B603ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F9B629ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911e4d"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X911e4e"></A><B>void mmode(Int16 </B><A HREF="mmode.html#Ysc2260marj"><I>mode</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911e29"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X911e2c"></A><B>SUBROUTINE MMODE(</B><I>mode</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>mode</I></PRE>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A78C12dd"></A><B>Note: </B>For FORTRAN users, this subroutine accepts long integer parameters (INTEGER*4) when started from a FORTRAN program, although it accepts short integers when started from a C program. The C and FORTRAN syntax shown here reflect this difference.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A213X911e51"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F9B771ceb"></A>The <B>mmode</B> subroutine sets the current matrix mode.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F9B802ceb"></A>The system is in single matrix mode after a call to the <A HREF="winopen.html#A142X91549"><B>winopen</B></A>, <A HREF="ginit.html#LDg21c0marj"><B>ginit</B></A>, or <A HREF="gbegin.html#JS4380nita"><B>gbegin</B></A> subroutines. This mode is sufficient except for lighting calculations; when performing those, use viewing matrix mode.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F9B828ceb"></A>Because the projection matrix is not stored on the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P06dd">matrix stack</A>, the projection matrix is not normally accessible. However, if you want to define your own projection matrix, put the system into projection matrix mode. You can then use the standard matrix manipulation commands to alter the projection matrix. When you are in projection matrix mode, do not use the <A HREF="pushmatrix.html#A144X9540"><B>pushmatrix</B></A> and <A HREF="popmatrix.html#A144X951e"><B>popmatrix</B></A> subroutines.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6F9B858ceb"></A>When you have finished modifying the projection matrix, return to viewing matrix mode and load a 4 by 4 identity matrix onto the matrix stack. (The standard transformation subroutines, <A HREF="rotate.html#A8g2120marj"><B>rotate</B></A>, <A HREF="rot.html#A144X9562"><B>rot</B></A>, <A HREF="translate.html#A144X95c8"><B>translate</B></A>, <A HREF="scale.html#A144X95a6"><B>scale</B></A>, <A HREF="lookat.html#A144X9452"><B>lookat</B></A>, and <A HREF="polarview.html#A144X94fc"><B>polarview</B></A>, all use matrix multiplication. Loading the identity matrix onto the matrix stack is a safe way to make sure that there is a matrix by which to multiply.)  </P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911e57"></A>Parameter</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="Ysc2260marj"></A><I>mode</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the current matrix mode to be set.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X911e58"></A></TD>
<TD>  There are three possible values for this function:


<TABLE BORDER="2"><TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>C</B></TD>

<TD><B>FORTRAN</B></TD>

<TD><B>Mode</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>MSINGLE</TD>

<TD>MSINGL</TD>

<TD>Single matrix</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>MPROJECTION</TD>

<TD>MPROJE</TD>

<TD>Projection matrix</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>MVIEWING</TD>

<TD>MVIEWI</TD>

<TD>Viewing matrix</TD></TR></TABLE></TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A30C010ff2"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F9C018ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="cylinder1_c.html#Ggi2e0marj"><B>cylinder1.c</B></A> uses the <B>mmode</B> subroutine, with MVIEWING as the value of the <I>mode</I> parameter, to specify that matrix operations manipulate only the modeling and viewing matrix (not the projection matrix). </P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015ce6"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6F9C090ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C12de"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C12df"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C12e0"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
```

```html
<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">
<HTML>
<HEAD>
<META HTTP-EQUIV="Content-Type" CONTENT="text/html; charset=iso-8859-1">

<TITLE>move  Subroutine
</TITLE>
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="mmode.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="multimap.html">Next</a>  |
<A href="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="pofmarj"></A>move  Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1189" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1190" REL="I2" TITLE="moveraw style"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1191" REL="I3" TITLE="move"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1192" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1193" REL="I2" TITLE="graphics position"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1194" REL="I3" TITLE="moving"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1195" REL="I1" TITLE="move subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912cb2"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6FAC908ceb"></A>Moves the current graphics position to a specified point.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C12f1"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6FAC950ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6FAC978ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912cb5"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X912cb6"></A><B>void move</B>
<B>(Coord </B><A HREF="move.html#A213X912cc0"><I>x</I></A><B>, Coord</B> <A HREF="move.html#A213X912cc1"><I>y</I></A><B>, Coord</B> <A HREF="move.html#A213X912cc2"><I>z</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A43c260marj"></A><B>void movei</B>
<B>(Icoord </B><A HREF="move.html#A213X912cc0"><I>x</I></A><B>, Icoord</B> <A HREF="move.html#A213X912cc1"><I>y</I></A><B>, Icoord</B> <A HREF="move.html#A213X912cc2"><I>z</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="J3c120marj"></A><B>void moves</B>
<B>(Scoord </B><A HREF="move.html#A213X912cc0"><I>x</I></A><B>, Scoord</B> <A HREF="move.html#A213X912cc1"><I>y</I></A><B>, Scoord</B> <A HREF="move.html#A213X912cc2"><I>z</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="Y3c2a0marj"></A><B>void move2</B>
<B>(Coord </B><A HREF="move.html#A213X912cc0"><I>x</I></A><B>, Coord</B> <A HREF="move.html#A213X912cc1"><I>y</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="m3c360marj"></A><B>void move2i</B>
<B>(Icoord </B><A HREF="move.html#A213X912cc0"><I>x</I></A><B>, Icoord</B> <A HREF="move.html#A213X912cc1"><I>y</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="Y4c360marj"></A><B>void move2s</B>
<B>(Scoord </B><A HREF="move.html#A213X912cc0"><I>x</I></A><B>, Scoord</B> <A HREF="move.html#A213X912cc1"><I>y</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010abf"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010ac0"></A><B>SUBROUTINE MOVE(</B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>, </B><I>z</I><B>)</B>
<B>REAL </B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>, </B><I>z</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010ac1"></A><B>SUBROUTINE MOVEI(</B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>, </B><I>z</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>, </B><I>z</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010ac2"></A><B>SUBROUTINE MOVES(</B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>, </B><I>z</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*2 </B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>, </B><I>z</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010ac3"></A><B>SUBROUTINE MOVE2(</B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>)</B>
<B>REAL </B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010ac4"></A><B>SUBROUTINE MOVE2I(</B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010ac5"></A><B>SUBROUTINE MOVE2S(</B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*2 </B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I></PRE>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A78C12f4"></A><B>Note: </B>For FORTRAN users, the INTEGER*2 versions of this subroutine, <B>MOVES</B> and <B>MOVE2S</B>, should not be called with integer constant parameters. For example, 2 is an integer constant; JJ is an integer variable. The XL FORTRAN compiler, invoked by the 

<B>xlf</B> command, stores all integer constants as long integers (INTEGER*4), not as short integers (INTEGER*2). Invoking one of the short versions of this subroutine with an integer constant will result in unexpected behavior.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A213X912cb9"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6FAD330ceb"></A>The <B>move </B>subroutine changes (without drawing) the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A25P03eb">current graphics position</A> to the point specified by the <I>x, y</I>, and <I>z</I> parameters. The graphics position is the point from which the next drawing routine starts drawing. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6FAD358ceb"></A>The value of <B>move2(</B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>) </B>is equivalent to <B>move(</B><I>x</I><B>, </B><I>y</I><B>, </B>0.0<B>)</B>. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6FAD387ceb"></A>The six different forms for the <B>move</B> subroutine are as follows:</P>

<TABLE BORDER="2"><TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><BR></TD>

<TD><B>2-D</B></TD>

<TD><B>3-D</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>Int16</TD>

<TD>move2s</TD>

<TD>moves</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>Int32</TD>

<TD>move2i</TD>

<TD>movei</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>float</TD>

<TD>move2</TD>

<TD>move</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P><A NAME="E1D6FAD435ceb"></A>The <A HREF="move.html#A213X912cb5">syntax</A> for each of the subroutine forms is the same except for the parameter types.  They differ only in that <A HREF="move.html#A213X912cb6"><B>move</B></A> expects real coordinates, <A HREF="move.html#A43c260marj"><B>movei</B></A> expects integer coordinates, and <A HREF="move.html#J3c120marj"><B>moves</B></A> expects short integer coordinates. In addition, the <A HREF="move.html#Y3c2a0marj"><B>move2</B></A>* routines assume a 2-D point instead of a 3-D point.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9dac"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A213X912cbf"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912cc0"></A><I>x</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the new <I>x</I> coordinate for the current graphics position.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912cc1"></A><I>y</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the new <I>y</I> coordinate for the current graphics position.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912cc2"></A><I>z</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the new <I>z</I> coordinate for the current graphics position.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A30C010ffc"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6FAD588ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="depthcue_c.html#A16C0c8ff"><B>depthcue.c</B></A> uses the <B>movei</B> subroutine when defining a graphical object to move the graphics position without drawing any lines. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015d16"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6FAD631ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C12f5"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C12f6"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C12f7"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912cd0"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6FAD755ceb"></A>Drawing a line with the <A HREF="draw.html#EYf2e0marj"><B>draw</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6FAD789ceb"></A>Specifying the starting point for a polygon with the <A HREF="pmv.html#A139X91eed"><B>pmv</B></A> subroutine.  </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6FAD824ceb"></A>Drawing a point with the <A HREF="pnt.html#Ptf3a0marj"><B>pnt</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6FAD866ceb"></A>Drawing a relative line with the <A HREF="rdr.html#gpf1c0marj"><B>rdr</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6FAD896ceb"></A>Moving the current graphics position to a point relative to the current point with the <A HREF="rmv.html#kzf90marj"><B>rmv</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6FAD931ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A> and Drawing with <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/move-draw.html">Move-Draw Style</A> Subroutines.</P><hr><center>
```

```html
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A146X9593"></A>multimap Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1196" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1197" REL="I2" TITLE="color map and RGB mode"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1198" REL="I3" TITLE="multimap"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1199" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1200" REL="I2" TITLE="color map"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1201" REL="I3" TITLE="organizing as 16 small maps"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1202" REL="I1" TITLE="multimap subroutine (GL)"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A146X9595"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6FBD425ceb"></A>Organizes the color map as 16 small maps.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C154"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6FBD466ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6FBD494ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A146X9598"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A146X9599"></A><B>void multimap(&nbsp;)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A146X9570"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A146X9573"></A><B>SUBROUTINE MULTIM</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A146X959c"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6FBD621ceb"></A>The <B>multimap</B> subroutine reorganizes the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A31996bc">color map</A> as 16 small independent maps. Only one of these small maps can be active, or current, at a time, and only the least significant bits in the frame buffer are passed through the current map. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6FBD657ceb"></A>On the 24-bit High-Performance 3-D Color Graphics Processor, these small maps are each 8-bit color maps having 256 entries. On the 8-bit High-Performance 3-D Color Graphics Processor, the maps are each 4-bit color maps having 16 entries.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6FBD691ceb"></A>After the <B>multimap</B> subroutine is called, the reorganization into multiple independent maps does not take effect until the <A HREF="gconfig.html#hS4260nita"><B>gconfig</B></A> subroutine is called.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><B>Notes: </B>
<OL><LI><A NAME="A258C01c42e"></A>The operation of this subroutine for the Supergraphics Processor Subsystem is modified. (See 
"<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/undergraphadapt.html#undergraphadapt.html">Understanding the Adapter</A>".) </LI>

<LI><A NAME="A258C01c42f"></A>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</LI></OL></BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A146X958d"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6FBD792ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>


<P><A NAME="E1D6FBD820ceb"></A>The POWER GXT1000 adapter does not support the <B>multimap</B> subroutine.</P>



<H3><A NAME="A78C157"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C158"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C159"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A146X95b6"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6FBD923ceb"></A>Configuring the system with the <A HREF="gconfig.html#hS4260nita"><B>gconfig</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6FBD956ceb"></A>Returning the organization of the current color map with the <A HREF="getcmmode.html#A146X948e"><B>getcmmode</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6FBD987ceb"></A>Returning the number of the current color map with the <A HREF="getmap.html#A146X94e2"><B>getmap</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6FBE012ceb"></A>Organizing the color map as one large map with the <A HREF="onemap.html#A146X95ef"><B>onemap</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6FBE045ceb"></A>Selecting one of 16 small color maps with the <A HREF="setmap.html#A146X9646"><B>setmap</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6FBE070ceb"></A>Working in 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/workcolor.html#workcolor.html">Color Map and RGB Modes</A>.</P><hr><center>
```

```html
<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">
<HTML>
<HEAD>

<TITLE>multmatrix Subroutine
</TITLE>
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="multimap.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="n3f.html">Next</a>  |
<A href="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A144X9474"></A>multmatrix Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1203" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1204" REL="I2" TITLE="coordinate transformation"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1205" REL="I3" TITLE="multmatrix"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1206" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1207" REL="I2" TITLE="matrix"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1208" REL="I3" TITLE="transformation"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1209" REL="I1" TITLE="multmatrix subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A144X9476"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6FD0510ceb"></A>Premultiplies the current transformation matrix.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C185"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6FD0560ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6FD0587ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A144X947a"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A144X947b"></A><B>void multmatrix(Matrix </B><A HREF="multmatrix.html#oPj110marj"><I>matrix</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A15C0c6e9"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A15C0c6ea"></A><B>SUBROUTINE MULTMA(</B><I>matrix</I><B>)</B>
<B>REAL </B><I>matrix</I><B>(4,4)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A144X947c"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6FD0724ceb"></A>The <B>multmatrix</B> subroutine premultiplies the current top of the transformation stack by the given matrix. If <I>T</I> is the current matrix, <B>multmatrix(M)</B> replaces <I>T</I> with <I>M</I>*<I>T</I>. If the system is in projection matrix mode (<SAMP>mmode(MPROJ);),</SAMP> the projection matrix is premultiplied.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6FD0786ceb"></A>Be sure to exit projection matrix mode before performing any drawing because drawing is not enabled while in this mode.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A258C01c454"></A><B>Note: </B>The operation of this subroutine for the Supergraphics Processor Subsystem is modified. (See 
"<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/powerstation730.html#NITAXIO">Hardware Considerations</A>".) </BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A144X947e"></A>Parameter</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="oPj110marj"></A><I>matrix</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the matrix that is to multiply the current top matrix of the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P06dd">matrix stack</A>.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A144X9484"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6FD0913ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="curve3_c.html#A16C0c81c"><B>curve3.c</B></A> calls the <B>multmatrix</B> subroutine with the control point matrix, the Bezier basis matrix, and the precision matrix to set up the transformation matrix to draw a Bezier curve.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015d2c"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6FD0966ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature. </P>
```

```html
<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">

</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>

<A href="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>

 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A139X91ef3"></A>n3f Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1210" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1211" REL="I2" TITLE="begin-end style"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1212" REL="I3" TITLE="n3f"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1213" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1214" REL="I2" TITLE="normal vector"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1215" REL="I3" TITLE="setting"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1216" REL="I1" TITLE="n3f subroutine (GL)"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A139X91ef5"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6FE2340ceb"></A>Specifies a normal vector for lighting calculations.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C113"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6FE2383ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6FE2408ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A139X91ef9"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A139X91efa"></A><B>void n3f(Float32 </B><A HREF="n3f.html#A139X91efe"><I>vector</I></A><B>&nbsp;[3]&nbsp;)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A20C0e2f1"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A61C0159d1"></A><B>SUBROUTINE N3F(</B><I>vector</I><B>)</B>
<B>REAL </B><I>vector </I><B>(3)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A139X91efb"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6FE2539ceb"></A>The <B>n3f</B> subroutine specifies the normal vector to be used for <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/lightbasics.html#A342C970d0">lighting calculations</A>.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6FE2572ceb"></A>The passed parameter (<I>vector</I>) becomes the current normal and is used when the lighting algorithm is rerun for all subsequent vertices. It is not necessary to respecify a normal if it is unchanged. For example, a single call to the 
<B>n3f </B>subroutine is sufficient for a flat-shaded polygon. 
However, the <B>n3f</B> subroutine must be called before the first vertex subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6FE2603ceb"></A>Lighting calculations assume that the specified 
normal is of unit length, as shown in the following equation: 
</P>


<PRE>   x<SUP>2</SUP> + y<SUP>2</SUP> + z<SUP>2</SUP> = 1.0</PRE>


<P><A NAME="E1D6FE2652ceb"></A>If the normal does not equal 1.0, or if no lighting model is active, the results are unpredictable. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6FE2679ceb"></A>When called with unequal arguments, the <A HREF="scale.html#A144X95a6"><B>scale</B></A> subroutine or any other nonorthonomial transformation causes a matrix skew that is corrected by renormalizing every normal. Lighting performance is reduced in this event.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6FE2710ceb"></A>The <A HREF="normal.html#A142X9b7"><B>normal</B></A> and <B>n3f </B>subroutines are the same in all respects. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A139X91efd"></A>Parameter</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A139X91efe"></A><I>vector</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the address of an array containing three floating point numbers. These numbers are used to set the value for the current vertex normal.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X911e72"></A></TD>
<TD>  Vector components are: 


<TABLE BORDER="2"><TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>Vector Component</B></TD>

<TD><B>C Index</B></TD>

<TD><B>FORTRAN Index</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>Nx</TD>

<TD>0</TD>

<TD>1</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>Ny</TD>

<TD>1</TD>

<TD>2</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>Nz</TD>

<TD>2</TD>

<TD>3</TD></TR></TABLE></TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A139X91f03"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6FE2882ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="cylinder2_c.html#A16C0c87c"><B>cylinder2.c</B></A> calls the <B>n3f</B> subroutine between the <A HREF="bgnpolygon.html#A144X9672"><B>bgnpolygon</B></A> subroutine and the <A HREF="bgnpolygon.html#A144X9672"><B>endpolygon</B></A> subroutine to specify the normal vectors of a polygon.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015d76"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6FE2943ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C116"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C117"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C118"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A139X91f13"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D6FE3082ceb"></A>Binding a new material, light, or lighting model definition with the <A HREF="lmbind.html#XeZ2340marj"><B>lmbind</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6FE3124ceb"></A>Defining a new material, light, or lighting model with the <A HREF="lmdef.html#rgZ2250marj"><B>lmdef</B></A> subroutine.<B>  </B></P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6FE3169ceb"></A>Specifying a current normal vector for lighting calculations with the <A HREF="normal.html#A142X9b7"><B>normal</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D6FE3212ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A>, Creating 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/crlighteff.html#crlighteff.html">Lighting Effects</A>, Drawing with 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawbeg-end.html">Begin-End Style</A> Subroutines, 
and Understanding the <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/glintro.html#A8G44310marj">Hardware Used by GL</A>.</P><hr><center>
```
