</TITLE>
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="pwlcurve.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="qenter.html">Next</a>  |
<A href="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A143X967"></A>qdevice Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1501" REL="I1" TITLE="qdevice subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1502" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1503" REL="I2" TITLE="queue"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1504" REL="I3" TITLE="enabling input device for event queuing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1505" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1506" REL="I2" TITLE="device"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1507" REL="I3" TITLE="enabling input device for event queuing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1508" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1509" REL="I2" TITLE="queue and device"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1510" REL="I3" TITLE="qdevice"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A143X969"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7255863ceb"></A>Enables a input device (keyboard, button, or valuator) for event queuing.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C116d"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7255902ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7255927ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X96d"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A143X96e"></A><B>void qdevice(Device </B><A HREF="qdevice.html#A143X972"><I>device</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010c65"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010c66"></A><B>SUBROUTINE QDEVIC(</B><I>device</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>device</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X96f"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7256039ceb"></A>The <B>qdevice</B> subroutine changes the state of the specified device so that events occurring within the device are entered in the event queue. The device can be the keyboard, a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A1819349">button</A>, a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A79P07a">valuator</A>, or certain other pseudo-devices. The maximum number of queue entries is 50. </P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9f7b"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A143X971"></A>Parameter</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X972"></A><I>device</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the device whose state is to be changed so that it enters events into the event queue.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A30C011062"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7256135ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="scrn_rotate_c.html#A16C0c92f"><B>scrn_rotate.c</B></A> uses the <B>qdevice</B> subroutine to enable input from various devices. </P>

<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A143X9152"></A>qenter Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1511" REL="I1" TITLE="qenter subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1512" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1513" REL="I2" TITLE="query"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1514" REL="I3" TITLE="qenter"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1515" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1516" REL="I2" TITLE="queue"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1517" REL="I3" TITLE="creating event queue entry"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1518" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1519" REL="I2" TITLE="queue and device"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1520" REL="I3" TITLE="qenter"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9154"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7264402ceb"></A>Creates an event queue entry.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1177"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7264441ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7264465ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9158"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A143X9159"></A><B>void qenter(Int16 </B><A HREF="qenter.html#A143X915d"><I>qtype</I></A><B>, Int16 </B><A HREF="qenter.html#A143X915e"><I>value</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010c76"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010c77"></A><B>SUBROUTINE QENTER(</B><I>qtype</I><B>, </B><I>value</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>qtype</I><B>,</B><I> value</I></PRE>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A79C117a"></A><B>Note: </B>For FORTRAN users, this subroutine accepts long integer parameters (INTEGER*4) when started from a FORTRAN program, although it accepts short integers when started from a C program. The C and FORTRAN syntax shown here reflect this difference.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A143X915a"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7264600ceb"></A>The <B>qenter</B> subroutine takes two 16-bit integers, the <A HREF="qenter.html#A143X915d"><I>dev</I></A> and <A HREF="qenter.html#A143X915e"><I>val</I></A> parameters, and enters them as an event in the
 <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0484">event queue</A>. There is no way to distinguish user-defined from system-defined entries unless disjointed sets of device numbers are used. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7264627ceb"></A>An event entered with the <B>qenter</B> subroutine cannot be distinguished from an event automatically generated by the system if the event type is equal to one of the predefined system event types. The system defines a large number of event types in the <B>gl/device.h </B>header file. In brief, types <SAMP>0</SAMP> through <SAMP>0xfff</SAMP> are predefined by the system; types <SAMP>0x1000</SAMP> through <SAMP>0x7fff</SAMP> are reserved for use by the user, while <SAMP>0x8000</SAMP> through <SAMP>0xffff</SAMP> are reserved for future use by the system. Devices in these ranges are defined by the <B>IsButton</B>, <B>IsValuator</B> and other macros in the <B>gl/device.h</B> header file.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7264654ceb"></A>Events entered with the <B>qenter</B> subroutine are <I>always</I>  placed in the event queue. These events are never filtered, whether or not the event type falls into the range predefined by the system, or reserved for the user. In other words, it is not necessary to use the <B>qdevice</B> subroutine prior to using the <B>qenter</B> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7264680ceb"></A>When the <B>qenter</B> subroutine is used from a signal handler to enter an event into the GL queue, and the GL application is blocked on the <B>qread</B> subroutine, the <B>qread</B> subroutine cannot unblock. The <B>qread</B> subroutine can be unblocked by using the <B>XSendEvent</B> subroutine within the signal handler to send some arbitrary event (preferably, a ClientMessage event) to a window belonging to the application.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A5CA5B0489bett"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A143X915c"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X915d"></A><I>qtype</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies a number indicating the device making the queue entry.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X915e"></A><I>value</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the value to be entered into the event queue.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A30C01106a"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7264796ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="scrn_rotate_c.html#A16C0c92f"><B>scrn_rotate.c</B></A> uses the <B>qenter</B> subroutine to enter a REDRAW device event into the queue. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A64C01661f"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7264839ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X916e"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C117b"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C117c"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C117d"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/device.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C117e"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fdevice.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9172"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7264974ceb"></A>Reading the first entry in the event queue with the <A HREF="qread.html#A143X989"><B>qread</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7264999ceb"></A>Emptying the event queue with the <A HREF="qreset.html#A143X9ab"><B>qreset</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7265025ceb"></A>Checking the contents of the event queue with the <A HREF="qtest.html#A143X9cd"><B>qtest</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7265050ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A> and <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/cntrlques.html#cntrlques.html">Controlling Queues and Devices</A>.</P><hr><center>

<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A143X989"></A>qread Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1521" REL="I1" TITLE="qread subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1522" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1523" REL="I2" TITLE="queue"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1524" REL="I3" TITLE="reading first entry in event queue"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1525" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1526" REL="I2" TITLE="queue and device"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1527" REL="I3" TITLE="qread"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1528" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1529" REL="I2" TITLE="query"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1530" REL="I3" TITLE="qread"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A143X98b"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7272186ceb"></A>Reads the first entry in the event queue. </P>

<H3><A NAME="C46F28E015nqui"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7272225ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7272249ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X98f"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A143X990"></A><B>Int32 qread(Int16 *</B><A HREF="qread.html#A143X995"><I>data</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010c6a"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010c6b"></A><B>INTEGER*4 FUNCTION QREAD(</B><I>data</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*2 </B><I>data</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X991"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7272361ceb"></A>The <B>qread</B> subroutine returns the first entry on the event queue. If the event queue is empty, the <B>qread</B> subroutine blocks. That is, this subroutine does not return until an event occurs. If the event queue is not empty, the <B>qread</B> subroutine returns the device number associated with the first event in the queue, writes the associated data into the <I>data</I> parameter, and removes that entry from the queue.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9f7e"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a display list.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A143X993"></A>Parameter</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X995"></A><I>data</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies a pointer to the variable that is to receive the data in the event queue.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X997"></A>Return Value</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7272456ceb"></A>The identifier for the device read.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A30C011064"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7272497ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="scrn_rotate_c.html#A16C0c92f"><B>scrn_rotate.c</B></A> uses the <B>qread</B> subroutine to read input from the event queue. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A64C016617"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7272541ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9a5"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="C46F28F043nqui"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="C46F28F120nqui"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="C46F28F196nqui"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/device.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="C46F28F272nqui"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fdevice.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9a9"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7272675ceb"></A>Enabling an input device for event queuing with the <A HREF="qdevice.html#A143X967"><B>qdevice</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7272701ceb"></A>Disabling an input device for event queuing with the <A HREF="unqdevice.html#A143X91b8"><B>unqdevice</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<A NAME="INDEX1531" REL="I1" TITLE="qreset subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1532" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1533" REL="I2" TITLE="queue"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1534" REL="I3" TITLE="emptying event queue"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1535" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1536" REL="I2" TITLE="queue and device"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1537" REL="I3" TITLE="qreset"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9ad"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D727F766ceb"></A>Empties the event queue.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C117f"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D727F805ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D727F830ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9b1"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A143X9b2"></A><B>void qreset(&nbsp;)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010c6e"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010c6f"></A><B>SUBROUTINE QRESET</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9b3"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D727F937ceb"></A>The<B> qreset</B> subroutine removes all entries from the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0484">event queue</A> and discards them. </P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9f81"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A30C011066"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D727F998ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="scrn_rotate_c.html#A16C0c92f"><B>scrn_rotate.c</B></A> uses the <B>qreset</B> subroutine to delete all input events from any devices. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A64C01661a"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7280041ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9c7"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1182"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1183"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1184"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/device.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1185"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fdevice.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9cb"></A>Related Information</H3>

<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A143X9cd"></A>qtest Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1538" REL="I1" TITLE="qtest subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1539" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1540" REL="I2" TITLE="queue"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1541" REL="I3" TITLE="checking event queue contents"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1542" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1543" REL="I2" TITLE="queue and device"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1544" REL="I3" TITLE="qtest"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9cf"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D728D903ceb"></A>Checks the contents of the event queue.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1186"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D728D942ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D728D966ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9d3"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A143X9d4"></A><B>Int32 qtest(&nbsp;)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010c72"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010c73"></A><B>INTEGER*4 FUNCTION QTEST</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9d5"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D728E075ceb"></A>The<B> qtest</B> subroutine returns zero if the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0484">event queue</A> is empty. Otherwise, it returns the device number of the first entry. The queue remains unchanged.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9f84"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A215X988e"></A>Return Value</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D728E136ceb"></A>The device number of the first entry (0 if the event queue is empty).</P>

<H3><A NAME="A30C011068"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D728E177ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="scrn_rotate_c.html#A16C0c92f"><B>scrn_rotate.c</B></A> uses the <B>qtest</B> subroutine to check if there is any input from the queued devices. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A64C01661d"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D728E220ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9e9"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1189"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C118a"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C118b"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/device.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C118c"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fdevice.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9ed"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D728E356ceb"></A>Creating an event queue entry with the <A HREF="qenter.html#A143X9152"><B>qenter</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D728E382ceb"></A>Reading the first entry in the event queue with the <A HREF="qread.html#A143X989"><B>qread</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D728E407ceb"></A>Emptying the event queue with the <A HREF="qreset.html#A143X9ab"><B>qreset</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="WRS2380marj"></A>rcrv Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1545" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1546" REL="I2" TITLE="wire frame curve and surface patch"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1547" REL="I3" TITLE="rcrv"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1548" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1549" REL="I2" TITLE="cubic spline curve"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1550" REL="I3" TITLE="rational"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1551" REL="I1" TITLE="rcrv subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A213X91105c"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D729B855ceb"></A>Draws a rational cubic spline curve.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C1132"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D729B894ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D729B918ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X91105f"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X911060"></A><B>void rcrv(Coord </B><A HREF="rcrv.html#EMi2f0marj"><I>geom</I></A><B>[4][4])</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X91103c"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X91103f"></A><B>SUBROUTINE RCRV(</B><I>geom</I><B>)</B>
<B>REAL </B><I>geom</I><B>(4,4)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911063"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D729C030ceb"></A>The <B>rcrv</B> subroutine draws a rational 
cubic spline curve segment using the current curve basis and precision.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D729C057ceb"></A>The <A HREF="rcrv.html#EMi2f0marj"><I>geom</I></A> parameter specifies the four 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A25P03e7">control points</A> of the curve segment. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911066"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="EMi2f0marj"></A><I>geom</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies an array containing the four control points of the curve segment.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A64C01658e"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D729C138ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C1135"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C1136"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C1137"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X91106f"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D729C235ceb"></A>Drawing a cubic spline curve with the <A HREF="crv.html#ZMS220marj"><B>crv</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D729C260ceb"></A>Drawing a series of curve segments with the <A HREF="crvn.html#ESS22c0marj"><B>crvn</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D729C286ceb"></A>Setting the current cubic spline curve basis matrix for drawing curves with the <A HREF="curvebasis.html#sTS23a0marj"><B>curvebasis</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D729C312ceb"></A>Setting the number of line segments that compose a cubic spline curve with the <A HREF="curveprecision.html#aUS2120marj"><B>curveprecision</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D729C339ceb"></A>Defining a cubic spline basis matrix with the <A HREF="defbasis.html#A150X930"><B>defbasis</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D729C365ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A>, Drawing <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawnurbs.html#drawnurbs.html">NURBS Curves and Surfaces</A>, and Drawing <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawwfcvs.html#drawwfcvs.html">Wire Frame Curves and Surface Patches</A>.</P><hr><center>

<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A1TS2220marj"></A>rcrvn Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1552" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1553" REL="I2" TITLE="wire frame curve and surface patch"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1554" REL="I3" TITLE="rcrvn"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1555" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1556" REL="I2" TITLE="cubic spline curve segments"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1557" REL="I3" TITLE="rational"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1558" REL="I1" TITLE="rcrvn subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A213X91109f"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D72A9975ceb"></A>Draws a series of rational curve segments.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C1139"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D72AA014ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D72AA038ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X9110a2"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X9110a3"></A><B>void rcrvn(Int32 </B><A HREF="rcrvn.html#L1j2290marj"><I>n</I></A><B>, Coord </B><A HREF="rcrvn.html#Z1j23b0marj"><I>geom</I></A><B> [&nbsp;][4]) </B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911080"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X911083"></A><B>SUBROUTINE RCRVN(</B><I>n</I><B>,</B><I> geom</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>n</I>
<B>REAL </B><I>geom</I><B>(4,</B><I>n</I><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X9110a6"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D72AA151ceb"></A>The <B>rcrvn</B> subroutine draws a series of rational 
cubic spline curve segments using the current basis and precision. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D72AA177ceb"></A>The control points specified in the <A HREF="rcrvn.html#Z1j23b0marj"><I>geom</I></A> parameter determine the shapes of the curve segments and are used four at a time. The <A HREF="rcrvn.html#L1j2290marj"><I>n</I></A> parameter specifies the number of 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A25P03e7">control points</A> to be used in drawing the curve. For example, if <I>n </I>is 6, three curve segments are drawn: </P>

<OL><LI><A NAME="A213X9110a9"></A>Using points 0,1,2,3 as control points.</LI>

<LI><A NAME="A213X9110aa"></A>Using points 1,2,3,4 as control points.</LI>

<LI><A NAME="A213X9110ab"></A>Using points 2,3,4,5 as control points.</LI></OL>

<P><A NAME="E1D72AA265ceb"></A>If the current basis is a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A150P1959">B-spline</A>, 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A25P03de">Cardinal spline</A>, or 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A25P03be">basis</A> with similar properties, the curve segments are joined end to end and appear as a single curve.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X9110ad"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="L1j2290marj"></A><I>n</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the number of control points to be used in drawing the curve.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="Z1j23b0marj"></A><I>geom</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the matrix containing the control points of the curve segments.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A64C016592"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D72AA363ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C113c"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C113d"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C113e"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X9110b3"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D72AA461ceb"></A>Drawing a cubic spline curve with the <A HREF="crv.html#ZMS220marj"><B>crv</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D72AA486ceb"></A>Drawing a series of curve segments with the <A HREF="crvn.html#ESS22c0marj"><B>crvn</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D72AA512ceb"></A>Setting the current cubic spline curve basis matrix with the <A HREF="curvebasis.html#sTS23a0marj"><B>curvebasis</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D72AA537ceb"></A>Setting the number of line segments that compose a cubic spline curve with the <A HREF="curveprecision.html#aUS2120marj"><B>curveprecision</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D72AA563ceb"></A>Defining a cubic spline basis matrix with the <A HREF="defbasis.html#A150X930"><B>defbasis</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D72AA588ceb"></A>Drawing a rational curve with the <A HREF="rcrv.html#WRS2380marj"><B>rcrv</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D72AA615ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A>, Drawing <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawnurbs.html#drawnurbs.html">NURBS Curves and Surfaces</A>, and Drawing <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawwfcvs.html#drawwfcvs.html">Wire Frame Curves and Surface Patches</A>.</P><hr><center>

<A NAME="INDEX1559" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>

<A NAME="INDEX1561" REL="I3" TITLE="rdr"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1562" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>

<A NAME="INDEX1564" REL="I3" TITLE="drawing relative to current point"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1565" REL="I1" TITLE="rdr subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912dff"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D72B8947ceb"></A>Draws a line relative to the current graphics point.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C1315"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D72B8987ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D72B9011ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912e02"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X912e03"></A><B>void rdr</B>
<B>(Coord </B><A HREF="rdr.html#A213X912e0d"><I>dx</I></A><B>, Coord</B> <A HREF="rdr.html#A213X912e0e"><I>dy</I></A><B>, Coord</B> <A HREF="rdr.html#A213X912e0f"><I>dz</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="Aze110marj"></A><B>void rdri</B>
<B>(Icoord </B><A HREF="rdr.html#A213X912e0d"><I>dx</I></A><B>, Icoord</B> <A HREF="rdr.html#A213X912e0e"><I>dy</I></A><B>, Icoord</B> <A HREF="rdr.html#A213X912e0f"><I>dz</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="DQe110marj"></A><B>void rdrs</B>
<B>(Scoord </B><A HREF="rdr.html#A213X912e0d"><I>dx</I></A><B>, Scoord</B> <A HREF="rdr.html#A213X912e0e"><I>dy</I></A><B>, Scoord</B> <A HREF="rdr.html#A213X912e0f"><I>dz</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="SQe290marj"></A><B>void rdr2</B>
<B>(Coord </B><A HREF="rdr.html#A213X912e0d"><I>dx</I></A><B>, Coord</B> <A HREF="rdr.html#A213X912e0e"><I>dy</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A2Ae2f0marj"></A><B>void rdr2i</B>
<B>(Icoord </B><A HREF="rdr.html#A213X912e0d"><I>dx</I></A><B>, Icoord</B> <A HREF="rdr.html#A213X912e0e"><I>dy</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="FAe230marj"></A><B>void rdr2s</B>
<B>(Scoord </B><A HREF="rdr.html#A213X912e0d"><I>dx</I></A><B>, Scoord</B> <A HREF="rdr.html#A213X912e0e"><I>dy</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010aee"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010aef"></A><B>SUBROUTINE RDR(</B><I>dx</I><B>, </B><I>dy</I><B>, </B><I>dz</I><B>)</B>
<B>REAL </B><I>dx</I><B>, </B><I>dy</I><B>, </B><I>dz</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010af0"></A><B>SUBROUTINE RDRI(</B><I>dx</I><B>, </B><I>dy</I><B>, </B><I>dz</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>dx</I><B>, </B><I>dy</I><B>, </B><I>dz</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010af1"></A><B>SUBROUTINE RDRS(</B><I>dx</I><B>, </B><I>dy</I><B>, </B><I>dz</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*2 </B><I>dx</I><B>, </B><I>dy</I><B>, </B><I>dz</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010af2"></A><B>SUBROUTINE RDR2(</B><I>dx</I><B>, </B><I>dy</I><B>)</B>
<B>REAL </B><I>dx</I><B>, </B><I>dy</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010af3"></A><B>SUBROUTINE RDR2I(</B><I>dx</I><B>, </B><I>dy</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>dx</I><B>, </B><I>dy</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010af4"></A><B>SUBROUTINE RDR2S(</B><I>dx</I><B>, </B><I>dy</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*2 </B><I>dx</I><B>, </B><I>dy</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912e06"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D72B9314ceb"></A>The <B>rdr</B> subroutine is the relative version of the <A HREF="draw.html#EYf2e0marj"><B>draw</B></A> subroutine. It connects the point <A HREF="rdr.html#A213X912e0d"><I>dx</I></A>, <A HREF="rdr.html#A213X912e0e"><I>dy</I></A>, <A HREF="rdr.html#A213X912e0f"><I>dz</I></A> and the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A25P03eb">current graphics position</A> with a line segment,  using the current line attributes: 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A172P1436">linestyle</A>, 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A172P1437">linewidth</A>, 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A31996bc">color</A> (if in 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A150P19d9">depth-cue mode</A>, the depth-cued color is used), and 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A3C0F2A4599mhay">writemask</A>. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D72B9339ceb"></A>The <B>rdr</B> subroutine updates the current graphics position to the specified point.  </P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A213X912e09"></A><B>Note: </B>Do not place routines that invalidate the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A25P03eb">current graphics position</A> within sequences of moves and draws.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<P><A NAME="E1D72B9385ceb"></A>The six different forms for the <B>rdr</B> subroutine are as follows:</P>

<TABLE BORDER="2"><TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><BR></TD>

<TD><B>2-D</B></TD>

<TD><B>3-D</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>Int16</TD>

<TD>rdr2s</TD>

<TD>rdrs</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>Int32</TD>

<TD>rdr2i</TD>

<TD>rdri</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>float</TD>

<TD>rdr2</TD>

<TD>rdr</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P><A NAME="E1D72B9428ceb"></A>The <A HREF="rdr.html#A213X912e02">syntax</A> for each of the subroutine forms is the same except for the parameter type. They differ only in that <A HREF="rdr.html#A213X912e03"><B>rdr</B></A> expects real coordinates, <A HREF="rdr.html#Aze110marj"><B>rdri</B></A> expects integer coordinates, and <A HREF="rdr.html#DQe110marj"><B>rdrs</B></A> expects short integer coordinates. In addition, the <A HREF="rdr.html#SQe290marj"><B>rdr2</B></A>* routines assume a 2-D point instead of a 3-D point.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912e0c"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912e0d"></A><I>dx</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the distance from the <I>x</I> coordinate of the current graphics position to the <I>x</I> coordinate of the new point.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912e0e"></A><I>dy</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the distance from the <I>y</I> coordinate of the current graphics position to the <I>y</I> coordinate of the new point.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912e0f"></A><I>dz</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the distance from the <I>z</I> coordinate of the current graphics position to the <I>z</I> coordinate of the new point.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015d20"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D72B9545ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C1318"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C1319"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C131a"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912e1d"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D72B9642ceb"></A>Drawing a line with the <A HREF="draw.html#EYf2e0marj"><B>draw</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D72B9668ceb"></A>Moving the current graphics position to a specified point with the <A HREF="move.html#pofmarj"><B>move</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D72B9694ceb"></A>Drawing a point with the <A HREF="pnt.html#Ptf3a0marj"><B>pnt</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D72B9719ceb"></A>Moving the current graphics position to a point relative to the current point with the <A HREF="rmv.html#kzf90marj"><B>rmv</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D72B9745ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A>, Drawing with <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/move-draw.html">Move-Draw Style</A> Subroutines, Performing <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/depth-cueing.html">Depth-Cueing</A>, <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/setglattrib.html#setglattrib.html">Setting Drawing Attributes</A>, and Working with <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/workcoords.html#workcoords.html">Coordinate Systems</A>.</P><hr><center>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">

<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A142X91059"></A>readpixels Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1566" REL="I1" TITLE="readpixels subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1567" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1568" REL="I2" TITLE="pixel block transfer"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1569" REL="I3" TITLE="returning color map mode pixel values"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1570" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1571" REL="I2" TITLE="pixel block transfer"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1572" REL="I3" TITLE="readpixels"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A142X9105b"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D72C7263ceb"></A>Returns values of specific pixels in color map mode.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1d0"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D72C7302ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D72C7327ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A142X9105f"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A142X91060"></A><B>Int32 readpixels(Int16 </B><A HREF="readpixels.html#A142X91064"><I>number</I></A><B>, Colorindex </B><A HREF="readpixels.html#A142X91065"><I>colors</I></A><B>[&nbsp;])</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010b2a"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010b2b"></A><B>INTEGER*4 FUNCTION READPI(</B><I>number</I><B>,</B> <I>colors</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>number</I>
<B>INTEGER*2 </B><I>colors</I><B>(</B><I>number</I><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A142X91061"></A>Description</H3>

<P><A NAME="E1D72C7441ceb"></A>The <B>readpixels</B> subroutine returns values of specific pixels from the 
frame buffer in 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A25P03e3">color map mode</A>. 
It reads them into the array starting from the 
current character position along a single scan line (constant y) in the direction of increasing x. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D72C7467ceb"></A>The <A HREF="readpixels.html#A142X91064"><I>number</I></A> parameter returns the number of pixels read, which is the number requested if the starting point is a valid character position (inside the current 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A27P039">viewport</A>.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D72C7493ceb"></A>The system must be in color map mode for the <B>readpixels</B> subroutine to function. Use the <A HREF="readRGB.html#A142X9107b"><B>readRGB</B></A> subroutine to read pixels in 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0743">RGB mode</A>.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D72C7520ceb"></A>The <B>readpixels</B> subroutine returns zero if the starting point is not a valid character position. The values of pixels read outside the viewport or the screen are undefined. The subroutine updates the current character position to one pixel to the right of the last one read. The current character position is undefined if the new position is outside the viewport.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D72C7547ceb"></A>In 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0474">double buffer mode</A>, only the back buffer 
is read by default. Use the <A HREF="readsource.html#A142X9cc0"><B>readsource</B></A> subroutine to specify 
which buffer is read.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D72C7573ceb"></A>When the system is in SINGLEMAP mode, only the lowest 12 bits contain valid data, and the 4 upper bits of a color value (an element of the array in the <A HREF="readpixels.html#A142X91065"><I>colors</I></A> parameter) are undefined. When the system is in MULTIMAP mode, only the lowest 8 bits contain valid data, and the upper 8 bits of a color value are undefined.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D72C7599ceb"></A>The <A HREF="rectread.html#A142X9c7c"><B>rectread</B></A> subroutine provides significantly better performance for pixel block transfers. Even when only one row of pixels needs to be read, use the <B>rectread</B> subroutine. </P>

<OL><LI><A NAME="A29C010b2c"></A>This subroutine is available only in 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A25P03e3">color map mode</A>.</LI>

<LI><A NAME="A318C9dc8"></A>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</LI>

<LI><A NAME="A81C129"></A>The use of this subroutine is deprecated. Do not use the <B>readpixels </B>subroutine in new development.</LI></OL>

<H3><A NAME="A142X91063"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A142X91064"></A><I>number</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the number of pixels to be read by the function.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A142X91065"></A><I>colors</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the array in which the pixel values are to be stored.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A142X91067"></A>Return Value</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D72C7770ceb"></A>The number of pixels actually read. A returned function value of 0 (zero) indicates that the starting point is not a valid character position.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A61C0159be"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D72C7815ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1d3"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1d4"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1d5"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A258C01c661"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D72C7913ceb"></A>Returning the value of specific pixels in RGB mode with the <A HREF="readRGB.html#A142X9107b"><B>readRGB</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D72C7938ceb"></A>Specifying the source for pixels to be read with the <A HREF="readsource.html#A142X9cc0"><B>readsource</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D72C7965ceb"></A>Copying a rectangle of pixels with an optional zoom with the <A HREF="rectcopy.html#A142X9d04"><B>rectcopy</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D72C7990ceb"></A>Reading a rectangular array of pixels into host memory with the <A HREF="rectread.html#A142X9c7c"><B>rectread</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D72C8016ceb"></A>Drawing a rectangular array of pixels into the frame buffer with the <A HREF="rectwrite.html#A142X9c9e"><B>rectwrite</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D72C8042ceb"></A>Painting a row of pixels on the screen in color map mode with the <A HREF="writepixels.html#A142X9e62"><B>writepixels</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D72C8068ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A>, Reading and Writing <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/rwpixels.html#rwpixels.html">Pixels</A>, 
Using <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/useviewprts.html#useviewprts.html">Viewports and Screenmasks</A>, 
and Working in <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/workcolor.html#workcolor.html">Color Map and RGB Modes</A>.</P><hr><center>

</TITLE>
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="readpixels.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="readsource.html">Next</a>  |
<A href="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A142X9107b"></A>readRGB Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1573" REL="I1" TITLE="readRGB subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1574" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1575" REL="I2" TITLE="pixel block transfer"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1576" REL="I3" TITLE="returning RGB mode pixel values"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1577" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1578" REL="I2" TITLE="pixel block transfer"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1579" REL="I3" TITLE="readRGB"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A142X9107d"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D72D5795ceb"></A>Returns values of specific pixels in RGB mode.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1f5"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D72D5835ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D72D5859ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A142X91081"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A142X91082"></A><B>Int32 readRGB</B>
<B>(Int16 </B><A HREF="readRGB.html#A142X91086"><I>number</I></A><B>, </B>
<B>RGBvalue</B> <A HREF="readRGB.html#A142X91087"><I>red</I></A><B>[&nbsp;], RGBvalue</B> <A HREF="readRGB.html#A142X91088"><I>green</I></A><B>[&nbsp;], RGBvalue</B> <A HREF="readRGB.html#N3R2170marj"><I>blue</I></A><B>[&nbsp;])</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010b45"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010b46"></A><B>INTEGER*4 FUNCTION READRG(</B><I>number</I><B>, </B><I>red</I><B>, </B><I>green</I><B>, </B><I>blue)</I>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>number</I>
<B>CHARACTER*(*) </B><I>red</I><B>, </B><I>green</I><B>, </B><I>blue</I><B>;</B></PRE>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A79C1f8"></A><B>Note: </B>For FORTRAN users, this function accepts long integer parameters (INTEGER*4) when invoked from a FORTRAN program, although it accepts short integers when invoked from a C program. The C and FORTRAN syntax shown here reflect this difference.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A142X91083"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D72D5995ceb"></A>The <B>readRGB</B> subroutine attempts to read specific pixel values from the frame buffer in 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0743">RGB mode</A>. The returned value of this 
function is the number of pixels actually read. A returned function value of 0 (zero) indicates that the 
starting point is not a valid character position. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D72D6021ceb"></A>The <B>readRGB</B> subroutine reads the pixel values into the arrays specified by the <A HREF="readRGB.html#A142X91087"><I>red</I></A>, <A HREF="readRGB.html#A142X91088"><I>green</I></A>, and <A HREF="readRGB.html#N3R2170marj"><I>blue</I></A> parameters starting from the current character position along a single scan line (constant y) in the direction of increasing x.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D72D6048ceb"></A>The <B>readRGB</B> subroutine returns the number of pixels read, which is the number requested if the starting point is a valid character position (inside the current viewport). The subroutine returns 0 (zero) if the starting point is not a valid character position. The values of pixels read outside of the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A27P039">viewport</A> or 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A27P018">screenmask</A> are undefined.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D72D6074ceb"></A>The <B>readRGB</B> subroutine updates the current character position to one pixel to the right of the last one read. The current character position is undefined if the new position is outside the viewport.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D72D6100ceb"></A>Use the <B>readsource</B> subroutine to specify which buffer is read. In RGB 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0474">double buffer mode</A>, by default the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P051c">back buffer</A> is read. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D72D6125ceb"></A>The <A HREF="rectread.html#A142X9c7c"><B>rectread</B></A> subroutine provides significantly better performance for pixel block transfers. Even when only one row of pixels needs to be read, use the <B>rectread</B> subroutine. </P>

<OL><LI><A NAME="A29C010b47"></A>This subroutine is available only in 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0743">RGB mode</A>. For new development, use the 
<A HREF="rectread.html#A142X9c7c"><B>lrectread</B></A> subroutine.</LI>

<LI><A NAME="A318C9dd7"></A>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</LI>

<LI><A NAME="A81C12a"></A>The use of this subroutine is deprecated. Do not use the <B>readRGB </B>subroutine in new development.</LI></OL>

<H3><A NAME="A142X91085"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A142X91086"></A><I>number</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the number of pixels read by the function.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A142X91087"></A><I>red</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the array in which the red pixel values will be stored.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A142X91088"></A><I>green</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the array in which the green pixel values will be stored.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="N3R2170marj"></A><I>blue</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the array in which the blue pixel values will be stored.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A142X91089"></A>Return Value</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D72D6335ceb"></A>The returned value of this function is the number of pixels that the system actually reads. The returned function value is 0 (zero) if any part of the specified rectangle is off the screen.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A61C0159ce"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D72D6379ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1f9"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1fa"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1fb"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A258C01c67c"></A>Related Information</H3>

<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A142X9cc0"></A>readsource Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1580" REL="I1" TITLE="readsource subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1581" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1582" REL="I2" TITLE="pixel block transfer"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1583" REL="I3" TITLE="specifying source for pixel read"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1584" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1585" REL="I2" TITLE="pixel block transfer"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1586" REL="I3" TITLE="readsource"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A142X9cc2"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D72E4667ceb"></A>Specifies the source for pixels to be read by various subroutines.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A74C1e4"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D72E4706ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D72E4730ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A142X9cc6"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A142X9cc7"></A><B>void readsource(Int32 </B><A HREF="readsource.html#A142X9ccb"><I>source</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010b1e"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010b1f"></A><B>SUBROUTINE READSO(</B><I>source</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>source</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A142X9cc8"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D72E4842ceb"></A>The <B>readsource</B> subroutine specifies the exact pixel source 
(<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P051c">front buffer, back buffer</A>, or 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A154P1160a">z-buffer</A>) that the <A HREF="rectcopy.html#A142X9d04"><B>rectcopy</B></A>, <A HREF="readpixels.html#A142X91059"><B>readpixels</B></A>, <A HREF="readRGB.html#A142X9107b"><B>readRGB</B></A>, and <A HREF="rectread.html#A142X9c7c"><B>rectread</B></A> subroutines use.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9dc2"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A142X9cca"></A>Parameter</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A142X9ccb"></A><I>source</I></TD>
<TD>  The defined values for this parameter are listed in the following table:


<TABLE BORDER="2"><TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD COLSPAN="3"><B>Values for the source Parameter</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>C</B></TD>

<TD><B>FORTRAN</B></TD>

<TD><B>Function</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>SRC_AUTO </TD>

<TD>SRCAUT </TD>

<TD>Selects the front buffer in single buffer mode and the back buffer in double buffer mode.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>SRC_FRONT</TD>

<TD>SRCFRO</TD>

<TD>Front color buffer. Valid for both single and double buffer operation.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>SRC_BACK </TD>

<TD>SRCBAC </TD>

<TD>Back color buffer. Valid during double buffer operation only.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>SRC_ZBUFFER </TD>

<TD>SRCZBU </TD>

<TD>Z-buffer. Valid during both single and double buffer operation.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>SRC_OVER</TD>

<TD>SRCOVE</TD>

<TD>Overlay planes.</TD></TR></TABLE>




<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A213X912074"></A><B>Note: </B>The 3-D Color Graphics Processor does not support SRC_OVER.   </BLOCKQUOTE>

</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A61C0159b8"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D72E4992ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3CFD27E332janb"></A>BLITs to and from the z-buffer are currently inoperational on the POWER GXT1000 adapter.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3CFD27E343janb"></A>When performing BLITs to and from the overlay planes on the GXT1000, the transparent pixel value on the GXT1000 is 255, not 0. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A74C1e7"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A74C1e8"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A74C1e9"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A258C01c665"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D72E5089ceb"></A>Copying a rectangle of pixels with an optional zoom with the <A HREF="rectcopy.html#A142X9d04"><B>rectcopy</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D72E5114ceb"></A>Reading a rectangular array of pixels into host memory with the <A HREF="rectread.html#A142X9c7c"><B>rectread</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D72E5140ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A>, Reading and Writing <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/rwpixels.html#rwpixels.html">Pixels</A>, and <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/configframebuf.html#configframebuf.html">Configuring the Frame Buffer</A>.</P><hr><center>

<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="KAg110marj"></A>rect Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1587" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1588" REL="I2" TITLE="high-level drawing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1589" REL="I3" TITLE="rect"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1590" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1591" REL="I2" TITLE="rectangle"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1592" REL="I3" TITLE="drawing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1593" REL="I1" TITLE="rect subroutine (GL)"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A213X9116da"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D72F2450ceb"></A>Draws an unfilled rectangle.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C1283"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D72F2489ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D72F2514ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X9116dd"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X9116de"></A><B>void rect</B>
<B>(Coord </B><A HREF="rect.html#A213X9116ea"><I>x1</I></A><B>, Coord</B> <A HREF="rect.html#A213X9116eb"><I>y1</I></A><B>,</B>
<B>Coord</B> <A HREF="rect.html#A213X9116ec"><I>x2</I></A><B>, Coord</B> <A HREF="rect.html#A213X9116ed"><I>y2</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X9116df"></A><B>void recti</B>
<B>(Icoord </B><A HREF="rect.html#A213X9116ea"><I>x1</I></A><B>, Icoord</B> <A HREF="rect.html#A213X9116eb"><I>y1</I></A><B>,</B>
<B>Icoord</B> <A HREF="rect.html#A213X9116ec"><I>x2</I></A><B>, Icoord</B> <A HREF="rect.html#A213X9116ed"><I>y2</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X9116e0"></A><B>void rects</B>
<B>(Scoord </B><A HREF="rect.html#A213X9116ea"><I>x1</I></A><B>, Scoord</B> <A HREF="rect.html#A213X9116eb"><I>y1</I></A><B>,</B>
<B>Scoord</B> <A HREF="rect.html#A213X9116ec"><I>x2</I></A><B>, Scoord</B> <A HREF="rect.html#A213X9116ed"><I>y2</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X9116b8"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X9116bb"></A><B>SUBROUTINE RECT(</B><I>x1</I><B>,</B><I> y1</I><B>,</B><I> x2</I><B>,</B><I> y2</I><B>)</B>
<B>REAL </B><I>x1</I><B>, </B><I>y1</I><B>, </B><I>x2</I><B>, </B><I>y2</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A28C010747"></A><B>SUBROUTINE RECTI(</B><I>x1</I><B>,</B><I> y1</I><B>,</B><I> x2</I><B>,</B><I> y2</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>x1</I><B>, </B><I>y1</I><B>, </B><I>x2</I><B>, </B><I>y2</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A28C010748"></A><B>SUBROUTINE RECTS(</B><I>x1</I><B>,</B><I> y1</I><B>,</B><I> x2</I><B>,</B><I> y2</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*2 </B><I>x1</I><B>, </B><I>y1</I><B>,</B> <I>x2</I><B>, </B><I>y2</I></PRE>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A78C1286"></A><B>Note: </B>For FORTRAN users, the INTEGER*2 version, the <B>RECTS</B> subroutine, should not be called with integer constant parameters. For example, 2 is an integer constant; JJ is an integer variable. The XL FORTRAN compiler, invoked by the <B>xlf</B> command, stores all integer constants as long integers (INTEGER*4), not as short integers (INTEGER*2). Invoking the short version of this subroutine with an integer constant will result in unexpected behavior.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A213X9116e5"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D72F2725ceb"></A>The <B>rect</B> subroutine draws a rectangle using the current line attributes: 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A172P1436">linestyle</A>, 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A172P1437">linewidth</A>, 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A31996bc">color</A>, and 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A3C0F2A4599mhay">writemask</A>. The sides of the rectangle are parallel to the <I>x</I> and <I>y</I> axes. Since a rectangle is a 2-D shape, the <B>rect</B> subroutine takes only 2-D arguments, and sets the <I>z</I> coordinate to zero. The current graphics position is set to (<I>x1, y1</I>) after the rectangle is drawn. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D72F2765ceb"></A>The syntax for each of the subroutine forms is the same except for the first argument.  They differ only in that <A HREF="rect.html#A213X9116de"><B>rect</B></A> expects real coordinates, <A HREF="rect.html#A213X9116df"><B>recti</B></A> expects integer coordinates, and <A HREF="rect.html#A213X9116e0"><B>rects</B></A> expects short integer coordinates. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X9116e9"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X9116ea"></A><I>x1</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>x</I> coordinate of one corner of the rectangle.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X9116eb"></A><I>y1</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>y</I> coordinate of one corner of the rectangle.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X9116ec"></A><I>x2</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>x</I> coordinate of the opposite corner of the rectangle.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X9116ed"></A><I>y2</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>y</I> coordinate of the opposite corner of the rectangle.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X9116f0"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D72F2900ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="tpbig_c.html#A16C0c9bd"><B>tpbig.c</B></A> uses the <B>recti</B> subroutine to draw the outline of a rectangle in green. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015cd4"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D72F2943ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C1287"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C1288"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C1289"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A258C01c563"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D72F3040ceb"></A>Drawing a polygon with the <A HREF="poly.html#avf2c0marj"><B>poly</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D72F3066ceb"></A>Drawing a filled rectangle with the <A HREF="rectf.html#Q5g330marj"><B>rectf</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D72F3092ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A>, <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/setglattrib.html#setglattrib.html">Setting Drawing Attributes</A>, <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawpoly.html#drawpoly.html">Drawing Rectangles, Circles, Arcs, and Polygons</A>.</P><hr><center>

 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
</center></BODY>

</HTML>

<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">
<HTML>

<TITLE>rectcopy Subroutine
</TITLE>
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="rect.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="rectf.html">Next</a>  |
<A href="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A142X9d04"></A>rectcopy Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1594" REL="I1" TITLE="rectcopy subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1595" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1596" REL="I2" TITLE="pixel block transfer"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1597" REL="I3" TITLE="copying pixel rectangle with zoom"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1598" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1599" REL="I2" TITLE="pixel block transfer"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1600" REL="I3" TITLE="rectcopy"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A213X91209f"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7300581ceb"></A>Copies a rectangle of pixels with an optional zoom.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1d6"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7300620ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7300644ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X9120a2"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X9120a3"></A><B>void rectcopy</B>
<B>(Screencoord </B><A HREF="rectcopy.html#XJN2220marj"><I>xll</I></A><B>, Screencoord </B><A HREF="rectcopy.html#eON2300marj"><I>yll</I></A><B>, </B>
<B>Screencoord </B><A HREF="rectcopy.html#AzON23a0marj"><I>xur</I></A><B>, Screencoord </B><A HREF="rectcopy.html#APN23a0marj"><I>yur</I></A><B>, </B>
<B>Screencoord </B><A HREF="rectcopy.html#rQN2300marj"><I>newx</I></A><B>, Screencoord </B><A HREF="rectcopy.html#DSN23a0marj"><I>newy</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010b31"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010b32"></A><B>SUBROUTINE RECTCO(</B><I>xll</I><B>,</B> <I>yll</I><B>,</B> <I>xur</I><B>,</B> <I>yur</I><B>,</B> <I>newx</I><B>,</B><I> newy</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>xll</I><B>,</B> <I>yll</I><B>,</B> <I>xur</I><B>,</B> <I>yur</I><B>,</B> <I>newx</I><B>,</B><I> newy</I></PRE>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A79C1d9"></A><B>Note: </B>For FORTRAN users, this subroutine accepts long integer parameters (INTEGER*4) when invoked from a FORTRAN program, although it accepts short integers when invoked from a C program. The C and FORTRAN syntax shown here reflect this difference.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A213X9120a6"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7300778ceb"></A>The <B>rectcopy</B> subroutine copies a rectangular array of pixels to another position on the screen. The current 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A27P039">viewport</A> and 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A27P018">screenmask</A> mask the drawing of the copied region. Self-intersecting copies work correctly in all cases.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7300804ceb"></A>Use the <A HREF="rectzoom.html#A142X9d26"><B>rectzoom</B></A> subroutine to zoom the destination independently in both the x and y directions. Self-intersecting copies also work correctly with zooming. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7300829ceb"></A>Use the <B>readsource</B> subroutine to specify the front buffer, the back buffer, or the z-buffer as the source. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7300855ceb"></A>On machines that support it, you can use the <B>rectzoom</B> subroutine to zoom the destination independently in both the x and y directions. Self-intersecting copies also work correctly with zooming. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7300881ceb"></A>Pixel format is not considered during the copy. For example, if you copy pixels that contain color index data into an RGB window, the display controller cannot correctly interpret it.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7300907ceb"></A>Use the <A HREF="frontbuffer.html#A145X9a0"><B>frontbuffer</B></A>, <A HREF="backbuffer.html#A145X94a"><B>backbuffer</B></A>, and <A HREF="zdraw.html#A143X97f5"><B>zdraw</B></A> subroutines to specify the destination.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7300933ceb"></A>All coordinates are relative to the lower left corner of the window, not the screen or viewport.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7300959ceb"></A>The <B>rectcopy </B>subroutine leaves the current character position unpredictable. The result of the <B>rectcopy </B>subroutine is undefined if the value of the <I>bool</I> parameter in the <A HREF="zbuffer.html#A143X97b1"><B>zbuffer</B></A> subroutine is TRUE.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9dcb"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A213X9120b0"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="XJN2220marj"></A><I>xll </I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>x </I>coordinate of one corner of the rectangle.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="eON2300marj"></A><I>yll </I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>y </I>coordinate of one corner of the rectangle.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="AzON23a0marj"></A><I>xur </I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>x </I>coordinate of the opposite corner of the rectangle.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="APN23a0marj"></A><I>yur </I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>y </I>coordinate of the opposite corner of the rectangle.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="rQN2300marj"></A><I>newx</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>x</I> coordinate of the lower left corner of the new position of the rectangle.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="DSN23a0marj"></A><I>newy</I><B></B></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>y</I> coordinate of the lower left corner of the new position of the rectangle.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A61C0159c1"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7301153ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1da"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1db"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1dc"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A258C01c669"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7301251ceb"></A>Specifying the source for pixels to be read with the <A HREF="readsource.html#A142X9cc0"><B>readsource</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7301276ceb"></A>Reading a rectangular array of pixels into host memory with the <A HREF="rectread.html#A142X9c7c"><B>rectread</B> or <B>lrectread</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7301302ceb"></A>Drawing a rectangular array of pixels into the frame buffer with the <A HREF="rectwrite.html#A142X9c9e"><B>rectwrite</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7301328ceb"></A>Specifying a zoom factor for rectangle copies and writes with the <A HREF="rectzoom.html#A142X9d26"><B>rectzoom</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7301354ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A> and Reading and Writing <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/rwpixels.html#rwpixels.html">Pixels</A>.</P><hr><center>

<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">

</TITLE>
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="rectcopy.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="rectread.html">Next</a>  |
<A href="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>

 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="Q5g330marj"></A>rectf Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1601" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1602" REL="I2" TITLE="high-level drawing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1603" REL="I3" TITLE="rectf"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1604" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1605" REL="I2" TITLE="rectangle"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1606" REL="I3" TITLE="filled"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1607" REL="I1" TITLE="rectf subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911733"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D730F751ceb"></A>Draws a filled rectangle.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C128a"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D730F790ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D730F814ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911736"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X911737"></A><B>void rectf</B>
<B>(Coord </B><A HREF="rectf.html#A213X911742"><I>x1</I></A><B>, Coord</B> <A HREF="rectf.html#A213X911743"><I>y1</I></A><B>,</B>
<B>Coord</B> <A HREF="rectf.html#A213X911744"><I>x2</I></A><B>, Coord</B> <A HREF="rectf.html#A213X911745"><I>y2</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X911738"></A><B>void rectfi</B>
<B>(Icoord </B><A HREF="rectf.html#A213X911742"><I>x1</I></A><B>, Icoord</B> <A HREF="rectf.html#A213X911743"><I>y1</I></A><B>,</B>
<B>Icoord</B> <A HREF="rectf.html#A213X911744"><I>x2</I></A><B>, Icoord</B> <A HREF="rectf.html#A213X911745"><I>y2</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X911739"></A><B>void rectfs</B>
<B>(Scoord </B><A HREF="rectf.html#A213X911742"><I>x1</I></A><B>, Scoord</B> <A HREF="rectf.html#A213X911743"><I>y1</I></A><B>,</B>
<B>Scoord</B> <A HREF="rectf.html#A213X911744"><I>x2</I></A><B>, Scoord</B> <A HREF="rectf.html#A213X911745"><I>y2</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911711"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X911714"></A><B>SUBROUTINE RECTF(</B><I>x1</I><B>, </B><I>y1</I><B>, </B><I>x2</I><B>, </B><I>y2</I><B>)</B>
<B>REAL </B><I>x1</I><B>, </B><I>y1</I><B>, </B><I>x2</I><B>, </B><I>y2</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A28C010749"></A><B>SUBROUTINE RECTFI(</B><I>x1</I><B>, </B><I>y1</I><B>, </B><I>x2</I><B>, </B><I>y2</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>x1</I><B>, </B><I>y1</I><B>, </B><I>x2</I><B>, </B><I>y2</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A28C01074a"></A><B>SUBROUTINE RECTFS(</B><I>x1</I><B>, </B><I>y1</I><B>, </B><I>x2</I><B>, </B><I>y2</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*2 </B><I>x1</I><B>, </B><I>y1</I><B>, </B><I>x2</I><B>, </B><I>y2</I></PRE>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A78C128d"></A><B>Note: </B>For FORTRAN users, the INTEGER*2 version, the <B>RECTFS</B> subroutine, should not be called with integer constant parameters. For example, 2 is an integer constant; JJ is an integer variable. The XL FORTRAN compiler, invoked by the
<B>xlf</B> command, stores all integer constants as long integers (INTEGER*4), not as short integers (INTEGER*2). Invoking the short version of this subroutine with an integer constant will result in unexpected behavior.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A213X91173e"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7310025ceb"></A>The <B>rectf </B>subroutine produces a filled rectangular region, using the current area attributes: 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A13791abd">pattern</A>, 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A31996bc">color</A>, and 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A3C0F2A4599mhay">writemask</A>. The sides of the rectangle are parallel to the <I>x</I> and <I>y</I> axes of the object coordinate system. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7310054ceb"></A>Since a rectangle is a 2-D shape, the <B>rectf</B> subroutine takes only 2-D arguments and sets the coordinate to zero. The current graphics position is set to (<I>x1, y1</I>) after the region is drawn. Backfacing polygon removal works correctly if (<I>x1, y1</I>) specifies the lower left corner and (<I>x2, y2</I>) the upper right corner of the rectangle.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7310080ceb"></A>The syntax for each of the subroutine forms is the same except for the first argument.  They differ only in that <A HREF="rectf.html#A213X911737"><B>rectf</B></A> expects real coordinates, <A HREF="rectf.html#A213X911738"><B>rectfi</B></A> expects integer coordinates, and <A HREF="rectf.html#A213X911739"><B>rectfs</B></A> expects short integer coordinates. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911741"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X911742"></A><I>x1</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>x</I> coordinate of one corner of the rectangle that is to be drawn.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X911743"></A><I>y1</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>y</I> coordinate of one corner of the rectangle that is to be drawn.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X911744"></A><I>x2</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>x</I> coordinate of the opposite corner of the rectangle that is to be drawn.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X911745"></A><I>y2</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>y</I> coordinate of the opposite corner of the rectangle that is to be drawn.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911748"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7310216ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="tpbig_c.html#A16C0c9bd"><B>tpbig.c</B></A> uses the <B>rectfi</B> subroutine to draw a filled, red rectangle. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015cd6"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7310259ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C128e"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C128f"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C1290"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911758"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7310356ceb"></A>Drawing a filled polygon with the <A HREF="polf.html#Zsf1c0marj"><B>polf</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7310381ceb"></A>Drawing a rectangle with the <A HREF="rect.html#KAg110marj"><B>rect</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7310407ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A>, <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/setglattrib.html#setglattrib.html">Setting Drawing Attributes</A>, and <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawpoly.html#drawpoly.html">Drawing Rectangles, Circles, Arcs, and Polygons</A>.</P><hr><center>

<a href="rectread.html">Next</a>  |

 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
</center></BODY>
