```html
<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">
<HTML>
<HEAD>
<META HTTP-EQUIV="Content-Type" CONTENT="text/html; charset=iso-8859-1">

<TITLE>rectread or lrectread Subroutine
</TITLE>
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="rectf.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="rectwrite.html">Next</a>  |
<A href="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A142X9c7c"></A>rectread or lrectread Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1608" REL="I1" TITLE="rectread subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1609" REL="I1" TITLE="lrectread subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1610" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1611" REL="I2" TITLE="pixel block transfer"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1612" REL="I3" TITLE="reading rectangular pixel array to host memory"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1613" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1614" REL="I2" TITLE="pixel block transfer"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1615" REL="I3" TITLE="rectread"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1616" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1617" REL="I2" TITLE="pixel block transfer"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1618" REL="I3" TITLE="lrectread"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A213X91203e"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D731E497ceb"></A>Reads a rectangular array of pixels into host memory.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1dd"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D731E537ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D731E563ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912041"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X912042"></A><B>Int32 rectread</B>
<B>(Screencoord </B><A HREF="rectread.html#d5P2150marj"><I>xll</I></A><B>, Screencoord </B><A HREF="rectread.html#o5P230marj"><I>yll</I></A><B>,</B>
<B>Screencoord </B><A HREF="rectread.html#I8P210marj"><I>xur</I></A><B>, Screencoord </B><A HREF="rectread.html#U8P2330marj"><I>yur</I></A><B>,</B>
<B>Int16 *</B><A HREF="rectread.html#A139X91ee9"><I>parray</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X912043"></A><B>Int32 lrectread</B>
<B>(Screencoord </B><A HREF="rectread.html#d5P2150marj"><I>xll</I></A><B>, Screencoord </B><A HREF="rectread.html#o5P230marj"><I>yll</I></A><B>,</B>
<B>Screencoord </B><A HREF="rectread.html#I8P210marj"><I>xur</I></A><B>, Screencoord </B><A HREF="rectread.html#U8P2330marj"><I>yur</I></A><B>,</B>
<B>Int32 *</B><A HREF="rectread.html#A139X91ee9"><I>parray</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010b17"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010b18"></A><B>INTEGER*4 RECTRE(</B><I>xll</I><B>, </B><I>yll</I><B>, </B><I>xur</I><B>, </B><I>yur</I><B>, </B><I>parray</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>xll</I><B>, </B><I>yll</I><B>,</B><I> xur</I><B>, </B><I>yur</I>
<B>INTEGER*2 </B><I>parray</I><B>(1)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010b19"></A><B>INTEGER*4 LRECTR(</B><I>xll</I><B>, </B><I>yll</I><B>, </B><I>xur</I><B>, </B><I>yur</I><B>, </B><I>parray</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>xll</I><B>,</B><I> yll</I><B>,</B><I> xur</I><B>,</B><I> yur</I><B>, </B><I>parray</I><B>(1)</B></PRE>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A79C1e0"></A><B>Note: </B>For FORTRAN users, these subroutines accept long integer parameters (INTEGER*4) when started from a FORTRAN program, although they accept short integers when started from a C program. The C and FORTRAN syntax shown here reflect this difference.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A213X912047"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D731E773ceb"></A>The <B>rectread</B> and <B>lrectread </B>subroutines each return a rectangular array of 16- and 32-bit pixels, respectively, to the host array specified in the <A HREF="rectread.html#A139X91ee9"><I>parray</I></A> parameter. For the <B>lrectread</B> subroutine, the <I>parray</I> parameter contains 32-bit packed RGB, RGBA, or <I>z</I> values. The returned value of this function is the number of pixels that the system actually reads, left to right, then bottom to top. The returned function value is 0 (zero) if any part of the specified rectangle is off the screen. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D731E799ceb"></A>The returned data is undefined if the <A HREF="rectread.html#d5P2150marj"><I>xll</I></A> and <A HREF="rectread.html#o5P230marj"><I>yll</I></A> parameters do not specify the lower-left corner of a rectangle that appears completely on the screen. All coordinates are relative to the lower left corner of the window and not to the screen or 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A27P039">viewport</A>.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D731E826ceb"></A>When performing operations with the <B>lrectread</B> subroutine on the POWER Gt4 and POWER Gt4x in RGBmode with a specified pixel size of 32, pixels are returned with one 24-bit pixel packed in a 32-bit word. The high-order byte (the A byte) is set to the value 0xff.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D731E851ceb"></A>The <A HREF="readsource.html#A142X9cc0"><B>readsource</B></A> subroutine specifies the pixel source from which the pixels are read. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D731E877ceb"></A>The behavior of the <B>lrectread</B> subroutine is modified by the attributes set with the <B>pixmode </B>subroutine. Please refer to the <A HREF="pixmode.html#bav30marj"><B>pixmode</B></A> subroutine for more detail.</P>

<OL><LI><A NAME="A213X91204b"></A>Both the <B>rectread</B> and <B>lrectread</B> subroutines leave the current character position unpredictable.</LI>

<LI><A NAME="A79C1e1"></A>Do not put the pixel array on the 
stack. Allocate the memory space for the pixel array dynamically, by using the <!--:libs:basetrf1:--><A HREF="../basetrf1/malloc.html#A174921e"><B>malloc</B></A> or <B>calloc</B> command (that is, place it on the heap), or specify it as a 
static variable. Do not specify the pixel array memory space as a block 
scope variable.</LI>

<LI><A NAME="A318C9dbf"></A>These subroutines cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</LI></OL>

<H3><A NAME="A213X91204d"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="d5P2150marj"></A><I>xll </I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>x </I>coordinate of the lower-left corner of the rectangle to be read.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="o5P230marj"></A><I>yll </I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>y</I> coordinate of the lower-left corner of the rectangle to be read.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="I8P210marj"></A><I>xur </I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>x </I>coordinate of the upper-right corner of the rectangle to be read.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="U8P2330marj"></A><I>yur </I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>y</I> coordinate of the upper-right corner of the rectangle to be read.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A139X91ee9"></A><I>parray</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the array to receive the pixels that are read. The returned data in the<I> parray </I>parameter are undefined if the <A HREF="rectread.html#d5P2150marj"><I>xll</I></A> and <A HREF="rectread.html#o5P230marj"><I>yll</I></A> parameters do not specify the lower-left corner of a rectangle that appears completely on the screen.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P><A NAME="E1D731F089ceb"></A>All coordinates are relative to the lower-left corner of the window and not to the screen or viewport.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912050"></A>Return Value</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D731F131ceb"></A>The returned value of this function is the number of pixels that the system actually reads. The returned function value is 0 (zero) if any part of the specified rectangle is off the screen.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D731F157ceb"></A>On the POWER GXT1000 adapter, the returned value of this function is always the width&nbsp;times&nbsp;height of the specified rectangle, or (<I>xur&nbsp;</I>-&nbsp;<I>xll</I>)(<I>yur&nbsp;</I>-&nbsp;<I>yll</I>).</P>


<H3><A NAME="A30C011006"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D731F214ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="paint_c.html#A13C0bd84"><B>paint.c</B></A> uses the <B>rectread</B> subroutine to get the color index value for a single pixel. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A61C0159b5"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D731F258ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1e2"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1e3"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1e4"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X91205d"></A>Related Information</H3>

<P><A NAME="E1D731F380ceb"></A>Controlling the transfer of pixels with the <A HREF="pixmode.html#bav30marj"><B>pixmode</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D731F405ceb"></A>Copying a rectangle of pixels with an optional zoom with the <A HREF="rectcopy.html#A142X9d04"><B>rectcopy</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D731F432ceb"></A>Drawing a rectangular array of pixels into the frame buffer with the <A HREF="rectwrite.html#A142X9c9e"><B>rectwrite </B>or <B>lrectwrite</B></A> subroutine.</P>
```

```html
<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">
<HTML>
<HEAD>
<META HTTP-EQUIV="Content-Type" CONTENT="text/html; charset=iso-8859-1">

<TITLE>rectwrite or lrectwrite Subroutine
</TITLE>
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="rectread.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="rectzoom.html">Next</a>  |
<A href="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A142X9c9e"></A>rectwrite or lrectwrite Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1619" REL="I1" TITLE="rectwrite subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1620" REL="I1" TITLE="lrectwrite subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1621" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1622" REL="I2" TITLE="pixel block transfer"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1623" REL="I3" TITLE="drawing rectangular pixel array into frame buffer"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1624" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1625" REL="I2" TITLE="pixel block transfer"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1626" REL="I3" TITLE="rectwrite"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1627" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1628" REL="I2" TITLE="pixel block transfer"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1629" REL="I3" TITLE="lrectwrite"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A213X91207e"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D732E497ceb"></A>Draws a rectangular array of pixels into the frame buffer.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1e5"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D732E535ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D732E560ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912081"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X912082"></A><B>void rectwrite</B>
<B>(Screencoord </B><A HREF="rectwrite.html#dpP2190marj"><I>xll</I></A><B>, Screencoord </B><A HREF="rectwrite.html#lpP2310marj"><I>yll</I></A><B>, </B>
<B>Screencoord </B><A HREF="rectwrite.html#isP290marj"><I>xur</I></A><B>, Screencoord </B><A HREF="rectwrite.html#usP2f0marj"><I>yur</I></A><B>,</B>
<B>Int16 *</B><A HREF="rectwrite.html#A9tP2350marj"><I>parray</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X912083"></A><B>void lrectwrite</B>
<B>(Screencoord </B><A HREF="rectwrite.html#dpP2190marj"><I>xll</I></A><B>, Screencoord </B><A HREF="rectwrite.html#lpP2310marj"><I>yll</I></A><B>, </B>
<B>Screencoord </B><A HREF="rectwrite.html#isP290marj"><I>xur</I></A><B>, Screencoord </B><A HREF="rectwrite.html#usP2f0marj"><I>yur</I></A><B>, </B>
<B>Int32 *</B><A HREF="rectwrite.html#A9tP2350marj"><I>parray</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010b23"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010b24"></A><B>SUBROUTINE RECTWR(</B><I>xll</I><B>,</B> <I>yll</I><B>,</B> <I>xur</I><B>,</B> <I>yur</I><B>, </B><I>parray</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>xll</I><B>,</B> <I>yll</I><B>,</B> <I>xur</I><B>,</B> <I>yur</I>
<B>INTEGER*2 </B><I>parray</I><B>(1&nbsp;)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010b25"></A><B>SUBROUTINE LRECTW(</B><I>xll</I><B>,</B> <I>yll</I><B>,</B> <I>xur</I><B>,</B> <I>yur</I><B>, </B><I>parray</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>xll</I><B>,</B> <I>yll</I><B>,</B> <I>xur</I><B>,</B> <I>yur</I><B>, </B><I>parray</I><B>(&nbsp;1)</B></PRE>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A79C1e8"></A><B>Note: </B>For FORTRAN users, these subroutines accept long integer parameters (INTEGER*4) when invoked from a FORTRAN program, although they accept short integers when invoked from a C program. The C and FORTRAN syntax shown here reflect this difference.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A213X912087"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D732E731ceb"></A>The <B>rectwrite</B> and <B>lrectwrite </B>subroutines draw pixels taken from the host array specified in the <A HREF="rectwrite.html#A9tP2350marj"><I>parray</I></A> parameter into the specified rectangular 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A270A984a">framebuffer</A> region. Both procedures are functionally the same. They differ only in that the <B>rectwrite </B>subroutine expects 16-bit values, and the <B>lrectwrite</B> subroutine expects 32-bit values. The system draws pixels left to right, then bottom to top. All normal drawing modes apply.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D732E758ceb"></A>When the frame buffer is configured to be 8 bits deep, only the lowest 8 bits of the <I>parray</I> parameter are used to fill the frame buffer. If the frame buffer has been configured to be 12 bits deep (for example, if the system is in color map, singlemap, doublebuffer mode), only the lowest 12 bits are written. If the frame buffer has been configured to be 24 bits deep (for instance, in singlebuffer RGB mode), only the lowest 24 bits are written.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D732E784ceb"></A>Because of the foregoing reasons, using the <B>rectwrite</B> subroutine in 24-bit mode is not logical. Use the <B>lrectwrite</B> subroutine instead. Likewise, do not use the <B>rectwrite</B> subroutine to write into the z-buffer.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D732E810ceb"></A>In a similar manner, these subroutines can be used to write into the overlay or underlay planes. Note that not all supported graphics adapters have 24-bit-deep frame buffers or have z-buffers.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A213X912089"></A><B>Note: </B>Both the <B>rectwrite </B>and <B>lrectwrite</B> subroutines leave the current character position unpredictable. </BLOCKQUOTE>


<P><A NAME="E1D732E855ceb"></A>If the zoom factors set by the <A HREF="rectzoom.html#A142X9d26"><B>rectzoom</B></A> subroutine are both 1.0, the screen region <I>xll </I>through <I>xur</I>, <I>yll </I>through <I>yur</I>, are filled. Other zoom factors result in filling past <I>xur </I>and/or past <I>yur</I> (<I>xll, yll </I>is always the lower left corner of the filled region). </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D732E880ceb"></A>The behavior of the <B>lrectwrite</B> subroutine is modified by the attributes set with the  <B>pixmode </B>subroutine. Please refer to the <A HREF="pixmode.html#bav30marj"><B>pixmode</B></A> subroutine for more detail.</P>

<OL><LI><A NAME="A79C1ea"></A>Do not put the pixel array on the 
stack. Allocate the memory space for the pixel array dynamically, by using the <!--:libs:basetrf1:--><A HREF="../basetrf1/malloc.html#A174921e"><B>malloc</B></A> or <B>calloc</B> command (that is, place it on the heap), or specify it as a 
static variable. Do not specify the pixel array memory space as a block 
scope variable.</LI>

<LI><A NAME="A318C9dc5"></A>These subroutines cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</LI></OL>

<H3><A NAME="A213X91208c"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="dpP2190marj"></A><I>xll </I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>x </I>coordinate of the lower-left corner of the rectangular frame-buffer region.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="lpP2310marj"></A><I>yll </I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>y </I>coordinate of the lower-left corner of the rectangular frame-buffer region.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="isP290marj"></A><I>xur </I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>x </I>coordinate of the upper-right corner of the rectangular frame-buffer region.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="usP2f0marj"></A><I>yur </I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>y </I>coordinate of the upper-right corner of the rectangular frame-buffer region.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A9tP2350marj"></A><I>parray</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the array containing the values of the pixels to be drawn. The size of <I>parray </I>is always (xur-xll+1) x (yur-yll+1). The format of the data in the <I>parray</I> parameter is controlled by the current setting of the <A HREF="pixmode.html#bav30marj"><B>pixmode</B></A> subroutine.


<P>The returned data is undefined if the <A HREF="rectwrite.html#dpP2190marj"><I>xll</I></A> and <A HREF="rectwrite.html#lpP2310marj"><I>yll</I></A> parameters do not specify the lower left corner of a rectangle that appears completely on the screen. All coordinates are relative to the lower left corner of the window, not the screen or viewport.</P></TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A61C0159bb"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D732F117ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1eb"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1ec"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1ed"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X91209a"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D732F214ceb"></A>Copying a rectangle of pixels with an optional zoom with the <A HREF="rectcopy.html#A142X9d04"><B>rectcopy</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D732F239ceb"></A>Controlling the transfer of pixels with the <A HREF="pixmode.html#bav30marj"><B>pixmode</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D732F264ceb"></A>Reading a rectangular array of pixels into host memory with the <A HREF="rectread.html#A142X9c7c"><B>rectread</B> or <B>lrectread</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D732F290ceb"></A>Specifying a zoom factor for rectangle copies and writes with the <A HREF="rectzoom.html#A142X9d26"><B>rectzoom</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D732F316ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A>, Reading and Writing <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/rwpixels.html#rwpixels.html">Pixels</A>, <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/configframebuf.html#configframebuf.html">Configuring the Frame Buffer</A>, and Working in <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/workcolor.html#workcolor.html">Color Map and RGB Modes</A>.</P><hr><center>
```

```html
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A142X9d26"></A>rectzoom Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1630" REL="I1" TITLE="rectzoom subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1631" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1632" REL="I2" TITLE="pixel block transfer"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1633" REL="I3" TITLE="specifying zoom factor for rectangular copies"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1634" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1635" REL="I2" TITLE="pixel block transfer"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1636" REL="I3" TITLE="rectzoom"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A142X9d28"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D733D306ceb"></A>Specifies a zoom factor for rectangle copies and writes.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1ef"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D733D345ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D733D370ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A142X9d2c"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A142X9d2d"></A><B>void rectzoom(Float32 </B><A HREF="rectzoom.html#A142X9d31"><I>xfactor</I></A><B>, Float32</B> <A HREF="rectzoom.html#A142X9d32"><I>yfactor</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010b35"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010b36"></A><B>SUBROUTINE RECTZO(</B><I>xfactor</I><B>,</B> <I>yfactor</I><B>)</B>
<B>REAL </B><I>xfactor</I><B>, </B><I>yfactor</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A142X9d2e"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D733D483ceb"></A>The <B>rectzoom</B> subroutine specifies independent x and y 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A27P040"><I>zoom factors</I></A> that the <A HREF="rectcopy.html#A142X9d04"><B>rectcopy</B></A> and <A HREF="rectwrite.html#A142X9c9e"><B>rectwrite</B></A> subroutines use. Float values are rounded to the nearest integer.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D733D509ceb"></A>The default value for the <I>xfactor</I> and <I>yfactor</I> parameters is 1.0.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9dce"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A142X9d30"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A142X9d31"></A><I>xfactor</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the multiplier of the rectangle in the x direction.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A142X9d32"></A><I>yfactor</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the multiplier of the rectangle in the y direction.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A61C0159c5"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D733D626ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1f2"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1f3"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1f4"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A142X9d46"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D733D723ceb"></A>Copying a rectangle of pixels with an optional zoom with the <A HREF="rectcopy.html#A142X9d04"><B>rectcopy</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D733D748ceb"></A>Drawing a rectangular array of pixels into the frame buffer with the <A HREF="rectwrite.html#A142X9c9e"><B>rectwrite</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D733D774ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A> and Reading and Writing <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/rwpixels.html#rwpixels.html">Pixels</A>.</P><hr><center>
```

```html
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A7LQ3b0marj"></A>reshapeviewport Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1637" REL="I1" TITLE="reshapeviewport subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1638" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1639" REL="I2" TITLE="viewport"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1640" REL="I3" TITLE="reshapeviewport"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1641" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1642" REL="I2" TITLE="viewport"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1643" REL="I3" TITLE="setting dimensions to window"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A318C9e29"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D734B936ceb"></A>Sets the viewport to the dimensions of the current window.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1285"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D734B976ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D734C000ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A318C9e2c"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A318C9e2d"></A><B>void reshapeviewport(&nbsp;)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010b6e"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010b6f"></A><B>SUBROUTINE RESHAP(&nbsp;)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A318C9e30"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D734C109ceb"></A>The <B>reshapeviewport</B> subroutine sets the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A27P039">viewport</A> to the dimensions of the current window.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D734C134ceb"></A>The <B>reshapeviewport</B> subroutine is equivalent to:</P>
<PRE><A NAME="A318C9e33"></A>long xsize, ysize;
getsize(&amp;xsize, &amp;ysize);
viewport(0, xsize-1, 0, ysize-1);</PRE>

<P><A NAME="E1D734C179ceb"></A>Use the <B>reshapeviewport</B> subroutine when REDRAW events are received. It is most useful in programs that are independent of the size and shape of the viewport.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9e35"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A30C011031"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D734C240ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="scrn_rotate_c.html#A16C0c92f"><B>scrn_rotate.c</B></A> uses the <B>reshapeviewport</B> subroutine to reshape the viewport on a REDRAW event. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015d52"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D734C283ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1288"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1289"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C128a"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A318C9e3d"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D734C380ceb"></A>Clearing the viewport with the <A HREF="clear.html#cEH1160marj"><B>clear</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D734C405ceb"></A>Returning the position of a window with the <A HREF="getorigin.html#A142X91f76"><B>getorigin</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D734C431ceb"></A>Returning the size of a window with the <A HREF="getsize.html#X513200marj"><B>getsize</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D734C457ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A> and Using <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/useviewprts.html#useviewprts.html">Viewports and Screenmasks</A>.</P><hr><center>
```

```html
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A143X9394"></A>RGBcolor Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1644" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1645" REL="I2" TITLE="attribute"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1646" REL="I3" TITLE="RGBcolor"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1647" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1648" REL="I2" TITLE="color"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1649" REL="I3" TITLE="current"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1650" REL="I1" TITLE="RGBcolor subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9396"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7359831ceb"></A>Sets the current color in RGB mode.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A77C1309"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7359870ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7359895ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X939a"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A143X939b"></A><B>RGBcolor</B>
<B>(short </B><A HREF="RGBcolor.html#A143X939f"><I>red</I></A><B>,</B> <B>short </B><A HREF="RGBcolor.html#A143X93a0"><I>green</I></A><B>,</B> <B>short </B><A HREF="RGBcolor.html#A143X93a1"><I>blue</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A19C0e0e2"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A19C0e0e3"></A><B>SUBROUTINE RGBCOL(</B><I>red</I><B>,</B> <I>green</I><B>,</B> <I>blue</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>red</I><B>,</B> <I>green</I><B>,</B> <I>blue</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X939c"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D735A008ceb"></A>The <B>RGBcolor</B> subroutine sets the current color when the system is in 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0743">RGB mode</A>. The lower-order 8 bits of the three arguments control the intensity of red, green, and blue colors displayed on the screen. The system writes these numbers directly into the bitplanes whenever it draws a pixel. </P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A213X91221a"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine is available only in 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0743">RGB mode</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A143X939e"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X939f"></A><I>red</I>  </TD>
<TD>  Specifies a value indicating the intensity of the color red to be displayed on the screen. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X93a0"></A><I>green</I>  </TD>
<TD>  Specifies a value indicating the intensity of the color green to be displayed on the screen.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X93a1"></A><I>blue</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies a value indicating the intensity of the color blue to be displayed on the screen.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015c73"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D735A145ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A77C130c"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C130d"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C130e"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A258C01c3be"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D735A243ceb"></A>Setting the current color in RGB mode with the <A HREF="c.html#A143X9262"><B>c</B></A> subroutine. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D735A268ceb"></A>Setting the current color in color map mode with the <A HREF="color.html#A146X9429"><B>color</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D735A294ceb"></A>Setting the current color as a packed 32-bit integer with the <A HREF="cpack.html#A143X9284"><B>cpack</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D735A319ceb"></A>Returning the current RGB value with the <A HREF="gRGBcolor.html#ESL13a0marj"><B>gRGBcolor</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D735A345ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/setglattrib.html#setglattrib.html">Setting Drawing Attributes</A>, Understanding the <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/glintro.html#A8G44310marj">Hardware Used by GL</A>,Working in <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/workcolor.html#workcolor.html">Color Map and RGB Modes</A>.</P><hr><center>
```

```html
<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>

<a href="RGBwritemask.html">Next</a>  |

 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>

<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A143X93b6"></A>RGBmode Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1651" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1652" REL="I2" TITLE="color map and RGB mode"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1653" REL="I3" TITLE="RGBmode"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1654" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1655" REL="I2" TITLE="display mode"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1656" REL="I3" TITLE="setting to RGB mode"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1657" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1658" REL="I2" TITLE="RGB mode"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1659" REL="I3" TITLE="setting display mode to"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1660" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1661" REL="I2" TITLE="color map"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1662" REL="I3" TITLE="setting display mode to bypass"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1663" REL="I1" TITLE="RGBmode subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A143X93b8"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7369986ceb"></A>Sets a display mode that bypasses the color map.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C160"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D736A025ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D736A049ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X93bc"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A143X93bd"></A><B>void RGBmode(&nbsp;)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A18C0dcf2"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A18C0dcf3"></A><B>SUBROUTINE RGBMOD</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X93be"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D736A157ceb"></A>The <B>RGBmode</B> subroutine makes the system interpret the contents of the main frame buffer as 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A255B9de">RGB values</A>. All drawing subroutines write values of red, green, and blue directly into the bitplanes; the contents of the frame buffer, in turn, directly control the intensity of the color displayed on the monitor.  </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D736A183ceb"></A>When the frame buffer is 24 bits deep, 8 bits each of red, green, and blue are stored. When the frame buffer is 12 bits deep, the 4 most significant bits of each of the red, green, and blue are stored. When the frame buffer is 8 bits deep, the 3 most significant bits of each of the red and green, and the 2 most significant bits of blue are stored. To improve the visual quality of the displayed image, 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A137915eb">dithering</A> is automatically turned on whenever the frame buffer is 8 bits deep.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D736A209ceb"></A>The depth of the frame buffer depends on the installed adapter, and on how it has been configured. In particular, the <A HREF="doublebuffer.html#A145X91a7"><B>doublebuffer</B></A> and <A HREF="singlebuffer.html#A145X9259"><B>singlebuffer</B></A> subroutines affect the configuration of the main frame buffer.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D736A234ceb"></A>The system will not enter into RGB mode until the <A HREF="gconfig.html#hS4260nita"><B>gconfig</B></A> subroutine is called.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9ca8"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A143X93d0"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D736A296ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D736A322ceb"></A>The <B>RGBmode</B> subroutine is useful for monitors with 12 or more bitplanes.</P>

<P><A NAME="A3CFD333938janb"></A>The POWERgraphics GXT1000 will ignore the<B> RGBmode</B> subroutine when applied to windows created with the <B>winX</B> subroutine. The <B>RGBmode</B> subroutine can be used with windows created with the <B>winopen</B> subroutine.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A30C010fd0"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D736A363ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="localatten_c.html#A10C0abc5"><B>localatten.c</B></A> puts the system in RGB mode with the <B>RGBmode</B> subroutine to perform lighting calculations. This lets the system calculate the correct colors for realistic shading.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C163"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C164"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C165"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A258C01c43f"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D736A461ceb"></A>Setting color map mode as the current mode with the <A HREF="cmode.html#A146X93d6"><B>cmode</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D736A486ceb"></A>Reconfiguring the system with the <A HREF="gconfig.html#hS4260nita"><B>gconfig</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D736A512ceb"></A>Returning the current display mode with the <A HREF="getdisplaymode.html#A145X9206"><B>getdisplaymode</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D736A537ceb"></A>Working in <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/workcolor.html#workcolor.html">Color Map and RGB Modes</A>.</P><hr><center>
```

```html
<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">
<HTML>
<HEAD>
<META HTTP-EQUIV="Content-Type" CONTENT="text/html; charset=iso-8859-1">

<TITLE>RGBwritemask Subroutine
</TITLE>
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="RGBmode.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="ringbell.html">Next</a>  |
<A href="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A143X93fa"></A>RGBwritemask Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1664" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1665" REL="I2" TITLE="frame buffer update control"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1666" REL="I3" TITLE="RGBwritemask"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1667" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1668" REL="I2" TITLE="bitplanes"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1669" REL="I3" TITLE="granting write permission to in RGB mode"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1670" REL="I1" TITLE="RGBwritemask subroutine (GL)"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A143X93fc"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7378285ceb"></A>Grants write access to a subset of available bitplanes.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C11fc"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7378325ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7378349ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9400"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A143X9401"></A><B>void RGBwritemask</B>
<B>(Int16 </B><A HREF="RGBwritemask.html#A143X9405"><I>red</I></A><B>,</B>
<B>Int16 </B><A HREF="RGBwritemask.html#A143X9406"><I>green</I></A><B>,</B>
<B>Int16 </B><A HREF="RGBwritemask.html#A143X9407"><I>blue</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A28C010777"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A28C010778"></A><B>SUBROUTINE RGBWRI(</B><I>red</I><B>, </B><I>green</I><B>, </B><I>blue</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>red</I><B>, </B><I>green</I><B>, </B><I>blue</I></PRE>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A78C11ff"></A><B>Note: </B>For FORTRAN users, this subroutine accepts long integer parameters (INTEGER*4) when invoked from a FORTRAN program, although it accepts short integers when invoked from a C program. The C and FORTRAN syntax shown here reflect this difference.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A143X9402"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7378482ceb"></A>The <B>RGBwritemask</B> subroutine sets the bitplane writemask in RGB mode. Writemasks are used to shield portions of the frame buffer from being written into. A writemask is a small set of bits (3 masks of 8 bits each in RGB mode), one bit for each bitplane of the frame buffer. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7378508ceb"></A>If a bit is set (1), the corresponding bitplane is enabled for writing, and any routine that draws into the frame buffer will be able to write into that bitplane. If a bit is reset (0), the corresponding bitplane is marked as read only, and the values stored in that bitplane are not changed.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7378534ceb"></A>Note that the writemask protects planes in the color frame buffer. Thus, writemasks essentially prevent certain colors from being written into the frame buffer. Colors that are drawn while a writemask is enabled appear different, depending on the color, the writemask, and the color value currently stored in the frame buffer (at a given pixel).</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7378560ceb"></A>Writemasks are useful for emulating overlay/underlay planes.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7378586ceb"></A>The <B>RGBwritemask</B> subroutine is intended for use in RGB mode only. To set the writemask in color map mode, use the <A HREF="writemask.html#A143X9592"><B>writemask</B></A> or <A HREF="wmpack.html#A143X9570"><B>wmpack</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9404"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X9405"></A><I>red</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the mask for the corresponding red bitplanes.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X9406"></A><I>green</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the mask for the corresponding green bitplanes.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X9407"></A><I>blue</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the mask for the corresponding blue bitplanes.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A64C0165d5"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7378703ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7378728ceb"></A>The POWER GXT1000 adapter supports only on/off control of individual R, G, and B bitplanes. Individual bits cannot be masked in the color planes.</P>


<H3><A NAME="A78C1200"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C1201"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C1202"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A258C01c4fd"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7378825ceb"></A>Returning the current RGB value with the <A HREF="gRGBcolor.html#ESL13a0marj"><B>gRGBcolor</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7378901ceb"></A>Granting write permission to available bitplanes with the <A HREF="writemask.html#A143X9592"><B>writemask</B></A> subroutine.</P>
```

```html
<H2><A NAME="A213X911463"></A>ringbell Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1671" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1672" REL="I2" TITLE="keyboard control"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1673" REL="I3" TITLE="ringbell"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1674" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1675" REL="I2" TITLE="keyboard bell"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1676" REL="I3" TITLE="ringing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1677" REL="I1" TITLE="ringbell subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911465"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7387067ceb"></A>Rings the keyboard bell.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C12b1"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7387107ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7387131ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911468"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X911469"></A><B>void ringbell(&nbsp;)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X911442"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X911445"></A><B>SUBROUTINE RINGBE</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X91146c"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7387239ceb"></A>The <B>ringbell</B> subroutine rings the 
keyboard
 bell for the length of time set by the <B>setbell</B> subroutine.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9e7c"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A30C01103c"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7387299ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="overlay_c.html#A11C0b47c"><B>ovrlay.c</B></A> uses the <B>ringbell</B> subroutine to ring the bell as a ball moves. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015d5c"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7387343ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C12b4"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C12b5"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C12b6"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X91147b"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7387439ceb"></A>Turning off the keyboard click with the <A HREF="clkoff.html#A213X9112de"><B>clkoff</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7387465ceb"></A>Turning on the keyboard click with the <A HREF="clkoff.html#A213X9112de"><B>clkon</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7387490ceb"></A>Turning on the keyboard display lights with the <A HREF="lampoff.html#A213X9113bc"><B>lampon</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7387516ceb"></A>Setting the duration of the keyboard bell sound with the <A HREF="setbell.html#A213X9114ae"><B>setbell</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7387542ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A> and <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/keyboardgl.html#keyboardgl.html">Using the Keyboard</A>.</P><hr><center>
```

```html
<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">

</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">

<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="kzf90marj"></A>rmv  Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1678" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1679" REL="I2" TITLE="moveraw style"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1680" REL="I3" TITLE="rmv"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1681" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1682" REL="I2" TITLE="graphics position"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1683" REL="I3" TITLE="moving relative to current point"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1684" REL="I1" TITLE="rmv subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912e24"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7396719ceb"></A>Moves the graphics position relative to the current point.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C131b"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7396792ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7396817ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912e27"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X912e28"></A><B>void rmv</B>
<B>(Coord </B><A HREF="rmv.html#A213X912e30"><I>dx</I></A><B>, Coord</B> <A HREF="rmv.html#A213X912e31"><I>dy</I></A><B>, Coord</B> <A HREF="rmv.html#A213X912e32"><I>dz</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="T8f70marj"></A><B>void rmvi</B>
<B>(Icoord </B><A HREF="rmv.html#A213X912e30"><I>dx</I></A><B>, Icoord</B> <A HREF="rmv.html#A213X912e31"><I>dy</I></A><B>, Icoord</B> <A HREF="rmv.html#A213X912e32"><I>dz</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="f8f170marj"></A><B>void rmvs</B>
<B>(Scoord </B><A HREF="rmv.html#A213X912e30"><I>dx</I></A><B>, Scoord</B> <A HREF="rmv.html#A213X912e31"><I>dy</I></A><B>, Scoord</B> <A HREF="rmv.html#A213X912e32"><I>dz</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="H9fd0marj"></A><B>void rmv2</B>
<B>(Coord </B><A HREF="rmv.html#A213X912e30"><I>dx</I></A><B>, Coord</B> <A HREF="rmv.html#A213X912e31"><I>dy</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="W9f170marj"></A><B>void rmv2i</B>
<B>(Icoord </B><A HREF="rmv.html#A213X912e30"><I>dx</I></A><B>, Icoord</B> <A HREF="rmv.html#A213X912e31"><I>dy</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="k9f250marj"></A><B>void rmv2s</B>
<B>(Scoord </B><A HREF="rmv.html#A213X912e30"><I>dx</I></A><B>, Scoord</B> <A HREF="rmv.html#A213X912e31"><I>dy</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010afa"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010afb"></A><B>SUBROUTINE RMV(</B><I>dx</I><B>, </B><I>dy</I><B>, </B><I>dz</I><B>)</B>
<B>REAL </B><I>dx</I><B>, </B><I>dy</I><B>, </B><I>dz</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010afc"></A><B>SUBROUTINE RMVI(</B><I>dx</I><B>, </B><I>dy</I><B>, </B><I>dz</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>dx</I><B>, </B><I>dy</I><B>, </B><I>dz</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010afd"></A><B>SUBROUTINE RMVS(</B><I>dx</I><B>, </B><I>dy</I><B>, </B><I>dz</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*2 </B><I>dx</I><B>, </B><I>dy</I><B>, </B><I>dz</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010afe"></A><B>SUBROUTINE RMV2(</B><I>dx</I><B>, </B><I>dy</I><B>)</B>
<B>REAL </B><I>dx</I><B>, </B><I>dy</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010aff"></A><B>SUBROUTINE RMV2I(</B><I>dx</I><B>, </B><I>dy</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>dx</I><B>, </B><I>dy</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010b00"></A><B>SUBROUTINE RMV2S(</B><I>dx</I><B>, </B><I>dy</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*2 </B><I>dx</I><B>, </B><I>dy</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912e2b"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7397120ceb"></A>The <B>rmv</B> subroutine is the relative version of the <A HREF="move.html#pofmarj"><B>move</B></A> subroutine. It moves the graphics position (without drawing) the specified amount relative to its current value. The value of <B>rmv2(</B><I>x</I><B>,</B><I> y</I><B>) </B>is equivalent to <B>rmv(</B><I>x</I><B>,</B><I> y</I><B>, </B>0.0<B>)</B>. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7397145ceb"></A>The six different forms for the <B>rmv</B> subroutine are as follows:</P>

<TABLE BORDER="2"><TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><BR></TD>

<TD><B>2-D</B></TD>

<TD><B>3-D</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>Int16</TD>

<TD>rmv2s</TD>

<TD>rmvs</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>Int32</TD>

<TD>rmv2i</TD>

<TD>rmvi</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>float</TD>

<TD>rmv2</TD>

<TD>rmv</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P><A NAME="E1D7397188ceb"></A>The <A HREF="rmv.html#A213X912e27">syntax</A> for each of the subroutine forms is the same except for the parameter type. They differ only in that <A HREF="rmv.html#A213X912e28"><B>rmv</B></A> expects real coordinates, <A HREF="rmv.html#T8f70marj"><B>rmvi</B></A> expects integer coordinates, and <A HREF="rmv.html#f8f170marj"><B>rmvs</B></A> expects short integer coordinates. In addition, the <A HREF="rmv.html#H9fd0marj"><B>rmv2</B></A>* routines assume a 2-D point instead of a 3-D point.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912e2f"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912e30"></A><I>dx</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the distance from the <I>x</I> coordinate of the current graphics position to the <I>x</I> coordinate of the new point.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912e31"></A><I>dy</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the distance from the <I>y</I> coordinate of the current graphics position to the <I>y</I> coordinate of the new point.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912e32"></A><I>dz</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the distance from the <I>z</I> coordinate of the current graphics position to the <I>z</I> coordinate of the new point.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015d22"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7397321ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C131e"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C131f"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C1320"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912e40"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7397418ceb"></A>Drawing a line with the <A HREF="draw.html#EYf2e0marj"><B>draw</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7397444ceb"></A>Moving the current graphics position to a specified point with the <A HREF="move.html#pofmarj"><B>move</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7397469ceb"></A>Drawing a relative line with the <A HREF="rdr.html#gpf1c0marj"><B>rdr</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7397495ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A> and Drawing with <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/move-draw.html">Move-Draw Style</A> Subroutines.</P><hr><center>
[  <a href="ringbell.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="rot.html">Next</a>  |

 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
</center></BODY>

</HTML>
```

```html
<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">
<HTML>
<HEAD>
<META HTTP-EQUIV="Content-Type" CONTENT="text/html; charset=iso-8859-1">

<TITLE>rot  Subroutine
</TITLE>
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="rmv.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="rotate.html">Next</a>  |
<A href="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A144X9562"></A>rot  Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1685" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1686" REL="I2" TITLE="coordinate transformation"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1687" REL="I3" TITLE="rot"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1688" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1689" REL="I2" TITLE="graphical primitives"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1690" REL="I3" TITLE="rotating (floating point version)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1691" REL="I1" TITLE="rot subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A144X9564"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D73A5607ceb"></A>Rotates graphical primitives (floating-point version).</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C1aa"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D73A5646ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D73A5670ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A144X9568"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A144X9569"></A><B>void rot(Float 32 </B><A HREF="rot.html#dOO1e0marj"><I>angle</I></A><B>, Char8</B> <A HREF="rot.html#rOO1340marj"><I>axis</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A15C0c6fa"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A15C0c6fb"></A><B>SUBROUTINE ROT(</B><I>angle</I><B>, </B><I>axis</I><B>) </B>
<B>REAL </B><I>angle</I>
<B>CHARACTER*1 </B><I>axis</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A144X956a"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D73A5783ceb"></A>The <B>rot </B>subroutine specifies an angle (<A HREF="rot.html#dOO1e0marj"><I>angle</I></A>) and an axis of rotation (<A HREF="rot.html#rOO1340marj"><I>axis</I></A>). The floating point angle is given in degrees according to the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A154P11365">right-hand rule</A>. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D73A5809ceb"></A>The <B>rot </B>subroutine is a modeling routine; it changes the current 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A27P021">transformation</A> matrix. All objects drawn after the <B>rot </B>subroutine executes are rotated. Use the <A HREF="pushmatrix.html#A144X9540"><B>pushmatrix</B></A> and <A HREF="popmatrix.html#A144X951e"><B>popmatrix</B></A> subroutines to preserve and restore unrotated modeling coordinates. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A144X956c"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="dOO1e0marj"></A><I>angle</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the angle of rotation of an object. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="rOO1340marj"></A><I>axis</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the relative axis of rotation. There are three values defined for this parameter (the character may be upper- or lowercase): </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X9126ef"></A><B></B></TD>
<TD>  x, X indicates the x-axis. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X9126f0"></A><B></B></TD>
<TD>  y, Y indicates the y-axis. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X9126f1"></A><B></B></TD>
<TD>  z, Z indicates the z-axis. </TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010b60"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D73A5968ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="cylinder1_c.html#Ggi2e0marj"><B>cylinder1.c</B></A> uses the <B>rot</B> subroutine to rotate a cylinder about the y- and z-axes. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015d3a"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D73A6012ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C1ad"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C1ae"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C1af"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A144X9582"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D73A6108ceb"></A>Popping the transformation matrix stack with the <A HREF="popmatrix.html#A144X951e"><B>popmatrix</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D73A6133ceb"></A>Pushing down the transformation matrix stack with the <A HREF="pushmatrix.html#A144X9540"><B>pushmatrix</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D73A6162ceb"></A>Rotating a graphical primitive (fixed-point version) with the <A HREF="rotate.html#A8g2120marj"><B>rotate</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D73A6188ceb"></A>Scaling and mirroring objects with the <A HREF="scale.html#A144X95a6"><B>scale</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D73A6213ceb"></A>Translating a graphical primitive with the <A HREF="translate.html#A144X95c8"><B>translate</B></A> subroutine.</P>
```

```html
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A8g2120marj"></A>rotate  Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1692" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1693" REL="I2" TITLE="coordinate transformation"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1694" REL="I3" TITLE="rotate"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1695" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1696" REL="I2" TITLE="graphical primitive"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1697" REL="I3" TITLE="rotating (fixed point version)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1698" REL="I1" TITLE="rotate subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A213X9126f7"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D73B3814ceb"></A>Rotates graphical primitives (fixed-point version).</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C1b1"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D73B3852ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D73B3877ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X9126fa"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X9126fb"></A><B>void rotate(Angle </B><A HREF="rotate.html#A213X912702"><I>angle</I></A><B>, Char8 </B><A HREF="rotate.html#A213X912703"><I>axis</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A15C0c6fd"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A15C0c6fe"></A><B>SUBROUTINE ROTATE(</B><I>angle</I><B>, </B><I>axis</I><B>) </B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>angle</I>
<B>CHARACTER*1 </B><I>axis</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X9126fe"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D73B3990ceb"></A>The <B>rotate </B>subroutine specifies an angle (<A HREF="rot.html#dOO1e0marj"><I>angle</I></A>) and an axis of rotation (<A HREF="rot.html#rOO1340marj"><I>axis</I></A>). The fixed- point angle is given in tenths of a degree according to the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A154P11365">right-hand rule</A>. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D73B4016ceb"></A>The <B>rotate </B>subroutine is a modeling routine; it changes the current 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A27P021">transformation</A> matrix. All objects drawn after the <B>rotate </B>subroutine executes are rotated. Use the <A HREF="pushmatrix.html#A144X9540"><B>pushmatrix</B></A> and <A HREF="popmatrix.html#A144X951e"><B>popmatrix</B></A> subroutines to preserve and restore unrotated modeling coordinates. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912701"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912702"></A><I>angle</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the angle of rotation of an object. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912703"></A><I>axis</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the relative axis of rotation. There are six values defined for this parameter (the character may be upper- or lowercase): </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912704"></A><B></B></TD>
<TD>  x, <B>X</B> indicates the x-axis. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912705"></A><B></B></TD>
<TD>  y, <B>Y</B> indicates the y-axis. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912706"></A><B></B></TD>
<TD>  z, <B>Z</B> indicates the z-axis. </TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912707"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D73B4174ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="backface_c.html#A16C0c7a2"><B>backface.c</B></A> uses the <B>rotate</B> modeling subroutine to alter the current transformation matrix when modelling the sides of a cube using a square.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015d3c"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D73B4218ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C1b4"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C1b5"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C1b6"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912712"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D73B4315ceb"></A>Popping the transformation matrix stack with the <A HREF="popmatrix.html#A144X951e"><B>popmatrix</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D73B4340ceb"></A>Pushing down the transformation matrix stack with the <A HREF="pushmatrix.html#A144X9540"><B>pushmatrix</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D73B4366ceb"></A>Rotating a graphical primitive (floating-point version) with the <A HREF="rot.html#A144X9562"><B>rot</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D73B4391ceb"></A>Scaling and mirroring objects with the <A HREF="scale.html#A144X95a6"><B>scale</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D73B4417ceb"></A>Translating a graphical primitive with the <A HREF="translate.html#A144X95c8"><B>translate</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D73B4442ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A> and Working with <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/workcoords.html#workcoords.html">Coordinate Systems</A>.</P><hr><center>
```

```html
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="O5k2marj"></A>rpatch Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1699" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1700" REL="I2" TITLE="wire frame curve and surface patch"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1701" REL="I3" TITLE="rpatch"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1702" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1703" REL="I2" TITLE="surface patch, wire frame"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1704" REL="I3" TITLE="rational"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1705" REL="I1" TITLE="rpatch subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912564"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D73C5006ceb"></A>Draws a rational surface patch.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C1141"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D73C5045ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D73C5069ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912567"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X912568"></A><B>void rpatch</B>
<B>(Matrix </B><A HREF="rpatch.html#QQk2a0marj"><I>geomx</I></A><B>, Matrix</B> <A HREF="rpatch.html#ERk2240marj"><I>geomy</I></A><B>,</B>
<B>Matrix</B> <A HREF="rpatch.html#hTk22e0marj"><I>geomz</I></A><B>, Matrix</B> <A HREF="rpatch.html#qTk2100marj"><I>geomw</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A26C0fdeb"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A26C0fdec"></A><B>SUBROUTINE RPATCH(</B><I>geomx</I>, <I>geomy</I>, <I>geomz, geomw</I><B>)</B>
<B>REAL </B><I>geomx</I><B>(4,4), </B><I>geomy</I><B>(4,4), </B><I>geomz</I><B>(4,4), </B><I>geomw</I><B>(4,4)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X91256b"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D73C5183ceb"></A>The <B>rpatch</B> subroutine draws a rational 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P06f7">surface patch</A> using the current settings from the <A HREF="patchbasis.html#A143X95d6"><B>patchbasis</B></A>, <A HREF="patchprecision.html#A143X961a"><B>patchprecision</B></A>, and <A HREF="patchcurves.html#A143X95f8"><B>patchcurves</B></A> subroutines. The 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A25P03e7">control points</A> <A HREF="rpatch.html#QQk2a0marj"><I>geomx</I></A>, <A HREF="rpatch.html#ERk2240marj"><I>geomy</I></A>, <A HREF="rpatch.html#hTk22e0marj"><I>geomz</I></A><I>, </I>and <A HREF="rpatch.html#qTk2100marj"><I>geomw</I></A> determine the shape of the patch.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X91256d"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="QQk2a0marj"></A><I>geomx</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies a 4x4 matrix containing the <I>x</I> coordinates of the 16 control points of the patch.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="ERk2240marj"></A><I>geomy</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies a 4x4 matrix containing the <I>y</I> coordinates of the 16 control points of the patch.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="hTk22e0marj"></A><I>geomz</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies a 4x4 matrix containing the <I>z</I> coordinates of the 16 control points of the patch.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="qTk2100marj"></A><I>geomw</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies a 4x4 matrix containing the <I>w</I> coordinates of the 16 control points of the patch.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A64C0165a2"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D73C5319ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C1144"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C1145"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C1146"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912572"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D73C5418ceb"></A>Defining a cubic spline basis matrix with the <A HREF="defbasis.html#A150X930"><B>defbasis</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D73C5443ceb"></A>Drawing a surface patch with the <A HREF="patch.html#A143X95b4"><B>patch</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D73C5468ceb"></A>Setting the current spline surface basis matrices with the <A HREF="patchbasis.html#A143X95d6"><B>patchbasis</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D73C5494ceb"></A>Setting the number of curves used to represent a patch with the <A HREF="patchcurves.html#A143X95f8"><B>patchcurves</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D73C5519ceb"></A>Setting the precision at which curves are drawn with the <A HREF="patchprecision.html#A143X961a"><B>patchprecision</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D73C5545ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A>, Drawing <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawnurbs.html#drawnurbs.html">NURBS Curves and Surfaces</A>, and Drawing <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/drawwfcvs.html#drawwfcvs.html">Wire Frame Curves and Surface Patches</A>.</P><hr><center>
```

```html
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="hrfa0marj"></A>rpdr Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1706" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1707" REL="I2" TITLE="moveraw style"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1708" REL="I3" TITLE="rpdr"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1709" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1710" REL="I2" TITLE="polygons"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1711" REL="I3" TITLE="drawing relative"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1712" REL="I1" TITLE="rpdr subroutine (GL)"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A213X912e6e"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D73D3476ceb"></A>Performs a relative polygon draw.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C1321"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D73D3515ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D73D3540ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912e71"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X912e72"></A><B>void rpdr</B>
<B>(Coord </B><A HREF="rpdr.html#A213X912e7d"><I>dx</I></A><B>, Coord</B> <A HREF="rpdr.html#A213X912e7e"><I>dy</I></A><B>, Coord</B> <A HREF="rpdr.html#A213X912e7f"><I>dz</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="QQf370marj"></A><B>void rpdri</B>
<B>(Icoord </B><A HREF="rpdr.html#A213X912e7d"><I>dx</I></A><B>, Icoord</B> <A HREF="rpdr.html#A213X912e7e"><I>dy</I></A><B>, Icoord</B> <A HREF="rpdr.html#A213X912e7f"><I>dz</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="cQf230marj"></A><B>void rpdrs</B>
<B>(Scoord </B><A HREF="rpdr.html#A213X912e7d"><I>dx</I></A><B>, Scoord</B> <A HREF="rpdr.html#A213X912e7e"><I>dy</I></A><B>, Scoord</B> <A HREF="rpdr.html#A213X912e7f"><I>dz</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="pQf1f0marj"></A><B>void rpdr2</B>
<B>(Coord </B><A HREF="rpdr.html#A213X912e7d"><I>dx</I></A><B>, Coord</B> <A HREF="rpdr.html#A213X912e7e"><I>dy</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A2Rf230marj"></A><B>void rpdr2i</B>
<B>(Icoord </B><A HREF="rpdr.html#A213X912e7d"><I>dx</I></A><B>, Icoord</B> <A HREF="rpdr.html#A213X912e7e"><I>dy</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="ERf230marj"></A><B>void rpdr2s</B>
<B>(Scoord </B><A HREF="rpdr.html#A213X912e7d"><I>dx</I></A><B>, Scoord</B> <A HREF="rpdr.html#A213X912e7e"><I>dy</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010b0d"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010b0e"></A><B>SUBROUTINE RPDR(</B><I>dx</I><B>, </B><I>dy</I><B>, </B><I>dz</I><B>)</B>
<B>REAL </B><I>dx</I><B>, </B><I>dy</I><B>, </B><I>dz</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010b0f"></A><B>SUBROUTINE RPDRI(</B><I>dx</I><B>, </B><I>dy</I><B>, </B><I>dz</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>dx</I><B>, </B><I>dy</I><B>, </B><I>dz</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010b10"></A><B>SUBROUTINE RPDRS(</B><I>dx</I><B>, </B><I>dy</I><B>, </B><I>dz</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*2 </B><I>dx</I><B>, </B><I>dy</I><B>, </B><I>dz</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010b11"></A><B>SUBROUTINE RPDR2(</B><I>dx</I><B>, </B><I>dy</I><B>)</B>
<B>REAL </B><I>dx</I><B>, </B><I>dy</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010b12"></A><B>SUBROUTINE RPDR2I(</B><I>dx</I><B>, </B><I>dy</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>dx</I><B>, </B><I>dy</I></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010b13"></A><B>SUBROUTINE RPDR2S(</B><I>dx</I><B>, </B><I>dy</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*2 </B><I>dx</I><B>, </B><I>dy</I></PRE>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A78C1324"></A><B>Note: </B>For FORTRAN users, the INTEGER*2 versions of this subroutine, <B>RPDRS</B> and <B>RPDR2S</B>, should not be called with integer constant parameters. For example, 2 is an integer constant; JJ is an integer variable. The XL FORTRAN compiler, invoked by the <B>xlf</B> command, stores all integer constants as long integers (INTEGER*4), not as short integers (INTEGER*2). Invoking one of the short versions of this subroutine with an integer constant will result in unexpected behavior.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A213X912e75"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D73D3862ceb"></A>The <B>rpdr</B> subroutine is the relative version of the <A HREF="pdr.html#bqf1c0marj"><B>pdr</B></A> subroutine. It specifies the next point in a filled polygon, using the previous point (the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A25P03eb">current graphics position</A>) as the origin.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D73D3888ceb"></A>There can be no more than 256 vertices in a polygon. Therefore, there can be no more than 255 calls to the <B>rpdr</B> subroutine between calls to the <A HREF="rpmv.html#lXf370marj"><B>rpmv</B></A> and <A HREF="pclos.html#t2g270marj"><B>pclos</B></A> subroutines. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D73D3914ceb"></A>The <B>rpdr</B> subroutine updates the current graphics position. The next routine starts drawing from that point. </P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A213X912e79"></A><B>Note: </B>Do not place routines that invalidate the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A25P03eb">current graphics position</A> within sequences of moves and draws.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<P><A NAME="E1D73D3959ceb"></A>The six different forms for the <B>rpdr</B> subroutine are as follows:</P>

<TABLE BORDER="2"><TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><BR></TD>

<TD><B>2-D</B></TD>

<TD><B>3-D</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>Int16</TD>

<TD>rpdr2s</TD>

<TD>rpdrs</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>Int32</TD>

<TD>rpdr2i</TD>

<TD>rpdri</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>float</TD>

<TD>rpdr2</TD>

<TD>rpdr </TD></TR></TABLE>

<P><A NAME="E1D73D4001ceb"></A>The syntax for each of the subroutine forms is the same except for the parameter type. They differ only in that <A HREF="rpdr.html#A213X912e72"><B>rpdr</B></A> expects real coordinates, <A HREF="rpdr.html#QQf370marj"><B>rpdri</B></A> expects integer coordinates, and <A HREF="rpdr.html#cQf230marj"><B>rpdrs</B></A> expects short integer coordinates. In addition, the <A HREF="rpdr.html#pQf1f0marj"><B>rpdr2</B></A> routines assume a 2-D point instead of a 3-D point.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912e7c"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912e7d"></A><I>dx</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the distance from the <I>x</I> coordinate of the current graphics position to the <I>x</I> coordinate of the next corner of the polygon.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912e7e"></A><I>dy</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the distance from the <I>y</I> coordinate of the current graphics position to the <I>y</I> coordinate of the next corner of the polygon.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A213X912e7f"></A><I>dz</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the distance from the <I>z</I> coordinate of the current graphics position to the <I>z</I> coordinate of the next corner of the polygon.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015d26"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D73D4119ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C1325"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C1326"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C1327"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X912e8d"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D73D4216ceb"></A>Allowing the system to draw concave polygons with the <A HREF="concave.html#HXf320marj"><B>concave</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D73D4241ceb"></A>Closing a filled polygon with the <A HREF="pclos.html#t2g270marj"><B>pclos</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D73D4267ceb"></A>Specifying the next point in a polygon with the <A HREF="pdr.html#bqf1c0marj"><B>pdr</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D73D4292ceb"></A>Specifying the starting point for a polygon with the <A HREF="pmv.html#A139X91eed"><B>pmv</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D73D4318ceb"></A>Moving the current graphics position to a starting point for a filled polygon relative to the current point with the <A HREF="rpmv.html#lXf370marj"><B>rpmv</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D73D4343ceb"></A>Selecting the shading model used to draw a polygon with the <A HREF="shademodel.html#A143X9ab9"><B>shademodel</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D73D4369ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A>, Drawing with <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/move-draw.html">Move-Draw Style</A> Subroutines, and <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/setglattrib.html#setglattrib.html">Setting Drawing Attributes</A>.</P><hr><center>
```

```html
<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">
<HTML>
<HEAD>
<META HTTP-EQUIV="Content-Type" CONTENT="text/html; charset=iso-8859-1">

<TITLE>rpmv Subroutine
</TITLE>
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="rpdr.html">Previous</a>  |
```
