<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A143X9afd"></A>splf Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1838" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1839" REL="I2" TITLE="high-level drawing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1840" REL="I3" TITLE="splf"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1841" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1842" REL="I2" TITLE="polygons"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1843" REL="I3" TITLE="filled, shaded"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1844" REL="I1" TITLE="splf subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9aff"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D74D8665ceb"></A>Draws a shaded filled polygon.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C129f"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D74D8704ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D74D8729ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9b03"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A143X9b04"></A><B>void splf</B>
<B>(Int32 </B><A HREF="splf.html#A143X9b08"><I>n</I></A><B>,</B>
<B>Coord </B><A HREF="splf.html#A143X9b09"><I>parray</I></A><B>[&nbsp;][3],</B>
<B>Colorindex </B><A HREF="splf.html#A143X9b0a"><I>iarray</I></A><B>[&nbsp;])</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="t7h1f0marj"></A><B>void splfi</B>
<B>(Int32 </B><A HREF="splf.html#A143X9b08"><I>n</I></A><B>,</B>
<B>Icoord </B><A HREF="splf.html#A143X9b09"><I>parray</I></A><B>[&nbsp;][3],</B>
<B>Colorindex </B><A HREF="splf.html#A143X9b0a"><I>iarray</I></A><B>[&nbsp;])</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="U8h2b0marj"></A><B>void splfs</B>
<B>(Int32 </B><A HREF="splf.html#A143X9b08"><I>n</I></A><B>,</B>
<B>Scoord </B><A HREF="splf.html#A143X9b09"><I>parray</I></A><B>[&nbsp;][3],</B>
<B>Colorindex </B><A HREF="splf.html#A143X9b0a"><I>iarray</I></A><B>[&nbsp;])</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="v8h2d0marj"></A><B>void splf2</B>
<B>(Int32 </B><A HREF="splf.html#A143X9b08"><I>n</I></A><B>,</B>
<B>Coord </B><A HREF="splf.html#A143X9b09"><I>parray</I></A><B>[&nbsp;][2],</B>
<B>Colorindex </B><A HREF="splf.html#A143X9b0a"><I>iarray</I></A><B>[&nbsp;])</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="D9h30marj"></A><B>void splf2i</B>
<B>(Int32 </B><A HREF="splf.html#A143X9b08"><I>n</I></A><B>,</B>
<B>Icoord </B><A HREF="splf.html#A143X9b09"><I>parray</I></A><B>[&nbsp;][2],</B>
<B>Colorindex </B><A HREF="splf.html#A143X9b0a"><I>iarray</I></A><B>[&nbsp;])</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="V9h2f0marj"></A><B>void splf2s</B>
<B>(Int32 </B><A HREF="splf.html#A143X9b08"><I>n</I></A><B>,</B>
<B>Scoord </B><A HREF="splf.html#A143X9b09"><I>parray</I></A><B>[&nbsp;][2],</B>
<B>Colorindex </B><A HREF="splf.html#A143X9b0a"><I>iarray</I></A><B>[&nbsp;])</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A28C01075b"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A28C01075c"></A><B>SUBROUTINE SPLF(</B><I>n</I><B>,</B> <I>parray</I><B>,</B> <I>iarray</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>n</I>
<B>REAL </B><I>parray</I><B>(3,</B><I>n</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*2 </B><I>iarray</I><B>(</B><I>n</I><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A28C01075d"></A><B>SUBROUTINE SPLFI(</B><I>n</I><B>,</B> <I>parray</I><B>,</B> <I>iarray</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>n</I>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>parray</I><B>(3,</B><I>n</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*2 </B><I>iarray</I><B>(</B><I>n</I><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A28C01075e"></A><B>SUBROUTINE SPLFS(</B><I>n</I><B>,</B> <I>parray</I><B>,</B> <I>iarray</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>n</I>
<B>INTEGER*2 </B><I>parray</I><B>(3,</B><I>n</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*2 </B><I>iarray</I><B>(</B><I>n</I><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A28C01075f"></A><B>SUBROUTINE SPLF2(</B><I>n</I><B>,</B> <I>parray</I><B>,</B> <I>iarray</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>n</I>
<B>REAL </B><I>parray</I><B>(2,</B><I>n</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*2 </B><I>iarray</I><B>(</B><I>n</I><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A28C010760"></A><B>SUBROUTINE SPLF2I(</B><I>n</I><B>,</B> <I>parray</I><B>,</B> <I>iarray</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>n</I>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>parray</I><B>(2,</B><I>n</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*2 </B><I>iarray</I><B>(</B><I>n</I><B>)</B></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A28C010761"></A><B>SUBROUTINE SPLF2S(</B><I>n</I><B>,</B> <I>parray</I><B>,</B> <I>iarray</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>n</I>
<B>INTEGER*2 </B><I>parray</I><B>(2,</B><I>n</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*2 </B><I>iarray</I><B>(</B><I>n</I><B>)</B></PRE>

<P><A NAME="E1D74D9020ceb"></A>All of the preceding routines are functionally the same. They differ only in the type declarations of their parameters and in whether they assume a two- or three-dimensional screen.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9b05"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D74D9066ceb"></A>The <B>splf</B> subroutine draws 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0611">Gouraud-shaded</A> polygons using the current 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A13791abd">pattern</A> and 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A3C0F2A4599mhay">writemask</A>. Polygons are represented as arrays of points. The first and last points automatically connect to close a polygon. After the polygon is drawn, the current graphics position is set to the first point in the array. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D74D9092ceb"></A>The six different forms for the <B>splf</B> subroutine are as follows:</P>

<TABLE BORDER="2"><TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><BR></TD>

<TD><B>2-D</B></TD>

<TD><B>3-D</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>Int16</TD>

<TD>splf2s</TD>

<TD>splfs</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>Int32</TD>

<TD>splf2i</TD>

<TD>splfi</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>float</TD>

<TD>splf2</TD>

<TD>splf</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P><A NAME="E1D74D9135ceb"></A>The 
syntax
 for each of the subroutine forms is the same except for the parameter type. They differ only in that <A HREF="splf.html#A143X9b04"><B>splf</B></A> expects real coordinates, <A HREF="splf.html#t7h1f0marj"><B>splfi</B></A> expects integer coordinates, and <A HREF="splf.html#U8h2b0marj"><B>splfs</B></A> expects short integer coordinates. In addition, the <A HREF="splf.html#v8h2d0marj"><B>splf2</B></A>* routines assume a 2-D point instead of a 3-D point.</P>

<OL><LI><A NAME="A28C010762"></A>This subroutine must be used in 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A25P03e3">color map mode</A>.</LI>

<LI><A NAME="A318C9d60"></A>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</LI></OL>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9b07"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X9b08"></A><I>n</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the number of vertices in the polygon. There can be no more than 256 vertices in a single polygon. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X9b09"></A><I>parray </I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies an array containing the vertices of a polygon.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X9b0a"></A><I>iarray </I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies an array containing the color map indexes that determine the intensities of the vertices of the polygon.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015cde"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D74D9307ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C12a2"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C12a3"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C12a4"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9b1d"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D74D9404ceb"></A>Setting color map mode as the current mode with the <A HREF="cmode.html#A146X93d6"><B>cmode</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D74D9430ceb"></A>Allowing the system to draw concave polygons with the <A HREF="concave.html#HXf320marj"><B>concave</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D74D9456ceb"></A>Specifying the next point in a polygon with the <A HREF="pdr.html#bqf1c0marj"><B>pdr</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D74D9481ceb"></A>Specifying the starting point for a polygon with the <A HREF="pmv.html#A139X91eed"><B>pmv</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D74D9506ceb"></A>Drawing a polygon with the <A HREF="poly.html#avf2c0marj"><B>poly</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D74D9532ceb"></A>Drawing a filled rectangle with the <A HREF="rectf.html#Q5g330marj"><B>rectf</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D74D9557ceb"></A>Drawing a relative polygon with the <A HREF="rpdr.html#hrfa0marj"><B>rpdr</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D74D9583ceb"></A>Moving the current graphics position to a starting point for a filled polygon relative to the current point with the <A HREF="rpmv.html#lXf370marj"><B>rpmv</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A142X91bd2"></A>stepunit Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1845" REL="I1" TITLE="stepunit subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1846" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1847" REL="I2" TITLE="window"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1848" REL="I3" TITLE="stepunit"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1849" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1850" REL="I2" TITLE="window sizes"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1851" REL="I3" TITLE="specifying changes by steps"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A142X91bd4"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D74E7274ceb"></A>Specifies that a window change size in discrete steps.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1327"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D74E7313ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D74E7337ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A142X91bd8"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X912b8a"></A><B>void stepunit(Int32 </B><A HREF="stepunit.html#wh53230marj"><I>xunit</I></A><B>, Int32</B> <A HREF="stepunit.html#A6i53370marj"><I>yunit</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010c45"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010c46"></A><B>SUBROUTINE STEPUN(</B><I>xunit</I><B>, </B><I>yunit</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>xunit</I><B>, </B><I>yunit</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A142X91bda"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D74E7452ceb"></A>The <B>stepunit</B> subroutine specifies the smallest steps (in pixels) by which a
 <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A13791dc4">window</A> can be resized. This subroutine is called at the beginning of a subroutine, but takes effect only when the <A HREF="winopen.html#A142X91549"><B>winopen</B></A> subroutine is called.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D74E7478ceb"></A>The <B>stepunit </B>subroutine can also be called in conjunction with the <A HREF="winconstraints.html#A142X914c1"><B>winconstraints</B></A> subroutine to modify the enforced step size after the window is created. The default step unit is one pixel by one pixel. In other words, by default, the window can be resized arbitrarily. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D74E7504ceb"></A>With the <B>stepunit</B> subroutine, the programmer can prevent the user from resizing a window except in discrete jumps. If the step unit is large, this subroutine essentially limits the sizes and shapes of a window.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9f67"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A142X91bdc"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="wh53230marj"></A><I>xunit</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the amount of change per unit in the <I>x</I> direction, measured in pixels.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A6i53370marj"></A><I>yunit</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the amount of change per unit in the <I>y</I> direction, measured in pixels.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A61C0159f8"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D74E7622ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C132a"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C132b"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C132c"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A142X91bf2"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D74E7720ceb"></A>Specifying pixel values to be added to a window with the <A HREF="fudge.html#A142X917a6"><B>fudge</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D74E7745ceb"></A>Binding window constraints to the current window with the <A HREF="winconstraints.html#A142X914c1"><B>winconstraints</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D74E7771ceb"></A>Creating a window with the <A HREF="winopen.html#A142X91549"><B>winopen</B></A> subroutine. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D74E7796ceb"></A>Creating and Managing <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/managewinds.html#managewinds.html">Windows</A>.</P><hr><center>

<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A144X93ec"></A>strwidth Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1852" REL="I1" TITLE="strwidth subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1853" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1854" REL="I2" TITLE="query"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1855" REL="I3" TITLE="returning"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1856" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1857" REL="I2" TITLE="text"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1858" REL="I3" TITLE="strwidth"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1859" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1860" REL="I2" TITLE="text"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1861" REL="I3" TITLE="returning text string width"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A144X93ee"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D74F5846ceb"></A>Returns the width of the specified text string.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1253"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D74F5885ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D74F5910ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A144X93f2"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X912662"></A><B>Int32 strwidth(Char8 * </B><A HREF="strwidth.html#A144X93f7"><I>string</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010c0c"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010c0d"></A><B>INTEGER*4 FUNCTION STRWID(</B><A HREF="strwidth.html#A144X93f7"><I>string</I></A><B>, </B><A HREF="strwidth.html#A144X93f8"><I>length</I></A><B>) </B>
<B>CHARACTER*(*) </B><I>string</I>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>length</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A144X93f4"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D74F6023ceb"></A>The <B>strwidth </B>subroutine returns the width of a text string in pixels, using the character-spacing parameters of the current 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P073b">raster font</A>. This subroutine is useful when you do a simple mapping from 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A27P017">screen space</A> to 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P06el">modeling space</A>. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D74F6048ceb"></A>Undefined characters have zero width. </P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9f25"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A144X93f6"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A144X93f7"></A><I>string</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the name of the string.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A144X93f8"></A><I>length</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the number of characters in the string.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A30C011056"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D74F6164ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="prompt_c.html#A16C0c8de"><B>prompt.c</B></A> uses the <B>strwidth</B> subroutine to get the number of pixels needed to draw a prompt string. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015d92"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D74F6207ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1256"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1257"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1258"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A144X940c"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D74F6305ceb"></A>Mapping a point on the screen into a line in 3-D modeling coordinates with the <A HREF="mapw.html#A213X9119fe"><B>mapw</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D74F6331ceb"></A>Mapping a point on the screen into a line in 2-D modeling coordinates with the <A HREF="mapw2.html#A213X911a56"><B>mapw2</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//EN">
<HTML>
<HEAD>
<META HTTP-EQUIV="Content-Type" CONTENT="text/html; charset=iso-8859-1">

<TITLE>subpixel Subroutine
</TITLE>
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="strwidth.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="swapbuffers.html">Next</a>  |
<A href="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="jIZ1120marj"></A>subpixel Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1862" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1863" REL="I2" TITLE="antialiasing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1864" REL="I3" TITLE="subpixel"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1865" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1866" REL="I2" TITLE="vertex"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1867" REL="I3" TITLE="placement control"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1868" REL="I1" TITLE="subpixel subroutine (GL)"></A>

<P><A NAME="E1D7504358ceb"></A>Controls the placement of point, line, and polygon vertices </P>

<H3><A NAME="A77C149"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7504397ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7504421ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A237X94495"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A237X94496"></A><B>void subpixel(Int32</B> <A HREF="subpixel.html#mEZ11c0marj"><I>bool</I></A><B>&nbsp;)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A237X94472"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A237X94475"></A><B>SUBROUTINE SUBPIX(</B><I>bool</I><B>)</B>
<B>LOGICAL</B> <I>bool</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A237X94499"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7504534ceb"></A>The <B>subpixel </B>subroutine controls the placement of point, line, and poygon vertices in 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A27P017">screen coordinates</A>. The default value of the <A HREF="subpixel.html#mEZ11c0marj"><I>bool</I></A> parameter is False, causing vertices to be snapped to the center of the nearest 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P06fd">pixel</A> after they have been transformed to screen coordinates. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7504560ceb"></A>Vertex snapping introduces artifacts into the scan conversion of lines and polygons. It is especially noticeable when points or lines are drawn smooth (see the <A HREF="pntsmooth.html#W3o220marj"><B>pntsmooth</B></A> and <A HREF="linesmooth.html#Ew1f0marj"><B>linesmooth</B></A> subroutines). The <B>subpixel </B>subroutine is typically set to True while smooth points or smooth lines are being drawn. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7504587ceb"></A>In addition to its effect on vertex position, the <B>subpixel </B>subroutine also modifies the 
scan conversion
 of lines. Specifically, non-subpixel-positioned lines are drawn <I>closed, </I>meaning that connected line segments draw the pixel at their shared vertex, while subpixel positioned lines are drawn <I>half open, </I>meaning that connected lines segments share no pixels. (Smooth lines are always drawn <I>half open, </I>regardless of the state of the <B>subpixel</B> subroutine.) </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7504616ceb"></A>Subpixel-positioned lines produce better results when you use the <A HREF="logicop.html#iM521a0marj"><B>logicop</B></A> or <A HREF="blendfunction.html#A143X9240"><B>blendfunction</B></A> subroutines, but will produce different, possibly undesirable results in 2-D applications where the endpoints of lines have been carefully placed. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7504645ceb"></A>For example, using the standard 2-D projection: </P>
<PRE><A NAME="A237X9449d"></A>ortho2(left-0.5,right+0.5,bottom-0.5,top+0.5);
viewport(left,right,bottom,top);</PRE>

<P><A NAME="E1D7504696ceb"></A>Subpixel-positioned lines match non-subpixel-positioned lines pixel for pixel, except that they omit either the right-most or top-most pixel. Thus, the non-subpixel-positioned line drawn from (0,0) to (0,2) fills pixels (0,0), (0,1), and (0,2), while the subpixel-positioned line drawn between the same coordinates fills only pixels (0,0) and (0,1). </P>

<H3><A NAME="A237X9449f"></A>Parameter</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="mEZ11c0marj"></A><I>bool</I></TD>
<TD>  Either True or False.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A237X944a0"></A></TD>
<TD>  False = forces screen vertices to the centers of pixels (default).</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A237X944a1"></A></TD>
<TD>  True = positions screen vertices exactly.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A237X944a4"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7504812ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7504845ceb"></A>On the High-Performance 3-D Graphics Processor polygons are always subpixel positioned, regardless of the value of the <B>subpixel</B> subroutine. Subpixel-positioned nonsmooth lines are not implemented.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7504870ceb"></A>On the Supergraphics Processor, lines and polygons are never subpixel-positioned, regardless of the value of the <B>subpixel</B> subroutine. Vertices are always snapped to the center of a pixel before rasterization begins.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7504896ceb"></A>The POWER Gt4 and POWER Gt4x adapters do not support subpixel positioning.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7504922ceb"></A>On the POWER GXT1000 adapter, subpixel positioning is always on.</P>


<H3><A NAME="A237X9448e"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C14c"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C14d"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A258C01c372"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7505019ceb"></A>Specifying antialiasing of lines with the <A HREF="linesmooth.html#Ew1f0marj"><B>linesmooth</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7505045ceb"></A>Specifying antialiasing of points with the <A HREF="pntsmooth.html#W3o220marj"><B>pntsmooth</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>

<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A16C0c9a6"></A>sunflower.c Example C Language Program
</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX2443" REL="I1" TITLE="sunflower.c example program (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2444" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2445" REL="I2" TITLE="example programs"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2446" REL="I3" TITLE="drawing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2447" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2448" REL="I2" TITLE="sunflower"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2449" REL="I3" TITLE="drawing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2450" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2451" REL="I2" TITLE="drawing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2452" REL="I3" TITLE="sunflower"></A>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EB96685ttay"></A>/*
sunflower.c</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EB96870ttay"></A>Make a sunflower-like pattern out of circles.
    Usage: sunflower &lt;&lt;nseeds> &lt;&lt;seedsize> &lt;&lt;growth>
Try "sunflower 400.05 1.1"</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EB97020ttay"></A>Paul Haeberli - 1984
*/</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EB97190ttay"></A>#include &lt;gl/gl.h>
#include &lt;gl/device.h>
#include &lt;stdio.h>
#include &lt;math.h></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EB97337ttay"></A>int seeds = 0;</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EB97513ttay"></A>main(argc,argv)
int argc;
char **argv;
{
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;int nseeds;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;float seedsize, grow;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;short val;    </PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EB97694ttay"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;if (argc&lt;4) {
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;fprintf(stderr,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;    "Usage: sunflower &lt;nseeds> &lt;seedsize> &lt;growth>\n");
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;exit(1);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EB97998ttay"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;nseeds = atoi(argv[1]);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;seedsize = atof(argv[2]);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;grow = atof(argv[3]);    
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;prefposition(XMAXSCREEN/4,XMAXSCREEN*3/4,YMAXSCREEN/4,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;    YMAXSCREEN*3/4);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;winopen("sunflower");
     &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;singlebuffer();
     &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;zbuffer (FALSE); 
        cmode();
 &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;gconfig (); 
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;makeframe();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;sunflower(nseeds,seedsize,grow);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;while (1) {
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;if (qread(&amp;val) == REDRAW)  {
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;makeframe();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;sunflower(nseeds,seedsize,grow);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;}
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EB98141ttay"></A>}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EB98307ttay"></A>sunflower(nseeds,seedsize,grow)
int nseeds;
float seedsize, grow;
{</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EB98462ttay"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;float rad = 20.0;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;int parity = 0;    </PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EB98664ttay"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;scale(10.0,10.0,0.0);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;pushmatrix();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;while (rad &lt; 100.0) {
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;rotate(1800/nseeds,'z');
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;scale(grow,grow,0.0);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;makering(nseeds,seedsize);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;rad = rad * grow;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EB98812ttay"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;popmatrix();
}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EB98976ttay"></A>makering(nseeds,seedsize)
int nseeds;
float seedsize;
{
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;int i;</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EB99162ttay"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;for (i=0; i&lt;nseeds; i++) {
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;pushmatrix();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;rotate((i*3600)/nseeds,'z');
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;drawseed(seedsize);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;popmatrix();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EB99305ttay"></A>}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EB99474ttay"></A>drawseed(seedsize)
float seedsize;
{
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;seeds++;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;circ(1.0,0.0,seedsize);
}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EB99621ttay"></A>makeframe()
{</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EB99776ttay"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;int xsize, ysize;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;float aspect;    </PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EB99973ttay"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;reshapeviewport();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;getsize(&amp;xsize,&amp;ysize);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(7);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;clear();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(0);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;aspect = xsize/(float)ysize;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;ortho2(-50.0,50.0,-50.0/aspect,50.0/aspect);
}</PRE>

<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A145X9302"></A>swapbuffers Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1869" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1870" REL="I2" TITLE="animation"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1871" REL="I3" TITLE="swapbuffers"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1872" REL="I1" TITLE="swapbuffers subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1873" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1874" REL="I2" TITLE="buffers"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1875" REL="I3" TITLE="exchanging front and back"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1876" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1877" REL="I2" TITLE="frame buffer configuration"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1878" REL="I3" TITLE="swapbuffers"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A145X9304"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7515246ceb"></A>Exchanges the front and back buffers in double buffer mode.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A77C137"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7515285ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7515310ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A145X9307"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A145X9308"></A><B>void swapbuffers(&nbsp;)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A145X92e1"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A145X92e4"></A><B>SUBROUTINE SWAPBU</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A145X930b"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7515419ceb"></A>The <B>swapbuffers</B> subroutine exchanges the front and back buffers in 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0474">double buffer mode</A>.  Once an image is fully drawn in the back buffer, the <B>swapbuffers</B> subroutine displays that image.  </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7515446ceb"></A>The swapping of buffers occurs only during a vertical retrace. A minimum of the number of vertical retraces specified by the <B>swapinterval</B> subroutine must have elapsed since the last call to <B>swapbuffers</B> before the current request is honored. After this call is made, all drawing to the front and back buffers is disabled until the swap occurs.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7515471ceb"></A>This subroutine is ignored in 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A27P01c">single buffer mode</A>.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A145X930f"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7515513ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="backface_c.html#A16C0c7a2"><B>backface.c</B></A> uses the <B>swapbuffers</B> subroutine to display a cube after drawing it in the back buffer. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015c99"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7515556ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A145X92fd"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C13a"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C13b"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A258C01c356"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7515654ceb"></A>Enabling drawing in the back buffer with the <A HREF="backbuffer.html#A145X94a"><B>backbuffer</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7515680ceb"></A>Setting the display mode to double buffer mode with the <A HREF="doublebuffer.html#A145X91a7"><B>doublebuffer</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7515706ceb"></A>Enabling drawing in the front buffer with the <A HREF="frontbuffer.html#A145X9a0"><B>frontbuffer</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7515731ceb"></A>Defining a minimum time between buffer swaps with the <A HREF="swapinterval.html#A145X92af"><B>swapinterval</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7515757ceb"></A>Understanding the <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/glintro.html#A8G44310marj">Hardware Used by GL</A> in<I> GL3.2 Version 4 for AIX: Programming Concepts</I>.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7515783ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/configframebuf.html#configframebuf.html">Configuring the Frame Buffer</A>
 and <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/animatescene.html#animatescene.html">Creating Animated Scenes</A>.</P><hr><center>

<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A145X92af"></A>swapinterval Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1879" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1880" REL="I2" TITLE="animation"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1881" REL="I3" TITLE="swapinterval"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1882" REL="I1" TITLE="swapinterval subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1883" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1884" REL="I2" TITLE="buffers"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1885" REL="I3" TITLE="setting time interval between swaps"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1886" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1887" REL="I2" TITLE="frame buffer configuration"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1888" REL="I3" TITLE="swapinterval"></A>
<H3><A NAME="A145X92b1"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7524168ceb"></A>Defines a minimum time between buffer swaps.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A77C13d"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7524207ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7524231ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A145X92b4"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A145X92b5"></A><B>void swapinterval(Int16 </B><A HREF="swapinterval.html#A145X92bd"><I>interval</I></A><B>&nbsp;)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A145X928c"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A145X928f"></A><B>SUBROUTINE SWAPINT(</B><A HREF="swapinterval.html#A145X92bd"><I>interval</I></A><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>interval</I></PRE>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A77C140"></A><B>Note: </B>For FORTRAN users, this subroutine accepts long integer parameters (INTEGER*4) when invoked from a FORTRAN program, although it accepts short integers when invoked from a C program. The C and FORTRAN syntax shown here reflect this difference.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A145X92b8"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7524365ceb"></A>The <B>swapinterval</B> subroutine defines a minimum time between 
buffer swaps. The time is measured in units of vertical retraces, with the default interval being 1. For example, for a swap interval of 5, the system refreshes the screen at least five times between successive buffer swaps. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7524391ceb"></A>The <B>swapinterval</B> subroutine changes frames at a steady rate if a new image can be created within one swap interval. This subroutine is valid only in 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0474">double buffer mode</A> and is ignored in 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A27P01c">single buffer mode</A>. </P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9c6f"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A145X92bc"></A>Parameter</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A145X92bd"></A> <I>interval</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the number of retraces to wait before swapping the front and back buffers. </TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015ca1"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7524489ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7524514ceb"></A>The POWER GXT1000 adapter does not support the <B>swapinterval</B> subroutine.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A145X92a9"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C141"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A77C142"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A258C01c35b"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7524612ceb"></A>Setting the display mode to double buffer mode with the <A HREF="doublebuffer.html#A145X91a7"><B>doublebuffer</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7524638ceb"></A>Exchanging the front and back buffers with the <A HREF="swapbuffers.html#A145X9302"><B>swapbuffers</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7524663ceb"></A>Understanding the <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/glintro.html#A8G44310marj">Hardware Used by GL</A> in<I> GL3.2 Version 4 for AIX: Programming Concepts</I>.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7524689ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/configframebuf.html#configframebuf.html">Configuring the Frame Buffer</A>
 and <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/animatescene.html#animatescene.html">Creating Animated Scenes</A>.</P><hr><center>

<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A144X9782"></A>swaptmesh Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1889" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1890" REL="I2" TITLE="begin-end style"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1891" REL="I3" TITLE="swaptmesh"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1892" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1893" REL="I2" TITLE="triangle mesh register"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1894" REL="I3" TITLE="toggling"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1895" REL="I1" TITLE="swaptmesh subroutine (GL)"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A144X9784"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7533662ceb"></A>Toggles the triangle mesh register pointer.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C11f"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7533701ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7533726ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A213X91288f"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X912890"></A><B>void swaptmesh(&nbsp;)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A20C0e2eb"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A20C0e2ec"></A><B>SUBROUTINE SWAPTM</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A144X978a"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7533834ceb"></A>The <B>swaptmesh</B> subroutine toggles the triangle mesh register pointer.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7533861ceb"></A>The triangle mesh hardware stores two vertices. After each new vertex is specified (and a triangle comprising the new vertex and the two stored vertices is drawn), one of the stored vertices is replaced by the new vertex. The value of a two-value pointer determines which vertex is replaced. This pointer is toggled after each vertex, replacing the alternate stored vertices. The <B>swaptmesh</B> subroutine toggles the pointer without specification of a new vertex (and no triangle is drawn). </P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015d74"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7533904ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A78C122"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C123"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A78C124"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A144X97a2"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7534001ceb"></A>Drawing triangle mesh vertices with the <A HREF="bgntmesh.html#A144X9694"><B>bgntmesh</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7534027ceb"></A>Ending a series of triangle mesh vertices with the <A HREF="bgntmesh.html#A144X9694"><B>endtmesh</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7534053ceb"></A>Transferring a vertex to the graphics pipe with the <A HREF="v.html#A144X97a4"><B>v</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A2T741b0nita"></A>swinopen Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1896" REL="I1" TITLE="swinopen subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1897" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1898" REL="I2" TITLE="window"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1899" REL="I3" TITLE="swinopen"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1900" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1901" REL="I2" TITLE="windows"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1902" REL="I3" TITLE="creating restricted subwindow"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1903" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1904" REL="I2" TITLE="subwindows"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1905" REL="I3" TITLE="creating restricted"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A58C015411"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7542835ceb"></A>Creates a restricted subwindow.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C132d"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7542874ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7542898ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A58C015414"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A58C015415"></A><B>Int32 swinopen(Int32 *</B><A HREF="swinopen.html#NL74f0nita"><I>parentid</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A58C015416"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A58C015417"></A><B>INTEGER*4 FUNCTION SWINOP(</B><I>parentid</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>parentid</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A58C015418"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7543010ceb"></A>The <B>swinopen </B>subroutine creates a subwindow inside a parent window. The subwindow is mapped (created and displayed) immediately upon receipt of this call. The subwindow then becomes the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A60P0189">current window</A>.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7543036ceb"></A>Subwindows have no border and therefore cannot be moved by the applications user. Other than this, subwindows behave very much like windows created with the <A HREF="winopen.html#A142X91549"><B>winopen</B></A> subroutine. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7543063ceb"></A>When a subwindow is created, a completely independent graphics context is also created for it. That is, subwindows have their own current color linestyle, pattern, matrix stack, viewport stack, attribute stack, name stack, and so on. These attributes are not shared with the parent. The attributes are initialized to their default values (for example, empty stack). See the <A HREF="greset.html#xW42e0nita"><B>greset</B></A> subroutine for the list of default values.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7543088ceb"></A>The position of a subwindow is measured relative to the origin of the parent window. Subwindows move with the parent window. If a parent window is moved, all of its subwindows move with it.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7543115ceb"></A>Subwindows are clipped to the boundaries of the parent window. That is, by drawing inside a subwindow, one can never draw outside of the boundaries of the parent window. Otherwise, subwindows can be positioned arbitrarily inside a parent window, even if such positioning means that the subwindow is completely clipped. If a subwindow is exposed or otherwise needs redrawing, both the parent and the subwindow receive redraw events.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7543141ceb"></A>Because subwindows cannot be moved or resized by the user, none of the window constraint subroutines have any meaning and therefore do not affect the state of a subwindow. Window constraint subroutines include the <A HREF="minsize.html#MJ13260marj"><B>minsize</B></A>, <A HREF="maxsize.html#A142X916d6"><B>maxsize</B></A>, and <A HREF="stepunit.html#A142X91bd2"><B>stepunit</B></A> subroutines. Because subwindows have no border, they cannot be given a title. Subwindows also cannot be iconified.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7543167ceb"></A>Subwindows can be pushed and popped. Subwindows can be positioned or moved with either the <A HREF="prefposition.html#A142X9164f"><B>prefposition</B></A> or <A HREF="prefsize.html#A142X91671"><B>prefsize</B></A> subroutine followed by a call to the <A HREF="winconstraints.html#A142X914c1"><B>winconstraints</B></A> subroutine, or by using the <A HREF="winposition.html#A142X9158d"><B>winposition</B></A> or <A HREF="winmove.html#A142X91527"><B>winmove</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7543196ceb"></A>Subwindows can have sub-subwindows. The origin of a sub-subwindow is measured relative to the origin of the subwindow (its parent).</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A59C0154a7"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>. </BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A58C015420"></A>Parameter</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="NL74f0nita"></A><I>parentid</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the identifier, or handle, of the parent window. </TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A58C015421"></A>Return Value</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7543292ceb"></A>The identifier, or handle, for the subwindow.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A61C015a06"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7543336ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C1330"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1331"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1332"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A58C015425"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7543432ceb"></A>Creating a new window with the <A HREF="winopen.html#A142X91549"><B>winopen</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7543458ceb"></A>Creating and Managing <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/managewinds.html#managewinds.html">Windows</A>.</P><hr><center>

</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX2453" REL="I1" TITLE="text.c example program (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2454" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2455" REL="I2" TITLE="example programs"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2456" REL="I3" TITLE="text"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2457" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>

<A NAME="INDEX2459" REL="I3" TITLE="example program"></A>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EBA3155ttay"></A>/*
text.c:</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EBA3320ttay"></A>A text drawing sample program using the charstr() subro utine.
*/</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EBA3476ttay"></A>#include &lt;gl/gl.h>
#include &lt;gl/device.h></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EBA3724ttay"></A>main()
{
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Device dev;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;short val;    
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;initialize();    
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;while (TRUE) {
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;if (qtest()) {
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;dev = qread(&amp;val);            
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;if (dev == ESCKEY) {
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;gexit();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;exit();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;}
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;else if (dev == REDRAW) {
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;reshapeviewport();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;drawtext();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;}
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;}
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EBA3867ttay"></A>}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EBA4019ttay"></A>initialize()
{
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;int gid;    </PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EBA4229ttay"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;prefposition(XMAXSCREEN/4, XMAXSCREEN*3/4, YMAXSCREEN/4, 
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;    YMAXSCREEN*3/4);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;gid = winopen("text");
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;winconstraints();    
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;qdevice(ESCKEY);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;qdevice(REDRAW);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;qenter(REDRAW,gid);
}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EBA4375ttay"></A>drawtext()
{</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EBA4583ttay"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(BLACK);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;clear();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(RED);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;cmov2i(300,380);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;charstr("The first line is drawn ");
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;charstr("in two parts. ");
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;cmov2i(300, 368);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;charstr("This line is 12 pixels lower. ");</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EBA4725ttay"></A>}</PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A201C11a7"></A>Related Information</H3>

<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A143X9cb7"></A>textport Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1906" REL="I1" TITLE="textport subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1907" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1908" REL="I2" TITLE="textport"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1909" REL="I3" TITLE="textport"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1910" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1911" REL="I2" TITLE="textport"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1912" REL="I3" TITLE="allocating screen area"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9cb9"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7551744ceb"></A>Allocates an area of the screen for the textport.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C11fa"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7551783ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7551807ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9cbd"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A143X9cbe"></A><B>void textport</B>
<B>(Screencoord </B><A HREF="textport.html#A143X9cc2"><I>left</I></A><B>, Screencoord </B><A HREF="textport.html#A143X9cc3"><I>right</I></A><B>,</B>
<B>Screencoord </B><A HREF="textport.html#A143X9cc4"><I>bottom</I></A><B>, Screencoord </B><A HREF="textport.html#A4Sj160nita"><I>top</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010bdf"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010be0"></A><B>SUBROUTINE TEXTPO(</B><I>left</I><B>, </B><I>right</I><B>, </B><I>bottom</I><B>, </B><I>top</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>left</I><B>, </B><I>right</I><B>, </B><I>bottom</I><B>, </B><I>top</I></PRE>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A79C11fd"></A><B>Note: </B>For FORTRAN users, this subroutine accepts long integer parameters (INTEGER*4) when started from a FORTRAN program, although it accepts short integers when started from a C program. The C and FORTRAN syntax shown here reflect this difference.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A143X9cbf"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7551941ceb"></A>The <B>textport</B> subroutine allocates an area on the screen for the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A154P11506">textport</A> window. </P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9f07"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A143X9cc1"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X9cc2"></A><I>left</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>x </I>screen coordinate for the left side of the textport.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X9cc3"></A><I>right</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>x</I> screen coordinate for the right side of the textport.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X9cc4"></A><I>bottom</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>y </I>screen coordinate for the bottom of the textport.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A4Sj160nita"></A><I>top</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the <I>y </I>screen coordinate for the top of the textport.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A30C011048"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7552094ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="tpbig_c.html#A16C0c9bd"><B>tpbig.c</B></A> uses the <B>textport</B> subroutine to define a textport. </P>

<H3><A NAME="A62C015d7c"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7552138ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C11fe"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C11ff"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1200"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9cd7"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7552235ceb"></A>Turning off the textport with the <A HREF="tpoff.html#A143X9c2f"><B>tpoff</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7552260ceb"></A>Turning on the textport with the <A HREF="tpon.html#A14k110nita"><B>tpon</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7552286ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A> and Working with the <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/textport.html#textport.html">Textport</A>.</P><hr><center>

</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A143X9196"></A>tie Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1913" REL="I1" TITLE="tie subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1914" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1915" REL="I2" TITLE="device"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1916" REL="I3" TITLE="tying two valuators to a button"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1917" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1918" REL="I2" TITLE="queue and device"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1919" REL="I3" TITLE="tie"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9198"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D755F970ceb"></A>Ties two valuators to a button.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C118d"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7560010ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7560034ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X919c"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A143X919d"></A><B>void tie(Device</B> <A HREF="tie.html#A143X91a1"><I>button</I></A><B>, Device </B><A HREF="tie.html#A143X91a2"><I>val1</I></A><B>, Device</B> <A HREF="tie.html#A143X91a3"><I>val2</I></A><B>)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A29C010c7f"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A29C010c80"></A><B>SUBROUTINE TIE(</B><I>button</I><B>, </B><I>val1</I><B>, </B><I>val2</I><B>)</B>
<B>INTEGER*4 </B><I>button</I><B>, </B><I>val1</I><B>, </B><I>val2</I></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X919e"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7560149ceb"></A>The <B>tie</B> subroutine requires a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A1819349">button</A> and two 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A79P07a">valuators</A>, specified by the <A HREF="tie.html#A143X91a2"><I>val1</I></A> and <A HREF="tie.html#A143X91a3"><I>val2</I></A> parameters. When a queued button changes state, three entries are made in the queue: one records the current state of the button, and two record the current positions of each valuator. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D7560174ceb"></A>Tie one valuator to a button by making the <I>val2</I> parameter = 0. Untie a button by making both the <I>val1</I> and <I>val2 </I>parameters = 0. The <A HREF="tie.html#A143X91a1"><I>button</I></A> parameter precedes both the <I>val1</I> and <I>val2</I> parameters in the
 <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0484">event queue</A>. The <I>val1 </I>parameter appears before the <I>val2</I> parameter. </P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9f8d"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A143X91a0"></A>Parameters</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X91a1"></A><I>button</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the current state of a button.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X91a2"></A><I>val1</I> </TD>
<TD>  Specifies the current position of the first valuator.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A143X91a3"></A><I>val2</I></TD>
<TD>  Specifies the current position of the second valuator.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A30C01106c"></A>Example</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7560308ceb"></A>The example C language program <A HREF="vlsi_c.html#A16C0c9fd"><B>vlsi.c</B></A> uses the <B>tie</B> subroutine to enter the current mouse coordinates into the event queue whenever the left or middle mouse buttons are pressed.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A64C016626"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7560352ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X91b2"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1190"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1191"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1192"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/device.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C1193"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fdevice.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X91b6"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D7560487ceb"></A>Returning the current state of a button with the <A HREF="getbutton.html#A143X91"><B>getbutton</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<HEAD>

<TITLE>Tokens for the getgdesc Subroutine
</TITLE>
</HEAD>

<body bgcolor="#fcfbf0">
<center>
[  <a href="getgdesc.html">Previous</a>  |
<a href="getgpos.html">Next</a>  |
<A href="toc.html" TARGET="_parent">Contents</A>  
 <A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html">| Glossary</A>  
 <A HREF="../topnav/topnav.html" TARGET="_top"></A>  
 <A HREF="/cgi-bin/ds_form?config=/usr/share/man/info/en_US/a_doc_lib/data/base.cfg" TARGET="_top"></A>  ]
<hr>
<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="QP3a0nita"></A>Tokens for the getgdesc Subroutine</H2>
<P><A NAME="E1B0ED1975ceb"></A>The following data is returned when the indicated token is passed to the subroutine:</P>

<TABLE BORDER="2"><TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD><B>C</B></TD>

<TD><B>FORTRAN</B></TD>

<TD><B>Description</B></TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_BITS_ALPHABUFFER</TD>

<TD>GDBITA</TD>

<TD>The number of alpha blending bitplanes available on adapter. A value of zero is returned if there are no alpha bitplanes.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_BITS_CURSOR</TD>

<TD>GDBITC</TD>

<TD>The number of cursor bitplanes available on adapter.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_BITS_LINESTYLE</TD>

<TD>GDBITL</TD>

<TD>The number of independent bits in a linestyle.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_BITS_NORM_DBL_CMODE</TD>

<TD>GDDBLC</TD>

<TD>The number of bitplanes in each of the pair of main display buffers when the main display buffer is configured for double-buffered color map mode.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_BITS_NORM_DBL_RGB</TD>

<TD>GDDBLR</TD>

<TD>The number of bitplanes in each of the pair of main display buffers when the main display buffer is configured for double-buffered RGB mode.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_BITS_NORM_SNG_CMODE</TD>

<TD>GDSNGC</TD>

<TD>The number of bitplanes in the main display buffer when it is configured for single-buffered color map mode.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_BITS_NORM_SNG_RGB</TD>

<TD>GDSNGR</TD>

<TD>The number of bitplanes in the main display buffer when it is configured for single-buffered RGB mode.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_BITS_OVERLAY</TD>

<TD>GDBITO</TD>

<TD>The maximum number of overlay bitplanes for which the overlay buffer can be configured. Note that some adapters possess auxiliary bitplanes that can be configured as overlay or underlay bitplanes, but not both.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_BITS_PLANE_MASK</TD>

<TD>GDBITP</TD>

<TD>The maximum number of plane mask bitplanes available on the adapter.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_BITS_UNDERLAY</TD>

<TD>GDBITU</TD>

<TD>The maximum number of underlay bitplanes for which the underlay buffer can be configured. Note that some adapters possess auxiliary bitplanes that can be configured as overlay or underlay bitplanes, but not both.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_BITS_ZBUFFER</TD>

<TD>GDBITZ</TD>

<TD>The number of bitplanes in the z-buffer. A value of zero is returned if a z-buffer is not installed.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_BLEND</TD>

<TD>GDBLEN</TD>

<TD>True if alphablending is supported, False if not. <B>Note:</B> Alphablending does not necessarily require alpha bitplanes.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_BUTBOX</TD>

<TD>GDBUTB</TD>

<TD>True if a button box is attached to the system, False if not.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_DIALS</TD>

<TD>GDDIAL</TD>

<TD>True if dials are attached to the system, False if not.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_DITHER</TD>

<TD>GDDITH</TD>

<TD>A bit flag is returned indicating which buffers support dithering. The bit flag is the bitwise OR of the following flags: <B>GD_BF_UNDER</B> - Dithering in the underlay planes is supported. <B>GD_BF_OVER</B> - Dithering in the overlay planes is supported. <B>GD_BF_MAIN</B> - Dithering in the main frame buffer is supported. <B>GD_BF_ALPHA</B> - Dithering in the alpha buffer is supported.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_LARGE_MAP_SIZE</TD>

<TD>GDLMAP</TD>

<TD>The size of the single "large" color map.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_LIGHTING_TWOSIDE</TD>

<TD>GDLIG2</TD>

<TD>True if two-sided lighting is supported, False if not.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_LINESMOOTH_CMODE</TD>

<TD>GDLINC</TD>

<TD>True if smooth lines (antialiased lines) are supported in color index mode.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_LINESMOOTH_RGB</TD>

<TD>GDLINR</TD>

<TD>True if smooth lines (antialiased lines) are supported in RGB mode.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_MAX_ATTR_STACKDEPTH</TD>

<TD>GDMAST</TD>

<TD>The maximum depth of the attribute stack.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_MAX_LSREPEAT</TD>

<TD>GDMLSR</TD>

<TD>The maximum linestyle repeat factor that can be set.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_MAX_MATRIX_STACKDEPTH</TD>

<TD>GDMMST</TD>

<TD>The maximum depth of the modeling/viewing matrix stack.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_MAX_NURBS_ORDER</TD>

<TD>GDMNOR</TD>

<TD>The maximum supported order of a NURBS surface.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_MAX_PATTERN_SIZE</TD>

<TD>GDMPSZ</TD>

<TD>The maximum dimension of a pattern bitmask.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_MAX_TRIM_ORDER</TD>

<TD>GDMTOR</TD>

<TD>The maximum supported order of a NURBS trimming curve.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_MAX_VERTS</TD>

<TD>GDMVER</TD>

<TD>The maximum number of vertices that can be specified between a <B>bgn...()</B> and <B>end...()</B> subroutine pair.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_MAX_VIEWPORT_STACKDEPTH</TD>

<TD>GDMVST</TD>

<TD>The maximum depth of the viewport stack.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_NUM_SMALL_MAPS</TD>

<TD>GDNSM</TD>

<TD>The number of small color maps.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_OVERUNDER_SHARED</TD>

<TD>GDOUSH</TD>

<TD>True if overlay and underlay bitplanes are shared, False if not.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_POINTSMOOTH_CMODE</TD>

<TD>GDPSCM</TD>

<TD>True if smooth points (antialiased, pixel-sized points) are supported in color index mode.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_POINTSMOOTH_RGB</TD>

<TD>GDPSRG</TD>

<TD>True if smooth points (antialiased, pixel-sized points) are supported in RGB mode.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_POLYMODE</TD>

<TD>GDPOLY</TD>

<TD>True if polymode is functional, FALSE if not.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_RGBMODE</TD>

<TD>GDRGBM</TD>

<TD>A bit flag is returned indicating which buffers support an RGB mode (color map mode is always supported in all bitplanes). The bit flag is the bitwise <I>or</I> of the following flags: <B>GD_BF_UNDER</B> - RGB mode in the underlay planes is supported. <B>GD_BF_OVER</B> - RGB mode in the overlay planes is supported. <B>GD_BF_MAIN</B> - RGB mode the main frame buffer is supported.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_SHADEBUFFERS</TD>

<TD>GDSHAB</TD>

<TD>A bit flag is returned indicating which buffers support smooth (Gouraud) shading. The bit flag is the bitwise <I>or</I> of the following flags: <B>GD_BF_UNDER</B> - Smooth shading in the underlay planes is supported. <B>GD_BF_OVER</B> - Smooth shading in the overlay planes is supported. <B>GD_BF_MAIN</B> - Smooth shading in the main frame buffer is supported. <B>GD_BF_ALPHA</B> - Smooth shading in the alpha buffer is supported.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_SHADEMODEL</TD>

<TD>GDSHAM</TD>

<TD>A bit flag is returned indicating which shading models are supported. The bit flag is the bitwise OR of the following flags: <B>GD_SHADEMODEL_FLAT</B> - Only flat shading is supported. <B>GD_SHADEMODEL_GOURAUD</B> - Gouraud shading (linear interpolation of colors) is supported. <B>GD_SHADEMODEL_PSEUDO_PHONG</B> - Pseudo Phong  shading (adaptive tessellation of lit polygons) is supported. <B>GD_SHADEMODEL_PHONG</B> - Phong  shading (hardware interpolation of normal vectors) is supported. <B>GD_SHADEMODEL_QUADRATIC</B> - Quadratic interpolation of colors and textures maps is supported. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_SMALL_MAP_SIZE</TD>

<TD>GDSMAP</TD>

<TD>The size of the multiple "small" color maps.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_SUBPIXEL_LINE</TD>

<TD>GDSPLI</TD>

<TD>A bit flag is returned indicating which buffers support subpixel-positioned lines. The bit flag is the bitwise <I>or</I> of the following flags: <B>GD_BF_UNDER</B> - Subpixel-positioned lines in the underlay planes are supported. <B>GD_BF_OVER</B> - Subpixel-positioned lines in the overlay planes are supported. <B>GD_BF_MAIN</B> - Subpixel-positioned lines in the main frame buffer are supported. <B>GD_BF_ALPHA</B> - Subpixel-positioned lines in the alpha buffer are supported.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_SUBPIXEL_PNT</TD>

<TD>GDSPPN</TD>

<TD>A bit flag is returned indicating which buffers support subpixel-positioned points. The bit flag is the bitwise <I>or</I> of the following flags: <B>GD_BF_UNDER</B> - Subpixel-positioned points in the underlay planes are supported. <B>GD_BF_OVER</B> - Subpixel-positioned points in the overlay planes are supported. <B>GD_BF_MAIN</B> - Subpixel-positioned points in the main frame buffer are supported. <B>GD_BF_ALPHA</B> - Subpixel-positioned points in the alpha buffer are supported.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_SUBPIXEL_POLY</TD>

<TD>GDSPPL</TD>

<TD>A bit flag is returned indicating which buffers support subpixel-positioned polygons. The bit flag is the bitwise <I>or</I> of the following flags: <B>GD_BF_UNDER</B> - Subpixel-positioned polygons in the underlay planes are supported. <B>GD_BF_OVER</B> - Subpixel-positioned polygons in the overlay planes are supported. <B>GD_BF_MAIN</B> - Subpixel-positioned polygons in the main frame buffer are supported. <B>GD_BF_ALPHA</B> - Subpixel-positioned polygons in the alpha buffer are supported.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_TEXTPORT</TD>

<TD>GDTXTP</TD>

<TD>True if the textport routines are functional, False if not.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_VERT_RETRACE_FREQ</TD>

<TD>GDVREF</TD>

<TD>The vertical retrace frequency.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_WSYS</TD>

<TD>GDWSYS</TD>

<TD>The type of windowing system running on the processor. Returns one of the following:<B>GD_WSYS_NONE</B> - No window system is running.<B>GD_WSYS_4S</B> - 4Sight Window System (TM) is currently running.<B>GD_WSYS_AIX113</B> - AIXwindows, derived from X Windows System release 11.3, is currently running.<B>GD_WSYS_AIX114</B> - AIXwindows, derived from Enhanced X-Windows System release 11.4, is currently running.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_XMMAX</TD>

<TD>GDXMAX</TD>

<TD>Horizontal size of the screen in millimeters. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_YMMAX</TD>

<TD>GDYMAX</TD>

<TD>Vertical size of the screen in millimeters.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_XPMAX</TD>

<TD>GDXPMA</TD>

<TD>Horizontal size of the screen in pixels.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_YPMAX</TD>

<TD>GDYPMA</TD>

<TD>Vertical size of the screen in pixels. </TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_ZDRAW_GEOM</TD>

<TD>GDZGEO</TD>

<TD>True if geometrical figures can be drawn into the z-buffer, False if not.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_ZDRAW_PIXELS</TD>

<TD>GDZPIX</TD>

<TD>True if pixel block transfers to and from the z-buffer are possible, False if not.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_ZMIN</TD>

<TD>GDZMIN</TD>

<TD>The smallest value that can be written into the z-buffer.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP" ALIGN="LEFT"><TD>GD_ZMAX</TD>

<TD>GDZMAX</TD>

<TD>The largest value that can be written into the z-buffer.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="C7D02E6457bett"></A>Related Information</H3>

</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A16C0c9bd"></A>tpbig.c Example C Language Program
</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX2460" REL="I1" TITLE="tpbig.c example program (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2461" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2462" REL="I2" TITLE="example programs"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2463" REL="I3" TITLE="textport"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2464" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2465" REL="I2" TITLE="example programs"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2466" REL="I3" TITLE="drawing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2467" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2468" REL="I2" TITLE="example programs"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2469" REL="I3" TITLE="text"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2470" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2471" REL="I2" TITLE="text"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2472" REL="I3" TITLE="example program"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2473" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2474" REL="I2" TITLE="textport"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2475" REL="I3" TITLE="example program"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2476" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2477" REL="I2" TITLE="drawing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2478" REL="I3" TITLE="arc"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2479" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2480" REL="I2" TITLE="arc"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2481" REL="I3" TITLE="drawing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2482" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2483" REL="I2" TITLE="drawing"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2484" REL="I3" TITLE="polygon"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2485" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2486" REL="I2" TITLE="polygons"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX2487" REL="I3" TITLE="drawing"></A>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EBAD294ttay"></A>/*
tpbig.c:</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EBAD469ttay"></A>Basic graphics program demonstrating arcs, polygons, character
strings, and use of a textport.
*/</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EBAD632ttay"></A>#include &lt;gl/gl.h>
#include &lt;gl/device.h>
#include &lt;stdio.h></PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EBAD797ttay"></A>long cone[][2] = {100, 300, 150, 100, 200, 300};
char *singlechar;</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EBAD999ttay"></A>main()
{
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;int gid;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;short val;    
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;singlechar = malloc(2); /* Space for a character and a Null */
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;memcpy(singlechar, "X", 2);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;prefposition(0,XMAXSCREEN,0,YMAXSCREEN); </PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EBAE258ttay"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;gid = winopen("tpbig");
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;qdevice(ESCKEY);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;qdevice(REDRAW);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;qenter(REDRAW,gid); 
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;reshapeviewport();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;drawstuff();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;textport(50,300,750,900); 
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;tpon();     
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;while(TRUE) {
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;switch(qread(&amp;val)) {
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;case ESCKEY:
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;gexit();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;exit();            
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;case REDRAW:
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;reshapeviewport();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;drawstuff();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EBAE401ttay"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EBAE714ttay"></A>}
drawstuff()
{    
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;register long i, j;             /* draw an ice-cream cone */
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(WHITE);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;clear();
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(YELLOW);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;polf2i(3, cone);                /* draw the ice-cream cone */
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(GREEN);                   /* first scoop is mint */
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;arcfi(150, 300, 50, 0, 1800);   /* only half of it shows */
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(RED);                     /* second scoop is cherry */
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;circf(150.0, 400.0, 50.0);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(BLACK);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;poly2i(3, cone);                /* outline the cone in black */</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EBAE941ttay"></A>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;/* Next, draw a few filled and unfilled arcs in the upper
   * left corner of the screen.
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; */  
  arcf(100.0, 650.0, 40.0, 450, 2700);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;arci(100, 500, 40, 450, 2700);    
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;arcfi(250, 650, 80, 2700, 450);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;arc(250.0, 500.0, 80.0, 2700, 450);</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EBAF279ttay"></A>  /* Now, put up a series of filled and unfilled rectangles with
   * the names of their colors printed inside of them across the
   * rest of the top of the screen.
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; */
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(GREEN);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;recti(400, 600, 550, 700);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;cmov2i(420, 640);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;charstr("Green");    
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(RED);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;rectfi(600, 600, 800, 650);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(BLACK);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;cmov2(690.0, 620.0);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;charstr("Red");    
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;color(BLUE);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;rect(810.0, 700.0, 1000.0, 20.0);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;cmov2i(900, 300);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;charstr("Blue");
   /* Now draw some text with a ruler on top to measure it by. */
   /* First the ruler: */  </PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EBAF468ttay"></A>  color(BLACK);    
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;move2i(300, 400);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;draw2i(650, 400);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;for (i = 300; i &lt;= 650; i += 10) {
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;move2i(i, 400);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;draw2i(i, 410);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EBAF759ttay"></A> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; /* Then some text: */ 
  cmov2i(300, 380);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;charstr("The first line is drawn ");
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;charstr("in two parts.");    
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;cmov2i(300, 368);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;charstr("This line is only 12 pixels lower.");    
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;cmov2i(300, 354);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;charstr("Now move down 14 pixels ...");    
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;cmov2i(300, 338);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;charstr("And now down 16 ...");    
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;cmov2i(300, 320);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;charstr("Now 18 ...");    
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;cmov2i(300, 300);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;charstr("And finally, 20 pixels.");</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EBB0067ttay"></A>   /* Finally, show off the entire font.  The cmov2i() before 
    * each character is necessary in case that character is not 
    * defined.
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;  */
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;for (i = 0; i &lt; 4; i++)
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;for (j = 0; j &lt; 32; j++) {
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;cmov2i(300 + 9*j, 200 - 18*i);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;*singlechar = (char)(32*i + j);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;charstr(singlechar);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;}
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;for (i = 0; i &lt; 4; i++) {
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;cmov2i(300, 100 - 18*i);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;for (j = 0; j &lt; 32; j++) {
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;*singlechar = (char)(32*i + j);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;charstr(singlechar);
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;}
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EBB0210ttay"></A>}</PRE>
<PRE><A NAME="A64EBB0420ttay"></A>/*
  Changes:
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;- Changed memcopy(singlechar, "X", 2); to memcpy ...
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;  - Added the &amp; in this statement:
          switch(qread(&amp;val)) {
      - Removed the textinit(); call for case ESCKEY
*/</PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A201C11aa"></A>Related Information</H3>

<font color="#a62a2a" size="+2">
<i>GL3.2 for AIX: Graphics Library (GL) Technical Reference</i></font>
</center>
<hr size=3 noshade>
<H2><A NAME="A143X9c2f"></A>tpoff Subroutine</H2>
<A NAME="INDEX1920" REL="I1" TITLE="tpoff subroutine (GL)"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1921" REL="I1" TITLE="GL subroutines"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1922" REL="I2" TITLE="textport"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1923" REL="I3" TITLE="tpoff"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1924" REL="I1" TITLE="GL"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1925" REL="I2" TITLE="textport"></A>
<A NAME="INDEX1926" REL="I3" TITLE="turning off"></A>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9c31"></A>Purpose</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D756E718ceb"></A>Turns off the textport.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C11ec"></A>Libraries</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D756E757ceb"></A>Graphics Library</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D756E782ceb"></A>C (<B>libgl.a</B>)</P>

<P>FORTRAN (<B>libfgl.a</B>)</P>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9c35"></A>C Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A143X9c36"></A><B>void tpoff(&nbsp;)</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A213X9125c1"></A>FORTRAN Syntax</H3>
<PRE><A NAME="A213X9125c2"></A><B>SUBROUTINE TPOFF</B></PRE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9c37"></A>Description</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D756E889ceb"></A>The <B>tpoff</B> subroutine pushes the 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A154P11506">textport</A>, the window associated with the shell that invoked the graphics program, behind all other windows. </P>

<P><A NAME="E1D756E915ceb"></A>When the textport is off, characters are not written to it, nor does it display on the screen. The textport automatically turns on when a program completes execution.</P>

<BLOCKQUOTE><A NAME="A318C9f0d"></A><B>Note: </B>This subroutine cannot be used to add to a 
<!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/specialterms.html#A26P0473">display list</A>.</BLOCKQUOTE>


<H3><A NAME="A62C015d80"></A>Implementation Specifics</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D756E977ceb"></A>This subroutine is part of GL in the AIXwindows Environment/6000 Version 1, Release 2 with AIXwindows/3D Feature.</P>

<H3><A NAME="A79C11ef"></A>Files</H3>
<TABLE><TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C11f0"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/gl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains C language constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR>

<TR VALIGN="TOP"><TD NOWRAP="NOWRAP"><A NAME="A79C11f1"></A><B>/usr/include/gl/fgl.h</B></TD>
<TD>  Contains FORTRAN constant and variable type definitions for GL.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<H3><A NAME="A143X9c4f"></A>Related Information</H3>
<P><A NAME="E1D756F075ceb"></A>Allocating an area of the screen for the textport with the <A HREF="textport.html#A143X9cb7"><B>textport</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D756F100ceb"></A>Turning on the textport with the <A HREF="tpon.html#A14k110nita"><B>tpon</B></A> subroutine.</P>

<P><A NAME="E1D756F126ceb"></A><!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/gloverview.html#gloverview.html">AIX Graphics Library Overview</A> and Working with the <!--gl32prgd:--><A HREF="../gl32prgd/textport.html#textport.html">Textport</A>.</P><hr><center>
